HAD-0365.text: When Allah grants ample means, one should also dress fittingly for the prayer; in straitened circumstances, what covers is enough.
HAD-0365.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0365.speaker: ʿUmar رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-0365.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains the renewed wording of the Prophet's statement on prayer in a single garment, together with ʿUmar's saying: When Allah grants ample means, the one praying should also make that plain by fitting clothing. He lists the various combinations of Izār, Ridāʾ, shirt, cloak and trousers and explains the clothing terms. At the same time he records that prayer in one garment was permitted because of earlier poverty. He distinguishes in detail the ruling on a permitted prayer from the recommendation to wear more clothing when means are sufficient. The statement is a further wording of the principle of HAD-0358.

HAD-0366.text: The Muḥrim avoids certain garments and traces of perfume; whoever finds no sandals wears Ḫuff below the ankles.
HAD-0366.narrator: Ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-0366.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0366.sharh: Ibn Raǧab expressly points out why al-Buḫārī cites a report about garments forbidden in Iḥrām in the chapter on prayer clothing: the shirt, trousers and hooded cloak were ordinary garments. That the Prophet ﷺ forbade them to the Muḥrim means at the same time that wearing them outside Iḥrām was in principle approved. These kinds of clothing, while the other conditions of prayer are observed, are therefore not unlawful for the prayer solely because of their form. The report also contains the particular instruction of that time to cut the Ḫuff below the ankles when sandals were lacking; this wording, which relates to Iḥrām, is not to be equated with general prayer clothing. Ibn Raǧab refers to Imām Aḥmad's application of this evidence to the wearing of trousers.

HAD-0367.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade tight wrapping without an opening and sitting in a garment without sufficient covering.
HAD-0367.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0367.speaker: He said:
HAD-0367.sharh: Ibn Raǧab treats two forbidden ways of wearing a single garment: the so-called Ištimāl aṣ-Ṣammāʾ and sitting with the legs drawn up, in which the ʿAwrah remains uncovered. He compares the purely linguistic explanation of the first kind of garment with the explanation of the early Fuqahāʾ, according to which the ʿAwrah can become visible by raising the garment on one side. For the Ḥadīṯ context Ibn Raǧab expressly prefers the interpretation which the scholars drew from the transmission. If the ʿAwrah is in fact covered, he documents a difference of opinion about the legal consequence of the forbidden manner of wearing for the validity of the prayer.

HAD-0368.text: Certain forms of trade were forbidden, and likewise kinds of clothing that violate modesty and covering.
HAD-0368.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0368.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ forbade:
HAD-0368.sharh: Ibn Raǧab places the transmission from Abū Hurayrah in the same chapter on covering the ʿAwrah. The text lists two unlawful forms of trade, Mulāmasah and Munābaḏah, and two ways of dressing, among them the Ṣammāʾ wrapping and sitting in the single garment without sufficient covering. In the context of the chapter he explains above all the ways of dressing and distinguishes their possible linguistic meanings from the earlier legal interpretations. The trade prohibitions are part of the authentic transmission, but here they are not the subject of a separate detailed writing on trade.

HAD-0369.text: Abū Bakr رضي الله عنه sent callers to Minā: After this year, no idolater at the Ḥajj and no naked Ṭawāf.
HAD-0369.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0369.speaker: He said:
HAD-0369.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains the report of Abū Hurayrah about the public announcement in Minā during the pilgrimage led by Abū Bakr. It was announced that after this year no idolaters should come to the Ḥaǧǧ and no one should perform the Ṭawāf unclothed. Ibn Raǧab points out that in the wording cited here the prophetic commission is not expressly stated in every single sentence; from the further paths of transmission and from the historical event, however, the instruction of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ follows. In doing so he expressly distinguishes the wordings and their chains of transmission.

HAD-0370.text: He prayed intentionally without a Ridāʾ, so that those who did not know would see that he had seen the Prophet ﷺ pray in that way.
HAD-0370.speaker: Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-0370.sharh: The report about Ǧābir's deliberate prayer in a single Izār serves, with Ibn Raǧab, as proof that this prayer clothing is permitted when the covering is sufficient. He expressly separates Ǧābir's own demonstration from the prophetic texts, which only report prayer in a single garment. If someone did not know the permission, Ǧābir could thereby show it in a way that could be seen. This presentation overlaps in content with HAD-0352 without producing an additional independent legal case.

HAD-0371.text: Follow and do not invent anew; you have already been given sufficiency.
HAD-0371.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0371.speaker: He said:

HAD-0372.text: Every Bidʿah is misguidance, even if people consider it good.
HAD-0372.narrator: It is transmitted of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-0372.speaker: He said:

HAD-0373.text: The people asked about the good; I asked about the evil, for fear that it would reach me.
HAD-0373.narrator: It is transmitted of Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0373.speaker: He said:

HAD-0374.text: Speak to people with what they understand; do you want Allah and His Messenger to be denied?
HAD-0374.narrator: It is transmitted of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0374.speaker: He said:

HAD-0375.text: How will you be when a Fitnah covers you, in which the adult grows old and the boy grows up?
HAD-0375.narrator: It is transmitted of ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0375.speaker: He said:

HAD-0376.text: There is transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās a warning not to displace the statement of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by the view of others; the widespread wording about stones from heaven has so far not been confirmed word for word in the early source named for it.
HAD-0376.narrator: It is transmitted of Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-0376.speaker: He said:

HAD-0377.text: Call yourselves to account before you are called to account; weigh yourselves before you are weighed.
HAD-0377.narrator: It is transmitted of ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0377.speaker: He said:

HAD-0378.text: Among the signs of understanding is that the servant examines his Īmān, looks at what of it has decreased, and checks whether it increases or decreases.
HAD-0378.narrator: It is transmitted of Abū ad-Dardāʾ رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0378.speaker: He said:

HAD-0379.text: It is transmitted from Muʿāḏ ibn Ǧabal: Knowledge alone brings no reward so long as it is not acted upon. (Translation according to the sense; the chain of attribution is interrupted.)
HAD-0379.narrator: It is transmitted of Muʿādh ibn Jabal رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0379.speaker: He said:

HAD-0380.text: Abū Bakr said in connection with administering the Ṣadaqah of the Prophet ﷺ: I will not omit anything that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to do without doing it as well; I fear otherwise to deviate from his path.
HAD-0380.narrator: It is transmitted of Abū Bakr aṣ-Ṣiddīq رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0380.speaker: He said:

HAD-0381.text: Moderation in the Sunnah is better than exertion in a Bidʿah.
HAD-0381.narrator: It is transmitted of Ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0381.speaker: He said:

HAD-0382.text: From Ibn ʿUmar there is cited, according to the sense, an admonition to hold fast to the Sunnah. The exact wording and the attribution of this particular wording must still be examined.
HAD-0382.narrator: It is transmitted of Ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-0382.speaker: He said:

HAD-0383.text: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb admonished: Hold to the path and the Sunnah. He mentioned Allah's mercy for the one who weeps on this path out of fear of Allah, and the merit of moderate action on the path of the Sunnah.
HAD-0383.narrator: It is transmitted of ʿUbayy ibn Kaʿb رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0383.speaker: He said:

HAD-0384.text: Knowledge is not abundant transmission alone; knowledge is that which benefits.
HAD-0384.narrator: It is transmitted of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-0384.speaker: He said:

HAD-0001.text: Deeds are judged according to intentions, and each person has only what he intended. So whoever emigrated for the sake of Allah and His Messenger, his emigration was to Allah and His Messenger; and whoever emigrated for a worldly matter or for a woman he wished to marry, his emigration was to that for which he emigrated.
HAD-0001.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0001.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains, following al-Muhallab, that al-Buḫārī placed this Ḥadīṯ at the beginning of his work in order to direct the reader to sincerity of intention: whoever reads this book, learns it, or transmits it should thereby intend the Face of Allah. In this way the Ḥadīṯ is set in the place of an introductory Ḫuṭbah. The meaning of the Ḥadīṯ is that outwardly identical actions are assessed differently according to intention. The Hiǧrah to Allah and His Messenger is therefore not like a Hiǧrah for a worldly matter or for marriage, even though the outward movement may appear the same.

HAD-0002.text: Islam was built upon five things: the testimony that none has the right to be worshipped except Allah and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah, the establishment of the prayer, the payment of the Zakāh, the pilgrimage, and fasting in Ramaḍān.
HAD-0002.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0002.sharh: The earliest explanation that can be grasped here already lies in al-Buḫārī’s chapter arrangement. He places the Ḥadīṯ at the beginning of Kitāb al-Īmān under the heading of the word of the Prophet ﷺ: ‘Islam was built upon five things,’ and before that he sets the principle: Īmān is statement and action; it increases and decreases. Then he cites Qurʾān evidences and Athār of the Salaf, among them the letter of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz: Īmān has obligations, legal rulings, limits, and Sunan; whoever fulfills them completely completes Īmān. Thereby al-Buḫārī explains the Ḥadīṯ not as a mere enumeration, but as proof that the visible pillars of Islām belong to the reality and completeness of Īmān.

HAD-0003.text: The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe; and the emigrant is the one who leaves what Allah has forbidden.
HAD-0003.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0003.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that ‘the Muslim’ here means the more complete and more comprehensive Islām: the one who does not harm a Muslim by word or deed. That the tongue and the hand are mentioned in particular covers the most common ways of harm: the tongue stands for insulting, slanderous and injurious speech; the hand stands for outward seizure, striking, taking or any other act. It does not follow from this that someone without this completeness is not a Muslim at all, but that the Ḥadīṯ describes the best and more complete form of Islām. The second part explains the complete Hiǧrah: not merely a change of place, but leaving what Allah has forbidden.

HAD-0004.text: None of you believes completely until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
HAD-0004.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0004.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the Ḥadīṯ as a negation of complete Īmān, not as a negation of Islām itself. He reports from Abū az-Zinād that the outward form of the Ḥadīṯ mentions equality, yet its real content even includes preference: a person ordinarily loves to possess a special preference himself. When he then loves the same for his brother, he includes him in the good that he wishes for himself. To this also belongs that the believer, in rights and claims, does not merely prefer himself, but is just toward his brother and gives him his right, even when this is hard against his own inclination.

HAD-0005.text: There are three qualities; whoever possesses them finds thereby the sweetness of faith: that Allah and His Messenger are more beloved to him than everything else, that he loves a person only for the sake of Allah, and that he hates to return to unbelief as he hates to be thrown into the fire.
HAD-0005.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0005.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the ‘sweetness of Īmān’ means the inner enjoyment of acts of obedience: the believer finds joy in obeying Allah and His Messenger, bears hardship in what pleases Allah and His Messenger, and prefers this to the passing shares of the world, because he hopes for the lasting reward in the Hereafter. The love of Allah and His Messenger therefore stands above every other love. Likewise, love of a person only for the sake of Allah is a sign of this sweetness, because it does not rest on passing worldly aims. And whoever has recognized where kufr leads hates to return there as he hates to be thrown into the fire.

HAD-0006.text: The signs of the hypocrite are three: when he speaks, he lies; when he promises, he breaks his promise; and when something is entrusted to him, he acts treacherously.
HAD-0006.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0006.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that these qualities do not belong to the qualities of the complete believers, but to the qualities of the hypocrites. Especially concerning lying, he points out: if a person repeats lying until he can be described with the exaggerated designation ‘liar,’ this does not belong to the marks of the complete Muʾminūn, but to the marks of the Munāfiqūn. The Ḥadīṯ therefore warns against a practical resemblance to Nifāq: untrue speech, treachery regarding what is entrusted, and breaking a promise. What is meant by this is a dangerous resemblance of character, not automatically the judgment that every single doer leaves Islām.

HAD-0007.text: Faith has more than seventy branches. The highest of them is the statement that none has the right to be worshipped except Allah; the lowest is the removal of an obstacle from the path. And modesty is a branch of faith.
HAD-0007.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0007.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the Schuʿab of Īmān show that the name Īmān is also applied in the Šarīʿah to actions and obedience. The highest level is Tawḥīd, without which no other Schuʿbah is valid; the lowest mentioned level is the removal of a harm from the path, whereby benefit for people and the warding off of harm take place. Between these two limits lie numerous doors of obedience. Their exact and complete enumeration is not a condition for the validity of Īmān; what is obligatory is to believe in the entirety of what the Prophet ﷺ has reported, while the foundations and branches of Īmān were made known in the Qurʾān and in the Sunnah. Ḥayāʾ is mentioned expressly because this inner quality holds a person back from evil and moves him toward good.

HAD-0008.text: The religion is sincere counsel. We asked: For whom? He said: For Allah, His Book, His Messenger, the leaders of the Muslims, and the generality of the Muslims.
HAD-0008.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0008.sharh: al-Māzirī explains that Naṣīḥah can linguistically have two directions of meaning: it can come from purification and cleansing, as when honey is purified of admixtures, and it can be connected with mending and joining together. Thereby it becomes clear why this Ḥadīṯ describes the religion so comprehensively: Naṣīḥah is sincere purity in relation to the one for whom it is due, and at the same time the striving to uphold his right completely. For Allah this means sincerity in Tawḥīd and in ʿIbādah; for His Book, belief, reverence, understanding and acting; for His Messenger ﷺ, confirmation, obedience, love and support of his Sunnah; for those responsible among the Muslims, righteous counsel and help upon the truth; and for the generality of the Muslims, wishing good, teaching, warning against harm, and refraining from fraud or betrayal.

HAD-0009.text: The lawful is clear and the forbidden is clear. Between the two lie doubtful matters which many people do not know. Whoever guards himself against the doubtful matters preserves his religion and his honor.
HAD-0009.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0009.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl reports from al-Muhallab: The intermediate areas between clear Ḥalāl and clear Ḥarām are attached to principles from both sides. If a proof preponderates, the matter is assigned to that side; if proofs or meanings pull from both sides and preference becomes difficult, the Schubha arises. Whoever avoids such doubtful matters protects his religion from deficiency and his honor from blame. The wording ‘many people do not know them’ shows at the same time that some people of knowledge and of derivation can recognize such matters. The parable of the protected area warns against approaching the boundary of the prohibitions, so that one does not fall into what Allah has forbidden.

HAD-0010.text: Allah is good and accepts only what is good. Allah has commanded the believers the same as He commanded the messengers. *Then he mentioned the man who travels long, disheveled and covered with dust, and raises his hands to the heaven*, while his food, his drink and his clothing come from what is forbidden. How should his supplication be answered?
HAD-0010.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0010.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that describing Allah as Ṭayyib here means: free of deficiencies, in the sense of al-Quddūs. The origin of Ṭayyib comprises purity, clarity and freedom from Ḫubṯ. Therefore Allah accepts only what is ṭayyib: that is, spending, outlay and action from lawful, pure acquisition and upon a sincere basis. The reference to the traveler shows that several reasons for the answering of Duʿāʾ can come together: a long journey, need, raised hands and repeated calling. Nevertheless his being answered becomes remote when food, drink, clothing and provision come from Ḥarām. The Ḥadīṯ therefore connects the acceptance of deeds and the answering of Duʿāʾ with purity of acquisition and avoidance of the forbidden.

HAD-0011.text: The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, yet in both there is good. Strive for what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not become incapable.
HAD-0011.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0011.sharh: An-Nawawī explains that strength here means above all determination, inner strength and energy in the affairs of the Āḫirah: stronger in obedience, in seeking good, in bearing hardship for Allah and in steadfastness. ‘Strive for what benefits you’ means: strive for obedience to Allah and for what brings benefit with Him; at the same time one should seek Allah’s help and not become lazy.

HAD-0012.text: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should not harm his neighbor; whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should honor his guest; and whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or remain silent.
HAD-0012.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0012.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the wording ‘whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day’ points to complete Īmān. The force of this Īmān moves the person to call himself to account already in this world, before he is called to account on the Last Day. Therefore he holds himself back from harm toward the neighbor, honors the guest and especially guards his tongue. Concerning speech: if the word is good, he should speak it; if no good word is present, he should remain silent, so that his speech does not become regret for him on the Day of Resurrection.

HAD-0013.text: Make it easy and do not make it difficult. Give glad tidings and do not drive people away.
HAD-0013.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0013.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that this Ḥadīṯ shows the prophetic method in teaching, admonishing and guiding. Facilitation does not mean abolishing duties or making light of prohibitions, but choosing the way that Allah has permitted and made easy, especially where there is a permission, a relief or a suitable gradation. People should be made familiar with the good and moved toward acceptance. Therefore facilitation is joined with glad tidings, and making things difficult is forbidden together with driving people away, because unnecessary harshness can remove people from knowledge, obedience and good acceptance.

HAD-0014.text: The deeds most beloved to Allah are those that are performed constantly, even if they are small.
HAD-0014.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0014.sharh: The earliest layer of explanation here already lies in al-Buḫārī’s chapter heading: ‘Moderation and constancy in action.’ Thereby the Ḥadīṯ is not understood as a call to heavy overload, but as guidance to a lasting, bearable worship. ʿĀʾišah also reports, in the narrations of this meaning, that the deed of the Prophet ﷺ was constant and that she herself, when she performed a deed, held to it. The sense is: a small deed that remains is more beloved to Allah than much deed that overburdens the person and then breaks off.

HAD-0015.text: Allah does not look at your outward form and your wealth, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds.
HAD-0015.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0015.sharh: An-Nawawī explains this Ḥadīṯ in the context of the prohibition of despising a Muslim: the measure with Allah is not outward form, beauty, standing or wealth, but what is in the heart of Īmān, sincerity and Taqwā, and the deeds that proceed from that. The Ḥadīṯ therefore points to purifying the heart, correcting the intention and not belittling other Muslims according to outward rank or possession.

HAD-0016.text: Whoever does not show mercy, to him no mercy is shown.
HAD-0016.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0016.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ urges mercy toward all creatures. This mercy is not limited only to believers, but also includes non-Muslims and animals, insofar as they fall under general mercy. To this belong food and drink, the easing of burdens, and refraining from unjust beating, torment or harm. Whoever himself practices mercy toward the creatures is thereby more subject to the mercy of Allah; whoever withholds it is warned accordingly.

HAD-0017.text: Gentleness is not found in anything without beautifying it, and it is not removed from anything without marring it.
HAD-0017.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0017.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the merit of ar-Rifq as a comprehensive quality by which actions become more beautiful, easier to accept and closer to the right measure. The Ḥadīṯ shows that gentleness adorns a thing because it pushes back harshness, exaggeration and an unsuitable way of proceeding. If gentleness is removed from a thing, it appears deficient and unattractive. The transmitted situation with the difficult mount shows that Rifq does not apply only in dealing with people, but also in practical situations in which anger or a coarse way of proceeding could lie near.

HAD-0018.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0018.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the short repeated counsel ‘Do not become angry’ was given because of its comprehensive benefit. What is meant is not that a person can completely extinguish every natural impulse, but that he avoids the causes of blameworthy anger and controls his soul before anger drives him to injustice, insult, striking, breaking of rights or another transgression. The Ḥadīṯ thereby gathers a great door of Adab: whoever controls anger protects religion, honor and dealings with people.

HAD-0019.text: The strong one is not the one who defeats others in wrestling. The truly strong one is the one who controls himself when he becomes angry.
HAD-0019.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0019.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ corrects the measure of strength. Not the one who throws others down in wrestling is truly strong, but the one who controls his own soul in the state of anger. For anger frequently moves a person to injustice, sharp speech, attack or transgression. Whoever holds it back overcomes something harder than the body of another person: he overcomes his own desire for retaliation and thereby protects religion, tongue and hand from harm.

HAD-0020.text: Hold to truthfulness, for truthfulness leads to righteousness and righteousness leads to Paradise. Beware of lying, for lying leads to wickedness and wickedness leads to the Fire.
HAD-0020.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0020.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ lays open the paths and consequences of truthfulness and lying. Truthfulness leads to Birr, that is, to comprehensive righteousness, obedience and good; Birr leads to Paradise. Lying leads to Fuǧūr, that is, to stepping out of obedience and to wickedness; Fuǧūr leads to the Fire. Whoever repeatedly strives for truthfulness is recorded with Allah as a truthful one; whoever becomes accustomed to lying is recorded as a liar. The Ḥadīṯ therefore warns not only against individual words, but against a lasting quality that shapes the person.

HAD-0082.text: Allah extends His hand at night so that the one who sinned by day may repent, and He extends His hand by day so that the one who sinned at night may repent. *This remains so until the sun rises in the West.*
HAD-0082.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0082.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the continuing opening of Tawbah: whoever has sinned by day finds the door of return open at night, and whoever has sinned at night finds it open by day. The mention of the hand is affirmed as befits Allah, without likening Him to created beings; the meaning of the Ḥadīṯ is Allah’s generosity in accepting repentance. This door remains open until the great sign occurs, that the sun rises from the West; then the acceptance of repentance ends in the general sense of this trial.

HAD-0083.text: Allah, the Exalted, says: ‘I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me.’
HAD-0083.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0083.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the servant should think well of Allah by hoping for His mercy, forgiveness and acceptance, and at the same time not falling into a sense of security from His punishment. The statement ‘I am with him when he remembers Me’ shows the merit of Ḏikr and Allah’s special nearness to those who remember Him, in a manner that befits His majesty. The Ḥadīṯ joins hope, Ḏikr and trust in Allah; good thinking here is not empty hope while persisting in sin, but hope together with Tawbah, obedience and sincerity.

HAD-0084.text: When you ask Allah, ask Him for al-Firdaws, for it is the highest and best part of Paradise; above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful, and from it spring the rivers of Paradise.
HAD-0084.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0084.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the Ḥadīṯ as an encouragement to ask Allah in Duʿāʾ for the highest ranks. al-Firdaws is named as the highest and best part of Paradise; through this the servant learns to make his hope great and to ask Allah for the best, without holding his request as slight. The mention of the Throne of the Most Merciful and the rivers of Paradise shows the special rank of this place and its nearness to the highest honours of the Hereafter.

HAD-0085.text: Whoever performs the two cool prayers will enter Paradise.
HAD-0085.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0085.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the two cool prayers mean Ṣubḥ and ʿAṣr. Their merit is especially emphasised because Ṣubḥ falls at a time when sleep and lethargy can weigh heavily, and ʿAṣr at a time when the day’s work and occupations distract a person. Whoever preserves these two prayers shows care for the Ṣalāh in difficult times; that is why the promise of Paradise is mentioned in the Ḥadīṯ.

HAD-0086.text: No Muslim servant offers Allah twelve voluntary units of prayer each day, besides the obligatory prayers, without Allah building for him a house in Paradise.
HAD-0086.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0086.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the Ḥadīṯ as a special encouragement to constancy in the regular voluntary prayers alongside the obligatory prayers. The twelve Rakʿah belong to the Rawātib, by which the servant completes his obligatory prayers, strengthens his bond with the Ṣalāh and each day preserves a fixed share of voluntary worship. The promise of a house in Paradise shows the rank of this constant deed and that a small daily constancy can have an immense reward with Allah.

HAD-0087.text: Whoever performs the night prayer in congregation, it is as though he spent half the night in prayer; and whoever performs the night prayer and the morning prayer in congregation, it is as though he spent the whole night in prayer.
HAD-0087.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0087.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the immense merit of ʿIšāʾ and Ṣubḥ in congregation. These two prayers fall at times when sleep, rest and darkness can weigh upon the soul; therefore preserving them is especially rewarded. Whoever prays ʿIšāʾ in congregation receives a reward like spending half the night in prayer, and whoever in addition preserves Ṣubḥ in congregation receives a reward like a whole night. The Ḥadīṯ is thus a strong encouragement not to neglect the congregation precisely at these two prayers.

HAD-0088.text: The best fasting after Ramaḍān is fasting in the month of Allah, al-Muḥarram; and the best prayer after the obligatory prayer is the night prayer.
HAD-0088.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0088.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the attribution ‘month of Allah’ highlights the rank of al-Muḥarram and encourages voluntary fasting in this month. The Ḥadīṯ ranks the voluntary deeds according to their merit: after Ramaḍān, Muḥarram is especially distinguished in voluntary fasting, and after the obligatory prayers the night prayer is the most excellent voluntary prayer. In this lies an indication of the value of hidden worship, patience and standing for Allah in times of rest.

HAD-0089.text: Whoever does not abandon false speech and acting upon it, Allah has no need of his abstaining from food and drink.
HAD-0089.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0089.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ warns the fasting person against reducing the meaning of fasting to mere abstention from food and drink. Whoever does not avoid false speech, lying, evil utterance and acting upon it, neglects a great purpose of fasting: to restrain the soul, guard the tongue and leave sins. The statement that Allah has no need of his abstaining from food and drink is a stern warning against a fast whose outward form remains while its inner purpose is severely damaged.

HAD-0090.text: Seek the Night of Decree in the odd nights of the last ten nights of Ramaḍān.
HAD-0090.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0090.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the command to seek Laylat al-Qadr in the odd nights of the last ten nights holds the servant to repeated striving. The night was not fixed and disclosed as one single night, so that people might enliven several nights with Qiyām, Duʿāʾ, Ḏikr, Qurʾān and Iʿtikāf. The emphasis on the odd nights shows their special precedence, without belittling the striving in the remaining nights of the last ten.

HAD-0091.text: When Ramaḍān begins, the gates of Paradise are opened, the gates of the Hellfire are closed and the devils are chained.
HAD-0091.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0091.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that Ramaḍān is distinguished by special causes of good. The opening of the gates of Paradise points to the increase of mercy, obedience and ways to good; the closing of the gates of the Fire points to the lessening of the causes of punishment; and the chaining of the devils shows that their effect is weakened in Ramaḍān. The Ḥadīṯ encourages not to treat this time like other times, but to make use of the facilitated doors of obedience.

HAD-0092.text: Two words are light on the tongue, heavy on the Scale and beloved to the Most Merciful: ‘Glory be to Allah and praise belongs to Him; glory be to Allah, the Magnificent.’
HAD-0092.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0092.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the great worth of Ḏikr, although its words are light upon the tongue. The two formulas join Tasbīḥ, that is, declaring Allah free of defects, with Ḥamd, that is, praise and acknowledgement of His perfection. They are beloved to the Most Merciful and heavy on the Scale, because their meaning is immense and because sincere Ḏikr has great weight with Allah, even when it appears outwardly short and light.

HAD-0093.text: Whoever says a hundred times a day: ‘Glory be to Allah and praise belongs to Him’, his sins will be forgiven, even if they were like the foam of the sea.
HAD-0093.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0093.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that this Ḏikr has an immense merit because it joins Tasbīḥ and Ḥamd. The repeated statement ‘subḥān Allāh wa-bi-ḥamdih’ purifies the tongue with praise of Allah, reminds the servant of the perfection of his Lord and becomes a cause of forgiveness. The mention of the sea’s foam shows the vastness of Allah’s forgiveness and encourages preserving this light yet weighty Ḏikr regularly and with a sincere heart.

HAD-0094.text: By Allah, I ask Allah for forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance more than seventy times each day.
HAD-0094.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0094.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the frequent Tawbah and the Istighfār of the Prophet ﷺ are a teaching for the Ummah and a sign of perfect humility before Allah. Although Allah has forgiven His Prophet ﷺ, he increased Istighfār out of gratitude, nearness to Allah and constant return to Him. The Ḥadīṯ shows that no one may belittle Istighfār; rather, frequent repentance is a quality of the best and a daily path to purification and nearness.

HAD-0095.text: The most excellent supplication for forgiveness is that the servant says: ‘O Allah, You are my Lord. None has the right to be worshipped except You. You created me and I am Your servant. I hold to Your covenant and Your promise as far as I am able. I seek refuge with You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your favour upon me and I acknowledge my sin. So forgive me, for none forgives sins except You.’
HAD-0095.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0095.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that this supplication is called Sayyid al-Istighfār because it gathers the most important meanings of repentance. The servant begins with Tawḥīd and the acknowledgement that Allah is his Lord, Creator and the only One worthy of worship. Then he confesses his servitude, his holding to Allah’s covenant, his weakness, his sin and his need of forgiveness. At the same time he acknowledges Allah’s favour. Thus the Duʿāʾ joins knowledge of Allah, humility, confession of guilt, gratitude, refuge and the request for forgiveness.

HAD-0096.text: Allah has written down the good deeds and the bad deeds. Whoever intends a good deed and does not carry it out, Allah writes for him a complete good deed; if he carries it out, Allah writes it from tenfold up to many times more. Whoever intends a bad deed and does not carry it out, Allah writes for him a complete good deed; if he carries it out, only one bad deed is written for him.
HAD-0096.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0096.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that this Ḥadīṯ is among the clearest texts about Allah’s mercy and generosity. A good intention is already written as a complete good deed, and when it is carried out it is multiplied many times. Whoever leaves a bad deed for Allah’s sake receives a reward for that; if he carries it out, however, it is written only once. Thereby the Ḥadīṯ shows that Allah makes the doors of good wide and does not multiply the punishment as He multiplies the reward.

HAD-0097.text: No Muslim plants a plant or sows something of which a bird, a person or an animal eats without it counting for him as a good deed.
HAD-0097.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0097.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the merit of planting, sowing and all the benefit that thereby reaches created beings. When a person, an animal or a bird eats of it, this is written for the one who plants or sows as Ṣadaqah, even if he does not know the exact beneficiary. The Ḥadīṯ shows that lawful work, agriculture and conferring benefit with a good intention can become ongoing reward, so long as Allah brings about benefit through this cause.

HAD-0098.text: Ǧibrīl kept enjoining the neighbour upon me so insistently that I thought he would make him an heir.
HAD-0098.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0098.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that Ǧibrīl’s repeated enjoining shows the immense rank of the neighbour’s right. The neighbour is not only to be protected from harm, but also to be met with kindness, consideration, help and good treatment. That the Prophet ﷺ thought the neighbour might even be made an heir shows the strength of this enjoining and how near his right was placed in dealings, care and respect.

HAD-0099.text: The one who truly maintains kinship is not merely the one who repays like with like. The true maintainer of kinship is the one who upholds the bond when his relatives sever it.
HAD-0099.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0099.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the complete maintaining of kinship does not consist only in repaying kindness with equal kindness. That is indeed permissible and good, but the special rank lies in upholding the bond when the relatives sever it, and in doing good although the same is not returned. The Ḥadīṯ trains one in patience, forbearance and upholding the rights of kinship for Allah’s sake, not only as a reaction to the good conduct of others.

HAD-0100.text: Treat women well. The woman was created from a rib, and the most curved part of the rib is its upper part. If you try to straighten her completely, you break her; if you leave her, her curvature remains. *Therefore treat women well.*
HAD-0100.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0100.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ guides to good dealings with women, to patience and to gentle treatment. The example of the rib makes clear that the man should not act with harshness, coercion or an excessive demand for complete conformity; for such a course leads to breaking. Rather, he should preserve the good, deal with natural difference, admonish without destruction and conduct the marriage with forbearance and just treatment.

HAD-0102.text: Wealth does not consist in the abundance of possessions; rather, true wealth is the wealth of the soul.
HAD-0102.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0102.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that true wealth is not measured by the abundance of possessions. A person may own much and still remain needy in the heart, because his greed does not end. The real wealth is the contentment of the soul: that the servant is pleased with what Allah has given him, does not constantly seek the possessions of others and that his heart is not ruled by desire for more. The Ḥadīṯ turns the gaze from outward quantity to the inner state.

HAD-0131.text: Whoever provides for two girls until they reach adulthood will be with me on the Day of Resurrection.
HAD-0131.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0131.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the merit of caring for daughters. What is meant is not merely food, but provision, protection, upbringing, patience, good treatment, and preservation of their rights until they become independent and reach adulthood. The promise of nearness to the Prophet ﷺ on the Day of Resurrection shows the high rank of this responsibility, especially because daughters were placed in a weaker position in many societies and need particular care.

HAD-0132.text: Every child is born upon the natural disposition. Thereafter his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a fire-worshipper.
HAD-0132.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0132.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ names the original disposition upon which Allah creates the child. The child does not come into the world with an acquired false religion; rather, parents, upbringing, and environment then act upon him. The mention of Judaism, Christianity, and fire-worship shows that outward shaping can be a strong cause of deviation from the original Fitrah. At the same time, the Ḥadīṯ makes clear the responsibility of parents and those who raise children.

HAD-0133.text: The names most beloved to Allah are ʿAbdullāh and ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān.
HAD-0133.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0133.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the special merit of these two names lies in their expressly showing the servanthood of the human being toward Allah. ʿAbdullāh joins the servant's name to the comprehensive name Allah, and ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān joins it to the name of the Most Merciful. Both names remind of Tawḥīd, humility, and the fact that the highest honor of the human being lies in his ʿUbūdiyyah toward Allah.

HAD-0134.text: Mention Allah's name, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is in front of you.
HAD-0134.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0134.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ gathers several foundations of the adab of eating. The Tasmiyah connects the food with gratitude and remembrance of Allah. Eating with the right hand belongs to Adab and to distinguishing oneself from blameworthy conduct. Eating from what lies before one preserves courtesy at a shared meal and prevents encroachment upon the share of others. The Prophet ﷺ taught this to a young Companion with brief, clear, and merciful upbringing.

HAD-0135.text: If a morsel falls from one of you, he should remove the dirt from it and eat it, and not leave it to Satan. *You do not know in which part of your food the blessing lies.*
HAD-0135.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0135.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the Ḥadīṯ trains the Muslim in gratitude and respect for food. If a morsel falls and can be cleaned, one should not throw it away and should not leave it to Satan. In this lies avoidance of waste, humility toward Allah's gift, and recognition that the Barakah does not always lie where the human being supposes. The Ḥadīṯ guards the servant from belittling food.

HAD-0137.text: The believer eats with one intestine, while the disbeliever eats with seven intestines.
HAD-0137.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0137.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ censures greed, excess, and attachment to mere appetite. The believer should be moderate in eating, because his aim does not lie in filling the belly, but in gaining strength for obedience and gratitude. The mention of the seven intestines in the case of the disbeliever points to excessive appetite and the absence of an inner limit. The Ḥadīṯ therefore calls to contentment, discipline, and distance from immoderation.

HAD-0138.text: When the evening meal is ready and the prayer begins, then begin with the evening meal.
HAD-0138.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0138.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ protects concentration in the prayer. When the food is ready and the heart clings to it strongly, the one praying can be distracted in the prayer. Therefore this immediate preoccupation should first be removed, so that he may afterwards pray more calmly and attentively. What is meant is not negligence toward the Ṣalāh, but the removal of a strong distraction, so long as the prayer time is not thereby missed and the obligation is not treated lightly.

HAD-0140.text: Whatever of the garment hangs below the ankles is in the Fire.
HAD-0140.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0140.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ contains a severe warning against letting the garment hang below the ankles. The wording does not make the matter a mere habit without religious weight; it connects it with a threat. The further reports concerning Isbāl show that arrogance has a particularly grave significance in this. The believer is thereby trained in humility, distance from ostentation, and following the prophetic limit in clothing.

HAD-0141.text: Distinguish yourselves from the idolaters: let the beards grow and shorten the mustaches.
HAD-0141.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0141.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ commands the Muslims a visible distinction from the Mušrikīn in this matter. Letting the beard grow and shortening the mustache belong to the features of the Fitrah and of prophetic Adab. The command is not merely an outward form without meaning; it joins obedience, natural purity, and distance from imitating religious opposition.

HAD-0142.text: Allah loves sneezing and detests yawning. When one of you sneezes and praises Allah, the Muslim who hears him should wish him mercy. Yawning is from Satan; one should suppress it as well as one can.
HAD-0142.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0142.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that sneezing is loved because Ḥamd and Duʿāʾ arise from it: the one who sneezes praises Allah, and the one who hears asks mercy for him. Yawning, by contrast, is connected with heaviness, lethargy, and heedlessness; therefore it is attributed to Satan and should be restrained as well as one can. The Ḥadīṯ teaches fine Adab even in everyday bodily states and connects them with Ḏikr, Duʿāʾ, and self-control.

HAD-0143.text: The angels do not enter a house in which there is a dog or an image.
HAD-0143.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0143.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the angels meant here are the angels of mercy, not the recording angels, who do not leave the human being. The Ḥadīṯ contains a warning against things in the house that prevent their entry: a dog without a permitted need, and images that fall under the prohibition. The Muslim is thereby called to keep his house away from causes that diminish Barakah, mercy, and good influence.

HAD-0144.text: Whoever keeps a dog — except for hunting, livestock, or agriculture — his reward diminishes every day.
HAD-0144.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0144.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ gives a strict warning against keeping a dog without a recognized benefit. Excepted are cases in which there is a clear need, such as hunting, guarding livestock, or agriculture. Whoever keeps a dog without such a need exposes himself to a daily diminution of his reward. The Ḥadīṯ thus shows that permitted exceptions are bound to benefit and need, while mere habit or keeping without need is not placed on the same level.

HAD-0145.text: When you hear the rooster crow, ask Allah for His favor, for it has seen an angel. When you hear a donkey bray, seek refuge with Allah from Satan, for it has seen a satan.
HAD-0145.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0145.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ leads the servant, at audible signs from created beings, to Ḏikr and right conduct. When the rooster crows, it is recommended to ask Allah for His favor, because it has seen an angel. When the donkey brays, refuge is sought with Allah from Satan, because it has seen a satan. In this lies the training not to treat ordinary perceptions heedlessly, but to connect them with Duʿāʾ, hope, and seeking protection with Allah.

HAD-0146.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0146.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ confirms the reality of the evil eye and rejects the claim that it has no effect. Its effect, however, does not occur independently, but only with Allah's permission and within the causes that Allah has created. The Ḥadīṯ therefore does not lead to superstition, but to confirmed Sunnah: protection through Ḏikr, Duʿāʾ, permitted Ruqyah, and trust in Allah, while one does not deny the real cause.

HAD-0147.text: Allah has not sent down any illness without also sending down its cure.
HAD-0147.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0147.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ encourages permitted treatment and opens hope. Illness and cure both stand under Allah's decree; the cure may be known or unknown, easily attainable or hidden. The Ḥadīṯ therefore contradicts neither Tawakkul nor patience, but shows that seeking permitted means of cure itself belongs to the created causes that Allah has placed in the world.

HAD-0148.text: When you hear of a plague in a land, do not enter it. If it breaks out in a land where you are, do not leave it in order to flee from it.
HAD-0148.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0148.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ joins protective measures with belief in Allah's decree. Whoever is outside a plague-stricken land should not enter it, so that he does not knowingly expose himself to a cause of harm. Whoever is in it should not flee, lest he thereby cause panic, harm, or spread, and lest he act as though he could escape Allah's decree. The Ḥadīṯ thus teaches caution, order, and Tawakkul together.

HAD-0151.text: The deed most beloved to Allah is the prayer at its prescribed time. Then comes goodness toward parents, then striving in Allah's path.
HAD-0151.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0151.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the order of duties according to their rank. The prayer at its prescribed time is named first, because it is the greatest regular bodily obligation, and by it the servant preserves his obedience directly. Then follows goodness toward parents because of their immense right, and then striving in Allah's path. The order shows that not every good deed has the same rank, and that duties at their proper time must not be displaced by deeds of lower rank.

HAD-0152.text: Between a human being and Širk and Kufr stands the abandonment of the prayer.
HAD-0152.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0152.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the immense standing of the Ṣalāh and the extreme gravity of abandoning it. The wording presents the Ṣalāh as a boundary between Islām and the paths of Širk and Kufr. In this, the general warning of the text is to be distinguished from judging a particular individual case, for individual cases depend on knowledge, denial, deliberate rejection, and further legal circumstances. The Ḥadīṯ nevertheless remains one of the strongest warnings against abandoning the prayer.

HAD-0153.text: Whoever abandons the ʿAṣr prayer, his deeds are nullified.
HAD-0153.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0153.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the particular warning against abandoning the ʿAṣr prayer makes its rank clear. ʿAṣr falls at a time when trade, work, tiredness, and the occupations of the day can strongly distract a person; whoever deliberately neglects it exposes himself to a tremendous threat. The statement about the nullification of deeds shows that this prayer must not be treated like a slight missed habit, but belongs to the gravest matters of the obligatory prayers.

HAD-0155.text: Whoever performs the morning prayer is under Allah's protection.
HAD-0155.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0155.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the Ḥadīṯ highlights the rank of the morning prayer and Allah's protection for the one who performs it. Whoever prays Ṣubḥ enters a special Amānah and a protection; therefore there follows in the reports the warning not to call Allah to account concerning this protection. The meaning is: whoever stands under Allah's protection must not be wrongfully harmed, threatened, or disregarded, and the one who prays should at the same time recognize the worth of this prayer.

HAD-0229.text: The first group to enter Paradise will shine like the full moon. Their hearts are like the heart of a single person; among them there is neither hatred nor envy.
HAD-0229.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0229.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the first group to enter Paradise is described with perfect beauty, light, and purity. The likeness of the full moon shows their radiance and their honor. That their hearts are like the heart of a single person, and that hatred and envy have been removed, shows the purification of the people of Paradise from inner illnesses and their unity in joy and peace.

HAD-0230.text: On the Day of Resurrection, death will be brought in the form of a white-and-black ram and slaughtered. Then it will be called out: People of Paradise — eternity without death; people of the Fire — eternity without death.
HAD-0230.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0230.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the slaughter of death on the Day of Resurrection shows the final ending of dying. Thereafter there is eternal joy without death for the people of Paradise and eternal punishment without death for the people of the Fire. The Ḥadīṯ strengthens hope and fear together: the Hereafter is not temporary, but final.

HAD-0231.text: If the son of Ādam had two valleys full of wealth, he would desire a third. In the end only the earth fills the belly of the human being; and Allah accepts the repentance of the one who repents.
HAD-0231.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0231.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the nature of unrestrained greed for wealth: even great possession does not end desire. That in the end only the earth fills the belly of the human being is a reminder of death and transience. At the same time the conclusion opens the door of hope: Allah accepts the repentance of the one who turns back from greed, attachment to the world, and sin.

HAD-0232.text: Allah has angels who travel along the paths and seek the people of remembrance. When they find people remembering Allah, they call to one another and surround them with their wings. Allah mentions these servants among those who are with Him.
HAD-0232.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0232.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the angels seek particular gatherings of Ḏikr, surround them, and their participants are mentioned with Allah. The Ḥadīṯ shows the rank of Ḏikr, Qurʾān, Duʿāʾ, and righteous gathering. That Allah mentions these servants among those who are with Him is a tremendous honor and shows that hidden or small Ḏikr sittings can have great rank with Allah.

HAD-0233.text: O Allah, I ask You for right guidance, fear of Allah, chastity, and contentment.
HAD-0233.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-0233.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that this Duʿāʾ gathers comprehensive foundations of the Dīn. Hidāyah is guidance to truth and steadfastness, Taqwā is protection from Allah’s anger through obedience and avoidance of the forbidden, ʿAfāf is chastity and preservation from unlawful desire, and Ġinā is contentment of the heart toward people and the world. The Ḥadīṯ shows that the servant should ask Allah for inward and outward righteousness.

HAD-0234.text: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from worry and grief, from incapacity and laziness, from stinginess and cowardice, and from the burden of debt and being overpowered by people.
HAD-0234.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-0234.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that this Duʿāʾ gathers several causes of weakness and harm. Worry and grief burden the heart and the present, incapacity and laziness hinder obedience and benefit, stinginess and cowardice weaken rights and duty, and the burden of debt as well as being overpowered by people can humiliate the servant. The Ḥadīṯ teaches one to ask Allah for protection from inward and outward obstacles on the path.

HAD-0235.text: Whoever recites the last two verses of Sūrah al-Baqarah in a night, they will suffice him.
HAD-0235.narrator: Abū Masʿūd ʿUqbah ibn ʿAmr reported:
HAD-0235.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0235.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the last two verses of Sūrah al-Baqarah hold a special rank. That they suffice the reciter in the night has been understood as protection from evil, a sufficient share of nightly recitation, and great reward. The Ḥadīṯ shows the merit of these two verses and that the servant should preserve them regularly at night.

HAD-0236.text: By the One in Whose hand is my soul: it equals a third of the Qurʾān.
HAD-0236.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said about Sūrah al-Iḫlāṣ:
HAD-0236.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that Sūrah al-Iḫlāṣ gathers Tawḥīd, the oneness of Allah, and the rejection of likeness, partnership, and need. Therefore it was given a tremendous rank, and it equals a third of the Qurʾān in meaning and reward. The Ḥadīṯ shows the merit of this Sūrah and its central relation to the ʿAqīdah of Tawḥīd.

HAD-0237.text: Every morning two angels descend. One says: O Allah, grant the one who spends a replacement. The other says: O Allah, grant the one who withholds a loss.
HAD-0237.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0237.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ encourages giving and warns against miserly withholding. The Duʿāʾ of the angels for the one who spends means a request for replacement, Barakah, and benefit in his wealth. The Duʿāʾ against the one who withholds shows that stinginess can be a cause of loss, removal of Barakah, and harm. The measure is lawful, appropriate spending without neglecting obligatory rights.

HAD-0239.text: Whoever sees me in a dream has truly seen me; for Satan cannot take on my form.
HAD-0239.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0239.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the particular statement of the Ḥadīṯ concerns the Prophet ﷺ: whoever sees him in a dream in his known true form has truly seen him, for Satan cannot take on his form. The Ḥadīṯ does not mean that every arbitrary dream claim is accepted without a measure; rather, the true seeing is bound to the transmitted description and to the impossibility of a satanic imitation of his form.

HAD-0240.text: How did you know that it is a Ruqyah?
HAD-0240.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said about Sūrah al-Fātiḥah:
HAD-0240.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ confirms the permission and the merit of Ruqyah with Sūrah al-Fātiḥah. The words of the Prophet ﷺ are approval that al-Fātiḥah may be used as a Ruqyah. Healing does not come independently of the text or of the reciter, but through Allah, while the recitation is a lawful means. The Ḥadīṯ also shows that Qurʾān-Ruqyah belongs to the best forms of lawful treatment.

HAD-0241.text: Give glad tidings of complete light on the Day of Resurrection to those who walk to the mosques in the darkness.
HAD-0241.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0241.sharh: al-Ḫaṭṭābī explains, in connection with walking to the prayer, that the effort of the way to the mosque, especially in darkness and at times when the soul is sluggish, is not lost with Allah. The promised complete light on the Day of Resurrection fits the deed: whoever in this world walks in darkness toward obedience receives light on the Day of Resurrection. The Ḥadīṯ especially urges Faǧr and ʿIšāʾ in congregation.

HAD-0243.text: Whoever spends the night of Laylat al-Qadr in prayer out of faith and in hope of Allah’s reward, his past sins will be forgiven.
HAD-0243.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0243.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that Qiyām in Laylat al-Qadr is bound to two conditions: Īmān in Allah’s promise and Iḥtisāb, that is, hope for Allah’s reward without showing off. Whoever brings this night to life in prayer receives forgiveness of past sins. The Ḥadīṯ shows the tremendous rank of Laylat al-Qadr and that acceptance is bound to sincerity, faith, and expectation of the reward with Allah.

HAD-0248.text: Speak to people about what they understand. Do you want Allah and His Messenger to be held as liars?
HAD-0248.narrator: It is authentically transmitted from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0248.speaker: He said:
HAD-0248.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that knowledge should be conveyed according to people’s capacity, understanding, and situation. Not every statement is suitable for every listener, even if it is true; if people do not understand something, it can confuse them or lead them to rejection. The Aṯar of ʿAlī رضي الله عنه therefore teaches wisdom in conveying: one speaks with people so that they can receive the truth and do not, through an unsuitable presentation, fall into misunderstanding about Allah and His Messenger ﷺ.

HAD-0251.text: The Ghusl of the Prophet ﷺ was performed with about one Ṣāʿ of water.
HAD-0251.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها showed:
HAD-0251.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the sparing and sufficient use of water in Ghusl. The Prophet ﷺ carried out the purification with a limited amount of water, without excess. From this, moderation in the area of Ṭahārah is understood: the purification must be complete, but waste and unnecessary exaggeration do not belong to the Sunnah.

HAD-0253.text: The Prophet ﷺ and Maymūnah رضي الله عنها used to perform Ghusl from a single vessel.
HAD-0253.narrator: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-0253.speaker: He reported:
HAD-0253.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the permission for a man and his wife to take water for Ghusl from the same vessel. There is no blemish in that so long as the limits of marriage are observed. The Ḥadīṯ also shows that water used together does not thereby become impure and that the Sunnah in purification is simple and without exaggerated hardship.

HAD-0254.text: As for me, I pour water over my head three times. And he showed it with both hands.
HAD-0254.narrator: Ǧubayr ibn Muṭʿim رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0254.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0254.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that pouring water over the head three times in Ghusl shows completeness and care in purification. The Prophet ﷺ thereby made clear how the water reaches the head, especially with thick hair. The Ḥadīṯ teaches thorough purification without unnecessary hardship or waste.

HAD-0257.text: She set out water for the Ghusl of the Prophet ﷺ. He first washed his hands, purified himself, rinsed his mouth and nose, washed his face and arms, poured water over his body, and washed his feet last.
HAD-0257.speaker: She reported:
HAD-0257.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that this report shows the ordered Sunnah of Ghusl: first the cleansing of the hands and of the relevant place, then the elements of Wuḍūʾ, then the pouring of water over the body. That the feet were washed at the end is explained by the place of standing and the water; if the place becomes wet or impure, the feet may be cleansed at the end. The Ḥadīṯ shows completeness, order, and practical ease in Ghusl.

HAD-0258.text: When the Prophet ﷺ performed Ghusl after Ǧanābah, he took fragrance, began with the right side of the head, then the left, and then passed his hand over the middle of his head.
HAD-0258.speaker: She reported:
HAD-0258.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows cleanliness, pleasant fragrance, and the preference for the right side in the purification rite. The Prophet ﷺ began with the right side of the head, then the left, and thereafter completed the purification. The Ḥadīṯ shows that outward purification is joined with good care and ordered performance.

HAD-0259.text: In Ghusl the Prophet ﷺ rinsed his mouth, cleaned his nose, washed his face, poured water over his head, and completed the Ghusl. A cloth was handed to him, but he did not use it.
HAD-0259.speaker: She reported:
HAD-0259.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the report confirms the ordered performance of Ghusl: cleansing, rinsing, washing, and pouring. That a cloth was handed to the Prophet ﷺ and he did not use it shows that drying after Ghusl is not obligatory. The Ḥadīṯ thereby establishes ease: whoever dries himself has latitude; whoever leaves it also follows a transmitted practice.

HAD-0264.text: The Prophet ﷺ and one of his wives used to perform ghusl from a single vessel.
HAD-0264.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0264.speaker: He reported:
HAD-0264.sharh: Ibn al-Mulaqqin, in explaining this report, cites Ibn Baṭṭāl’s distinction: if the hand is free of actual impurity, the state of Ǧanābah does not make it impure. Therefore the person in the state of Ǧanābah may immerse his clean hand into the vessel of water for the full-body washing. According to this explanation, washing the hand before immersing it refers to the concern that an impurity may be clinging to it, not to an impurity of the body through Ǧanābah alone. The report about the shared vessel thus does not contradict the reports in which the hands were washed beforehand.

HAD-0265.text: She set out water for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for the Ghusl. He washed his hands, cleansed himself, rinsed his mouth and nose, washed his face and arms, washed his head three times, poured water over his body, and washed his feet at the end.
HAD-0265.speaker: She reported:
HAD-0265.sharh: Ibn Raǧab treats Maymūnah’s report under the question of whether the individual acts in Wuḍūʾ and Ġusl must follow one another immediately. He explains that the Prophet ﷺ, between washing the head and washing the feet, first poured water over the rest of the body and then changed his place. From this a short interruption within the described sequence of purification becomes apparent. Ibn Raǧab explains different classifications of the interval of time in this regard; the report is therefore not to be read as though the washing of the feet must, in every performance, necessarily take place immediately after the washing of the head.

HAD-0266.text: She set out water for the Ghusl of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and screened him. He performed the Ghusl, washed his feet last, and when she handed him a cloth, he did not take it.
HAD-0266.narrator: Maymūnah bint al-Ḥārith رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-0266.speaker: She reported:
HAD-0266.sharh: Ibn Raǧab cites Maymūnah’s report in the explanation of purification after Ǧanābah. He treats in particular the sequence in which the hands are first washed, then water is poured with the right hand onto the left, and the private parts are cleansed with it. He compares the different wordings of the transmission so that one does not mistakenly conclude from an abbreviated version that only one hand was cleansed before it was immersed. Maymūnah’s report also describes the final washing of the feet and the not taking of the cloth that was offered; from this description alone no general prohibition of drying is derived here.

HAD-0267.text: She used to perfume the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. After that he was with his wives, and in the morning he entered Iḥrām while the scent was still perceptible on him.
HAD-0267.speaker: ʿĀʾishah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-0267.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that ʿĀʾišah, with this report, opposed the objection to scent before the beginning of Iḥrām. The Prophet ﷺ was perfumed before entering Iḥrām; that the scent was still perceptible afterward does not mean that new scent was applied during Iḥrām. Ibn Raǧab also discusses the expression that the Prophet ﷺ visited his wives, and he explains al-Buḫārī’s inference: the persistence of the scent indicates that after several visits he performed a single Ġusl, instead of bathing again with each individual wife.

HAD-0268.text: The Prophet ﷺ used to visit his wives in one round by day and by night. Anas رضي الله عنه mentioned that he was given a special strength.
HAD-0268.speaker: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0268.sharh: Ibn Raǧab states that al-Buḫārī infers from the report of Anas the permissibility of a single Ġusl after several marital encounters: the short span of time does not allow one to assume that a complete Ġusl took place after each encounter. He also explains the different wordings of the transmission concerning the number of wives (nine or eleven). The mention of a strength of thirty is given as a conversational report transmitted from Anas, not as an independent statement of the Prophet ﷺ.

HAD-0269.text: Wash your member and perform Wuḍūʾ.
HAD-0269.narrator: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0269.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0269.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that al-Buḫārī derives two rules from this report: when Maḏy comes out, the affected place is to be cleansed and Wuḍūʾ is to be performed. He reports the difference of opinion as to whether only the soiled place or the whole member must be washed. For Maḏy that ordinarily comes out, Wuḍūʾ is required; a complete Ġusl does not become required by it. He treats the particulars of continual discharge separately.

HAD-0270.text: She perfumed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. After that he was with his wives and in the morning he entered Iḥrām.
HAD-0270.speaker: ʿĀʾishah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-0270.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains, on the basis of the report of ʿĀʾišah, that the remainder of scent left after Ġusl does not impair the validity of the washing, so long as the water still reaches the skin. The perfuming took place before entering Iḥrām; the later perceptibility of the scent does not mean a fresh application during Iḥrām. This report overlaps strongly in content with HAD-0267 and is not presented as an independent additional matter.

HAD-0271.text: It is as if I still saw the gleam of the scent in the parting of the hair of the Prophet ﷺ while he was in Iḥrām.
HAD-0271.speaker: She reported:
HAD-0271.sharh: Ibn Raǧab emphasizes that ʿĀʾišah still saw the scent in the parting of the hair of the Prophet ﷺ after he had already entered Iḥrām. He cites this as evidence that the scent applied before Iḥrām could cling for a while to the hair and the beard, even across repeated washings. The report concerns the persistence of a previous perfuming; from it does not follow permission to apply scent again after entering Iḥrām.

HAD-0272.text: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed Ghusl after Janābah, he washed his hands, performed Wuḍūʾ as for the prayer, rubbed his hair thoroughly until the scalp was wetted, and then poured water over it three times.
HAD-0272.speaker: ʿĀʾishah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-0272.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that the Prophet ﷺ, before pouring water over the head three times, brought water with his fingers to the roots of the hair until the scalp was sufficiently wetted. Passing through the hair served to reach the scalp; the subsequent pouring three times served to wash the hair. He compares the various wordings of the transmission in this regard and stresses that the authentic wording of Hišām ibn ʿUrwah is decisive where the variants differ.

HAD-0274.text: During the Ghusl after Janābah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ washed his limbs in an ordered manner, did not wash again the Wuḍūʾ places already washed, and removed the water with his hand.
HAD-0274.speaker: She reported:
HAD-0274.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that the parts of the body already washed during Wuḍūʾ do not have to be washed again separately during the subsequent Ġusl. The feet were washed only at the end, because this had not yet taken place before. He bases this interpretation on the further wording of the transmission in Muslim and explains that “sāʾir ǧasadih” here means the remaining body.

HAD-0275.text: The Iqāmah had been called and the rows had been aligned. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remembered that he was in the state of Janābah, ordered the people to remain, performed the Ghusl, and then returned to the prayer.
HAD-0275.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0275.speaker: He reported:
HAD-0275.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains al-Buḫārī’s conclusion from this report: whoever, in the state of Ǧanābah, notices that he is in the mosque may leave it to perform Ġusl without first performing Tayammum. The Prophet ﷺ returned after the complete washing and led the prayer. Ibn Raǧab mentions the differing legal views on merely passing through a mosque and treats the report as evidence against an obligation of Tayammum merely for leaving.

HAD-0276.text: After the Ghusl a cloth was handed to the Prophet ﷺ, but he did not take it. He removed the water with his hands.
HAD-0276.speaker: She reported:
HAD-0276.sharh: Ibn Raǧab distinguishes shaking off the water with the hand from drying with a cloth. He bases the shaking off on the authentic report of Maymūnah and holds it not to be disliked. That the Prophet ﷺ once declined the cloth that was offered does not prove a general prohibition or a disapproval of drying; it only shows that the cloth is not preferred in every case. He states that the majority of the scholars do not hold drying after Wuḍūʾ or Ġusl to be disliked.

HAD-0277.text: When one of them performed Ghusl after Janābah, she poured water over the head three times, then passed her hand over the right side of the head and after that over the left.
HAD-0277.speaker: She reported:
HAD-0277.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that the report of ʿĀʾišah indicates beginning with the right side of the head in Ġusl. This procedure is, according to his explicit statement, recommended but not obligatory. He transmits from ʿAlī that it does no harm with which side of the head one begins. For the preference of the right side of the body, Ibn Raǧab refers to the general report about the preference of the Prophet ﷺ for the right side in purification, without claiming for this a separate explicit report specifically about Ġusl.

HAD-0278.text: The Children of Isrāʾīl used to bathe naked together, while Mūsā عليه السلام bathed alone. Allah showed the soundness of his body when the people saw him.
HAD-0278.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0278.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-0278.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that Mūsā عليه السلام bathed alone and screened, out of modesty and decency. When some of the Children of Israel, on that account, wrongly attributed to him a bodily defect, Allah made the soundness of his body visible; Ibn Raǧab connects this with Qurʾān 33:69. He explicitly rejects the conclusion that Mūsā intentionally uncovered himself before the people. For bathing without clothing in complete seclusion he mentions a fiqh difference of opinion; from this report alone no general permission follows to uncover oneself before others.

HAD-0279.text: When Ayyūb عليه السلام bathed, golden locusts fell upon him. He gathered them and said that he could never do without the blessing of Allah.
HAD-0279.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0279.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-0279.sharh: Ibn Raǧab mentions the report about Ayyūb عليه السلام together with the report about Mūsā عليه السلام in the chapter on Ġusl in complete seclusion. Ayyūb’s reply, that he could not do without the blessing of Allah, belongs to the authentic report itself. As a fiqh reference, Ibn Raǧab discusses to what extent bathing unclothed in a secluded place can be derived from reports about earlier prophets; he poses the decisive question in this, whether an earlier law can be regarded as binding for this Ummah without a corresponding proof. Covering remains preferable according to the chapter heading.

HAD-0280.text: She came in the year of the conquest of Makkah to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and found him bathing, while Fāṭimah رضي الله عنها screened him.
HAD-0280.narrator: Umm Hānī bint Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-0280.speaker: She reported:
HAD-0280.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that the report of Umm Hāniʾ proves screening during Ġusl in the presence of others. A daughter, or another maḥram relative, may also not see the ʿAwrah; therefore Fāṭimah رضي الله عنها held a visual screen while the Prophet ﷺ was bathing. He mentions further reports about covering by another person, without limiting the actual rule to the mere presence of non-relatives.

HAD-0281.text: She screened the Prophet ﷺ while he performed the Ghusl after Janābah. He performed Wuḍūʾ as for the prayer, poured water over the body, and washed his feet at the end.
HAD-0281.speaker: She reported:
HAD-0281.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains the report of Maymūnah رضي الله عنها as evidence that screening the person who is bathing is preferable, even when he is accompanied by a person who, according to the respective fiqh conditions, would be permitted to see him. He expressly distinguishes the question of screening from the disputed question of the gaze between spouses and mentions differing earlier views. The report also describes the sequence of washing up to the final washing of the feet, while the chapter places modesty and covering at the center.

HAD-0282.narrator: Umm Salamah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-0282.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0282.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains the reply to Umm Sulaym: for a woman too, Ġusl is required after a nocturnal emission of semen if, upon waking, the corresponding fluid is found. A mere dream without fluid being found does not, as a rule, obligate one to Ġusl. He also distinguishes a clear emission of semen from doubtful moisture and records differing views of early scholars on this.

HAD-0283.text: Subḥān Allah! A believer does not become impure.
HAD-0283.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0283.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0283.sharh: Ibn Raǧab makes clear that Ǧanābah denotes a ritual impurity, not a bodily impurity of the believer. Therefore a person in the state of Ǧanābah may attend to his affairs and sit with scholars. Sweat, tears, and saliva remain pure; Ibn Raǧab describes this as the agreed view and additionally transmits the statement of Ibn al-Munḏir on the purity of sweat.

HAD-0284.text: The Prophet ﷺ used to visit his wives in one night, and at that time he had nine wives.
HAD-0284.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0284.speaker: He reported:
HAD-0284.sharh: Ibn Raǧab expressly points out that al-Buḫārī had already cited this report about the nightly visits to the wives earlier in a corresponding sense. The inference for the chapter on a man’s freedom of movement in the state of Ǧanābah presupposes that the visits took place with only one concluding Ġusl. For this, Ibn Raǧab refers to further paths of transmission from Anas, which al-Buḫārī does not cite in full at this place. It is thus a related report to HAD-0268, and not a new independent matter.

HAD-0285.text: Subḥān Allah, Abū Hurayrah! A believer does not become impure.
HAD-0285.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0285.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0285.sharh: Ibn Raǧab highlights, as an additional aspect of this version, that the Prophet ﷺ took Abū Hurayrah by the hand and walked on with him, although he was in the state of Ǧanābah. The report therefore also establishes the permissibility of giving one’s hand to a ǧunub, even if there should be sweat on the hand. The basic principle that ritual Ǧanābah does not make the believer physically impure is already the subject of HAD-0283.

HAD-0286.text: Yes, the Prophet ﷺ slept in the state of Janābah, but he performed Wuḍūʾ beforehand.
HAD-0286.speaker: ʿĀʾishah رضي الله عنها said:
HAD-0286.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that al-Buḫārī, by the report of ʿĀʾišah and the following report of Ibn ʿUmar, establishes the permissibility of postponing the complete Ġusl after Ǧanābah, even when one wishes to sleep at home. For sleep it is recommended to perform Wuḍūʾ beforehand; this Wuḍūʾ does not, by itself, lift the state of Ǧanābah.

HAD-0287.text: Yes. When one of you performs Wuḍūʾ, he may sleep while he is in the state of Janābah.
HAD-0287.narrator: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0287.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0287.sharh: Ibn Raǧab draws from the reply of the Prophet ﷺ to ʿUmar the same legal consequence as from the preceding report of ʿĀʾišah: a person may postpone the Ġusl after Ǧanābah until after sleep. Whoever wishes to sleep in this state should, according to his explanation, preferably perform Wuḍūʾ beforehand. There is a further authentic transmission of the same legal question, which agrees closely in content with HAD-0286.

HAD-0288.text: When the Prophet ﷺ wished to sleep while he was in the state of Janābah, he washed his private parts and performed Wuḍūʾ as for the prayer.
HAD-0288.speaker: She reported:
