HAD-0288.sharh: Ibn Raǧab presents the transmission of ʿĀʾišah with the additional detail that the Prophet ﷺ, before sleeping in the state of Ǧanābah, cleansed the private parts and performed Wuḍūʾ as for the prayer. He compares the related chains of transmission; in a further version through az-Zuhrī he explains differing Isnāde as the reason why al-Buḫārī did not include it. The report supplements HAD-0286 with a detail of cleansing, without the Wuḍūʾ taking the place of the complete Ġusl.

HAD-0289.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0289.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0289.sharh: Ibn Raǧab cites a further transmission from Ibn ʿUmar concerning ʿUmar’s question whether a person may sleep in the state of Ǧanābah. The brief reply, “Yes, if the person performs Wuḍūʾ,” concerns postponing the complete Ġusl until after sleep, not the falling away of the obligation of Ġusl. This version is, in content, a parallel to HAD-0287 and is therefore not presented as a new independent legal rule.

HAD-0290.text: Perform Wuḍūʾ, wash your private parts, and then sleep.
HAD-0290.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0290.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0290.sharh: Ibn Raǧab cites, as a second version of the transmission from Ibn ʿUmar, the explicit command, in the case of nocturnal Ǧanābah, to wash the private parts, to perform Wuḍūʾ, and then to sleep. This transmission thus supplements the brief permission to sleep with the cleansing of the private parts. The complete Ġusl remains required for the subsequent purity for prayer; the wording is closely related to HAD-0288.

HAD-0291.text: When a man sits between the four limbs of the woman and sexual intercourse takes place, Ghusl is obligatory.
HAD-0291.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0291.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0291.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains the report of Abū Hurayrah concerning the obligation of Ġusl after actual sexual intercourse. He cites further versions of the transmission which expressly clarify that this applies even without ejaculation. He examines the chains of transmission through Qatādah, al-Ḥasan and Abū Rāfiʿ, as well as the objections to individual Isnāde, while the base text transmitted by al-Buḫārī remains authentic. For the legal classification, therefore, ejaculation alone is not decisive.

HAD-0292.text: Whoever completes sexual intercourse without ejaculation occurring should perform Wuḍūʾ as for the prayer and wash his private parts. ʿUṯmān رضي الله عنه said that he heard this from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
HAD-0292.narrator: Zayd ibn Khālid al-Juhanī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0292.speaker: ʿUṯmān ibn ʿAffān رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-0292.sharh: Ibn Raǧab expressly explains that the information transmitted here from ʿUṯmān — that after sexual intercourse without ejaculation, washing the private parts and Wuḍūʾ sufficed — reflects an earlier ruling. After the later transmission concerning the obligation of Ġusl upon sexual intercourse, this facilitation no longer applies. He names the repeal of this earlier rule as the widespread view of the scholars of fiqh and ḥadīṯ, among them aš-Šāfiʿī, Aḥmad, Muslim and at-Tirmiḏī; another interpretation of the formula “al-māʾ min al-māʾ,” as referring only to nocturnal dreams, he considers insufficient to explain all the versions concerned. HAD-0292 must therefore not be presented as a present-day exemption from Ġusl.

HAD-0293.text: He should wash what was affected by the contact, then perform Wuḍūʾ and pray. Imām al-Buḫārī explained regarding this that Ghusl is safer and is the later ordinance.
HAD-0293.narrator: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0293.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0293.sharh: Ibn Raǧab presents this report together with the preceding transmission no. 292 as evidence of an earlier facilitation: after sexual intercourse without ejaculation, only washing the affected place and Wuḍūʾ were at first commanded. He explains in detail why this earlier legal rule was repealed by the later obligation of Ġusl upon sexual intercourse. Al-Buḫārī’s remark that Ġusl is safer must therefore not be understood to mean that mere Wuḍūʾ would today be permissible as an equivalent alternative. Ibn Raǧab cites early scholars in this regard and the withdrawal of earlier differing views of the Ṣaḥābah.

HAD-0294.text: This is something that Allah has prescribed for the daughters of Ādam. Do what the pilgrims do, except that you do not perform the Ṭawāf around the House until you are pure.
HAD-0294.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said to ʿĀʾishah رضي الله عنها:
HAD-0294.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains the words “Allah has decreed this for the daughters of Ādam” as an indication that menstruation has belonged to human nature since the creation of women. He highlights the special chain of transmission of the report from ʿĀʾišah. The Prophet ﷺ permitted her the other rites of the Ḥaǧǧ, while the Ṭawāf remained excluded until the end of menstruation. Menstruation itself is therefore no reason to abandon all the rites of pilgrimage.

HAD-0295.text: During her menstruation she used to comb the hair of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
HAD-0295.speaker: She reported:
HAD-0295.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that the menstruating woman remains physically pure: her state of menstruation does not make her hands impure. Therefore ʿĀʾišah was permitted to comb, oil and clean the hair of the Prophet ﷺ. Ibn Raǧab expressly explains that “tarǧīl” here means tending and combing the hair of the head, and he cites ʿUrwah’s corresponding interpretation.

HAD-0296.text: ʿĀʾishah رضي الله عنها combed the hair of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while she was menstruating and he was in Iʿtikāf in the mosque. He brought his head to her into her chamber.
HAD-0296.narrator: ʿUrwah reported from ʿĀʾishah رضي الله عنها:
HAD-0296.speaker: She reported:
HAD-0296.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains, on the basis of the report of ʿĀʾišah and ʿUrwah’s reply, that menstruation does not forbid serving the husband or combing or washing his head. The Prophet ﷺ remained in Iʿtikāf in the mosque and brought his head into ʿĀʾišah’s room so that she could comb it. The particular addition concerns the Iʿtikāf and the proximity to the mosque; the principle of physical purity overlaps with HAD-0295.

HAD-0297.text: The Prophet ﷺ reclined in her lap and recited the Qurʾān while she was menstruating.
HAD-0297.speaker: She reported:
HAD-0297.sharh: Ibn Raǧab makes clear: when the Prophet ﷺ recited the Qurʾān in ʿĀʾišah’s lap although she was menstruating, this establishes the permission to recite in the vicinity of a menstruating woman. According to Ibn Raǧab’s express statement, the report does not directly prove that a menstruating woman herself may recite the Qurʾān. He thus separates the purity of the sphere of contact and presence from the distinct legal question of her own recitation.

HAD-0298.text: When she began menstruating while under the shared cover with the Prophet ﷺ, she withdrew and took her menstruation garment. The Prophet ﷺ called her back to himself under the same cover.
HAD-0298.narrator: Umm Salamah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-0298.speaker: She reported:
HAD-0298.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that the Prophet ﷺ invited Umm Salamah again to lie together, although her menstruation had begun. The report refutes the notion that the menstruating woman must be avoided because of physical impurity. Ibn Raǧab distinguishes at length the linguistic use of “nafasa” for menstruation and for childbirth; in this report the word denotes menstruation, not the postpartum period.

HAD-0299.text: She and the Prophet ﷺ used to perform Ghusl from a single vessel, while both were in the state of Janābah.
HAD-0299.speaker: She reported:
HAD-0299.sharh: Ibn Raǧab reproduces the connected transmission of ʿĀʾišah, the first part of which describes the shared Ġusl of the Prophet ﷺ and ʿĀʾišah from the same water vessel. He cites it here together with two further statements, permitted marital physical closeness during menstruation and washing the head during Iʿtikāf, which al-Buḫārī lists as nos. 299-301 under one chain of transmission. According to the report, shared use of the vessel is possible when both are in Ǧanābah at the same time; for the detailed interpretation of this aspect, the earlier chapters on Ghusl are also relevant. The statement is a thematic parallel to HAD-0253, but that report comes from Maymūnah.

HAD-0300.text: During menstruation the Prophet ﷺ commanded her to wear an Izār; thereafter marital closeness without sexual intercourse was possible.
HAD-0300.speaker: She reported:
HAD-0300.sharh: Ibn Raǧab presents the second part of the same transmission from ʿĀʾišah: during her menstruation the Prophet ﷺ had her put on an Izār and was then physically close to her. The expression mubāšarah is distinguished in the chapter from sexual intercourse; the basic prohibition of sexual intercourse during Ḥayḍ remains. Ibn Raǧab also treats the independent second chain of transmission at HAD-0302 and the version of Maymūnah at HAD-0303. HAD-0300 is the same connected report as HAD-0299 and 0301, not a further incident with its own chain.

HAD-0301.text: During the time of Iʿtikāf the Prophet ﷺ brought his head out to her, and she washed it, although she was menstruating.
HAD-0301.speaker: She said:
HAD-0301.sharh: Ibn Raǧab cites the authentic version from ʿĀʾišah, according to which the Prophet ﷺ during Iʿtikāf stretched his head out to her and she washed it despite menstruation. The report confirms the purity of the body of a menstruating woman and shows that tending the hair of the head during Iʿtikāf was possible without the Prophet ﷺ ending his stay in the mosque for that purpose. The transmission in question also joins statements about the shared Ġusl and marital closeness; the statement explained here is therefore a partial repetition of other reports from ʿĀʾišah.

HAD-0302.text: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ desired marital closeness during menstruation, he commanded the woman to wear an Izār. ʿĀʾishah رضي الله عنها recalled that no one mastered his desire as the Prophet ﷺ did.
HAD-0302.narrator: ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad reported from his father:
HAD-0302.speaker: ʿĀʾishah رضي الله عنها said:
HAD-0302.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains, on the basis of ʿĀʾišah’s statement, that marital closeness during menstruation without sexual intercourse is permitted. The instruction to put on an Izār applied especially to the beginning, with heavier bleeding. He expressly distinguishes the permitted physical closeness from the forbidden sexual intercourse and explains that the transmission of ʿĀʾišah has its own chain through ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad.

HAD-0303.text: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ desired marital closeness during menstruation, he had his wife wear an Izār.
HAD-0303.speaker: She said:
HAD-0303.sharh: Ibn Raǧab clarifies that the transmission of Maymūnah about wearing an Izār during menstruation reaches her through ʿAbdullāh ibn Šaddād; her chain must not be confused with the transmission of ʿĀʾišah. This version too establishes the permissibility of marital physical closeness over the Izār, while sexual intercourse during menstruation is excluded. The content is a parallel to HAD-0302, with a different chain of transmission.

HAD-0304.text: The Prophet ﷺ reminded the women on the day of ʿĪd of Ṣadaqah and explained that the menstruating woman does not pray and does not fast during her bleeding.
HAD-0304.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0304.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0304.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that al-Buḫārī expressly cites this report here as evidence that the menstruating woman does not fast during her menstruation. According to his presentation, there is agreement that this fast would not be valid and that the missed fast days are to be made up after the end of menstruation. He distinguishes this making up from the separate question of the prayer, for which al-Buḫārī brings a chapter of its own.

HAD-0325.text: In the case of continuous bleeding she should leave the prayer only for the days on which she usually menstruated; thereafter she should perform Ghusl and pray.
HAD-0325.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said to Fāṭimah bint Abī Ḥubayš:
HAD-0325.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that Fāṭimah bint Abī Ḥubayš, in the case of persistent bleeding, should distinguish between Ḥayḍ and Istiḥāḍah on the basis of her previous usual days of menstruation. He documents the fiqh dispute over whether the plural “days” means at least three full days; the counterarguments understand it as a general designation of the accustomed time. The individual reply of the Prophet ﷺ to Fāṭimah therefore does not establish a general minimum duration of three days for every woman.

HAD-0326.text: We did not regard yellowish or brownish fluid outside the days of menstruation as Ḥayḍ.
HAD-0326.narrator: Umm ʿAṭiyyah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-0326.speaker: She said:
HAD-0326.sharh: Ibn Raǧab discusses the report of Umm ʿAṭiyyah, according to which yellowish and brownish discharges outside the time of menstruation were not treated as menstruation. He distinguishes the transmission with the explicit restriction “after purity” from the shorter wording in al-Buḫārī and sets further earlier statements alongside it. The assessment therefore depends on the time of the discharge; the statement must not be shortened to the claim that every yellowish or brownish discharge during menstruation is of no account. Ibn Raǧab marks a corresponding statement of ʿĀʾišah, transmitted by a weak route, as weak.

HAD-0327.text: Umm Ḥabībah رضي الله عنها had Istiḥāḍah for seven years. The Prophet ﷺ explained that it came from a blood vessel, and he ordered her to perform Ghusl.
HAD-0327.speaker: She said:
HAD-0327.sharh: Ibn Raǧab distinguishes, in the report about Umm Ḥabībah bint Ǧaḥš, the ordered Ġusl after the days of menstruation from her subsequent personal practice of bathing again before every prayer. He examines the different chains of transmission: in the wordings preserved by the reliable transmitters, the repeated Ġusl is reported as an act of Umm Ḥabībah, not as an explicit command of the Prophet ﷺ for every prayer. Ibn Raǧab sets out the legal opinions on this additional washing; a general obligation of a Ġusl for each individual prayer cannot be derived from the wording preserved by al-Buḫārī.

HAD-0328.text: When Ṣafiyyah رضي الله عنها menstruated after Ṭawāf al-Ifāḍah, the Prophet ﷺ asked whether she had already performed the Ṭawāf. When this was confirmed, he permitted her to depart.
HAD-0328.speaker: She said:
HAD-0328.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains, in the case of Ṣafiyyah, that a menstruating woman would not be permitted to depart if she had not yet performed the obligatory Ṭawāf al-Ifāḍah. Since Ṣafiyyah had already performed this Ṭawāf, she was permitted to depart by the instruction of the Prophet ﷺ; a further farewell Ṭawāf was then not obligatory for her. He reports the differing early legal views and places the later facilitation in context on the basis of the prophetic transmission.

HAD-0329.text: The menstruating woman was permitted to depart if her menstruation began after Ṭawāf al-Ifāḍah.
HAD-0329.narrator: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-0329.speaker: He said:
HAD-0329.sharh: Ibn Raǧab names the facilitation transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās by way of Ṭāwūs, that the menstruating woman may depart after Ṭawāf al-Ifāḍah has already been performed, as the second basis of this chapter. The facilitation concerns the farewell Ṭawāf that is still outstanding and does not lift the obligation of Ṭawāf al-Ifāḍah. In substance this corresponds to the situation of Ṣafiyyah in HAD-0328.

HAD-0330.text: Ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنه first held the opposite view, but then said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had permitted them to depart.
HAD-0330.narrator: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-0330.speaker: He said:
HAD-0330.sharh: Ibn Raǧab documents that Ibn ʿUmar first forbade a menstruating woman to depart before the farewell Ṭawāf, but later changed his statement because of the permission of the Prophet ﷺ. The change concerns the woman who has already performed her obligatory Ṭawāf al-Ifāḍah. This report explains the same matter as HAD-0328 and HAD-0329 from the perspective of a Ṣaḥābī’s changed view.

HAD-0331.text: When menstruation begins, leave the prayer; when it ends, wash off the blood and pray.
HAD-0331.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0331.sharh: Ibn Raǧab expressly emphasizes, regarding this further transmission from ʿĀʾišah, that al-Buḫārī repeats it here in order to clarify his distinction between the onset and the end of the actual menstruation. He relates the phrase “When menstruation comes ... when it goes” here in particular to recognizing the characteristic menstrual blood and its transition to another persistent bleeding, Istiḥāḍah. He connects this comment with the previously set out opinion of Ibn ʿAbbās and with the interpretation of Aḥmad and Isḥāq ibn Rāhawayh. The ceasing of the actual menstrual blood permits the resumption of prayer after the necessary purification; the older detailed explanation of the same legal question is not presented as a new independent statement.

HAD-0332.text: The Prophet ﷺ performed the funeral prayer for a woman who had died in childbirth, and he stood at the middle of her body.
HAD-0332.narrator: Samurah ibn Jundub رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0332.speaker: He said:
HAD-0332.sharh: Ibn Raǧab records that al-Buḫārī does not transmit in this chapter a general report on all the legal rules of the postpartum period, but expressly only the funeral prayer over a woman who died during childbirth or in the postpartum period. The Prophet ﷺ performed her funeral prayer and stood at the level of the middle of the body. From this single report no general statement may be derived about the prayer obligation of a living woman with postpartum bleeding.

HAD-0333.text: During her menstruation she did not pray, but she sat near the prayer place of the Prophet ﷺ; when he performed Suǧūd, part of his garment touched her.
HAD-0333.speaker: She said:
HAD-0333.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains, regarding the report of Maymūnah, that the clothing of a menstruating woman does not become impure merely by her wearing it during menstruation. If this clothing touches a person who is praying during the prayer, that person’s prayer is not thereby invalidated. He also points out that the prayer place of the Prophet ﷺ mentioned in the transmission most likely means his prayer area inside the house and not the public mosque of Madīnah. He refers further details to the Kitāb aṣ-Ṣalāh.

HAD-0334.text: When her necklace was lost on a journey and there was no water, Allah revealed the Āyah of Tayammum.
HAD-0334.speaker: She said:
HAD-0334.sharh: Ibn Raǧab presents the transmission of ʿĀʾišah about the lost necklace and the revelation of the Tayammum verse as the opening chapter on purification with clean earth. He explains that the permission of Tayammum is a facilitation when water is absent. The case is a concrete occasion of revelation, not a proof that one may arbitrarily omit water that is available and usable without danger.

HAD-0335.text: I was given five things that were given to no one before me; among them: the earth was made for me a place of prayer and a means of purification.
HAD-0335.narrator: Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0335.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0335.sharh: Ibn Raǧab expressly highlights, in the transmission of Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdullāh about the five special gifts to the Prophet ﷺ, the connected chain of transmission. The Ḥadīṯ joins two facilitations: the earth can be for this Ummah a place of prayer and, when the prescribed conditions are met, a means of purification. The indication of the purity of the earth does not set aside the other conditions of ritual purification.

HAD-0336.text: When there was no water because of her lost necklace, the Āyah of Tayammum was revealed. Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr رضي الله عنه called this a blessing of the family of Abū Bakr.
HAD-0336.speaker: ʿĀʾishah رضي الله عنها said:
HAD-0336.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains the report about ʿĀʾišah’s borrowed necklace in the chapter on the absence of both water and earth. The Companions performed the prayer in that situation of necessity before the revelation concerning Tayammum had come. Only afterwards was the verse about the facilitation revealed. The report is therefore not a proof for deliberately neglecting Wuḍūʾ or Tayammum when one of the two is possible.

HAD-0337.text: The Prophet ﷺ returned the Salām only after he went to a wall, wiped his face and his hands with it, and thereby performed Tayammum.
HAD-0337.narrator: Abū al-Juhaym al-Anṣārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0337.speaker: He said:
HAD-0337.sharh: Ibn Raǧab treats the report of Abū Ǧuhaym: the Prophet ﷺ returned the greeting only after he had wiped his face and hands on a wall. The commentary distinguishes between a purity that is only recommended at the time of remembrance or when returning a greeting, and the prescribed purity for the prayer. Ibn Raǧab mentions as a possible explanation that no water was available at that place; he also reports differing scholarly opinions on whether, in special circumstances, Tayammum is permissible before an immediately threatening omission of the prayer. The report does not establish a general prohibition of returning the Salām without Wuḍūʾ.

HAD-0338.text: The Prophet ﷺ explained to him that it would have sufficed to strike the earth lightly with the hands, blow off the dust, and wipe the face and the hands.
HAD-0338.speaker: ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-0338.sharh: Ibn Raǧab discusses the transmission of ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir about the correction of his Tayammum: instead of rolling the whole body in earth, the Prophet ﷺ showed the simple application to the face and the hands. Lightly blowing off excess dust is permissible according to this wording of the transmission; from it there follows no necessity of covering the whole body with earth. The occurrence also concerns Tayammum for a person in the state of Ǧanābah.

HAD-0339.text: Tayammum is sufficient for the Muslim when no water is available.
HAD-0339.narrator: Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Abzā reported from his father:
HAD-0339.speaker: ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-0339.sharh: Ibn Raǧab presents this report as one of the wordings of ʿAmmār’s instruction transmitted by Šuʿbah. Wiping the face and the palms suffices in Tayammum; the whole body need not be covered with earth. He compares in this the variants through al-Ḥakam, Ḏarr and Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Abzā and mentions the practical demonstration of Šuʿbah. The shortened report is not a second independent event, but belongs to the shared ʿAmmār transmission of HAD-0338 and HAD-0341.

HAD-0340.text: They were traveling in a detachment and became junub; ʿAmmār رضي الله عنه reminded ʿUmar رضي الله عنه of the application of Tayammum.
HAD-0340.speaker: ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-0340.sharh: Ibn Raǧab assigns this report of ʿAmmār and ʿUmar to the different reliable paths of transmission concerning the application of Tayammum. The essential difference from HAD-0341 is the shorter presentation of the event. The further wordings explain that in Tayammum wiping the face and the palms suffices; they do not report an independent second occurrence.

HAD-0341.text: He rolled in the dust and came to the Prophet ﷺ. He explained: The face and the hands would have sufficed for you.
HAD-0341.speaker: ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-0341.sharh: Ibn Raǧab presents this wording in the chapter on Tayammum for the face and the palms. The prophetic reply to ʿAmmār explains that in Tayammum the face and the palms suffice. The differing paths of transmission of the same occurrence are to be considered separately; rubbing the whole body with earth is not required.

HAD-0342.text: He reported the same occurrence concerning Tayammum; the instruction of the Prophet ﷺ showed that the face and the hands suffice.
HAD-0342.narrator: ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0342.speaker: He said:
HAD-0342.sharh: Ibn Raǧab cites the further wording of the ʿAmmār report as evidence that in Tayammum wetting or wiping the face and both palms suffices; the complete wiping of the arms up to the elbows is not reported in this wording. He sets the paths of transmission side by side and distinguishes the procedure practically demonstrated by Šuʿbah from the directly transmitted wording of the Prophet ﷺ. The matter overlaps with HAD-0338 and HAD-0341.

HAD-0343.text: The Prophet ﷺ struck the earth with his hands and then wiped his face and his palms.
HAD-0343.narrator: ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0343.speaker: He said:
HAD-0343.sharh: Ibn Raǧab presents the wording about the simple Tayammum together with the other paths of transmission from ʿAmmār. He distinguishes the transmitted descriptions of the hand movements and records that the prophetic instruction concerned wiping the face and the palms. The report provides no proof for wiping the whole body with earth; nor is an independent further occurrence claimed.

HAD-0344.text: On a journey they overslept the prayer. A man was junub and found no water; the Prophet ﷺ told him that clean earth suffices.
HAD-0344.narrator: ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0344.speaker: He said:
HAD-0344.sharh: Ibn Raǧab expressly comments on the question of the man who, because of Ǧanābah and without water, did not pray with them. The Prophet ﷺ directed him to clean earth. Ibn Raǧab concludes that Tayammum, when water is absent, also suffices for Ǧanābah and that the prayer may not be omitted on that account. In the same report the man later received water for Ġusl: the facilitation in the absence of water does not permanently set aside the duty to wash when water is available again. Ibn Raǧab further distinguishes real lack of water from situations in which a person can use available water for purification.

HAD-0345.text: In the discussion with Abū Mūsā رضي الله عنه, ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه showed caution, so that people would not abandon water out of convenience and choose tayammum.
HAD-0345.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-0345.sharh: Ibn Raǧab relates the discussion between Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī and ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd about tayammum in the case of ǧanābah and the absence of water. Ibn Masʿūd feared that people might extend the concession to situations in which the water is merely cold. Ibn Raǧab distinguishes this reservation from the permissibility of tayammum when water is actually lacking, which is established from the Prophet ﷺ. He also reports narrations according to which Ibn Masʿūd later abandoned his restrictive view.

HAD-0346.text: He remained cautious on the question of tayammum for the junub who has no water, while Abū Mūsā رضي الله عنه cited the āyah and the statement of ʿAmmār رضي الله عنه.
HAD-0346.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-0346.sharh: Ibn Raǧab discusses this second, more detailed route of transmission concerning the exchange between Abū Mūsā and Ibn Masʿūd. Abū Mūsā cited both the report of ʿAmmār and the Qurʾān verse about tayammum. Ibn Masʿūd explained his reserve by the fear of an abusive application. Ibn Raǧab explains that later legal practice followed the authentic evidences for tayammum even in the state of ǧanābah. The incident is a parallel version of HAD-0345, not a second independent dispute.

HAD-0347.text: The Prophet ﷺ showed for tayammum a light strike upon the earth, then wiping the hands and the face.
HAD-0347.speaker: ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-0347.sharh: In the chapter on a single strike upon the earth, Ibn Raǧab examines the differing transmitted versions of the act of tayammum. Among them he relates the practical description of Imām Aḥmad: one strike upon the earth, then wiping the face and both palms. He distinguishes this understanding from views that require two strikes or wiping up to the elbows, and he discusses their proofs. The specific prophetic evidence for the simple act must not be confused with the differing fiqh opinions discussed later.

HAD-0348.text: When a man did not pray with the others because of Janābah and having no water, the Prophet ﷺ said: Take clean earth, for it suffices you.
HAD-0348.narrator: ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn al-Ḫuzāʿī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0348.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0348.sharh: Ibn Raǧab states expressly that al-Buḫārī, at the end of Kitāb at-Tayammum, repeats in shortened form the incident, already reported at length, of the man who stayed away because of ǧanābah. The statement “Take clean earth, for it suffices you” establishes tayammum also for ǧanābah when water is absent. If, after careful assessment, water is not present, Ibn Raǧab’s discussion holds that no pointless further search is necessary. This entry is a shortened parallel version of the report in HAD-0344. He also points to an additional route of transmission which Ibn Raǧab expressly calls weak, and which is not adopted as proof.

HAD-0349.text: On the night of the Isrāʾ the prayers were prescribed. In the end there remained five prayers, whose reward equals that of fifty.
HAD-0349.narrator: Abū Dharr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0349.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0349.sharh: Ibn Raǧab sets side by side the various authentic routes of transmission of the report about the night journey. The fifty prayers first imposed were lightened to five daily obligatory prayers; according to the transmitted versions the reward continues to equal fifty. He examines the differing wordings concerning the counsel of Mūsā and explains that some versions show a special distinction of this ummah by the five daily prayers. At the same time he treats further reports about the prayer times of earlier prophets and distinguishes their own prayer practice from the obligation of their communities. These additional conclusions he presents as commentary and legal interpretation, not as a literal part of the Buḫārī text cited here in a strongly shortened form.

HAD-0350.text: The prayer was at first prescribed as two rakʿah, in residence and on a journey. The travel prayer remained so, while the prayer in residence was extended.
HAD-0350.speaker: She said:
HAD-0350.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains the statement of ʿĀʾišah about the original prescription of two rakʿah each: according to his interpretation, the later extension at the place of residence concerned the prayers that were originally of two units, Ẓuhr, ʿAṣr and ʿIšāʾ, which were extended to four rakʿah. Fajr remained at two rakʿah and Maġrib at three. The travel prayers remained, in principle, in their initial form. For this, Ibn Raǧab compares further versions in al-Buḫārī, Aḥmad and Ibn Ḫuzaymah and distinguishes the respective routes of transmission; an additional narration which he calls weak he does not use as an equivalent proof.

HAD-0351.text: The women were commanded to attend the ʿīd gatherings and the duʿāʾ of the Muslims; menstruating women kept away from the prayer place.
HAD-0351.narrator: Umm ʿAṭiyyah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-0351.speaker: She said:
HAD-0351.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains the report of Umm ʿAṭiyyah about the attendance of women at the two ʿīd gatherings. The Prophet ﷺ allowed a woman who had no ǧilbāb of her own to borrow one from her companion for going out. Ibn Raǧab stresses expressly: wearing the ǧilbāb here is a ruling for going out among people, not the proof that precisely this outer garment would be required for the prayer at home. He explains the ǧilbāb by early statements, among them those of Ibn Masʿūd, Muǧāhid and ʿAbīdah as-Salmānī, and he discusses the ḫimār in the prayer separately. Concerning the routes of transmission, he points out that al-Buḫārī cites an additional chain in order to establish that Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn heard Umm ʿAṭiyyah directly. The attendance of menstruating women at the gathering does not mean that they themselves perform the festival prayer.

HAD-0352.text: He prayed in a single izār, in order to show that this occurred in the time of the Prophet ﷺ because of scant clothing.
HAD-0352.speaker: Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-0352.sharh: In this chapter Ibn Raǧab expressly distinguishes Ǧābir’s own action from an immediate prophetic instruction. Ǧābir tied his izār behind the neck, although further clothing was available, in order to show that a single garment can in principle suffice for the prayer. The report about the manner in which the Companions wore their izārs is a further proof, but it does not literally contain the command of the Prophet ﷺ to apply precisely this tying method at all times. What remains decisive is that the parts of the body which are to be covered are protected in the prayer.

HAD-0353.text: He saw the Prophet ﷺ praying in a single garment.
HAD-0353.speaker: Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-0353.sharh: Ibn Raǧab cites this second route of transmission from Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir to Ǧābir in the same chapter. While the preceding version reports the concrete tying of the izār by Ǧābir, the statement attributed to the Prophet here only says that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed in one garment, without naming the exact manner of wearing it. Ibn Raǧab makes this difference expressly clear: a particular tying at the neck must not be presented as a prophetic command of its own. A parallel in content to HAD-0352.

HAD-0354.text: The Prophet ﷺ prayed in one garment and laid its ends over the shoulders.
HAD-0354.narrator: ʿUmar ibn Abī Salamah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0354.speaker: He said:
HAD-0354.sharh: Concerning the prayer in a single garment, Ibn Raǧab explains the expression “multaḥif”, or “muta waššiḥ”: the cloth is laid over both shoulders so that its ends are drawn over them, or crossed. He treats the narration of ʿUmar ibn Abī Salamah as proof of the permissibility of this clothing in the prayer, provided the necessary covering is ensured. The mere permission to wear a single garment does not mean that a person should neglect a better covering that is available.

HAD-0355.text: He saw the Prophet ﷺ praying in the house of Umm Salamah in a garment whose ends lay on the shoulders.
HAD-0355.narrator: ʿUmar ibn Abī Salamah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0355.speaker: He said:
HAD-0355.sharh: Ibn Raǧab treats this report as a route of transmission of its own from ʿUmar ibn Abī Salamah, who observed the prayer of the Prophet ﷺ in a single garment laid over both shoulders. What is decisive is the manner of laying it and the covering described in the report. The version supplements the shorter narration HAD-0354, without establishing a second, fully independent legal case.

HAD-0356.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed in a single garment, which he wrapped around his body and whose ends lay on the shoulders.
HAD-0356.narrator: ʿUmar ibn Abī Salamah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0356.speaker: He said:
HAD-0356.sharh: Ibn Raǧab cites the version through ʿUmar ibn Abī Salamah, according to which the Prophet ﷺ prayed at Umm Salamah’s in a single garment and laid its ends on his shoulders. He classifies it as proof that the wide garment can be wrapped around the shoulders. The report is a parallel version of HAD-0354 and 0355; the additional mention of the house of Umm Salamah concerns the wording of the transmission and establishes no additional duty.

HAD-0357.text: The Prophet ﷺ performed eight rakʿah at the time of ḍuḥā, while he was wrapped in a single garment.
HAD-0357.narrator: Umm Hānīʾ bint Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-0357.speaker: She said:
HAD-0357.sharh: Ibn Raǧab cites the authentic report of Umm Hāniʾ that the Prophet ﷺ, in the year of the conquest of Makkah, prayed eight rakʿah at the time of ḍuḥā, wrapped in a single garment. He points out that the beginning of this report was already treated in Kitāb al-Ġusl, and that the further subjects of the ḍuḥā prayers and the grant of protection given by Umm Hāniʾ each deserve a commentary of their own. For this chapter, the manner of covering in the prayer is decisive; the eight rakʿah are not falsely declared a general obligation.

HAD-0358.text: When he was asked about the prayer in a single garment, the Prophet ﷺ said, in meaning: Does every one of you have two garments?
HAD-0358.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0358.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0358.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains the answer of the Prophet ﷺ to the question about the prayer in a single garment as a relief for those who did not possess a second one. He compares several authentic routes of transmission from az-Zuhrī through Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib and Abū Salamah from Abū Hurayrah, and he mentions that Abū Ḥātim ar-Rāzī regarded both variants as authentic. Laying the cloth over the shoulders remains, when there is enough material, better than merely tying a tight izār. In content, HAD-0365 repeats the principle together with the later explanation of ʿUmar.

HAD-0359.text: No one should pray in a single garment without something of it lying on his shoulders.
HAD-0359.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0359.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0359.sharh: Ibn Raǧab sets in order the instruction that, with a single garment, something of it is to be laid over the shoulders. The report of Abū Hurayrah distinguishes the mere covering of the lower body from a way of arranging the garment that also takes in the shoulders. Other authentic narrations show that a plain tight undergarment could be used out of necessity. The commentary thereby discusses the extent of the clothing and the question of obligation or recommendation; from a single shortened translation, an unrestricted invalidity of every prayer in an izār must not be derived.

HAD-0360.text: Whoever prays in a single garment should cross its ends.
HAD-0360.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0360.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-0360.sharh: In the chapter on the shoulders in the prayer, Ibn Raǧab, alongside the report about covering the shoulders, cites a second narration from Abū Hurayrah that the ends of a single garment are to be brought over one another. This act explains the covering of the shoulders by the two ends of the garment. Ibn Raǧab presents the differing versions together and places them within the rules for wide or tight clothing; from a single short version, no new duty of additional garments, independent of HAD-0359, can be derived.

HAD-0361.text: If the garment is wide, it is wrapped around the body; if it is tight, it is worn as an izār.
HAD-0361.speaker: Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-0361.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains the report of Ǧābir about a single tight garment on a journey. The Prophet ﷺ distinguished expressly according to the amount of cloth: a wide garment is taken over the shoulders; if the cloth does not suffice for that, it is worn as an izār around the hips. Therefore the duty to cover the shoulders must not be applied to cases in which the clothing at hand does not allow it. The instruction at the same time preserves the covering required in the prayer.

HAD-0362.text: Men prayed with the Prophet ﷺ while their izārs were tied at the neck; the women were instructed to show restraint when rising.
HAD-0362.speaker: He said:
HAD-0362.sharh: Ibn Raǧab treats Sahl’s report about men who, in the congregational prayer, fastened their izārs at the neck because of scant clothing. The women praying behind them were charged to raise their heads only after the men had risen. The reason lies in protecting modesty in view of the tight clothing of that time, not in a later prayer movement of women prescribed in general. The report is placed in the chapter on garments that are too tight.

HAD-0363.text: I was with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey. After he had withdrawn for his need, he wore a Syrian ǧubbah. Its sleeves were too tight to take the hands out for wuḍūʾ. He therefore brought his hands out from the bottom of the garment. I poured water for him; he performed wuḍūʾ, wiped over his ḫuff and then prayed.
HAD-0363.narrator: al-Muġīrah ibn Šuʿbah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0363.speaker: He reported:
HAD-0363.sharh: Ibn Raǧab presents the report of al-Muġīrah in the chapter on the prayer in a Syrian ǧubbah. From it he concludes the permissibility of praying in garments that come from non-Muslim lands, and likewise the permissibility of the prayer in woollen clothing. For wuḍūʾ, when the sleeves are tight, one can take the arms out through the lower opening. The transmitted act also includes wiping over the ḫuff. Ibn Raǧab points to a further report about gifted silk garments, but he names the uncertainty of a transmitter who appears there; this additional route is not used uncritically as proof.

HAD-0364.text: Since the incident of carrying the stones of the Kaʿbah, the Prophet ﷺ was no longer seen uncovered.
HAD-0364.narrator: Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0364.speaker: He said:
HAD-0364.sharh: In the section on avoiding exposure, Ibn Raǧab comments on the report of Ǧābir about the work on the Kaʿbah. After the Prophet ﷺ was to raise the izār onto the shoulders in order to carry the stones, he lost consciousness, and afterwards he was no longer seen unclothed. The matter explains the special importance of covering and of modesty. It is neither a command to uncover nor a permission to do so in the prayer.

HAD-0042.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0042.sharh: al-Ḫaṭṭābī explains that Duʿāʾ belongs to the reality of ʿIbādah, because the one who supplicates shows in it his need, humility, and dependence before Allah. Whoever asks Allah thereby acknowledges that benefit, harm, granting, and withholding lie in Allah’s hand. Therefore Duʿāʾ is not merely a request for needs, but an expression of Tawḥīd, submission, and hope. The Ḥadīṯ thus indicates that Duʿāʾ is a mighty form of worship and that the servant should not turn away from Allah by means of it.

HAD-0043.text: The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim. He does not wrong him and does not hand him over. Whoever fulfills his brother’s need, Allah fulfills his need; whoever removes a distress from a Muslim, Allah removes from him a distress from the distresses of the Day of Resurrection.
HAD-0043.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0043.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the statement ‘The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim’ sums up the rights of brotherhood in Islām. This includes not wronging him, not abandoning him when he needs help, and not leaving him to those who harm him. Whoever fulfills his brother’s need is rewarded by Allah with the fulfillment of his own need; whoever removes a distress from a Muslim, Allah removes from him a distress on the Day of Resurrection. The Ḥadīṯ does not make help for Muslims mere courtesy, but a religious duty and a path to Allah’s help in this world and the Hereafter.

HAD-0044.text: Whoever leads to something good receives the same reward as the one who does it.
HAD-0044.narrator: Abū Masʿūd ʿUqbah ibn ʿAmr reported:
HAD-0044.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0044.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the one who leads to something good receives a share of the reward, because he was a cause, a guide, or a helper for that good deed. This includes teaching, reminding, mediation, practical help, and every lawful guidance by which another is led to obedience. The reward of the one who acts is not diminished thereby; rather, the Ḥadīṯ shows the vastness of Allah’s mercy and the great value of opening doors of good for others. Therefore it is among the best paths to guide people to beneficial knowledge, obedience, Ṣadaqah, assistance, and every kind of Birr.

HAD-0045.text: Whoever calls to right guidance receives the same reward as those who follow him in it, without anything being diminished from their rewards. Whoever calls to a path of error bears sin corresponding to the sins of those who follow him, without anything being diminished from their sins.
HAD-0045.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0045.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the immense responsibility of invitation and guidance. Whoever calls to right guidance, through knowledge, reminder, example, or practical leadership, receives a share of the reward of those who follow him in it, without their reward being diminished. Likewise, the one who calls to a path of error, innovation, sin, or false practice bears a share of the guilt of those who follow him in it, without their guilt being lessened. The meaning is not merely a one-time speech, but every cause by which people are lastingly led to good or to evil.

HAD-0046.text: The believer is not bitten twice from the same hole.
HAD-0046.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0046.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ trains the believer in caution, insight, and learning from experience. If harm, deception, or sin has come to him from a cause, he should not heedlessly fall again into the same cause. The Ḥadīṯ joins Īmān with vigilance: the believer should not be naive toward repeated harm, but should recognize causes, protect himself, and avoid the means that have already led him to loss, sin, or humiliation. Therein lies no call to suspicion without proof, but to reasonable caution after recognizable experience.

HAD-0047.text: None of you should wish for death because of a calamity that has befallen him. If he absolutely must do so, he should say: “O Allah, let me live as long as life is better for me, and let me die when death is better for me.”
HAD-0047.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0047.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ keeps the servant from wishing for death out of impatience because of illness, suffering, or worldly distress. The human being does not know whether life is better for him, because he may repent in it, increase good deeds, and gain rank, or whether death is better for him, because he is preserved from trial. Therefore the wish is not based on one’s own judgment, but is left to Allah: the servant asks for life when good lies in it, and for death when good lies in it. Thus the Ḥadīṯ joins patience, resignation, and trust in Allah’s knowledge.

HAD-0048.text: The Muslim has six rights over his Muslim brother: when you meet him, greet him; when he invites you, accept his invitation; when he asks you for advice, advise him sincerely; when he sneezes and praises Allah, wish him mercy; when he falls ill, visit him; and when he dies, follow his funeral.
HAD-0048.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0048.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that these rights gather the visible forms of Muslim brotherhood. The Salām opens safety and affection; accepting the invitation strengthens the bond; sincere advice protects the brother from harm; the Duʿāʾ after sneezing joins praise of Allah with mercy; visiting the sick gives comfort and reminds of the Hereafter; following the funeral fulfills the right of the deceased and reminds the living. The Ḥadīṯ thus shows that brotherhood is not only a feeling, but becomes visible through concrete duties and help in daily life.

HAD-0049.text: There is no fasting on two days: the day of breaking the fast and the day of the sacrifice festival.
HAD-0049.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0049.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the prohibition of fasting on ʿĪd al-Fiṭr and ʿĪd al-Aḍḥā protects the special meaning of these two days. The day of breaking the fast is the visible completion of the Ramaḍān fast, on which the servant thanks Allah for the fulfillment of the duty. The day of the sacrifice festival is bound to sacrifice, eating, food, and festive joy. Therefore these days are not places of voluntary abstinence, but days on which accepting Allah’s permission, gratitude, and communal joy become visible. The prohibition shows that obedience lies not only in fasting, but also in not fasting at the proper time.

HAD-0050.text: Fear Allah and be just toward your children.
HAD-0050.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0050.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ obliges justice among children in gifts and bestowals, or strongly admonishes to it, because preference without a justified reason can produce wrong, envy, hatred, and the breaking of the family bond. The statement ‘Fear Allah’ shows that parents stand before Allah even in private family matters and may not act merely according to inclination. Justice means not setting children against one another by arbitrary preference, but ordering rights, affection, and giving with Taqwā and responsibility.

HAD-0051.text: Whomever Allah wants good for, He grants him understanding in the religion.
HAD-0051.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0051.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the rank of Fiqh in the Dīn: whoever receives understanding of the religion, Allah has opened for him a great door of good. This understanding does not comprise merely memorizing individual texts, but recognizing their meanings, their application, and the paths of obedience. The Ḥadīṯ also indicates that ignorance and indifference toward religious understanding are a loss, because the special share of good lies in comprehending and acting rightly according to the Dīn.

HAD-0052.text: Seven will Allah shade in His shade on the day when there is no shade except His shade: a just ruler; a young person who grew up in the worship of Allah; a man whose heart is attached to the mosques; two people who love each other for Allah’s sake, meet upon that and part upon that; a man whom a woman of standing and beauty calls to herself and who says: ‘I fear Allah’; a man who gives charity so secretly that his left hand does not know what his right hand spends; and a man who remembers Allah in seclusion and whose eyes shed tears.
HAD-0052.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0052.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ gathers several high doors of sincerity and steadfastness. The just ruler bears the weight of the rights of people; the young person who grows up in worship resists desires early; the servant bound to the mosque shows constant longing for Ṣalāh; love for Allah’s sake is free of mere worldly purpose; rejecting temptation despite the woman’s beauty and rank shows perfect fear of Allah; hidden Ṣadaqah protects from Riyāʾ; and tears at Ḏikr in seclusion show sincere fear and softness of the heart. These qualities deserve special shade, because they contain hidden sincerity and hard self-restraint.

HAD-0053.text: Whoever guarantees for me what is between his jaws and what is between his legs, I guarantee for him Paradise.
HAD-0053.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0053.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that what is between the two jaws means the tongue, and what is between the two legs means the private part. These two areas are among the greatest trials of the human being, because many sins arise through them: false speech, lying, slander, wounding words, and forbidden desire. Whoever guards both closes two great doors of ruin and is protected from immense evil. Therefore the Ḥadīṯ joins the guarding of the tongue and chastity with the promise of Paradise.

HAD-0054.text: Two gifts in which many people suffer loss: health and free time.
HAD-0054.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0054.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the human being is truly free for obedience only when he is physically healthy and not pressed in his provision. Whoever possesses health and free time but does not use them for obedience, gratitude, and preparation for the Hereafter deceives himself and loses. Gratitude for these two gifts includes fulfilling Allah’s commands, avoiding His prohibitions, and not wasting the available opportunity through heedlessness. The Ḥadīṯ therefore warns against the loss that does not arise from a lack of means, but from a wrong dealing with gifts that are present.

HAD-0055.text: Be in this world like a stranger or a traveler.
HAD-0055.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0055.sharh: The earliest layer of explanation lies in the transmitted context of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنه: When you reach the evening, do not expect the morning; when you reach the morning, do not expect the evening. Take from your health for your illness and from your life for your death. Thereby the meaning of the prophetic word is explained: the believer should not treat the world as a lasting home, but like a stranger or a traveler who knows his way, takes provision, and does not lose himself in an unnecessary stay. The heart remains directed to the Hereafter, while the time that is available is used for obedience.

HAD-0056.text: No one has ever eaten better food than that which he earned by the work of his own hands. *And Allah’s Prophet Dāwūd ate from the work of his own hands.*
HAD-0056.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0056.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the merit of lawful earning through one’s own work. Work with one’s own hand preserves a person from humiliating begging, strengthens independence, and joins provision with lawful effort. That Dāwūd عليه السلام is mentioned, although he was a prophet and a king, shows that one’s own earning is not a lessening of rank, but honor and gratitude. The Ḥadīṯ therefore calls not to belittle lawful work and to seek one’s livelihood in a way free of wrong, fraud, and neediness toward people.

HAD-0057.text: May Allah have mercy on a man who is generous and lenient when he sells, when he buys, and when he collects a debt.
HAD-0057.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0057.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ urges Samāḥah, that is generosity, mildness, and leniency in dealing with people. In selling, this means not being harsh, fraudulent, or excessively quarrelsome; in buying, not pressing the seller unjustly; in collecting debts, not meeting the debtor with harshness, humiliation, or unnecessary tightness. The prayer for Allah’s mercy upon such a person shows that good character in trade is part of the Dīn and that economic dealing is not separated from Taqwā and Adab.

HAD-0058.text: I and the one who cares for an orphan will be like this in Paradise, and he indicated with the index and middle finger.
HAD-0058.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0058.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the immense merit of the one who cares for an orphan. What is meant is not merely food and clothing, but care, protection, upbringing, preservation of the property, and setting upright what the child lacks because of the loss of his father. Nearness to the Prophet ﷺ in Paradise is made clear by the sign with the index and middle finger, because the one who provides for an orphan fulfills a great door of mercy, care, and strengthening of a weak person. The Ḥadīṯ makes care for orphans a deed of special rank.

HAD-0059.text: A man asked: ‘Who has the most right to my good companionship?’ He said: ‘Your mother.’ He asked: ‘Then who?’ He said: ‘Your mother.’ He asked: ‘Then who?’ He said: ‘Your mother.’ He asked: ‘Then who?’ He said: ‘Your father.’
HAD-0059.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0059.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the threefold mention of the mother shows her special precedence in good treatment. She bears burdens that the father does not bear: pregnancy, birth, nursing, care, and special solicitude in the child’s early weakness. Therefore her right to good companionship, gentleness, service, and gratitude is highlighted repeatedly before the father is mentioned. The Ḥadīṯ does not lessen the father’s right, but orders the claims according to the special toil and care that Allah has laid upon the mother.

HAD-0060.text: Whoever wants his provision to be expanded and his lifespan to be lengthened should maintain the ties of kinship.
HAD-0060.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0060.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that Ṣilat ar-Raḥim is among the causes by which Allah places Barakah in provision and life. The expansion of Rizq can appear through actual increase, eased benefit, blessing, and the turning away of tightness. The lengthening of the lifespan is understood by the scholars as an actual lengthening according to Allah’s knowledge or as Barakah in life: the person uses his time better, his traces remain, and his good increases. The Ḥadīṯ shows that maintaining kinship is not only social propriety, but a religious deed with effect upon Dunyā and Āḫirah.

HAD-0061.text: No Muslim is struck by exhaustion, illness, worry, sadness, harm, or grief – not even by a thorn that pricks him – without Allah thereby erasing something of his sins.
HAD-0061.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0061.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the vastness of Allah’s mercy toward the believing servant. Not only severe illness, but also worry, grief, harm, and even a small thorn can erase sins. The value does not lie in seeking suffering, but in that Allah makes unavoidable suffering a purification. The servant should therefore be patient, hope for Allah’s reward, and not think that small discomforts are meaningless; for Allah can make even slight pains an expiation and an elevation.

HAD-0103.text: Look at those who are below you, and do not look at those who are above you. *Thus you will not belittle the gifts of Allah that He has given you.*
HAD-0103.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0103.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the Ḥadīṯ trains the servant in gratitude. Whoever, in worldly matters, constantly looks at the one who possesses more runs the risk of belittling Allah’s gifts and becoming discontent. Whoever instead looks at those who have less recognizes Allah’s favor upon himself more clearly and is more likely to be grateful. The Ḥadīṯ thus orders the gaze of the heart: in Dīn and obedience one should strive upward, but with worldly gifts one should not despise one’s own provision.

HAD-0107.text: The words most beloved to Allah are four: ‘Glory be to Allah’, ‘All praise belongs to Allah’, ‘None has the right to be worshipped except Allah’, and ‘Allah is greater’.
HAD-0107.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0107.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that these four words are especially distinguished because of their comprehensive meanings. Tasbīḥ declares Allah free of every deficiency, Ḥamd contains praise and acknowledgment of His perfection, Lā ilāha illa Allāh is the statement of Tawḥīd, and Allāhu akbar contains the magnification of Allah above all things. The Ḥadīṯ shows that a short Ḏikr can have immense rank when its meaning is recognized and it is spoken with a sincere heart.

HAD-0109.text: Allah rejoices over the repentance of His servant more strongly than one of you rejoices when he finds his lost mount again in a lonely desert.
HAD-0109.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0109.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the report about the extraordinary joy at recovered property and points out that the man, because of overwhelming joy, even swapped the words; such an unintended slip of the tongue is not held against him. The comparison makes clear the immense significance of sincere Tawbah.

HAD-0110.text: Paradise is closer to each of you than his shoe strap — and the Fire likewise.
HAD-0110.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0110.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ makes clear the nearness of salvation and ruin. A deed, a word, or a decision can become for the servant a cause of Paradise; likewise, a sin that he belittles can be a cause of great danger. The comparison with the shoe strap shows that the paths to the Hereafter are very near to the human being and that he should neither belittle any good deed nor trivialize any bad deed. The Ḥadīṯ calls for constant vigilance, repentance, and making use of the nearby doors of good.

HAD-0111.text: A man found a harmful branch on the path and removed it. Allah thanked him for that and forgave him.
HAD-0111.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0111.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that removing harm from the path is a real kindness toward people. The man performed an outwardly small deed, but it was a benefit to others and protection from harm. That Allah thanked him for it and forgave him shows the merit of beneficial deeds, even when they appear slight, when they are done with sincerity and good intention. The Ḥadīṯ trains one not to belittle paths of good and to remove harm from the Muslims and from people in general.

HAD-0112.text: A man saw a dog that was eating earth from thirst, and he gave it water to drink. Allah thanked him for that and forgave him. For every living being to which one does good there is reward.
HAD-0112.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0112.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the merit of mercy toward every living being. The man helped a dog in severe distress, although a dog appears outwardly insignificant; yet this deed became great with Allah. From this it is understood that benefit, provision, and mercy toward creatures are rewarded when they occur in a permitted and sincere manner. The statement that there is reward for every living being widens the servant’s view: kindness is valuable not only toward people, but also toward animals.

HAD-0113.text: A woman entered the Fire because of a cat: she had confined it, given it nothing to eat, and not released it so that it could eat from the small creatures of the earth.
HAD-0113.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0113.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the grave guilt that can arise through cruelty toward animals. The woman was not blamed because she owned the cat, but because she confined it, denied it food, and did not release it so that it could seek food itself. From this it is understood that an animal one keeps has a right to provision; whoever does not wish to provide for it may not expose it to death by confinement. The Ḥadīṯ is a warning against wrongdoing even toward weak animals.

HAD-0114.text: Whoever deceives us is not of us.
HAD-0114.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0114.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that deceit contradicts the way of the Muslims and the duty of sincerity. Whoever deceives in trade, in counsel, in knowledge, or in any matter violates trust and harms his brother. The statement ‘is not of us’ is a severe warning and means: he does not act according to our complete guidance nor according to the character of the sincere Muslims. The Ḥadīṯ makes clear that deception is not a light matter, but a breach of Amānah and Naṣīḥah.

HAD-0115.text: Delaying a debt by one who is able to pay is wrongdoing.
HAD-0115.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0115.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that delaying a due debt by someone who can pay is Ẓulm. The debtor then withholds a right although he is able to fulfill it. The Ḥadīṯ protects the wealth and the rights of the creditor and shows that the ability to pay brings responsibility. Whoever cannot pay does not fall under the same blame as the one who delays intentionally; what is meant is the one who can, but delays without right.

HAD-0116.text: Whoever takes people’s wealth intending to repay it, Allah helps him to repay it. Whoever takes it in order to destroy it, Allah destroys him.
HAD-0116.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0116.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the importance of intention in debts and in the wealth of others. Whoever takes money while seriously intending to return it has a righteous intention; for him Allah will open help, ease, and ways to repayment. Whoever takes it, however, in order to consume it, waste it, or destroy the rights of others exposes himself to Allah’s punishment. The Ḥadīṯ joins financial Amānah with inner honesty and warns against deceit under the name of a loan or a debt.

HAD-0118.text: For every joint of yours a kindness is due in the morning. Every glorification, every praise, every declaration of Allah’s oneness, and every magnification is a kindness. Two units of the Ḍuḥā prayer suffice for that.
HAD-0118.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0118.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the human body, through its joints and limbs, experiences daily a favor of Allah for which thanks are due. This thanks can be fulfilled through many kinds of good: Tasbīḥ, Taḥmīd, Tahlīl, Takbīr, enjoining good, forbidding evil, and further good deeds. Two Rakʿah of the Ḍuḥā prayer suffice for that, because they employ the body in worship and gather the thanks for these bodily gifts. The Ḥadīṯ shows the breadth of the concept of Ṣadaqah and the merit of the Ḍuḥā prayer.

HAD-0120.text: Beware of wrongdoing, for wrongdoing will be darknesses on the Day of Resurrection. Beware also of stinginess.
HAD-0120.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0120.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that Ẓulm becomes darknesses on the Day of Resurrection because it leads the doer into terror, darkness, and punishment. Wrongdoing includes the violation of the rights of Allah and the rights of creatures. The warning against stinginess follows because stinginess drives a person to withhold rights, sever kinship, covet the property of others, and fall into enmity. The Ḥadīṯ therefore joins inner illness with outward wrongdoing and calls for fulfilling rights, restraining greed, and harming no one.

HAD-0121.text: Do you know who the bankrupt one is? The bankrupt one from my community is the one who comes on the Day of Resurrection with prayer, fasting, and Zakāh, but has insulted others, slandered them, robbed them of their wealth, shed blood, or struck them. His good deeds will be given to those who were harmed. When his good deeds are exhausted, their sins will be placed upon him and he will be cast into the Fire.
HAD-0121.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0121.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that true bankruptcy is not only the loss of property in this world, but the loss of good deeds on the Day of Reckoning. A person may come with Ṣalāh, Ṣiyām, and Zakāh, but his violations of the rights of others cause his good deeds to be distributed: to the one insulted, the one slandered, the one struck, and the one robbed. If his good deeds do not suffice, the sins of those harmed are placed upon him. The Ḥadīṯ thereby warns severely against separating worship from bad conduct, Ẓulm, and the violation of people’s rights.

HAD-0122.text: You will not enter Paradise until you believe; and you will not truly believe until you love one another. Shall I point you to something by which you will love one another? Spread the greeting of peace among you.
HAD-0122.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0122.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the connection between Īmān, mutual love, and visible conduct. What is meant is the completeness of Īmān, which appears in love for Allah’s sake, mercy, and good relations among the believers. Spreading the Salām is a practical way to that, because the greeting of peace expresses safety, nearness, and brotherhood. The Ḥadīṯ therefore teaches that Īmān does not remain only an inner claim, but becomes visible in conduct.

HAD-0125.text: A person will be with the one he loves.
HAD-0125.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0125.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ contains an immense hope for the believer: whoever loves the prophets, the truthful, and the righteous for Allah’s sake will be gathered with them, even if his own deeds do not reach their rank. At the same time there is a warning in it, for love shows attachment, direction, and following. A person should therefore examine whom he loves, whom he emulates, and with whom his heart is bound.

HAD-0126.text: The likeness of the good and the bad companion is like that of a musk seller and a blacksmith. From the good companion you receive good; from the bad one harm can reach you.
HAD-0126.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0126.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the effect of company upon religion and character. The good companion is like the musk seller: either he gives you something, you buy from him, or at least you take away a good scent. Thus the righteous person benefits through counsel, example, reminder, and good influence. The bad companion is like the blacksmith’s bellows: either he burns clothing or he leaves a bad smell. Thus bad company can lead to sin, bad character, suspicion, and imitation of evil.

HAD-0127.text: A woman is married for four things: for her wealth, her lineage, her beauty, and her religion. So choose the religious woman.
HAD-0127.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0127.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ does not forbid noticing beauty, lineage, or wealth. It does, however, order the standards: the lastingly beneficial and safest reason is the Dīn. Wealth can disappear, beauty fades, and lineage alone does not protect against bad character or weak religion. Whoever chooses the religious woman seeks a marriage on the basis of fear of Allah, fidelity, preservation of rights, and help in obedience to Allah.

HAD-0128.text: A believing man should not hate a believing woman. If one trait in her displeases him, another will please him.
HAD-0128.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0128.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the Ḥadīṯ guides to a just view and good living together. A man should not develop complete hatred toward his wife because of one trait that displeases him and thereby overlook her good traits. If one thing troubles him, he finds in her other traits that please him: Dīn, modesty, care, patience, fidelity, or other virtues. The Ḥadīṯ calls for forbearance, balance, and a just consideration, instead of reducing the marriage to a single weakness.

HAD-0129.text: The world is a passing enjoyment, and the best of its enjoyment is a righteous woman.
HAD-0129.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0129.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the world is, in its nature, a passing benefit. The best part of this permitted benefit is the righteous wife, because her benefit does not remain merely worldly. She helps in the Dīn, preserves rights, protects the home, strengthens chastity, supports patience, and reminds of obedience. The Ḥadīṯ thereby does not merely highlight outward enjoyment, but the joining of worldly life together with religious benefit and righteousness.

HAD-0130.text: O young men: whoever among you has the means for marriage should marry. That helps to lower the gaze and to preserve chastity. Whoever is not able should fast, for fasting is a protection for him.
HAD-0130.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0130.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that marriage is recommended for the one who possesses its means and its responsibility, because it protects the gaze and the private parts more strongly. It helps to direct unlawful desires into lawful channels and to preserve chastity. Whoever is not able to do so should fast, because fasting weakens desire, restrains the soul, and serves as protection against forbidden paths. The Ḥadīṯ thereby joins practical conduct of life with preservation of the religion.

HAD-0177.text: Whoever sends blessings upon me once, upon him Allah sends blessings ten times.
HAD-0177.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0177.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the great merit of the Ṣalāh upon the Prophet ﷺ: whoever sends blessings upon him once, Allah grants him tenfold blessing for that. The Ḥadīṯ shows that this deed belongs to the immense doors of Ḏikr, that it strengthens love for the Prophet ﷺ, and that it brings the servant a great reward. The meaning remains that Allah raises the servant’s rank, praises him, and grants him mercy.

HAD-0178.text: It is not permissible for a Muslim to shun his brother for more than three nights. If they meet and each turns away from the other, the better of the two is the one who begins with the greeting of peace.
HAD-0178.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0178.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that mutual shunning among Muslims may not be continued without a legal ground. The limit of three nights attaches to ordinary human hurt; after that the way to reconciliation should be opened. The better of the two is the one who begins the Salām, because he breaks pride, takes the first step toward connection, and weakens the cause of enmity.

HAD-0179.text: A man should not be alone with a woman unless a Maḥram is with her. And a woman should not travel without a Maḥram.
HAD-0179.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0179.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the Ḥadīṯ closes paths to Fitnah and protects honor. Ḫalwah, that is, an unrelated man being alone with a woman without a Maḥram, is forbidden, because it can be a cause of temptation and suspicion. Likewise the wording mentions a woman’s travel without a Maḥram. The Ḥadīṯ shows the protective frame of the Šarīʿah for dealings, travel, and the preservation of limits.

HAD-0180.text: Fasting on the Day of ʿArafah: I hope from Allah that it expiates the sins of the past year and of the coming year.
HAD-0180.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0180.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the special merit of voluntary fasting on the Day of ʿArafah. The mentioned expiation concerns the sins of the past year and of the coming year, and the scholars relate this to minor sins, whereas major sins require repentance and return to Allah. The Ḥadīṯ urges one to use this day with fasting, hope in Allah’s forgiveness, and sincerity.

HAD-0182.text: I know that you are only a stone that neither harms nor benefits. Had I not seen the Prophet ﷺ kiss you, I would not have kissed you.
HAD-0182.narrator: It is authentically transmitted from ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0182.speaker: He said to the Black Stone:
HAD-0182.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the statement of ʿUmar رضي الله عنه shows pure Ittibāʿ. The Black Stone possesses in itself neither benefit nor harm; touching it or kissing it is not done because of an independent effect, but solely because the Prophet ﷺ did it. The Aṯar preserves Tawḥīd and the Sunnah together: no exaggeration toward a stone, yet complete following of what is transmitted from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

HAD-0183.text: People were judged in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by revelation; now revelation has ended. We judge you by what becomes visible of your deeds. Your hidden matters Allah reckons.
HAD-0183.narrator: It is authentically transmitted from ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0183.speaker: He said:
HAD-0183.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that this Aṯar shows an important rule in dealings and in judgments: people are judged by what appears outwardly from them; what is hidden and the inner intentions are left to Allah. In the time of the Prophet ﷺ, revelation could uncover hidden states; after the end of revelation the standard remains what is manifest, while Allah reckons the secrets of the hearts.

HAD-0185.text: Sit with us so that we may strengthen our Īmān for an hour – by that he meant: remembering Allah.
HAD-0185.narrator: It is authentically transmitted from Muʿāḏ ibn Ǧabal رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0185.speaker: He said:
HAD-0185.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains, in connection with the statements about the increase and decrease of Īmān, that Ḏikr, obedience, and remembrance of Allah strengthen Īmān. The statement of Muʿāḏ ibn Ǧabal رضي الله عنه shows that the Ṣaḥābah understood sitting for Ḏikr, admonition, and renewal of the heart as a means by which Īmān increases. What is meant is not an empty claim, but strengthening through obedience, knowledge, and remembrance of Allah.

HAD-0187.text: We were forbidden to spy on people. If, however, something becomes openly visible to us, we act upon it.
HAD-0187.narrator: It is authentically transmitted from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0187.speaker: He said:
HAD-0187.sharh: al-Ḫaṭṭābī explains, in connection with the prohibition of Taǧassus, that people’s hidden affairs may not be spied upon. The Aṯar of ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه shows the same rule: one does not search for concealed faults, secrets, or sins. If, however, something appears openly and visibly, one acts according to the outward. Thereby both the honor of the Muslims and the order according to what is manifest are preserved.

HAD-0201.text: Whoever among you sees something reprehensible should change it with his hand; if he cannot, then with his tongue; if he cannot do that either, then with his heart. *That is the weakest degree of faith.*
HAD-0201.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0201.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that changing Munkar takes place according to ability, knowledge, responsibility, and possible benefit. Whoever can change it with the hand without bringing about a greater evil has this degree; whoever cannot do that uses the tongue with admonition and clarification; whoever cannot do that either detests the reprehensible in his heart. That this is the weakest degree of Īmān shows: even when outward change is not possible, the heart must not approve of the Munkar.

HAD-0204.text: In Paradise there is a gate called ar-Rayyān. Through this gate those who fast will enter on the Day of Resurrection, and no one besides them will enter through it.
HAD-0204.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0204.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that ar-Rayyān is a special gate of Paradise for those who fast. The distinction fits the hardship of fasting, because the fasting person withholds thirst and desire for the sake of Allah; on the Last Day he is honored by a gate whose name points to quenching and joy after thirst. The Ḥadīṯ shows the special rank of Ṣawm and the particular honor of those who preserve it sincerely.

HAD-0205.text: Whoever fasts one day in the path of Allah, Allah thereby removes his face seventy years from the Fire.
HAD-0205.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0205.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the great merit of fasting in the path of Allah. The removal of the face from the Fire by seventy years makes visible the immense protection and reward that are joined to sincerity, patience, and effort. The Ḥadīṯ urges voluntary fasting, especially when it does not lead to neglecting other duties or to harm.

HAD-0208.text: Whoever shows enmity to one of My near servants, I declare war on him. My servant does not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than what I have made obligatory upon him, and he continues to draw near to Me through voluntary deeds until I love him.
HAD-0208.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ narrated from his Lord:
HAD-0208.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Walī of Allah is described by Īmān, Taqwā, and obedience, not by mere claim. The greatest drawing near to Allah occurs through the obligations, for they are most beloved to Allah. Thereafter voluntary deeds increase the servant’s nearness until Allah loves him. The Ḥadīṯ at the same time shows the severe threat toward the one who shows enmity to Allah’s near servants.

HAD-0211.text: Help your brother, whether he does wrong or wrong is done to him. His help, when he does wrong, is to restrain him from the wrong.
HAD-0211.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0211.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that help in the Dīn does not mean blind partisanship. One helps the oppressed by supporting him and turning wrong away from him. One helps the one who commits wrong by restraining him from Ẓulm and bringing him back to the truth. The Ḥadīṯ thereby corrects tribal and group loyalty: true Naṣīḥah is adherence to right and justice.

HAD-0214.text: Whoever strives in the care of a widow and a needy person is like one who strives in the path of Allah, or like one who prays at night and fasts during the day.
HAD-0214.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
