HAD-0214.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that constant care for widows and the needy, because of its great benefit and the patience required in it, is compared to the rank of the Mujāhid and of the one who constantly prays and fasts. He calls to take up this form of care as a great, lasting good deed.

HAD-0218.text: Whoever removes from a believer a distress of this world, Allah removes from him a distress of the Day of Resurrection. Whoever grants relief to a needy person, Allah grants him relief. Allah helps the servant as long as the servant helps his brother.
HAD-0218.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0218.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the Ḥadīṯ gathers several doors of help: whoever removes a distress from a believer, whoever grants relief to a needy person, and whoever helps his brother receives corresponding help and relief from Allah. The recompense is according to the kind of deed. The Ḥadīṯ teaches that mercy, relief, and active help among Muslims belong to the great causes of Allah’s help.

HAD-0220.text: When a Muslim supplicates for his brother in his absence, the entrusted angel says: Āmīn – and for you the same.
HAD-0220.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0220.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that Duʿāʾ for the brother in his absence belongs to the pure forms of Naṣīḥah, because there is in it no visible return benefit and no display. The entrusted angel says Āmīn and asks the same for the one who supplicates. The Ḥadīṯ shows the merit of sincere love for Muslims, of hidden supplications, and of wishing good for others.

HAD-0221.text: Paradise is surrounded by hardship, and the Fire by desires.
HAD-0221.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0221.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the things by which Paradise is reached often weigh heavily on the soul: obligations, patience, struggle against desires, and avoiding the forbidden. The Fire, by contrast, is surrounded by desires, because the way to it appears eased by uncontrolled appetite, comfort, and sins. The Ḥadīṯ makes the servant watchful: not every easy path leads to salvation, and not every hardship is loss.

HAD-0222.text: This world, compared with the Hereafter, is like the water that remains on a finger after one dips it into the sea.
HAD-0222.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0222.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the Prophet ﷺ, with this likeness, makes visible the insignificance of the world before the Hereafter. What remains on the finger after dipping it into the sea is vanishingly little compared with the expanse of the sea. Likewise, worldly life is slight, short, and passing compared with the duration, expanse, and reality of the Āḫirah. The Ḥadīṯ trains one in Zuhd, preparation for the Hereafter, and a right weighing of the world.

HAD-0224.text: Whoever gives in charity even the value of a date from good earning – and Allah accepts only what is good –, Allah accepts his charity and causes it to grow for him until it becomes like a mountain.
HAD-0224.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0224.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that Allah accepts only what comes from lawful, good earning. Even a small Ṣadaqah, such as the value of a date, can become immense with Allah when it is given sincerely and from ṭayyib property. The Ḥadīṯ joins purity of earning, sincerity of the gift, and Allah’s multiplication of the reward, until the small charity grows for the servant like a mountain.

HAD-0228.text: Allah said: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has imagined.
HAD-0228.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ narrated from his Lord:
HAD-0228.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that this Ḥadīṯ shows the greatness and hiddenness of the gifts of Paradise. What Allah has prepared for His righteous servants surpasses what eyes have seen, ears have heard, and hearts have imagined. The Ḥadīṯ trains one not to measure the Āḫirah by limited worldly standards and to hope in Allah’s promise.

HAD-0305.text: This is something Allah has decreed for the daughters of Ādam. Perform all the actions of the pilgrims, except that you do not perform Ṭawāf around the Kaʿbah until you are pure.
HAD-0305.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said to her:
HAD-0305.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains, on the basis of the report of ʿĀʾishah, that menstruation does not prevent all the pilgrimage rites. The Prophet ﷺ expressly excepted the Ṭawāf until she would be pure again; Ḏikr and Duʿāʾ remain possible according to his discussion. Ibn Raǧab mentions legal discussions about Ṭawāf in special cases and does not equate those views with the wording of the regular prophetic instruction.

HAD-0306.text: This bleeding is from a blood vessel and is not Ḥayḍ. When the actual menstruation begins, leave the prayer; when it ends, purify yourself and pray.
HAD-0306.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said to Fāṭimah bint Abī Ḥubayš:
HAD-0306.sharh: Ibn Raǧab distinguishes the ordinary menstrual flow from Istiḥāḍah as bleeding that occurs outside the state of menstruation. The Prophet ﷺ instructed Fāṭimah bint Abī Ḥubayš to leave the prayer during the actual menstruation and, after it ended, to wash off the blood and pray again. Ibn Raǧab therefore compares the different authentic wordings of the same report and separates the actual time of menstruation from ongoing bleeding.

HAD-0307.text: If menstrual blood touches a garment, the spot should be loosened, washed with water, and the prayer then offered in it.
HAD-0307.narrator: Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-0307.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0307.sharh: Ibn Raǧab presents the report of Asmāʾ about removing menstrual blood from a garment and, for the detailed explanation, expressly refers to his earlier treatment in the Kitāb al-Wuḍūʾ. In the later comparison with the report of ʿĀʾishah he highlights the difference: there the washing out of the blood is expressly mentioned; merely rubbing off a slight trace must therefore not be generalized without further qualification as a sufficient cleansing of every amount of blood. The passage in question is a cross-reference and a comparison of variants, not an independent, complete new legal discussion.

HAD-0308.text: When one of them became pure after menstruation, she cleaned the blood spot on the garment, washed the place thoroughly, sprinkled water over the rest of the cloth, and prayed in it.
HAD-0308.speaker: She said:
HAD-0308.sharh: Ibn Raǧab sets the report of ʿĀʾishah against the other transmission about rubbing a blood spot: according to her account, the affected place was first worked on, the blood was then washed out with water, and the rest of the cloth was sprinkled with water; afterwards the garment could be used for prayer. Ibn Raǧab expressly stresses that precisely this wording contains the washing of the blood. A rubbing based only on saliva in other wordings he interprets cautiously in connection with a slight amount of blood and differing views.

HAD-0309.text: A wife of the Prophet ﷺ performed Iʿtikāf with him even though she had Istiḥāḍah. She saw blood and sometimes placed a vessel beneath her.
HAD-0309.speaker: She said:
HAD-0309.sharh: Ibn Raǧab presents the report of ʿĀʾishah about the Iʿtikāf of a wife of the Prophet ﷺ who had Istiḥāḍah. The report shows that ongoing bleeding outside the actual menstruation does not, as a rule, prevent taking part in Iʿtikāf. The vessel beneath her served to catch the blood and protected the place of prayer from impurity. Ibn Raǧab cites three routes of the same report for this.

HAD-0310.text: A wife of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed Iʿtikāf with him while she saw blood and a yellowish fluid; during the prayer a vessel stood beneath her.
HAD-0310.speaker: She said:
HAD-0310.sharh: Ibn Raǧab cites the wording about the woman with ongoing bleeding, together with a reddish and yellowish discharge, in the same chapter on Iʿtikāf. That a vessel stood beneath her concerns the practical avoidance of blood impurity during prayer, not a prohibition of the prayer. The wording shares its core point with HAD-0309 and is not presented as a new, independent occurrence.

HAD-0311.text: One of the Mothers of the Believers performed Iʿtikāf even though she had Istiḥāḍah.
HAD-0311.speaker: She said:
HAD-0311.sharh: Ibn Raǧab mentions this short report about the Iʿtikāf of a Mother of the Believers who had Istiḥāḍah as the third wording of the transmission through ʿIkrimah from ʿĀʾishah. The sentence establishes the same principle as HAD-0309: Istiḥāḍah is to be distinguished from menstruation and does not of itself cancel the Iʿtikāf. A new occurrence independent of the other two wordings is not claimed.

HAD-0312.text: None of them possessed more than one garment for the time of menstruation. When blood came upon it, she removed it with saliva and rubbed it off with the fingernail.
HAD-0312.speaker: She said:
HAD-0312.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains ʿĀʾishah’s report about the one garment worn during menstruation and examines the differing wordings of the terms for rubbing or scraping off a blood spot with the fingernail. He quotes al-Ḫaṭṭābī on the meaning of the word and sets against it the wording that expressly mentions washing out. According to his discussion, mere removal with saliva can point to a very small spot and a lenient treatment of it; alternatively, he discusses the question of cleansing by means other than water. He expressly marks the weaker routes of transmission as weak or unknown. This must not be understood as a general instruction to clean every menstrual blood with saliva alone.

HAD-0313.text: We were forbidden to mourn longer than three days, except for the husband. After purification from Ḥayḍ, however, a light scent was permitted to us.
HAD-0313.narrator: Umm ʿAṭiyyah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-0313.speaker: She said:
HAD-0313.sharh: Ibn Raǧab treats the limited exception for scented substances after the Ġusl from menstruation in connection with the rules of the mourning period. The Ḥadīṯ of Umm ʿAṭiyyah permits even the widow who is obliged to mourn a small amount of a scented substance at the purification after Ḥayḍ. The exception must not be confused with a general permission to use perfume throughout the entire mourning period.

HAD-0314.text: Take a cloth perfumed with musk and purify yourself with it. ʿĀʾishah رضي الله عنها explained to her that she should remove the trace of the blood with it.
HAD-0314.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said to a woman:
HAD-0314.sharh: Ibn Raǧab gives the explanation of the instruction that ʿĀʾishah clarified: the cloth serves, after the Ġusl, to clean the traces of the menstrual blood. The repetition of the question by the woman of the Anṣār makes clear why ʿĀʾishah afterwards explained the practical meaning herself. The report concerns the cleansing after the end of menstruation, not the ordinary washing of a soiled garment.

HAD-0315.text: Take a cloth perfumed with musk and purify yourself with it. Out of modesty the Prophet ﷺ turned his face away, and ʿĀʾishah رضي الله عنها explained the meaning to her.
HAD-0315.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said to a woman of the Anṣār:
HAD-0315.sharh: In this wording Ibn Raǧab explains the expression «firṣah», a small portion of cloth or wool, and that «mumsakah», according to the preferred interpretation, means a piece provided with musk. He distinguishes this explanation from the reading that it is merely a piece of hide. The application after the end of menstruation serves, according to the statements of Aḥmad that he cites, to remove the smell of the menstrual blood. ʿĀʾishah’s additional explanation makes understandable why the Prophet ﷺ did not answer the question in greater detail out of modesty. This is a second wording of the occurrence treated in HAD-0314.

HAD-0316.text: During the Farewell Pilgrimage she began to menstruate. The Prophet ﷺ commanded her to loosen her hair, comb it, and postpone the ʿUmrah.
HAD-0316.speaker: She said:
HAD-0316.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains the instruction to ʿĀʾishah, during the Farewell Pilgrimage, to loosen her hair, comb it, and enter the Iḥrām for Ḥaǧǧ. He makes clear that at that time she was still menstruating. The washing she was commanded to perform was for entering the Ḥaǧǧ-Iḥrām; it was not the concluding Ġusl after the end of menstruation. The report by itself is therefore not suitable as a direct proof that every woman must always loosen her braided hair for the menstrual Ġusl. Ibn Raǧab documents the later fiqh discussion on this separately.

HAD-0317.text: When she menstruated on the day of ʿArafah, the Prophet ﷺ commanded her to leave the ʿUmrah, loosen her hair, comb herself, and enter the Iḥrām for Ḥajj.
HAD-0317.speaker: She said:
HAD-0317.sharh: Ibn Raǧab examines the long wording about ʿĀʾishah’s menstruation on the day of ʿArafah and her instruction to loosen the hair before the Iḥrām for Ḥaǧǧ. He expressly warns against citing it in a shortened form as proof of an ordinary Ġusl after the end of menstruation: ʿĀʾishah still had her menstruation at that time. He reports that Aḥmad objected to a shortening of such a report that distorted the meaning, and he discusses differing views on whether the Ġusl at menstruation requires loosening braided hair. What is decisive in the views he cites is that water reaches the roots of the hair; if it does not reach them, loosening becomes necessary according to the widespread opinion. The connected question of ʿUmrah and Ḥaǧǧ is presented as a difference of opinion.

HAD-0318.text: Allah commissions an angel in the womb. When the creation is completed, the person’s sex, provision, lifespan, and outcome are written down.
HAD-0318.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0318.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0318.sharh: Ibn Raǧab places the report of Anas about the angel assigned to the womb into the chapter on the stages of human creation. He treats the Qurʾān words «formed and unformed» (22:5) and distinguishes the various early explanations concerning completed development and miscarriage. The details about sex, lifespan, provision, and the person’s outcome are part of the reported divine decree; no independent medical time prognosis can be derived from the report.

HAD-0319.text: During the Farewell Pilgrimage the Prophet ﷺ commanded her, because of the menstruation, to enter the Iḥrām for Ḥajj and later to perform an ʿUmrah from at-Tanʿīm.
HAD-0319.narrator: ʿUrwah reported from ʿĀʾishah رضي الله عنها:
HAD-0319.speaker: She said:
HAD-0319.sharh: Ibn Raǧab cites the report of ʿĀʾishah about the Farewell Pilgrimage: because of her menstruation she loosened her hair, combed it, and moved into the Iḥrām for Ḥaǧǧ after she had postponed her original ʿUmrah. After the pilgrimage was completed she was sent with ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr to at-Tanʿīm for the ʿUmrah. The report shows the permissibility of the pilgrimage rites for the menstruating woman, with the separate restriction of the Ṭawāf.

HAD-0320.text: This bleeding is from a blood vessel and is not the menstruation. When the menstruation begins, leave the prayer; when it ends, perform Ghusl and pray.
HAD-0320.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said about Istiḥāḍah:
HAD-0320.sharh: Ibn Raǧab cites this authentic report about Fāṭimah bint Abī Ḥubayš and highlights a disagreement about the expression «When the menstruation begins and ends»: what may be meant is recognizing the menstruation by the quality of the blood, or the arrival of the known ordinary days of menstruation. He explains both views and the differing criteria for Istiḥāḍah that follow from them. The Prophet ﷺ separated the actual menstruation, in which the prayer is left, from the remaining ongoing bleeding, after the end of whose menstrual phase Ġusl and prayer follow. The related wording HAD-0306 describes the same legal complex.

HAD-0321.text: We had our menstruation in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, yet he did not command us to make up the missed prayers.
HAD-0321.speaker: ʿĀʾishah رضي الله عنها said:
HAD-0321.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains ʿĀʾishah’s reply «Are you a Ḥarūriyyah?»: the question referred to the erroneous demand to make up the prayers left after menstruation. The Prophet ﷺ did not instruct the women to make them up, and the women of his time did not do so either. Ibn Raǧab expressly distinguishes making up the days of fasting from the obligatory prayers missed during the complete time of menstruation; borderline cases in which menstruation covers only part of a prayer time are judged differently among the scholars.

HAD-0322.text: When she lay during menstruation under the same cover with the Prophet ﷺ, she withdrew; the Prophet ﷺ called her back to himself under the cover.
HAD-0322.speaker: Umm Salamah رضي الله عنها said:
HAD-0322.sharh: Ibn Raǧab relates the report of Umm Salamah: at the beginning of menstruation she withdrew from the shared cover, whereupon the Prophet ﷺ called her back to himself. Ibn Raǧab expressly refers to his earlier explanation of the same matter in the chapter on the expression «Nifās» for menstruation. Ḥayḍ does not make the woman’s body impure; being together under one cover is permissible. The report also contains statements about a shared ritual washing and marital closeness, without this being counted from the wording present here as a new case.

HAD-0323.text: While she lay with the Prophet ﷺ under a cover, her menstruation came, she put on her menstruation garment, and the Prophet ﷺ called her back to himself.
HAD-0323.narrator: Umm Salamah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-0323.speaker: She said:
HAD-0323.sharh: Ibn Raǧab cites precisely this wording of Umm Salamah again, now under the chapter heading about special clothing during menstruation. He explains the difference from the earlier statement of ʿĀʾishah that some women possessed only a single garment: Umm Salamah evidently had clothing designated specifically for her menstruation. From both reports it follows that special menstruation clothing is permissible, but not generally obligatory. Menstruation in itself does not make clothing impure; actual blood spots must be treated separately. This report repeats the occurrence of HAD-0322 from another chapter context.

HAD-0324.text: Young women and menstruating women should come out to the ʿĪd gatherings and take part in the good; the menstruating women, however, stayed away from the place of prayer.
HAD-0324.narrator: Ḥafṣah bint Sīrīn reported from Umm ʿAṭiyyah رضي الله عنها:
HAD-0324.speaker: Umm ʿAṭiyyah رضي الله عنها said:
HAD-0324.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains the report of Umm ʿAṭiyyah: menstruating women too may attend the gatherings of the two ʿĪd days and take part in the good, Duʿāʾ, and Ḏikr, even though they themselves do not perform the prayer. He discusses the instruction to avoid the Muṣallā and reports a difference of opinion on whether the ʿĪd prayer place has the legal qualities of a mosque. Attendance at the gathering must therefore not be equated with taking part in the prayer itself.

HAD-0021.text: Beware of suspicions, for suspicions are among the most untrue of statements. Do not spy on one another, do not search for one another’s faults, do not envy one another, do not turn away from one another, and do not hate one another.
HAD-0021.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0021.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the forbidden suspicion is the one pursued without clear proof and used against the Muslim. Mere thoughts may occur to a person; what is censured is clinging to them, acting upon them, and allowing spying, the hunting of faults, envy, hatred, or turning away to arise from them. The Ḥadīṯ gathers several causes by which brotherhood is destroyed, and it leads the believer to preserve the honor of his brother, not to search for hidden faults, and not to build the relationship upon unfounded conjectures.

HAD-0022.text: There is a justified wish for something equal only in two cases: in a man to whom Allah has given wealth and who spends it on what is right, and in a man to whom Allah has given wisdom, by which he judges and which he teaches.
HAD-0022.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0022.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the ḥasad mentioned here is not the blameworthy envy in which one wishes that the gift disappear from the other. What is meant is Ġibṭah: the wish to possess a comparable gift without it being taken from the other. The Ḥadīṯ highlights two doors of good in which this Ġibṭah is praiseworthy: wealth that is spent in what is right, and Ḥikmah by which one judges and which one teaches. Thereby knowledge is joined to just action, and not merely to the bare possession of information.

HAD-0023.text: Your smile in the face of your brother is a charity for you. Your enjoining what is good, your forbidding what is evil, and the removal of obstacles from the path are also charities.
HAD-0023.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0023.sharh: Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr explains, in connection with the report about removing an obstacle from the path, that removing harm belongs to good deeds and that one should not belittle even works of good that appear small. Immediately afterward he transmits the Ḥadīṯ of Abū Ḏarr about the smile, the enjoining of good, help for others, and the removal of obstacles. The connection shows that charity is not limited to money, but also includes kind conduct and practical help.

HAD-0024.text: Purity is half of faith. “All praise belongs to Allah” fills the scale; “Glory be to Allah” and “All praise belongs to Allah” fill what lies between heaven and earth. The prayer is light, charity is a proof, patience is brightness, and the Qurʾān is a proof for you or against you.
HAD-0024.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0024.sharh: al-Māzirī explains that the statement “aṭ-ṭuhūr is half of Īmān” carries several closely connected meanings. Among them is that purification is a major condition of the prayer, and that the prayer itself was called Īmān in the texts. Thus outward purification becomes a tremendous part of that by which the servant makes his worship valid. At the same time the Ḥadīṯ indicates that the path of the believer comprises purification and refinement: purification of the body from Ḥadaṯ and Naǧāsah, and purification of the inward through Īmān, obedience, and avoidance of evil. The further sentences of the Ḥadīṯ then show the great doors of good: Ḏikr, Ṣalāh, Ṣadaqah, Ṣabr, and Qurʾān; the Qurʾān is thereby either a proof for the person when he follows it, or against him when he neglects it.

HAD-0025.text: The servant is nearest to his Lord while he is prostrating. Therefore increase the supplication in prostration.
HAD-0025.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0025.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the Suǧūd is the state of the servant’s greatest humility, submission, and lowliness before his Lord. The servant places his noblest outward limb, the face, upon the ground and thereby shows complete need of Allah. For this reason this state is especially suited to Duʿāʾ and to hope of acceptance. The instruction to increase supplication in the Suǧūd shows that nearness to Allah is joined to humility, obedience, and sincere asking; the Suǧūd is not merely an outward movement, but a place of worship, supplication, and submission.

HAD-0026.text: The places most beloved to Allah are the mosques, and the places most hateful to Allah are the markets.
HAD-0026.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0026.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the meaning of the Ḥadīṯ concerning the contrast between mosques and markets: mosques are places of worship, prayer, Ḏikr, recitation, gathering upon obedience, and the seeking of knowledge. For this reason they are the places most beloved to Allah. Markets, by contrast, are often places of worldly occupation, loud dispute, false oaths, fraud, quarrel over measure and price, heedlessness, and the mixing of many desires. The Ḥadīṯ does not mean that lawful trade is forbidden in itself; it warns against the predominant condition of the markets and points to the merit of the places in which obedience to Allah visibly stands at the center.

HAD-0027.text: The congregational prayer surpasses the prayer of the individual by twenty-seven degrees.
HAD-0027.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0027.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that this Ḥadīṯ shows the great merit of prayer in congregation over the prayer of the individual. The twenty-seven degrees mentioned are an increase of reward and a raising of rank, because several meanings come together in the congregational prayer: the visible establishment of the prayer, the coming together of the Muslims, mutual reminder, order behind the Imām, an increase of steps to the mosque, and the open appearance of the Šaʿīrah. The Ḥadīṯ is therefore a strong encouragement not to perform the obligatory prayer alone without an excuse, but to seek the congregation and not to belittle its merit.

HAD-0028.text: The two units of prayer before the morning prayer are better than the world and all that is in it.
HAD-0028.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0028.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the merit of the two Rakʿah before Faǧr as an indication of the tremendous standing of this Sunnah. Its reward and its lasting benefit with Allah are better than the passing world and all that is desired in it. What is meant is not that the outward act would be greater in quantity than the world, but that the value in the Hereafter of obedience surpasses the whole world. In this lies an encouragement not to belittle the Sunnah of Faǧr, to perform it briefly and constantly, and to open the beginning of the day with obedience and nearness to Allah.

HAD-0029.text: Allah has ninety-nine names, one hundred minus one. Whoever encompasses them will enter Paradise.
HAD-0029.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0029.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that “aḥṣāhā” comprises more than mere counting with the tongue. It includes preserving the names of Allah, believing in them, understanding their meanings as far as possible, calling upon Allah by them, and acting according to what these names require of reverence, hope, love, fear, and obedience. The Ḥadīṯ points to the special merit of these ninety-nine names and to the fact that encompassing them is a path to Paradise. This elevates their rank without meaning that Allah would have no further names which He has preserved in His knowledge.

HAD-0030.text: Fasting is a shield. When one of you is fasting, he should neither speak indecently nor behave foolishly. If someone fights him or insults him, he should say: “I am fasting.”
HAD-0030.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0030.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that fasting is a shield because it protects the person from sins and from the Fire when it is joined to the guarding of the limbs. For this reason the warning against indecent speech, foolish behavior, quarrel, and insult follows directly. The fasting person should not only leave food and drink, but also restrain his tongue, his conduct, and his reaction to provocation. The statement “I am fasting” reminds him himself and the other that the state of fasting should hold him back from quarrel, retaliation, and low speech.

HAD-0031.text: Whoever fasts Ramaḍān out of faith and in hope of Allah’s reward, his past sins will be forgiven.
HAD-0031.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0031.sharh: The earliest layer of explanation here lies in al-Buḫārī’s chapter arrangement: he places the fasting of Ramaḍān out of Īmān and Iḥtisāb expressly under Kitāb al-Īmān. He thereby shows that fasting is not merely an outward habit, but an act of Īmān when it is performed out of affirmation of the truth, obedience to Allah, and hope for His reward. Iḥtisāb means not doing the act out of reputation, imitation, or mere routine, but seeking the reward with Allah. The forgiveness of past sins is bound to this inward foundation: fasting with Īmān, sincerity, and expectation of the reward.

HAD-0032.text: One ʿUmrah until the next ʿUmrah is an expiation for what lies between them, and for an accepted pilgrimage there is no reward other than Paradise.
HAD-0032.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0032.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the merit of the ʿUmrah and of the Ḥaǧǧ mabrūr. The ʿUmrah until the next ʿUmrah is an expiation for what lies between them, insofar as the servant observes the rights of Allah and keeps away from that which destroys the acceptance of his act. The Ḥaǧǧ mabrūr is the righteous, accepted Ḥaǧǧ: it is performed with sincerity, without Riyāʾ, without blameworthy action, with lawful earning, good performance of the rites, and a return to better obedience. That its reward is only Paradise shows its tremendous rank when its conditions and its inward meaning are fulfilled.

HAD-0033.text: Protect yourselves from the Fire, even if it is only with half a date.
HAD-0033.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0033.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ encourages not to despise good deeds because of their small amount. Even half a date can, when it is given sincerely, be a cause of protection from the Fire. The meaning is: the servant should use every attainable door of good, even if it appears small, for Allah does not let sincere charity go to waste. The Ḥadīṯ opens hope especially for the poor, because protection from the Fire is not sought only through great expenditure, but also through what a person possesses and can give honestly.

HAD-0034.text: The upper hand is better than the lower hand.
HAD-0034.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0034.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the upper hand means the hand that gives and spends, while the lower hand is the hand that takes or asks. The Ḥadīṯ shows the merit of giving over taking and trains the Muslim in contentment, dignity, and independence from people. At the same time it indicates that Ṣadaqah and support should take place according to ability: one begins with those for whom one is responsible, and one gives from a condition that does not lead to oneself or one’s own family being harmfully neglected. The merit therefore lies in sincere generosity without humiliating begging.

HAD-0035.text: Whoever builds a mosque for Allah, Allah builds for him something of the same kind in Paradise.
HAD-0035.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0035.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the tremendous reward is bound to the intention: “for Allah.” Whoever builds a mosque so that Allah is worshiped in it, His name is mentioned, the prayer is performed, and knowledge is spread, to him the Ḥadīṯ promises a house in Paradise. The meaning is not merely the raising of walls, but the support of a place of obedience. For this reason the act is raised by sincerity and endangered by Riyāʾ, the seeking of fame, or worldly boasting. The Ḥadīṯ shows the merit of caring for places of worship when this takes place with a pure intention and lawful means.

HAD-0036.text: The best among you are those who learn the Qurʾān and teach it.
HAD-0036.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0036.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that this Ḥadīṯ shows the special merit of those who learn the Qurʾān and teach it. In them two kinds of good come together: they benefit themselves through learning, preserving, reciting, and understanding the Book of Allah, and they benefit others by passing on the Qurʾān. For this reason the one who does not stop at his own learning, but conveys what he has learned with sincerity, is especially excellent. The Ḥadīṯ also indicates that the best occupation with the Qurʾān is not merely voice or outward recitation, but learning, teaching, and holding to what Allah has revealed.

HAD-0037.text: The one who recites the Qurʾān skillfully is with the noble and righteous scribes. Whoever recites the Qurʾān and has difficulty in doing so receives two rewards.
HAD-0037.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0037.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the one who recites the Qurʾān skillfully, securely, and carefully is mentioned with the noble righteous scribes, because he is distinguished in the service of the Qurʾān by mastery, preservation, and good recitation. The one who has difficulty in reciting is not belittled; rather he receives two rewards: one for the recitation itself and one for the effort, patience, and exertion that he bears in it. The Ḥadīṯ thereby joins a high rank for mastery with comfort and encouragement for the learner who holds to the Qurʾān despite difficulty.

HAD-0038.text: Recite the Qurʾān, for on the Day of Resurrection it will come as an intercessor for its companions.
HAD-0038.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0038.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the Qurʾān intercedes on the Day of Resurrection for its companions. By its companions are not meant merely people who possess it outwardly, but those who recite it, preserve it, honor it, and act according to its guidance. The Ḥadīṯ therefore encourages constant recitation of the Qurʾān and indicates that the relationship to the Qurʾān becomes visible in the Hereafter: whoever accompanies it in this world, for him it will be, by Allah’s permission, a benefit and an intercession on the Day of Resurrection.

HAD-0040.text: Whoever travels a path on which he seeks knowledge, Allah thereby makes easy for him a path to Paradise.
HAD-0040.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0040.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that traveling a path toward knowledge comprises both the actual path to gatherings of knowledge and the religious path of learning, understanding, and acting. Allah thereby makes easy for the seeker of knowledge a path to Paradise, because beneficial knowledge leads to sound ʿAqīdah, valid worship, avoidance of the forbidden, and sincere fear of Allah. The Ḥadīṯ therefore shows the rank of knowledge: it is not mere information, but a means by which Allah makes easy for the servant obedience, guidance, and the path to the Hereafter.

HAD-0041.text: Convey from me, even if it is only a single verse. But whoever deliberately lies about me, let him take his place in the Fire.
HAD-0041.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0041.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the urging, “Convey from me, even if it is only a single verse,” contains the encouragement to pass on what one knows with certainty from the Prophet ﷺ. Whoever knows something of the Qurʾān, the Sunnah, or securely transmitted guidance should not conceal it, but pass it on according to his knowledge. At the same time the Ḥadīṯ joins this permission and this encouragement to a grave warning: transmission must not become unchecked attribution or invention. Whoever deliberately lies about the Prophet ﷺ commits a tremendous sin and is threatened with the Fire. Thus the Ḥadīṯ protects at once the spread of knowledge and the purity of transmission.

HAD-0062.text: The believer is to the believer like a building whose parts strengthen one another.
HAD-0062.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0062.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ describes the mutual support of the believers. Just as a building does not stand by separate individual stones, but by parts that hold and strengthen one another, so the believer should strengthen his brother in what is good, protect him from harm, help him, and compensate for his weakness. The Ḥadīṯ calls for cooperation, assistance, mercy, and protection of the community. The individual believer does not remain isolated thereby, but becomes part of a firm structure of Īmān and brotherhood.

HAD-0063.text: You see the believers, in their mercy, their mutual love, and their compassion, like a single body: when one limb suffers, the whole body responds with sleeplessness and fever.
HAD-0063.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0063.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ obliges the believers to mutual mercy, love, and compassion. The parable of the one body shows that the harm of a believer should not be met with indifference: just as the whole body responds to the pain of one limb with fever and sleeplessness, so the believers should respond to the suffering, need, and distress of their brothers. The Ḥadīṯ calls for help, sympathy, concern, and protection of the community, and makes clear that complete brotherhood is more than outward belonging.

HAD-0064.text: The one whose neighbor is not safe from his harm will not enter Paradise.
HAD-0064.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0064.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the gravity of harm toward the neighbor. Whoever does not let his neighbor be safe from his tongue, his hand, his cunning, his annoyance, or repeated wrongdoing violates a right that is especially emphasized. The threat “he will not enter Paradise” is a severe warning against this grave sin and against the loss of complete security and complete reward; it shows that good conduct toward the neighbor is not mere courtesy, but a religious right.

HAD-0065.text: Whoever carries in his heart even the weight of a speck of pride will not enter Paradise.
HAD-0065.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0065.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the Ḥadīṯ does not locate pride in well-kept clothing or a handsome appearance; for the Prophet ﷺ himself explains Kibr as rejecting the truth and despising people. The threat is directed against an inner state that keeps the servant from accepting the truth and leads him to look down on others. Through this, Kibr becomes a dangerous disease of the heart, because it corrupts both the relationship to Allah’s truth and the conduct toward Allah’s servants.

HAD-0066.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0066.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the praised modesty is a quality that restrains a person from what is ugly and leads him to noble conduct, obedience, and the safeguarding of rights. For this reason it brings only good. What is meant is not a weakness by which someone omits the truth, duty, knowledge, or justified speech. Praiseworthy Ḥayāʾ is rather a religious restraint before sin and shame before Allah, which beautifies character and protects a person from coarse conduct.

HAD-0067.text: Among the best of you are those with the best character.
HAD-0067.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0067.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the high rank of good character. The best of people are distinguished not only by outward claim or status, but by noble conduct, truthfulness, gentleness, patience, forbearance, good speech, and the safeguarding of the rights of others. Good character gathers many doors of obedience, because it leads the servant, in his dealings with Allah’s creatures, to justice, mildness, and protection from harm.

HAD-0068.text: On every day on which the sun rises, a charitable deed is due for every joint of the human being: to reconcile justly between two people is a charitable deed; to help someone with his mount is a charitable deed; a good word is a charitable deed; every step toward the prayer is a charitable deed; and to remove an obstacle from the path is a charitable deed.
HAD-0068.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0068.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that Ṣadaqah in this Ḥadīṯ is broadly understood and does not mean only a gift of money. The human being has each day numerous gifts of Allah in his body, and he can show gratitude for them through many kinds of good actions: just reconciliation, help in mounting or carrying, a good word, steps toward the prayer, and removing harm from the path. The Ḥadīṯ thereby opens many doors of good for every person, even if he possesses no wealth.

HAD-0069.text: Every good deed is a charitable deed.
HAD-0069.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0069.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that Maʿrūf includes every action that is recognized in the religion as good and that brings a person benefit or keeps harm away from him. Therefore not only money is Ṣadaqah, but also good speech, help, guidance, consolation, reconciliation, visiting, and every other form of good. The Ḥadīṯ broadens the understanding of the charitable deed, so that no one thinks the door of Ṣadaqah is closed to him merely because he possesses no wealth.

HAD-0070.text: Do not belittle any good deed, even if it is only that you meet your brother with a kindly face.
HAD-0070.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0070.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the Ḥadīṯ guides one not to belittle any door of good. A kindly face when meeting one’s brother belongs to Maʿrūf, because it opens the heart and the relationship, strengthens love, and pushes coarseness back. The benefit of an action is not measured only by its outward size; a small action can weigh heavily when there is sincerity, a good moment, and benefit for the other. Therefore the believer should also cultivate forms of good that seem slight.

HAD-0071.text: Allah has prescribed goodness in every matter. When you kill, kill in a good manner; and when you slaughter, slaughter in a good manner. One of you should sharpen his blade and give the animal relief.
HAD-0071.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0071.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that Iḥsān in every matter means carrying out the action according to the Šarīʿah, with precision, justice, and the avoidance of unnecessary harshness. Even in killing or slaughter, where the action is in itself grave, the servant remains obliged to avoid unnecessary suffering, to sharpen the blade, and not to torment the animal. The Ḥadīṯ thereby shows that mercy and good execution are not limited to pleasant situations, but also apply where the Šarīʿah permits or commands a serious action.

HAD-0072.text: A charitable gift does not diminish wealth. Allah only increases a servant in honor through forgiveness, and no one humbles himself for Allah without Allah raising him.
HAD-0072.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0072.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that Ṣadaqah does not diminish wealth in the decisive sense: the outward decrease is offset by Barakah, replacement, and reward in the hereafter. Likewise, forgiveness does not mean humiliation; rather, Allah raises thereby the honor of the servant, because he masters his soul and forgoes for the sake of Allah. Whoever humbles himself for Allah is raised by Allah; true elevation lies not in pride, but in obedience, sincerity, and refraining from self-exaltation.

HAD-0073.text: Whoever raises a weapon against us is not of us.
HAD-0073.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0073.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the wording “is not of us” is a very severe warning. Whoever raises a weapon against Muslims tramples the protection, the brotherhood, and the security of the community and opens a door to intimidation, bloodshed, and Fitnah. What is meant is a grave threat and a separation from the complete guidance of the Prophet ﷺ in this conduct; the Ḥadīṯ shows how immense the protection of Muslim life is, and the prohibition of violence against the community.

HAD-0074.text: Insulting a Muslim is iniquity, and fighting him is Kufr.
HAD-0074.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0074.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the immense gravity of a Muslim’s right. Insulting a Muslim is Fisq, because it leads the tongue into iniquity and violation of honor. Fighting him is called Kufr in order to bring out the danger and the resemblance to the actions of the people of Kufr; what is meant is a grave kufr-like act and Kufr dūna Kufr, not automatically the judgment of leaving Islām for every individual perpetrator. The Ḥadīṯ protects the honor, the blood, and the brotherhood of the Muslims.

HAD-0075.text: Do not return after me to being unbelievers, by some of you striking the necks of others.
HAD-0075.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0075.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Prophet ﷺ, with this severe warning, warned the Muslims against killing one another and against falling back into the conduct of the people of Kufr. Striking the necks stands for bloodshed, Fitnah, and the abolition of the protected Muslim brotherhood. The designation with Kufr serves to deter from this immense sin and from its resemblance to the way of the unbelievers; it does not mean that every individual perpetrator is thereby, without examination, automatically taken out of Islām.

HAD-0076.text: Whoever kills a person who stands under a covenant of protection will not smell the fragrance of Paradise, although its fragrance is perceived from a distance of forty years.
HAD-0076.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0076.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that this Ḥadīṯ contains one of the strictest warnings against unjust bloodshed. Whoever kills a Muʿāhad, that is, a person under covenant and protection, without a lawful cause, violates a protection that the Šarīʿah recognizes. The threat of not smelling the fragrance of Paradise shows the immense gravity of this sin and that protected blood must not be touched lightly. The Ḥadīṯ excludes deception, breach of covenant, and unjust killing.

HAD-0077.text: Whoever introduces into this matter of ours something that does not belong to it, his action is rejected.
HAD-0077.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0077.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that this Ḥadīṯ is a basic measure for accepting and rejecting actions. What is introduced into the matter of the Prophet ﷺ and does not belong to it is rejected, because religion is accepted only through what agrees with his guidance. The Ḥadīṯ covers innovations in belief, worship, and judgments, insofar as they have no valid origin in the Šarīʿah. It protects the religion from people attributing to it what Allah and His Messenger ﷺ have not legitimized.

HAD-0078.text: The world is the prison of the believer and the paradise of the unbeliever.
HAD-0078.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0078.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the world is like a prison for the believer, because he is bound by commands, prohibitions, patience, responsibility, and restraint from desires. At the same time, compared with what Allah has prepared for him in the hereafter, it is narrow and slight. For the unbeliever, compared with what awaits him in the hereafter, it is like a paradise, even if he experiences suffering in it. The Ḥadīṯ therefore teaches Zuhd, patience, and the right relation between the passing world and the lasting hereafter.

HAD-0079.text: How amazing is the affair of the believer! His whole affair is good for him, and that applies only to the believer: if something pleasing befalls him, he is grateful and it is good for him; if something hard befalls him, he is patient and it is good for him. For the believer there is good in both states.
HAD-0079.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0079.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that this distinction belongs to the believer in its full meaning only, because he turns both states into worship: if joy befalls him, he recognizes the gift of Allah and gives thanks; thereby the joy becomes good and reward. If hardship befalls him, he holds to patience and seeks the reward of Allah; thereby the trial also becomes good. The Ḥadīṯ teaches that the measure is not only the outward state, but how the heart and the action of the believer respond to it.

HAD-0080.text: Allah is pleased with a servant when he eats a meal and praises Him for it, or drinks a drink and praises Him for it.
HAD-0080.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0080.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the great rank of Ḥamd after everyday gifts. Eating and drinking are continuing favors of Allah, and by praise the servant acknowledges that the gift comes from Allah and not from his own independence. That Allah is pleased with this praise shows the breadth of His grace: a simple, regularly recurring action becomes, through thanks and acknowledgment, an occasion of His pleasure. The Ḥadīṯ trains one not to use the small and the great gifts thoughtlessly.

HAD-0081.text: Allah rejoices over the repentance of His servant more than one of you rejoices when he finds his lost mount again in a desolate wilderness.
HAD-0081.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0081.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the immense acceptance of Tawbah and the breadth of the mercy of Allah. The image of the man in the wilderness who finds his lost mount again makes clear a joy after the utmost need and hopelessness; by this the greatness of Tawbah is brought near to the servant. The joy of Allah is understood in the manner that befits His majesty, without equating it with the joy of creatures. The Ḥadīṯ calls one not to despair of repentance, but to return quickly to Allah.

HAD-0156.text: If the people knew what reward lies in the call to prayer and in the first row, and found no other way than to draw lots for it, they would draw lots for it. If they knew what lies in coming early to the prayer, they would vie for it.
HAD-0156.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0156.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the immense merit of the Aḏān, the first row, and coming early to the prayer. The mention of drawing lots means: if the people knew the hidden reward of these deeds, they would contend for them even amid competition and equal standing. The Ḥadīṯ urges that the visible means to the prayer not be belittled, for the Aḏān, the first row, and early appearance are signs of eagerness, nearness to the congregation, and going ahead toward obedience.

HAD-0157.text: The best rows of the men are the first, and the worst are the last. The best rows of the women are the last, and the worst are the first.
HAD-0157.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0157.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the first rows of the men are especially distinguished because of their nearness to the Imām, their precedence in the prayer, and their going ahead toward obedience. For the women, the merit of the rear rows is mentioned because they are farther from the men, and thereby protection, modesty, and distance from Fitnah are more strongly preserved. The Ḥadīṯ thus orders the rows not merely by place, but according to meaning: nearness to the good where it is fitting, and distance where protection and modesty are stronger.

HAD-0158.text: The best day on which the sun rises is Friday. On it Ādam was created, on it he was admitted into Paradise, and on it he was brought out of it; and the Hour will occur only on a Friday.
HAD-0158.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0158.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that Friday is distinguished by several immense events: the creation of Ādam, his entry into Paradise, his being brought out of it, and the future coming of the Hour. Thereby the special rank of this day becomes visible. The Ḥadīṯ calls for Friday not to be treated like ordinary days, but for its merit to be recognized through prayer, Ḏikr, preparation, and honoring the day of Ǧumuʿah.

HAD-0159.text: The five prayers, from one Friday to the next, and from one Ramaḍān to the next are an expiation for what lies between them, when the major sins are avoided.
HAD-0159.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0159.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the five prayers, the Ǧumuʿah, and Ramaḍān belong to the regular causes of the forgiveness of sins. The expiation refers to the lesser sins that occur between them, so long as the major sins are avoided. The Ḥadīṯ therefore joins hope with vigilance: the servant should maintain the recurring duties, and at the same time not suppose that major sins would simply be placed on the same level without repentance and avoidance.

HAD-0160.text: Whoever fasts Ramaḍān and follows it with six days of Šawwāl, for him it is like the fasting of an entire year.
HAD-0160.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0160.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the merit of following the fast of Ramaḍān with six days of Šawwāl. The meaning of the reward of a year lies in the multiplication of the good deed: Ramaḍān corresponds to the reward of ten months, and six days, with a tenfold multiplication, correspond to about two months. Thus the continuation of obedience after Ramaḍān is recommended, without equating Ramaḍān itself with voluntary fasting.

HAD-0161.text: Take the meal before dawn, for in it lies blessing.
HAD-0161.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0161.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Suḥūr is recommended because of the Barakah that lies in it. Part of this Barakah is that the fasting person is strengthened, remains more readily able to obey, and follows the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ. The Suḥūr also distinguishes the Islamic fast from the practice of other communities. The exhortation shows recommendation and strong encouragement, not that the Suḥūr would be a condition for the validity of the fast.

HAD-0162.text: The people will remain in good so long as they hasten the breaking of the fast.
HAD-0162.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0162.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that hastening the breaking of the fast after the night has securely set in belongs to the Sunnah. In it lies good, because the servant observes the limit of Allah, accepts ease, and does not burden himself through excessive strictness. The Ḥadīṯ shows that the good of the Ummah is also recognizable in that it follows the Sunnah and does not, out of a claim to piety, delay what the Prophet ﷺ recommended hastening.

HAD-0163.text: Whoever performs the pilgrimage for the sake of Allah and therein neither speaks indecently nor sins returns like on the day his mother gave birth to him.
HAD-0163.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0163.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the immense merit of a Ḥaǧǧ that is performed for Allah and remains free of Rafath and Fisq. Rafath comprises indecent speech and what contradicts the state of Iḥrām; Fisq comprises sins and transgressions. Whoever preserves his Ḥaǧǧ in this way receives a comprehensive promise of forgiveness, until he returns as on the day of his birth. The Ḥadīṯ thereby joins the outward pilgrimage act with purity of tongue, conduct, and intention.

HAD-0164.text: I had forbidden you to visit the graves. Now visit them, for they remind of the Hereafter.
HAD-0164.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0164.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the earlier prohibition of visiting graves was lifted. Visiting graves is permitted when it takes place within the bounds of the Sunnah and reminds the servant of death, the Āḫirah, transience, and preparation for Allah. The Ḥadīṯ directs the purpose of the visit away from forbidden customs and toward admonition, Duʿāʾ for the deceased, and reflection upon the Hereafter.

HAD-0165.text: When a person dies, his deeds come to an end except in three cases: an ongoing charity, knowledge from which benefit is drawn, or a righteous child who offers supplication for him.
HAD-0165.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0165.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that a person's own deeds in principle come to an end with his death. Excepted are causes that he established during his lifetime and whose benefit continues: an ongoing charity, beneficial knowledge, and a righteous child who makes Duʿāʾ for him. The Ḥadīṯ shows the value of lasting benefit, and that the servant should attend not only to immediate deeds, but to works whose benefit continues after his death.

HAD-0166.text: Whoever follows a funeral until the funeral prayer is performed receives one Qīrāṭ; whoever remains until the burial is completed receives two. Each Qīrāṭ is like an immense mountain.
HAD-0166.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0166.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the great reward for accompanying a Ǧanāzah. Whoever stays until the funeral prayer receives one Qīrāṭ; whoever additionally stays until the burial receives two. The description of each Qīrāṭ as an immense mountain makes the rank of this deed visible: taking part in the funeral prayer, Duʿāʾ for the deceased, accompanying the Muslims, and remembrance of death are joined with great reward.

HAD-0167.text: Hasten with the funeral. If the deceased is righteous, you bring him to something good; if he is otherwise, you lay something bad down from your shoulders.
HAD-0167.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0167.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ǧanāzah should not be delayed without cause. If the deceased is righteous, he is thereby hastened to good and to what Allah has prepared for him. If he is otherwise, a heavy burden is laid down from the shoulders of the living. The Ḥadīṯ trains toward dignity, promptness, and the avoidance of unnecessary delay at the burial.

HAD-0168.text: Whomever Allah wills good for, He afflicts with trials.
HAD-0168.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0168.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that trials for the believer need not mean only punishment, but can be a sign of the good of Allah. Through illness, pain, and other trials, sins are erased, the servant is trained in patience, and his rank can be raised. The Ḥadīṯ directs the gaze toward meeting trials with Ṣabr, hope of reward, and a good opinion of Allah.

HAD-0169.text: In black cumin lies a cure for every disease except death.
HAD-0169.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0169.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ confirms the benefit of the black seed as a remedy, while death is expressly excepted. The benefit occurs by the decree of Allah and with suitable use; remedies do not act by themselves, but as causes that Allah has created. The Ḥadīṯ strengthens the permission to take medical causes without abandoning trust in Allah.

HAD-0170.text: Show me your Ruqyah formulas. There is nothing objectionable in a Ruqyah so long as it contains no Širk.
HAD-0170.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0170.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that Ruqyah is permitted when it is free of Širk, forbidden meanings, and unclear invocation of other than Allah. The standard is that the wording is permitted and that the servant knows that healing comes only from Allah. The Ḥadīṯ thus preserves permitted Ruqyah as a cause and excludes every form that violates Tawḥīd.

HAD-0172.text: When Allah loves a servant, He calls Ǧibrīl and says that He loves this servant. Then Ǧibrīl loves him and calls out to the inhabitants of heaven to love him. Thereafter acceptance is granted to him on earth.
HAD-0172.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0172.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the love of Allah for a servant has consequences in heaven and on earth. When Allah loves a servant, Ǧibrīl loves him, then the angels love him, and acceptance is given to him among the people of the earth. This acceptance does not mean mere worldly popularity, but a love and recognition that Allah sets among the people of Īmān. The Ḥadīṯ shows the rank of obedience, sincerity, and the good pleasure of Allah.

HAD-0173.text: Whoever severs the ties of kinship will not enter Paradise.
HAD-0173.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0173.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that severing kinship is a grave sin, because it breaks rights, destroys mercy, and violates the bond whose maintenance Allah has commanded. The threat "will not enter Paradise" shows the gravity of this deed and warns against cutting kinship rights out of anger, pride, or worldly reasons. The Ḥadīṯ stands together with the texts that mention Ṣilat ar-Raḥim as a cause of Barakah and the good pleasure of Allah.

HAD-0174.text: Whoever exerts himself for a widow or a needy person is like the one who strives in the path of Allah, or like someone who prays at night and fasts by day.
HAD-0174.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0174.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that exerting oneself for widows and the needy belongs to the great doors of good. Whoever cares for them, eases their situation, and protects their rights receives a reward that is compared with striving in the path of Allah and with constant prayer and fasting. The Ḥadīṯ shows that social service, provision for the weak, and mercy toward the needy belong to the immense deeds of the Dīn.

HAD-0175.text: On Mondays and Thursdays the gates of Paradise are opened, and every servant who associates nothing with Allah is forgiven, except two people between whom there is enmity, until they reconcile.
HAD-0175.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0175.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the danger of enmity, rancor, and mutual avoidance among Muslims. Although the door of forgiveness is opened wide, two people between whom there is enmity are held back until they reconcile. This makes clear that a pure heart, reconciliation, and the removal of Šaḥnāʾ belong to the important causes of forgiveness, and that personal enmity can harm the servant severely.

HAD-0176.text: Shall I tell you the words most beloved to Allah? The words most beloved to Allah are: Glorified is Allah, and praise belongs to Him.
HAD-0176.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0176.sharh: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the merit of this formula by the fact that it joins Tasbīḥ and Ḥamd. Tasbīḥ means to declare Allah free of every deficiency, and Ḥamd means to praise Him for His perfection, favor, and dominion. Therefore "subḥān Allāh wa-bi-ḥamdih" belongs to the words most beloved to Allah: it is short upon the tongue, yet immense in meaning, and it leads the servant to constant Ḏikr.

HAD-0586.text: Learn knowledge, for learning it for the sake of Allah is fear of Allah.
HAD-0586.narrator: It is reported from Muʿāḏ ibn Ǧabal رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0586.speaker: He said:

HAD-0587.text: The Qurʾān will be a reward for you or a proof against you.
HAD-0587.narrator: It is reported from Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0587.speaker: He said:

HAD-0588.text: Whoever speaks about what does not concern him misses much of what does concern him.
HAD-0588.narrator: It is reported from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-0588.speaker: He said:

HAD-0589.text: Knowledge is abundant and life is short; take from knowledge what sets your religion upright.
HAD-0589.narrator: It is reported from Salmān al-Fārisī رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0589.speaker: He said:

HAD-0590.text: Whoever wishes to adhere to a Sunnah should adhere to the Sunnah of those who have already died.
HAD-0590.narrator: It is reported from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0590.speaker: He said:

HAD-0591.text: This knowledge is religion; so look from whom you take your religion.
HAD-0591.narrator: It is reported from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn رحمه الله:
HAD-0591.speaker: He said:

HAD-0592.text: The Sunnah with Allah lies between the one who goes to excess and the one who falls short; so be patient upon it.
HAD-0592.narrator: It is reported from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī رحمه الله:
HAD-0592.speaker: He said:

HAD-0593.text: Hold fast to the Āṯār of the Salaf, even if the people reject you.
HAD-0593.narrator: It is reported from al-Awzāʿī رحمه الله:
HAD-0593.speaker: He said:

HAD-0594.text: Be patient upon the Sunnah, and stop where the people before you stopped.
HAD-0594.narrator: It is reported from al-Awzāʿī رحمه الله:
HAD-0594.speaker: He said:

HAD-0595.text: Bidʿah is dearer to Iblīs than sin, for one repents from sin, while one rarely repents from Bidʿah.
HAD-0595.narrator: It is reported from Sufyān aṯ-Ṯawrī رحمه الله:
HAD-0595.speaker: He said:

HAD-0596.text: If it reaches you that a man in the East is upon the Sunnah, then send him the Salām, for the people of the Sunnah have become few.
HAD-0596.narrator: It is reported from Sufyān aṯ-Ṯawrī رحمه الله:
HAD-0596.speaker: He said:

HAD-0597.text: Follow the paths of guidance; the small number of those who walk them does not harm you.
HAD-0597.narrator: It is reported from al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ رحمه الله:
HAD-0597.speaker: He said:

HAD-0598.text: Whoever honors a follower of Bidʿah has helped to tear down Islam.
HAD-0598.narrator: It is reported from al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ رحمه الله:
HAD-0598.speaker: He said:

HAD-0599.text: A person of Bidʿah does not increase in effort except that he draws further away from Allah.
HAD-0599.narrator: It is reported from Ayyūb as-Saḫtiyānī رحمه الله:
HAD-0599.speaker: He said:

HAD-0600.text: The chain of transmission belongs to the religion; without the Isnād everyone would say what he wishes.
HAD-0600.narrator: It is reported from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mubārak رحمه الله:
HAD-0600.speaker: He said:

HAD-0601.text: Whoever holds the scholars in low regard loses his Hereafter.
HAD-0601.narrator: It is reported from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mubārak رحمه الله:
HAD-0601.speaker: He said:

HAD-0602.text: From everyone one takes and one rejects, except from the inhabitant of this grave.
HAD-0602.narrator: It is reported from Mālik ibn Anas رحمه الله:
HAD-0602.speaker: He said:

HAD-0603.text: What was not religion then is not religion today.
HAD-0603.narrator: It is reported from Mālik ibn Anas رحمه الله:
HAD-0603.speaker: He said:

HAD-0604.text: If the Ḥadīṯ is authentic, then that is my Madhhab.
HAD-0604.narrator: It is reported from aš-Šāfiʿī رحمه الله:
HAD-0604.speaker: He said:

HAD-0605.text: The foundations of the Sunnah with us are holding fast to that upon which the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were.
HAD-0605.narrator: It is reported from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal رحمه الله:
HAD-0605.speaker: He said:

HAD-0646.text: Ahl as-Sunnah die and their mention remains; Ahl al-Bidʿah die and their mention passes away.
HAD-0646.narrator: It is transmitted from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal رحمه الله:
HAD-0646.speaker: He said:

HAD-0647.text: Our Madhhab is holding fast to the Qurʾān, to the Sunnah, and to that upon which the Companions were.
HAD-0647.narrator: It is transmitted from Abū Ḥātim ar-Rāzī رحمه الله:
HAD-0647.speaker: He said:

HAD-0648.text: Hold fast to the Sunnah; it will suffice you as it sufficed them.
HAD-0648.narrator: It is transmitted from al-Awzāʿī رحمه الله:
HAD-0648.speaker: He said:

HAD-0649.text: The Sunnah is like the ark of Nūḥ: whoever boards it is saved.
HAD-0649.narrator: It is transmitted from Mālik ibn Anas رحمه الله:
HAD-0649.speaker: He said:

HAD-0650.text: Be patient upon the Sunnah and stop where the people before you stopped.
HAD-0650.narrator: It is transmitted from al-Awzāʿī رحمه الله:
HAD-0650.speaker: He said:

HAD-0651.text: Deeds are only according to intentions, and each person has only what he intended.
HAD-0651.narrator: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0651.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0652.text: The lawful is clear and the forbidden is clear; between them lie doubtful matters.
HAD-0652.narrator: an-Nuʿmān ibn Bašīr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0652.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0653.narrator: Tamīm ad-Dārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0653.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0654.text: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or remain silent.
HAD-0654.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0654.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0655.text: The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe.
HAD-0655.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0655.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0656.text: None of you believes completely until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
HAD-0656.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0656.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0657.text: A strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than a weak one; in both there is good.
HAD-0657.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0657.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0658.text: A person should leave what does not concern him; that belongs to good Islām.
HAD-0658.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0658.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0659.text: Your smile in the face of your brother is a charity.
HAD-0659.narrator: Abū Dharr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0659.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0660.text: Purity is a part of Īmān.
HAD-0660.narrator: Abū Mālik al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0660.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0661.text: A good word is a charity.
HAD-0661.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0661.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0662.text: Whoever removes a distress from a believer, Allah removes from him a distress on the Day of Resurrection.
HAD-0662.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0662.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0663.text: Whoever seeks a path in order to acquire knowledge, Allah makes easy for him a path to Paradise.
HAD-0663.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0663.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0664.text: The strong one is not the wrestler, but the one who controls himself when angry.
HAD-0664.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0664.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0665.text: Allah does not look at your bodies and forms, but at your hearts and deeds.
HAD-0665.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0665.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0686.text: Carry knowledge with calm, dignity, and gentleness.
HAD-0686.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-0686.speaker: He said:

HAD-0687.text: You will not be knowledgeable until you learn, and you will not have learned until you act.
HAD-0687.narrator: It is transmitted from Abū ad-Dardāʾ رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0687.speaker: He said:

HAD-0688.text: The truth is ancient; the truth abrogates nothing except falsehood.
HAD-0688.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0688.speaker: He said:

HAD-0689.text: A person's worth lies in what he masters well of knowledge.
HAD-0689.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0689.speaker: He said:

HAD-0690.text: These hearts are vessels; fill them with the Qurʾān and the Sunnah.
HAD-0690.narrator: It is transmitted from Ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0690.speaker: He said:

HAD-0691.text: The believer joins Iḥsān with fear; the hypocrite joins wrongdoing with security.
HAD-0691.narrator: It is transmitted from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī رحمه الله:
HAD-0691.speaker: He said:

HAD-0692.text: This knowledge is religion; so see from whom you take your religion.
HAD-0692.narrator: It is transmitted from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn رحمه الله:
HAD-0692.speaker: He said:

HAD-0693.text: Do not seek knowledge so that you may be honored, but so that you fear Allah.
HAD-0693.narrator: It is transmitted from Sufyān aṯ-Ṯawrī رحمه الله:
HAD-0693.speaker: He said:

HAD-0694.text: Be patient upon the Sunnah, and stop where the people before you stopped.
HAD-0694.narrator: It is transmitted from al-Awzāʿī رحمه الله:
HAD-0694.speaker: He said:

HAD-0695.text: Nothing will set right the latter part of this Ummah except that which set right its beginning.
HAD-0695.narrator: It is transmitted from Mālik ibn Anas رحمه الله:
HAD-0695.speaker: He said:

HAD-0696.text: The foundation of the Sunnah is holding fast to what the Companions were upon, and avoiding Bidʿah.
HAD-0696.narrator: It is transmitted from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal رحمه الله:
HAD-0696.speaker: He said:

HAD-0697.text: If a deed is sincere but not correct, it is not accepted.
HAD-0697.narrator: It is transmitted from al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ رحمه الله:
HAD-0697.speaker: He said:

HAD-0698.text: They used to learn how they acted, not only how they spoke.
HAD-0698.narrator: It is transmitted from Ibrāhīm an-Naḫaʿī رحمه الله:
HAD-0698.speaker: He said:

HAD-0699.text: Stop where the people stopped; they stood upon knowledge.
HAD-0699.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz رحمه الله:
HAD-0699.speaker: He said:

HAD-0700.text: Islām is Sunnah, and the Sunnah is Islām.
HAD-0700.narrator: It is transmitted from al-Barbahārī رحمه الله:
HAD-0700.speaker: He said:

HAD-0701.text: Hold to the Āṯār; whoever holds to them is upon salvation.
HAD-0701.narrator: It is transmitted from Sahl ibn ʿAbdillāh رحمه الله:
HAD-0701.speaker: He said:

HAD-0702.text: The people of the Sunnah examine the transmitters and preserve the religion.
HAD-0702.narrator: It is transmitted from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān رحمه الله:
HAD-0702.speaker: He said:

HAD-0703.text: The Isnāds belong to the religion; without Isnāds everyone would say what he wishes.
HAD-0703.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mubārak رحمه الله:
HAD-0703.speaker: He said:

HAD-0704.text: Hold to knowledge before it is lost and its bearers pass away.
HAD-0704.narrator: It is transmitted from Ibn Šihāb az-Zuhrī رحمه الله:
HAD-0704.speaker: He said:

HAD-0705.text: People need knowledge more than food and drink, for it preserves their religion.
HAD-0705.narrator: It is transmitted from al-Layṯ ibn Saʿd رحمه الله:
HAD-0705.speaker: He said:

HAD-0606.text: The Sunnah is not measured by reason; rather, it is followed.
HAD-0606.narrator: It is transmitted from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal رحمه الله:
HAD-0606.speaker: He said:

HAD-0607.text: Know that Islam is the Sunnah and the Sunnah is Islam.
HAD-0607.narrator: It is transmitted from al-Barbahārī رحمه الله:
HAD-0607.speaker: He said:

HAD-0608.text: They used to hate it when a man answered everything he was asked about.
HAD-0608.narrator: It is transmitted from Ibrāhīm an-Naḫaʿī رحمه الله:
HAD-0608.speaker: He said:

HAD-0609.text: Stop where the people stopped, for they stopped with knowledge.
HAD-0609.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz رحمه الله:
HAD-0609.speaker: He said:

HAD-0610.text: Whoever does not know should say: Allah knows better.
HAD-0610.narrator: It is transmitted from Qatādah رحمه الله:
HAD-0610.speaker: He said:

HAD-0611.text: Whoever is humble for Allah, Allah raises him thereby.
HAD-0611.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0611.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0612.text: Allah does not look at your bodies nor at your forms, but at your hearts and your deeds.
HAD-0612.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0612.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0612.sharh: Al-Qurṭubī explains that Allah knows all the outward and inward states of people. The statement that Allah does not look at bodies and form therefore does not deny Allah’s knowledge of appearances; it indicates that bodily features and wealth by themselves are not a basis for special reward. What is decisive is the sincerity of the heart and the deeds that belong to it. The present entry repeats the authentic report of Muslim already commented upon in HAD-0457.

HAD-0613.text: Beware of conjecture, for conjecture is the most lying speech.
HAD-0613.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0613.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0614.text: Do not envy one another, do not outbid one another, and do not hate one another.
HAD-0614.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0614.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0615.text: The believers, in love and mercy, are like a single body.
HAD-0615.narrator: an-Nuʿmān ibn Bašīr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0615.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0616.text: The believer is to the believer like a building; one part strengthens the other.
HAD-0616.narrator: Abū Mūsā رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0616.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0617.text: Whoever takes a path on which he seeks knowledge, Allah thereby makes easy for him a path to Paradise.
HAD-0617.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0617.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0617.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains the excellence of the path of seeking knowledge in the long narration of Abū Hurayrah. The path includes both actual steps toward instruction and reading, memorizing, reflecting, and discussing, insofar as beneficial knowledge is thereby attained. The promise that Allah thereby makes easy a path to Paradise joins the search to the benefit of knowledge for right deeds. The wording is an excerpt from the same narration of Muslim as HAD-0458.

HAD-0618.text: Whomever Allah wills good for, He grants him understanding in the religion.
HAD-0618.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0619.text: Convey from me, even if it is only one verse.
HAD-0619.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-0619.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0620.text: Whoever deliberately lies about me, let him take his place in the Fire.
HAD-0620.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0620.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0621.text: Whoever among you sees something reprehensible, let him change it with his hand.
HAD-0621.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0621.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0622.text: The one who repents before the sun rises from the west, Allah accepts his repentance.
HAD-0622.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0622.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0623.text: Allah rejoices over the repentance of His servant more than one of you rejoices over his lost mount.
HAD-0623.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0623.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0624.text: This world is a prison for the believer and a paradise for the unbeliever.
HAD-0624.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0624.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0624.sharh: An-Nawawī interprets the world as the prison of the believer in comparison with the reward of the hereafter, and as the paradise of the non-believer in comparison with the punishment of the hereafter. The obligations of this world and the voluntary restraint from what is forbidden are limited; the reward of the hereafter remains incomparably greater. From the image it follows neither that every believer must be poor, nor that prosperity in this world would be guaranteed to every non-believer. The entry corresponds to the authentic wording of Muslim in HAD-0459.

HAD-0625.text: A believer is not stung twice from the same hole.
HAD-0625.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0625.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0706.text: Seek help in memorization by abandoning sins.
HAD-0706.narrator: It is transmitted of Wakīʿ ibn al-Ǧarrāḥ رحمه الله:
HAD-0706.speaker: He said:

HAD-0707.text: Knowledge consists of fear of Allah and acting according to the Sunnah.
HAD-0707.narrator: It is transmitted of al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī رحمه الله:
HAD-0707.speaker: He said:

HAD-0708.text: Whoever takes knowledge should begin with humility; arrogance extinguishes benefit.
HAD-0708.narrator: It is transmitted of Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah رحمه الله:
HAD-0708.speaker: He said:

HAD-0709.text: Follow the Āṯār of the Salaf, even if the people reject you.
HAD-0709.narrator: It is transmitted of al-Awzāʿī رحمه الله:
HAD-0709.speaker: He said:

HAD-0710.text: Everyone may be accepted and rejected, except the occupant of this grave ﷺ.
HAD-0710.narrator: It is transmitted of Mālik ibn Anas رحمه الله:
HAD-0710.speaker: He said:

HAD-0711.text: Deeds are only according to intentions, and each person is due only what he intended.
HAD-0711.narrator: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0711.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0712.text: The lawful is clear and the forbidden is clear; between them lie doubtful things.
HAD-0712.narrator: an-Nuʿmān ibn Bašīr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0712.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0713.narrator: Tamīm ad-Dārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0713.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0714.text: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or remain silent.
HAD-0714.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0714.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0715.text: The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe.
HAD-0715.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0715.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0716.text: None of you believes completely until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
HAD-0716.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0716.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0717.text: A strongly believing person is better and more beloved to Allah than a weak one; in both there is good.
HAD-0717.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0717.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0718.text: A person should leave what does not concern him; that belongs to good Islām.
HAD-0718.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0718.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0719.text: Your smile in your brother's face is a charity.
HAD-0719.narrator: Abū Dharr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0719.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0720.text: Purity is a part of Īmān.
