HAD-0720.narrator: Abū Mālik al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0720.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0721.text: A good word is a charity.
HAD-0721.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0721.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0722.text: Whoever removes a distress from a believer, from him Allah removes a distress on the Day of Resurrection.
HAD-0722.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0722.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0723.text: Whoever seeks a path in order to attain knowledge, for him Allah eases a path to Paradise.
HAD-0723.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0723.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0724.text: The strong one is not the wrestler, but the one who controls himself in anger.
HAD-0724.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0724.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0725.text: Allah does not look at your bodies and forms, but at your hearts and deeds.
HAD-0725.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0725.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0626.text: Make use of five before five: your youth before your old age, and your health before your illness.
HAD-0626.narrator: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-0626.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0627.text: Two words are beloved to the All-Merciful, light on the tongue and heavy on the scale.
HAD-0627.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0627.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0628.text: Whoever says: Subḥānallāh wa bi-ḥamdih, one hundred times a day, his sins are forgiven.
HAD-0628.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0628.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0629.text: A person is upon the religion of his close friend; so let everyone look to whom he takes as a friend.
HAD-0629.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0629.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0630.text: Whoever calls to guidance receives a reward equal to that of those who follow him.
HAD-0630.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0630.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0631.text: The one who cares for a widow and a poor person is like the fighter on the path of Allah.
HAD-0631.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0631.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0632.text: I and the guardian of the orphan are in Paradise like these two.
HAD-0632.narrator: Sahl ibn Saʿd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0632.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0633.text: Whoever is not merciful is not shown mercy.
HAD-0633.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0633.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0634.text: Whoever is not merciful to people, Allah is not merciful to him.
HAD-0634.narrator: Ǧarīr ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0634.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0635.text: The All-Merciful shows mercy to the merciful; be merciful to those on the earth, then the One in heaven will be merciful to you.
HAD-0635.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-0635.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0636.text: The believer is the mirror of the believer.
HAD-0636.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0636.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0637.text: Whoever deceives us is not of us.
HAD-0637.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0637.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0638.text: Truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise.
HAD-0638.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0638.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0639.text: Nothing is heavier on the believer’s scale on the Day of Resurrection than good character.
HAD-0639.narrator: Abū ad-Dardāʾ رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0639.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0640.text: Make things easy and do not make them difficult; give glad tidings and do not frighten away.
HAD-0640.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0640.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0641.text: Formerly they did not ask about the Isnād. When the Fitnah occurred, however, they demanded: “Name your transmitters for us!” Thereupon one looked to the people of the Sunnah and accepted their reports; the transmissions of the people of Bidʿah were not accepted.
HAD-0641.narrator: Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn رحمه الله reported:
HAD-0641.speaker: He said:

HAD-0642.text: How many small deeds are made great by the intention, and how many great deeds are made small by the intention.
HAD-0642.narrator: It is transmitted from Ibn al-Mubārak رحمه الله:
HAD-0642.speaker: He said:

HAD-0643.text: The believer is strong toward his own soul; he holds it to account for Allah.
HAD-0643.narrator: It is transmitted from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī رحمه الله:
HAD-0643.speaker: He said:

HAD-0644.text: Whoever worships Allah without knowledge causes more harm than he sets right.
HAD-0644.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz رحمه الله:
HAD-0644.speaker: He said:

HAD-0645.text: Everything I said that an authentic report from the Prophet ﷺ contradicts, the report of the Prophet ﷺ takes precedence.
HAD-0645.narrator: It is transmitted from aš-Šāfiʿī رحمه الله:
HAD-0645.speaker: He said:

HAD-0385.text: Prayer is light for the servant; whoever preserves it preserves a pillar of his religion.
HAD-0385.narrator: It is narrated from Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0385.speaker: He said:

HAD-0386.text: The human being is weak; his strength lies in holding fast to that with which Allah guides him aright.
HAD-0386.narrator: It is narrated from Salman al-Fārisī رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0386.speaker: He said:

HAD-0387.text: Whoever speaks about knowledge should preserve respect for the transmission and for what has been transmitted.
HAD-0387.narrator: It is narrated from Zayd ibn Thābit رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0387.speaker: He said:

HAD-0388.text: We learned the right guidance of the Prophet ﷺ by following his visible Sunnah.
HAD-0388.narrator: It is narrated from Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0388.speaker: He said:

HAD-0389.text: Whoever holds fast to the Athar holds to something certain; whoever prefers opinions opens a door of confusion.
HAD-0389.narrator: It is narrated from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0389.speaker: He said:

HAD-0390.text: The measure of the religion is not custom, but what has been confirmed from the Prophet ﷺ.
HAD-0390.narrator: It is narrated from ʿĀʾishah رضي الله عنها:
HAD-0390.speaker: She said:

HAD-0391.text: This knowledge is religion. So look from whom you take your religion.
HAD-0391.narrator: It is narrated from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn رحمه الله:
HAD-0391.speaker: He said:

HAD-0392.text: Knowledge is of two kinds: knowledge on the tongue and knowledge in the heart; the beneficial one is the knowledge in the heart.
HAD-0392.narrator: It is narrated from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī رحمه الله:
HAD-0392.speaker: He said:

HAD-0393.text: If you report to a person something from the Sunnah and he says, “Leave that, and speak to us from the Qurʾān instead,” then know that he thereby stands upon deviation.
HAD-0393.narrator: It is narrated from Ayyūb as-Saḫtiyānī رحمه الله:
HAD-0393.speaker: He said:

HAD-0394.text: Hold to what has been transmitted from the earlier ones, even if the people reject you; and beware of the opinions of the people, even if they adorn them for you with fine words.
HAD-0394.narrator: It is narrated from al-Awzāʿī رحمه الله:
HAD-0394.speaker: He said:

HAD-0395.text: Sufyān aṯ-Ṯawrī رحمه الله said: “The angels are the guardians of heaven, and the people of Ḥadīṯ are the guardians of the earth.”
HAD-0395.narrator: It is narrated from Sufyān ath-Thawrī رحمه الله:
HAD-0395.speaker: He said:

HAD-0396.text: Imām Mālik رحمه الله is reported with the statement: “The end of this Ummah is improved only by that through which its beginning was improved.” He uttered it, according to the version transmitted by al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, in connection with the question whether the inhabitants of Madīnah should regularly stand at the grave of the Prophet ﷺ for greeting and for longer supplications.
HAD-0396.narrator: It is narrated from Mālik ibn Anas رحمه الله:
HAD-0396.speaker: He said:

HAD-0397.text: Be patient upon the Sunnah, remain standing where the people stood, and speak with that with which they spoke.
HAD-0397.narrator: It is narrated from al-Awzāʿī رحمه الله:
HAD-0397.speaker: He said:

HAD-0398.text: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah رحمه الله said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ is the greatest measure. Things are weighed by his character, his way of life and his right guidance. What agrees with that is truth; what contradicts it is false.”
HAD-0398.narrator: It is narrated from Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah رحمه الله:
HAD-0398.speaker: He said:

HAD-0399.text: Imām aš-Šāfiʿī رحمه الله said in substance: “If you find in my book something that contradicts the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then follow his Sunnah and leave my statement.”
HAD-0399.narrator: It is narrated from aš-Šāfiʿī رحمه الله:
HAD-0399.speaker: He said:

HAD-0400.text: The foundations of the Sunnah with us are holding fast to that upon which the Ṣaḥābah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were.
HAD-0400.narrator: It is narrated from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal رحمه الله:
HAD-0400.speaker: He said:

HAD-0401.text: al-Barbahārī رحمه الله wrote at the beginning of Šarḥ as-Sunnah: “Know: Islam is the Sunnah, and the Sunnah is Islam; neither of the two stands without the other.”
HAD-0401.narrator: It is narrated from al-Barbahārī رحمه الله:
HAD-0401.speaker: He said:

HAD-0402.text: The Isnād belongs to the religion; were it not for the Isnād, everyone would say what he wishes.
HAD-0402.narrator: It is narrated from Ibn al-Mubārak رحمه الله:
HAD-0402.speaker: He said:

HAD-0403.text: Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī رحمه الله said: “The believer joins good deeds with fear [of Allah], while the hypocrite joins bad deeds with a feeling of security.” In connection with this he recited Qurʾān 23:57–60 about those whose hearts are reverent despite their deeds.
HAD-0403.narrator: It is narrated from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī رحمه الله:
HAD-0403.speaker: He said:

HAD-0404.text: From every human being a statement may be accepted or rejected – except from the Prophet ﷺ.
HAD-0404.narrator: It is narrated from Muǧāhid ibn Ǧabr رحمه الله:
HAD-0404.speaker: He said:

HAD-0486.text: It is reported from Ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه: “You are today upon the Fiṭrah. Yet you will introduce innovations, and they will be introduced to you. When you see something newly introduced, hold fast to the first right guidance.”
HAD-0486.narrator: It is reported from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0486.speaker: He said:

HAD-0487.text: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه said on the way to aš-Šām, in substance: We were a humiliated people; Allah gave us honor through Islam. If we seek honor apart from that by which Allah honored us, He humiliates us.
HAD-0487.narrator: It is reported from ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0487.speaker: He said:

HAD-0488.text: Speak to the people according to what they recognize; do you want Allah and His Messenger to be denied?
HAD-0488.narrator: It is reported from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0488.speaker: He said:

HAD-0489.text: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما explained the word Rabbāniyyūn as: composed, discerning people and those learned in Fiqh. Al-Buḫārī adds, separately from that, the explanation that a Rabbānī first teaches people the foundations of knowledge and only afterwards the more difficult questions.
HAD-0489.narrator: It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-0489.speaker: He said:

HAD-0490.text: I have preserved two vessels of knowledge; one I spread, and if I spread the other, this throat would be severed.
HAD-0490.narrator: It is reported from Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0490.speaker: He said:

HAD-0491.text: This knowledge is religion; so look from whom you take your religion.
HAD-0491.narrator: It is reported from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn رحمه الله:
HAD-0491.speaker: He said:

HAD-0492.text: The Sunnah — by the One besides Whom none is worthy of worship — lies between the one who exaggerates and the one who is negligent.
HAD-0492.narrator: It is reported from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī رحمه الله:
HAD-0492.speaker: He said:

HAD-0493.text: Hold to the transmissions of the Salaf, even if the people reject you.
HAD-0493.narrator: It is reported from al-Awzāʿī رحمه الله:
HAD-0493.speaker: He said:

HAD-0494.text: Sufyān aṯ-Ṯawrī رحمه الله said: “Treat the people of the Sunnah well, for they are strangers.”
HAD-0494.narrator: It is reported from Sufyān aṯ-Ṯawrī رحمه الله:
HAD-0494.speaker: He said:

HAD-0495.text: Nothing will improve the end of this Ummah except that which improved its beginning.
HAD-0495.narrator: It is reported from Imām Mālik رحمه الله:
HAD-0495.speaker: He said:

HAD-0496.text: Whoever introduces an innovation into Islam and calls it good thereby claims that Muḥammad ﷺ did not convey the message completely.
HAD-0496.narrator: It is reported from Imām Mālik رحمه الله:
HAD-0496.speaker: He said:

HAD-0497.text: The foundations of the Sunnah with us are: holding fast to that upon which the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were, and following them.
HAD-0497.narrator: It is reported from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal رحمه الله:
HAD-0497.speaker: He said:

HAD-0498.text: The Isnād belongs to the religion; were it not for the Isnād, everyone would say what he wishes.
HAD-0498.narrator: It is reported from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mubārak رحمه الله:
HAD-0498.speaker: He said:

HAD-0499.text: When people in the mosque practiced a new form of collective Ḏikr with pebbles, Ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه said to them: “How many want the good, yet do not attain it!”
HAD-0499.narrator: It is reported of ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0499.speaker: He said to the men in the Ḏikr circles:

HAD-0500.text: This counsel is attributed to al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ رحمه الله: “Follow the paths of right guidance; the small number of those who walk them should not harm you. Avoid the paths of misguidance, and do not let the great number of those who are astray deceive you.”
HAD-0500.narrator: It is reported from al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ رحمه الله:
HAD-0500.speaker: He said:

HAD-0501.text: al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ رحمه الله explained, regarding Qurʾān 67:2, “which of you performs the best deeds”: the most sincere and the most correct. He clarified: sincere means for Allah; correct means according to the Sunnah.
HAD-0501.narrator: It is reported from al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ رحمه الله:
HAD-0501.speaker: He said:

HAD-0502.text: If the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ left something, then leave it yourselves as well.
HAD-0502.narrator: It is reported from Ibrāhīm an-Naḫaʿī رحمه الله:
HAD-0502.speaker: He said:

HAD-0503.text: If you tell a man something of the Sunnah and he says: Leave that aside for us and bring the Qurʾān — then know that he is going astray.
HAD-0503.narrator: It is reported from Ayyūb as-Saḫtiyānī رحمه الله:
HAD-0503.speaker: He said:

HAD-0504.text: From Allah comes the message, upon the Messenger lies the conveyance, and upon us lies submission.
HAD-0504.narrator: It is reported from az-Zuhrī رحمه الله:
HAD-0504.speaker: He said:

HAD-0505.text: The Sunnah is ten; whoever accepts it completely completes the Sunnah, and whoever leaves any of it leaves the Sunnah.
HAD-0505.narrator: It is reported from Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah رحمه الله:
HAD-0505.speaker: He said:

HAD-0666.text: Whoever does not show mercy to people is not shown mercy.
HAD-0666.narrator: Ǧarīr ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0666.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0667.text: Whoever points to good receives a reward like the one who does it.
HAD-0667.narrator: Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0667.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0668.text: Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most lying speech.
HAD-0668.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0668.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0669.text: Whoever is not grateful to people is not grateful to Allah.
HAD-0669.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0669.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0670.text: Allah has prescribed Iḥsān in all things.
HAD-0670.narrator: Šaddād ibn Aws رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0670.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0671.text: Follow and do not invent anew; you have already been given sufficiency.
HAD-0671.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0671.speaker: He said:

HAD-0672.text: Hold yourselves to account before you are held to account.
HAD-0672.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0672.speaker: He said:

HAD-0673.text: Knowledge calls for action; if action does not answer, knowledge moves on.
HAD-0673.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0673.speaker: He said:

HAD-0674.text: Linger with knowledge and carry it with gentleness.
HAD-0674.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-0674.speaker: He said:

HAD-0675.text: Be a scholar, a learner, or a listener; do not be the fourth, or you will perish.
HAD-0675.narrator: It is transmitted from Abū ad-Dardāʾ رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0675.speaker: He said:

HAD-0676.text: Learn knowledge, for learning it for the sake of Allah is fear of Allah.
HAD-0676.narrator: It is transmitted from Muʿāḏ ibn Ǧabal رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0676.speaker: He said:

HAD-0677.text: The believer sees his sins as though he were sitting under a mountain that might fall upon him.
HAD-0677.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0677.speaker: He said:

HAD-0678.text: No calamity befalls a servant except because of a sin, and nothing is lifted except through repentance.
HAD-0678.narrator: It is transmitted from Abū Bakr aṣ-Ṣiddīq رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0678.speaker: He said:

HAD-0679.text: Hold fast to the Sunnah; it suffices you against every innovation.
HAD-0679.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0679.speaker: He said:

HAD-0680.text: If our heart were pure, it would never be sated with the word of Allah.
HAD-0680.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿUṯmān ibn ʿAffān رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0680.speaker: He said:

HAD-0681.text: The Dunyā departs and the hereafter comes; be children of the hereafter.
HAD-0681.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0681.speaker: He said:

HAD-0682.text: When you reach the evening, do not expect the morning; use your health before illness.
HAD-0682.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-0682.speaker: He said:

HAD-0683.text: How many want good yet do not attain it.
HAD-0683.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0683.speaker: He said:

HAD-0684.text: I preserved with me two vessels of knowledge; one I spread, and the other remained hidden out of fear.
HAD-0684.narrator: It is transmitted from Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0684.speaker: He said:

HAD-0685.text: The first matter of this Ummah was made firm through truth and clear guidance.
HAD-0685.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها:
HAD-0685.speaker: She said:

HAD-0566.text: Faith has over seventy branches, and modesty is a branch of faith.
HAD-0566.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0566.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0566.sharh: Al-Qurṭubī explains Abū Hurayrah’s statement about the numerous branches of Īmān and explains the word “šuʿbah” as a single quality or manifestation. The various authentic versions mention more than sixty or more than seventy branches. As examples, the testimony of Tawḥīd, the removal of dangers from the path, and modesty are named. The commentary assigns these various qualities to the comprehensive concept of faith; the number of branches is not to be understood as a call to draw up, on one’s own authority, a new list of religious duties.

HAD-0567.text: The best among you are those who learn the Qurʾān and teach it.
HAD-0567.narrator: ʿUṯmān ibn ʿAffān رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0567.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0567.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains the excellence of those who learn the Qurʾān and pass this knowledge on: whoever learns himself and then teaches joins his own benefit with the benefit of others. He discusses the differing textual versions with “and” and “or,” and explains why the version with “and” has the more comprehensive sense. At the same time he examines a transmission-critical objection as to whether Abū ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān as-Sulamī heard the report directly from ʿUṯmān, and he gives reasons why al-Buḫārī preferred the connected path of transmission. The commentary does not establish that mere memorization without understanding and action surpasses all other kinds of righteous knowledge.

HAD-0568.text: The companion of the Qurʾān will be told: Read, ascend, and recite as you recited in this world.
HAD-0568.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-0568.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0568.sharh: The commentator explains the address to the “companion of the Qurʾān” as a reward for someone who recites the Qurʾān regularly and acts according to it, not merely someone who reads individual words and neglects its content. He relates “Read and ascend” to the ranks in Paradise, and “recite in a measured way” to a calm, careful reading. According to this interpretation, the last recited Āyah determines the rank reached. The text is a promise and must not be extended into an independent, detailed calculation of rank for every person.

HAD-0569.text: Every good deed is a Ṣadaqah.
HAD-0569.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-0569.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0569.sharh: An-Nawawī explains the words “Every good action is Ṣadaqah” in the commentary on the Muslim version concerning Ḥuḏayfah by saying that all righteous good deeds count, as to their reward, like a charitable gift. Therefore the Muslim should neither belittle nor refuse any good deed, however slight, if he can perform it. The wording of Ǧābir transmitted by al-Buḫārī and the version of Ḥuḏayfah transmitted by Muslim support the same principle; their transmitters and chains, however, are different. “Ṣadaqah” here is not only the giving away of wealth, but denotes the meritorious effect of good.

HAD-0570.text: Your smile in the face of your brother is a Ṣadaqah for you.
HAD-0570.narrator: Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0570.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0570.sharh: ʿAlī al-Qārī explains the transmission of Abū Ḏarr, according to which even a friendly smile in the face of a Muslim brother counts as Ṣadaqah. By the smile, according to his lexical explanation, an open, friendly facial expression is meant; the act brings good to the other and is therefore rewarded like a charitable gift. In the same longer report, enjoining the good, warning against injustice, showing the way to one who has gone astray, support of the visually impaired, the removal of obstacles, and help in drawing water also belong to the forms of Ṣadaqah. At-Tirmiḏī himself grades the report as ḥasan ġarīb.

HAD-0571.text: Obey me so long as I obey Allah; if I disobey Him, there is no obedience to me over you.
HAD-0571.narrator: It is transmitted of Abū Bakr aṣ-Ṣiddīq رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0571.speaker: He said:

HAD-0572.text: Call yourselves to account before you are called to account.
HAD-0572.narrator: It is transmitted of ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0572.speaker: He said:

HAD-0573.text: Acquire religious knowledge before you are made leaders.
HAD-0573.narrator: It is transmitted of ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0573.speaker: He said:

HAD-0574.text: We are a people whom Allah has honored through Islam.
HAD-0574.narrator: It is transmitted of ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0574.speaker: He said:

HAD-0575.text: Follow and do not invent anew; you have already been given sufficiency.
HAD-0575.narrator: It is transmitted of ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0575.speaker: He said:

HAD-0576.text: The Ǧamāʿah is that which accords with the truth, even if you are alone.
HAD-0576.narrator: It is transmitted of ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0576.speaker: He said:

HAD-0577.text: Moderation upon the Sunnah is better than exertion upon a Bidʿah.
HAD-0577.narrator: It is transmitted of ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0577.speaker: He said:

HAD-0578.text: How will it be with you when a Fitnah comes upon you in which the old man grows gray and the boy grows up?
HAD-0578.narrator: It is transmitted of ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0578.speaker: He said:

HAD-0579.text: Every person’s statement may be taken and rejected, except the Prophet ﷺ.
HAD-0579.narrator: It is transmitted of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-0579.speaker: He said:

HAD-0580.text: Tafsīr is of four kinds; among them is a kind that no one knows except Allah.
HAD-0580.narrator: It is transmitted of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-0580.speaker: He said:

HAD-0581.text: Every Bidʿah is misguidance, even if the people regard it as good.
HAD-0581.narrator: It is transmitted of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-0581.speaker: He said:

HAD-0582.text: Speak to people according to what they recognize; do you want Allah and His Messenger to be denied?
HAD-0582.narrator: It is transmitted of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0582.speaker: He said:

HAD-0583.text: Knowledge calls for action; if it responds, it remains, otherwise it departs.
HAD-0583.narrator: It is transmitted of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0583.speaker: He said:

HAD-0584.text: The people asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the good, and I asked him about the evil out of fear of it.
HAD-0584.narrator: It is transmitted of Ḥuḏayfah ibn al-Yamān رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0584.speaker: He said:

HAD-0585.text: You will not be a scholar until you learn; and you will not be knowing through knowledge until you act upon it.
HAD-0585.narrator: It is transmitted of Abū ad-Dardāʾ رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0585.speaker: He said:

HAD-0405.text: In a letter on divine predestination, ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz رحمه الله wrote in substance: “Hold fast to the Sunnah, for with Allah’s permission it is a protection for you.” He then recalled that the early generations knowingly remained with the transmitted foundations.
HAD-0405.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz رحمه الله:
HAD-0405.speaker: He wrote:

HAD-0406.text: They used to dislike it when a man spoke without knowledge and thereby threw people into confusion.
HAD-0406.narrator: The statement is attributed to Ibrāhīm an-Naḫaʿī رحمه الله (unchecked):
HAD-0406.speaker: He said:

HAD-0407.text: Qatādah رحمه الله explained Allah’s word, “And do not follow that of which you have no knowledge” (Qurʾān 17:36): “Do not say: I have seen, though you did not see; or: I have heard, though you did not hear; or: I have known, though you did not know.”
HAD-0407.narrator: It is transmitted from Qatādah رحمه الله:
HAD-0407.speaker: He said:

HAD-0408.text: al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ رحمه الله said: “I encountered the best of people; they all held fast to the Sunnah and warned against religious innovations.”
HAD-0408.narrator: It is transmitted from al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ رحمه الله:
HAD-0408.speaker: He said:

HAD-0409.text: Wakīʿ ibn al-Ǧarrāḥ رحمه الله said: “Whoever seeks the Ḥadīṯ as it was transmitted belongs to the people of the Sunnah. Whoever seeks it in order to support his own opinion thereby follows an innovation.”
HAD-0409.narrator: It is transmitted from Wakīʿ ibn al-Jarrāḥ رحمه الله:
HAD-0409.speaker: He said:

HAD-0410.text: Abū Bakr ibn Ḫallād reported that he asked Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān رحمه الله whether he did not fear that the transmitters he had rejected would rise against him on the Day of Resurrection. Yaḥyā replied: “I would rather that they be my opponents than that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ be my opponent and ask me: Why did you not ward off the lies concerning my Ḥadīṯ?”
HAD-0410.narrator: It is transmitted from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān رحمه الله:
HAD-0410.speaker: He said:

HAD-0411.text: On the expedition to Ḫaybar they performed the morning prayer while it was still dark. Anas saw the Izār of the Prophet ﷺ slip back from his thigh. After the taking of Ḫaybar, Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy was chosen from among the captives. The Prophet ﷺ set her free and married her; her manumission was her bridal gift. On the way the Companions prepared a shared meal for the wedding.
HAD-0411.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0411.speaker: He reported:
HAD-0411.sharh: Ibn Raǧab cites the report of Anas from Ḫaybar in the chapter on covering the thigh. He places the statements about its uncovering beside other reports that call the thigh an ʿAwrah, and he documents the difference between the majority view and dissenting opinions. After his discussion, most of the early jurists hold that the thigh belongs to the ʿAwrah. He distinguishes the question of visibility in everyday life from the question of which covering is required for the validity of the prayer. The original German statement about a prayer on a Ḥaṣīr did not belong to Buḫārī no. 371 and was therefore replaced by a summary faithful to the actual Ḫaybar report.

HAD-0412.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to perform the Faǧr prayer. Some believing women attended it, fully wrapped in their outer garments (Murūṭ). They then returned to their houses without being recognized, because of the darkness that still prevailed.
HAD-0412.speaker: She reported:
HAD-0412.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains, on the basis of ʿĀʾišah’s report, that women were present at the Faǧr prayer and covered their bodies with Murūṭ on the way to the mosque. He distinguishes the clothing worn when going out in public from the fiqh question of the covering required in the prayer itself. In the chapter heading he discusses the number and kind of garments, while the wording of this report first attests the women’s attendance and the darkness of that time. The original HAD-0412 text about the patterned garment and Abū Ǧahm was a repetition of Buḫārī no. 373 and did not belong to no. 372.

HAD-0413.text: The Prophet ﷺ prayed in a patterned garment (ḫamīṣah) and looked at its pattern during the prayer. After the prayer he had the garment sent back to Abū Ǧahm and asked instead for his plain, unpatterned garment (anbiǧāniyyah), for the pattern had distracted him during the prayer.
HAD-0413.speaker: She reported:
HAD-0413.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that the patterned garment was not forbidden in itself: the Prophet ﷺ returned it because its pattern claimed his attention in the prayer. The plainer replacement garment received from Abū Ǧahm and the explanation of the reason at the same time prevented the giver from being hurt by the return. Ibn Raǧab compares different paths of transmission and points out that the expression “Fitnah,” in the version commented through ʿUrwah and ʿĀʾišah, is not equally attested in all the chains. From this follows the recommendation to remove what distracts from the place of prayer, not a blanket invalidity of a prayer in clothing with patterns.

HAD-0414.text: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها had hung a patterned curtain (qirām) on one side of her dwelling. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Remove this curtain from us, for its images keep appearing to me during my prayer.”
HAD-0414.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0414.speaker: He reported:
HAD-0414.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that the images of the curtain distracted the Prophet ﷺ during his prayer. In the commentary he distinguishes various kinds of images and fabric ornaments, as well as the disagreement about their use on clothing, mats or curtains. In doing so he rejects the claim that every addition recorded in further reports automatically possesses a reliable chain. The dislike of distracting images in the place of prayer must not be confused with an explicit report that the Prophet ﷺ broke off or repeated the prayer in question. The legal question of the validity of the prayer is discussed separately by the commentators.

HAD-0415.text: The Prophet ﷺ decisively took off a silk garment after the prayer and said that this was not the clothing of the God-fearing.
HAD-0415.narrator: ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0415.speaker: He said:
HAD-0415.sharh: Ibn Raǧab first explains that “farrūǧ” denotes a cloak slit at the back, and he names the transmitters Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb and Abū al-Ḫayr by their full names. From the report he derives the basic permissibility of prayer in such a form of cloak. That the Prophet ﷺ at first wore the silk garment in the prayer, Ibn Raǧab expressly understands as an occurrence before the later prohibition of silk for men; this earlier wearing is therefore no evidence for the validity of a prayer in unlawful silk after its prohibition. He distinguishes the special concession in illness and the further discussion of the scholars.

HAD-0416.text: The Prophet ﷺ prayed in a red garment toward an ʿAnazah; people and animals passed behind the Sutrah.
HAD-0416.narrator: Abū Juḥayfah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0416.speaker: He said:
HAD-0416.sharh: In the report of Abū Ǧuḥayfah, Ibn Raǧab highlights that the Prophet ﷺ prayed two Rakʿah before the people in a red Ḥullah garment, while Bilāl stuck a short lance into the ground as a Sutrah. People and animals passed behind this Sutrah. The immediate probative purpose of the chapter, according to Ibn Raǧab’s explicit statement, is the permissibility of red prayer clothing. Alongside this he explains that a Ḥullah consists of two garments that belong together. The remaining details of the longer report are treated in other chapters.

HAD-0417.text: The Prophet ﷺ prayed on the Minbar so that the people would see his prayer and learn from him.
HAD-0417.narrator: Sahl ibn Saʿd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0417.speaker: He said:
HAD-0417.sharh: Ibn Raǧab comments on the report of Sahl ibn Saʿd about the prayer on the pulpit: the Prophet ﷺ stood there for the Takbīr and the recitation, bowed, went backward down for the prostration, and then returned. The commentary treats this event as evidence that a prayer on elevated supports is possible in principle. He records differing legal views on how high the Imām may stand relative to those praying with him, and he distinguishes the prophetic demonstration for learning the prayer from a general recommendation of a permanently higher position for the one who leads.

HAD-0418.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ fell from a horse and was injured in the leg or the shoulder. He withdrew for a month into an elevated room with stairs made of palm trunks. When his Companions visited him, he led them in prayer while seated, and they stood. He then explained that the Imām is appointed so that one follows him. After twenty-nine days he left the room and explained that a month can also comprise twenty-nine days.
HAD-0418.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0418.speaker: He reported:
HAD-0418.sharh: Ibn Raǧab cites the report about the Prophet ﷺ, injured after a fall, as a further narration within the chapter on prayer on elevated surfaces. The upper room resting on palm trunks is especially relevant to the chapter heading. The report also relates that the Prophet ﷺ, because of his injury, led the prayer seated and that the Companions at first stood. His explanation binds the movements of those praying with him to the Imām. The particular question of how those praying with a seated Imām are to conduct themselves requires comparison with further authentic reports and must not be reduced, from the original brief description alone, to this single case.

HAD-0419.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed while I was menstruating and beside him. When he prostrated, his garment sometimes touched my body. He used to pray on a small prayer mat, the Ḫumrah.
HAD-0419.narrator: Maymūnah رضي الله عنها reported (via ʿAbdullāh ibn Šaddād):
HAD-0419.speaker: She reported:
HAD-0419.sharh: Ibn Raǧab cites Maymūnah’s report in a chapter of its own, that the garment of the one praying can touch his wife during the prostration. Physical contact with a menstruating wife does not automatically defile the garment. The version also mentions a Ḫumrah as a permitted underlay in the prayer; this question is treated separately in a following chapter. The report contains neither ʿItbān ibn Mālik nor his request that the Prophet ﷺ designate a place of prayer in his house; that German statement originally entered was therefore removed.

HAD-0420.text: His grandmother Mulaykah invited the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to a meal. He then said: “Stand up, so that I may pray for you.” Anas sprinkled water on an old mat that had grown dark from long use. The Prophet ﷺ stood for the prayer, and Anas and an orphan stood in a row behind him; the elderly woman stood behind them. He led them in two Rakʿah and then departed.
HAD-0420.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0420.speaker: He said:
HAD-0420.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that this report permits the prayer and the prostration on a mat woven from plant material. Sprinkling the old mat with water need not necessarily mean that an established impurity was present; Ibn Raǧab considers an ordinary cleaning and the softening of the mat the more likely explanation. From other reports it appears that this was a voluntary prayer. Concerning the identity of Mulaykah, Ibn Raǧab compares several genealogical interpretations and variant transmissions. The arrangement of Anas and the orphan behind the Prophet ﷺ, and of the elderly woman behind them, is part of the authentic primary report. Additional divergent paths of transmission about particular mats Ibn Raǧab treats critically, instead of judging each of them equally reliable.

HAD-0421.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray on a small mat, the Ḫumrah.
HAD-0421.speaker: She said:
HAD-0421.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains the term Ḫumrah as a small prayer underlay woven from palm fibers, sufficient approximately for the face and the hands in the Suǧūd. A larger carpet, by contrast, is called Ḥaṣīr. He mentions that the Prophet ﷺ prayed on a Ḫumrah, and he classifies this as evidence for the permissibility of prayer on such an underlay. He also reports the preference of some early scholars for direct contact with the earth when prostrating, without presenting their view as a prohibition of the Ḫumrah.

HAD-0422.text: The Prophet ﷺ prayed while she lay in front of him; at the movement of the Suǧūd he gave her a sign and she drew her feet back.
HAD-0422.speaker: She said:
HAD-0422.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains ʿĀʾišah’s report that the Prophet ﷺ prayed at night while she lay crosswise in front of him and her feet were in the area of his Qiblah. For the Suǧūd he touched her so that she drew her feet back, and she stretched them out again when he rose. The statement that there were at that time no lamps in the house explains the necessary touching. On the basis of the different paths of transmission, Ibn Raǧab discusses whether the feet lay on the bed or partly on the floor in the area of prostration; he therefore does not present the exact spatial position as established wording.

HAD-0423.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed while she lay on the bed between him and the Qiblah.
HAD-0423.speaker: She said:
HAD-0423.sharh: Ibn Raǧab cites the second report from ʿĀʾišah about the night prayer of the Prophet ﷺ, while she lay crosswise between him and the Qiblah on the family’s bed. The report compares her bodily position with the transverse position at a Ǧanāzah. He explains its agreement with the previous version, in which the Prophet ﷺ touched her feet at the Suǧūd. The report is treated in the chapter on prayer on a bed or near the bed; it is not evidence that touching a woman automatically invalidates the Ṣalāh.

HAD-0424.text: The Prophet ﷺ prayed while ʿĀʾishah رضي الله عنها lay between him and the Qiblah on their shared bed.
HAD-0424.speaker: ʿĀʾishah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-0424.sharh: Ibn Raǧab cites this third version via ʿUrwah from ʿĀʾišah: the Prophet ﷺ prayed while ʿĀʾišah lay crosswise between him and the Qiblah on the shared bed. The mention of the shared bed supplements the preceding versions. The divergence concerns the exact description of the surface for lying, not the invention of another encounter. Ibn Raǧab discusses in this connection the prayer on beds and the differing interpretations of the position of the person in front of the one praying. The Ḥadīṯ is marked as a parallel to HAD-0423.

HAD-0445.text: We prayed with the Prophet ﷺ and, in the heat, placed our garment at the place of suǧūd.
HAD-0445.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0445.speaker: He reported:
HAD-0445.sharh: This is a parallel wording in content of HAD-0425 and goes back to the same authentic report of Anas. Ibn Raǧab explains that, when the ground was intensely hot, the Companions placed their garments beneath the forehead so that they could perform the prostration. He distinguishes a concession grounded in heat from general arbitrariness regarding the surface of suǧūd, and he treats transmission variants and their connection separately.

HAD-0446.text: Ibrāhīm an-Naḫaʿī رحمه الله explained that they were pleased with the Ḥadīṯ of Ǧarīr ibn ʿAbdullāh about wiping over the ḫuffayn (leather socks), for Ǧarīr was among those who accepted Islam late. The report thus remained significant even after the revelation of the wuḍūʾ verses in Sūrat al-Māʾidah.
HAD-0446.narrator: It is transmitted of Ibrāhīm an-Naḫaʿī رحمه الله:
HAD-0446.speaker: He said:

HAD-0447.text: ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī reported that Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal asked him about the Ḥadīṯ concerning the prayer of the Prophet ﷺ on the minbar. The inference is related that the Prophet ﷺ stood higher than the people and that one may derive from this the basic possibility of an elevated position for the imām. Ibn Raǧab, however, states expressly that this view transmitted from Aḥmad is unusual and contradicts the well-known position otherwise transmitted from him by his students.
HAD-0447.narrator: ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī رحمه الله reported a conversation with Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal رحمه الله:
HAD-0447.speaker: Transmission of ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī:

HAD-0448.text: When Sahl ibn Saʿd رضي الله عنه was asked about the minbar of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he explained that none of those present knew more about it than he did. The minbar had been made of aṯl wood from al-Ġābah. He then described how the Prophet ﷺ stood upon it, prayed, and stepped backward down to the ground for the prostration.
HAD-0448.narrator: It is transmitted of Sahl ibn Saʿd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0448.speaker: He said:

HAD-0449.text: When ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه was asked about prayer in one garment, he said: If Allah has granted you ample means, then make use of that abundance. He then named several combinations of clothing in which one may pray.
HAD-0449.narrator: It is transmitted of ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0449.speaker: He said:

HAD-0450.text: O people, you will introduce new things, and new things will be introduced for you. When you see an innovation, hold to the original matter.
HAD-0450.narrator: It is transmitted of Ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0450.speaker: He said:

HAD-0451.text: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak what is good or remain silent.
HAD-0451.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0451.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0451.sharh: Ibn Raǧab cites the report of Abū Hurayrah in full with the three duties: to speak what is good or remain silent, to honor the neighbor, and to honor the guest. He stresses that faith also includes actions toward other people. The command to remain silent does not require silence without exception; whoever can fittingly say what is good and thereby benefit should do so, and should leave aside harmful speech and idle talk. Ibn Raǧab quotes several statements of early scholars on the effort to restrain one’s tongue, and he distinguishes the benefit of good words from the protection of silence.

HAD-0452.text: The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer; in both there is good.
HAD-0452.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0452.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0452.sharh: An-Nawawī explains the expression “the strong believer” above all as strength of resolve and will in matters of the Hereafter: zeal and perseverance in worship, patience in hardship, and steadfastness in good. He stresses that the second clause, “in both there is good,” expressly grants the weaker believer as well the good of his faith and of his acts of worship. The complete Ḥadīṯ further urges one to strive for what is beneficial, to ask Allah for help, and, after an event, not to fall into useless retrospective suppositions. Strength is therefore not equated here in a blanket way with mere muscular power.

HAD-0453.text: The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe.
HAD-0453.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-0453.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0453.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that the Muslim from whose tongue and hand other Muslims are safe means the Muslim who fulfills the obligatory completeness of this quality. The lack of protection from injurious words or deeds is a grave breach of duty, yet on the basis of this wording it does not automatically amount to a denial of Islam in its entirety. The commentator compares the differing wordings in al-Buḫārī and Muslim, examines the evidence that aš-Šaʿbī actually heard ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr, and explains that the tongue harms by forbidden words and the hand by forbidden deeds. The complete Buḫārī wording adds: The true muhaǧir avoids what Allah has forbidden.

HAD-0454.text: The likeness of good and bad company is that of the bearer of musk and the bellows.
HAD-0454.narrator: Abū Mūsā رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0454.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0454.sharh: Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Qurṭubī explains the comparison of good and bad company with a bearer of musk and a man at the bellows. The Prophet ﷺ describes several possible effects of the encounter: a good companion may directly give or teach something beneficial; through the company one may acquire something good or at least experience a good influence. Bad company, by contrast, may bring direct harm or disadvantageous accompanying effects. Al-Qurṭubī derives from this the encouragement to seek the company of people of sound knowledge and good conduct.

HAD-0455.text: The believer is not bitten twice from the same opening.
HAD-0455.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0455.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0455.sharh: An-Nawawī explains the saying “The believer is not stung twice from the same burrow” as a pointer to the prudence of a discerning believer who does not continually let himself be outwitted by the same deception. He names two readings of the Arabic verb: as a descriptive statement and as an exhortation to vigilance. The connection he adduces with the capture of Abū ʿAzzah speaks rather for the descriptive interpretation. The saying concerns learning from experience, not the claim that a believing person can never repeat a mistake.

HAD-0456.text: None of you believes completely until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
HAD-0456.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0456.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that loving the good for the brother in faith is not merely a voluntary courtesy, but belongs to the obligatory qualities of faith. The denial of faith stated in the Ḥadīṯ denotes the lack of an obligatory quality, not automatically a complete departure from Islam. Real love of the good for others requires, according to Ibn Raǧab, overcoming envy, resentment, deceit, and hatred. The believer should wish for others a comparable religious or worldly benefit without his own having to be taken from him. His commentary cites statements of Ibn ʿAbbās and aš-Šāfiʿī on this.

HAD-0457.text: Allah does not look at your forms and your wealth, but at your hearts and your deeds.
HAD-0457.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0457.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0457.sharh: Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Qurṭubī explains that Allah’s knowledge and sight encompass all creatures and all their outward and inward states. The negation in this Ḥadīṯ therefore does not mean that outward appearances or wealth would be unknown to Allah. What is meant is that outward possession and bodily appearance are not, by themselves, a measure of His special reward and acceptance. These relate to inner sincerity and the corresponding deeds. The statement is thus neither narrowed to the merely inward nor misunderstood as a denial of divine all-knowledge.

HAD-0458.text: Whoever takes a path on which he seeks knowledge, Allah makes easy for him a path to the Garden.
HAD-0458.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0458.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0458.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that the path to knowledge includes both the actual path to the gatherings of the scholars and the means of learning: reading, memorizing, studying, discussing, and understanding. The promise of the eased path to the Garden points to the benefit of acquired knowledge for right deeds and guidance. The statement stands in the longer authentic report of Muslim, which also addresses relieving another’s distress, mutual help, and studying the Qurʾān together.

HAD-0459.text: The world is a prison for the believer and a paradise for the kāfir.
HAD-0459.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0459.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0459.sharh: An-Nawawī explains the comparison of the world as a prison for the believer and as a paradise for the kāfir by the constraints of this life and the recompense of the next. The believer keeps away from forbidden desires and fulfills duties. In view of the lasting reward of the next life, the constraints of this life are like a prison. For the other, worldly well-being is fleeting and, compared with the threatened punishment of the next life, like a paradise. The statement does not mean that every believer must be poor on earth.

HAD-0460.text: A person is upon the religion of his close friend; so let each one look to whom he takes as a friend.
HAD-0460.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0460.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0460.sharh: ʿAlī al-Qārī explains that a person is, in general, influenced by the religion and way of life of his close friend. True intimate friendship often goes together with shared religious attitudes; even outward association can lead to taking on the friend’s manners. The Ḥadīṯ therefore urges that the choice of close friends be examined deliberately. Al-Qārī refers to Qurʾān 9:119 (being with the truthful) and cites al-Ġazālī’s observation that frequent company can shape the pursuit of worldly things or abstinence. He distinguishes this explanation of the content from various classical judgments on the transmission: at-Tirmiḏī calls it ḥasan ġarīb, while an-Nawawī calls its chain ṣaḥīḥ.

HAD-0461.text: Make things easy and do not make them hard; give glad tidings and do not drive people away.
HAD-0461.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0461.sharh: Badr ad-Dīn al-ʿAynī explains the deliberately paired commands “Make things easy and do not make them hard” and “Give glad tidings and do not drive people away” as reinforced instructions. Merely easing things now and then is not enough if one ordinarily imposes needless hardship. Especially in teaching, in dealing with new Muslims, and in admonition, one should proceed step by step and in such a way that people are encouraged to keep to what is permitted. The commentary does not lift the prohibitions that are expressly established; what is meant is refraining from needless hardship in conveying the matter.

HAD-0462.text: Allah is gentle and loves gentleness in all matters.
HAD-0462.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0462.sharh: An-Nawawī brings together several wordings of the transmission: Allah loves gentleness and grants for it what He does not grant for harshness. Gentleness beautifies dealings and makes it easier to reach good aims; its opposite, needless harshness, is disapproved. The commentary explains the words as an encouragement to practice gentleness in conduct, without deriving from them a permission to disregard legal duties. The various wordings join this virtue with a corresponding reward and with practical benefits.

HAD-0464.text: The lawful is clear and the forbidden is clear; between them lie doubtful matters.
HAD-0464.narrator: an-Nuʿmān ibn Bašīr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-0464.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0464.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that what is clearly lawful and what is clearly forbidden each have legal limits that can be plainly recognized. Between them stand matters whose ruling is not known to many people; the wording “many” does not mean that no one could know their ruling. Whoever keeps away from such doubtful matters protects his religion and his reputation. Ibn Raǧab links the example of a shepherd near a protected tract with the danger of falling step by step into the forbidden; the closing words about the heart explain the influence of inner uprightness upon deeds.

HAD-0465.text: Deeds are only according to intentions.
HAD-0465.narrator: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0465.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0465.sharh: Ibn Raǧab presents the authentic report of ʿUmar as a first foundational text. The worth of an act is bound up with its intention; the same outwardly recognizable act can receive a different religious assessment according to the inner aim. The example of the hiǧrah shows this with particular clarity: one who emigrates for the sake of Allah and His Messenger differs from one whose emigration aims only at a worldly gain or a marriage. The statement regulates the intention behind deeds, not the blanket permissibility of any outward acts.

HAD-0466.text: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should honor his neighbor.
HAD-0466.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0466.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0466.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that good speech, the rights of the neighbor, and hospitality occur together in the prophetic statement as qualities of faith. The transmitted wordings differ: one expressly requires honoring the neighbor, another forbids causing him harm. He counts consideration and help among the rights of the neighbor, regardless of kinship; neighborhood is an independent obligation alongside the rights of kinship. The command to honor is therefore not merely polite address, but includes concrete consideration and refraining from harm.

HAD-0467.text: Each of you is a shepherd, and each is responsible for his flock.
HAD-0467.narrator: Ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-0467.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0467.sharh: An-Nawawī explains the word “Rāʿin” as a person to whom the custody of something has been entrusted and who is responsible for its well-being. The Prophet ﷺ names different spheres of responsibility, among them public leadership, the family, the household, and entrusted property. The statement obliges every person in charge to justice, to the careful observance of rights, and to the protection of what has been entrusted to him. It does not mean that every person possesses the same authority.

HAD-0468.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The believer is to the believer like a mirror. The believer is the brother of the believer: he guards him from harm in his affairs and protects him also in his absence.”
HAD-0468.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0468.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0468.sharh: Al-Munāwī explains the mirror metaphor as the mutual pointing out of faults that a person easily overlooks in himself. He relates on this the explanations of aṭ-Ṭībī and al-ʿĀmirī: the believing brother should counsel sincerely, gently, and as far as possible without public exposure; he should also recognize good qualities and encourage gratitude. The statement is not a charge to spread faults publicly. The complete Arabic report additionally mentions that a believer protects his brother’s concerns and stands up for him even in his absence. The earlier shortened German wording did not contain this second part; it was supplied from Abū Dāwūd no. 4918.

HAD-0469.text: Truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise.
HAD-0469.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0469.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0469.sharh: An-Nawawī explains that truthfulness leads to righteous action and that the word “Birr” comprehensively denotes the good. Truthfulness that is deliberately cultivated becomes established as a personal quality. By contrast, habituation to lying leads step by step to wrongdoing. He distinguishes the acquisition of such a character trait from the mere claim that a single true word already secures a person’s final standing with Allah.

HAD-0470.text: A good word is a charity.
HAD-0470.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0470.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0470.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains why a good word is called Ṣadaqah: just as a material gift can gladden the heart of the one who receives it and help him, so kind and useful speech also brings about good. He treats the effect of good words upon other people as a reason why the prophetic transmission counts them as an act of charity. The complete report on the forms of Ṣadaqah that are possible each day also mentions just reconciliation, help with a mount, steps toward prayer, and removing obstacles from the path. These additional deeds must not be silently read into the short wording “A good word is a charity”; they belong to the longer authentic version.

HAD-0471.text: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه said: “Follow, and do not introduce innovations; you have already been given what suffices.”
HAD-0471.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0471.speaker: He said:

HAD-0472.text: Moderation upon the Sunnah is better than exertion upon Bidʿah.
HAD-0472.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0472.speaker: He said:

HAD-0473.text: Hardly a year comes upon the people without their bringing forth a Bidʿah and letting a Sunnah die.
HAD-0473.narrator: It is transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-0473.speaker: He said:

HAD-0474.text: Call yourselves to account before you are called to account.
HAD-0474.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0474.speaker: He said:

HAD-0475.text: Knowledge calls to action; if action answers, it remains, otherwise it departs.
HAD-0475.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0475.speaker: He said:

HAD-0476.text: People are enemies of what they do not know.
HAD-0476.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0476.speaker: He said:

HAD-0477.text: It is transmitted from Abū ad-Dardāʾ رضي الله عنه: Three signs of ignorance are self-satisfaction, speaking much about what does not concern one, and keeping others from things that one does oneself.
HAD-0477.narrator: It is transmitted from Abū ad-Dardāʾ رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0477.speaker: He said:

HAD-0478.text: You will not be a scholar until you are a learner; and you will not be taught by knowledge until you act upon it.
HAD-0478.narrator: It is transmitted from Abū ad-Dardāʾ رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0478.speaker: He said:

HAD-0479.text: Obedience to me holds as long as I obey Allah and His Messenger.
HAD-0479.narrator: It is transmitted from Abū Bakr aṣ-Ṣiddīq رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0479.speaker: He said:

HAD-0480.text: No Islam without a community, no community without leadership, and no leadership without obedience.
HAD-0480.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0480.speaker: He said:

HAD-0481.text: Every Bidʿah is misguidance, even if people consider it good.
HAD-0481.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-0481.speaker: He said:

HAD-0482.text: Every act of worship that the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ did not perform, do not perform it yourselves as worship.
HAD-0482.narrator: It is transmitted from Ḥuḏayfah ibn al-Yamān رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0482.speaker: He said:

HAD-0483.text: Learn knowledge; for learning it for Allah is fear of Him.
HAD-0483.narrator: It is transmitted from Muʿāḏ ibn Ǧabal رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0483.speaker: He said:

HAD-0484.text: Muʿāḏ ibn Ǧabal رضي الله عنه warned of a time in which someone recites the Qurʾān, yet invents new religious teachings in order to be followed by people. He said in substance: “Beware of what such a person newly introduces; for what he introduces is misguidance.”
HAD-0484.narrator: It is transmitted from Muʿāḏ ibn Ǧabal رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0484.speaker: He said:

HAD-0485.text: Whoever wishes to follow a path, let him follow the path of those who have already died: the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ.
HAD-0485.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0485.speaker: He said:

HAD-0527.text: Allah accepts only what is good.
HAD-0527.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0527.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0527.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains the tenth Ḥadīṯ of his collection: Allah accepts only what is good. He connects the command to the messengers to eat of lawful good things and to act righteously (Qurʾān 23:51) with the same charge to the believers (2:172). He especially highlights the closing scene of the traveler: although travel, raised hands, and earnest supplication can be grounds for the prayer to be answered, forbidden food, clothing, and provision stand against acceptance. The shortened German source sentence gives only the beginning of the Ḥadīṯ; the explanation that follows refers to the longer authentic report.

HAD-0528.narrator: Abū Mālik al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0528.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0528.sharh: Ibn Raǧab examines the wording “aṭ-ṭuhūr is half of Īmān.” He explains that outward ritual purity and inward purification are distinct yet connected aspects of the religion. He presents differing interpretations of the expression “half” and points to the connection between Ṣalāh and the purification that precedes it. The phrase therefore cannot be understood as a statement that an ablution by itself already fulfills all duties of faith.

HAD-0529.text: al-Ḥamdu lillāh fills the Scale, and Subḥānallāh wal-ḥamdu lillāh fill what is between heaven and earth.
HAD-0529.narrator: Abū Mālik al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0529.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0529.sharh: Ibn Raǧab presents the differing authentic wordings about the Scale being filled by al-Ḥamdu lillāh and the meaning of Tasbīḥ. He distinguishes praise as affirmation of the perfect attributes of Allah, and Tasbīḥ as declaring freedom from defects. These forms of Ḏikr are considered together in the commentary; from the variants there follows no call to replace the other transmitted words with a self-invented formula.

HAD-0530.text: The Qurʾān is a proof for you or against you.
HAD-0530.narrator: Abū Mālik al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0530.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0530.sharh: Ibn Raǧab treats the statement that the Qurʾān acts as a proof for or against its reader as part of the authentic longer report of Abū Mālik al-Ašʿarī. The guidance of the revelation concerns not merely reading, but also knowledge of its directives and corresponding action. If the message is deliberately disregarded, the same proof can stand against the person concerned. The sentence is a partial transmission, not an independent new prophetic statement.

HAD-0531.text: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should honor his guest.
HAD-0531.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0531.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0531.sharh: Ibn Raǧab presents the honorable treatment of a guest as part of the fifteenth Ḥadīṯ. The authentic wording joins three instructions to belief in Allah and the Last Day: to speak only what is good or remain silent, to honor the neighbor, and to honor the guest. The guest’s right is thus not treated as a secondary social custom, but as an expression of lived faith. This passage is only an excerpt of the connected transmission; its remaining instructions are treated together in the one classical commentary.

HAD-0532.text: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should maintain his kinship ties.
HAD-0532.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0532.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0532.sharh: Al-ʿAynī explains the words of the Prophet ﷺ that one who believes in Allah and the Last Day should maintain the bond of kinship: this includes letting relatives share in good things and bringing good to them. He points out that al-Buḫārī cites again the transmission of Abū Hurayrah in the chapter on showing honor to guests, and that the wording expressly contains the addition about maintaining kinship. This wording joins hospitality, maintenance of kinship, and good speech or silence, without making them identical duties.

HAD-0533.text: The one who maintains kinship is not the mere reciprocator; rather, it is the one who joins the tie when they sever it.
HAD-0533.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-0533.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0533.sharh: Ibn al-Mulaqqin explains the report about the one who truly maintains kinship in the chapter “The one who merely reciprocates is not the one who joins the tie.” Mere return of a prior kind act by relatives is reciprocity, not the especially praised independent maintenance of the bond of kinship. Exemplary, rather, is the one who continues to treat relatives well even when they have broken off contact. Ibn al-Mulaqqin also cites a corresponding statement of ʿUmar; because of the anonymous intermediary, the chain given for it is not to be treated as an authentic Aṯar without an independent examination of the Isnād.

HAD-0534.text: Whoever wishes that his provision be expanded and his trace prolonged should maintain his kinship ties.
HAD-0534.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0534.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0534.sharh: An-Nawawī explains, concerning the report of Anas, that the expansion of provision can denote both an increase of wealth and its blessing. He first explains the “deferral of the trace” (yunsaʾ lahu fī aṯarih) by lifespan. He then discusses the relation to the fixed divine decree: the scholars mention, for example, blessing in the years of life and the possibility that only conditional indications are visible to creatures, while Allah’s knowledge remains unchanged. The prolongation through maintenance of kinship must therefore not be presented as an arbitrary change of Allah’s foreknowledge.

HAD-0535.text: The strong one is not the wrestler; strong is he who controls himself when angry.
HAD-0535.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0535.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0535.sharh: Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr explains, in his commentary on the report of Abū Hurayrah transmitted by Mālik, the special importance of self-control in anger. The original wording uses “ṣuraʿah” for the one who overpowers others in wrestling. The strength highlighted by the Prophet ﷺ consists, by contrast, in controlling oneself in the state of anger. The comparison does not deny the physical strength of the wrestler; it places above it the inner strength that is especially meritorious for character. The report is transmitted in Muslim, no. 2609.

HAD-0536.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0536.speaker: A man said: Give me advice. The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0536.sharh: Ibn Raǧab presents this Ḥadīṯ as the sixteenth report of his collection. A man repeatedly asked the Prophet ﷺ for advice; the answer remained each time: “Do not become angry.” The commentary treats control of the reaction of anger as a summarizing moral instruction. It concerns not acting upon uncontrolled anger, and protection from the misdeeds that follow from it. The repeated question and the unchanged answer belong to the complete authentic wording of Buḫārī, not merely the isolated German two-word sentence.

HAD-0537.text: Fear Allah wherever you are, and follow a bad deed with a good one that effaces it.
HAD-0537.narrator: Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0537.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0537.sharh: Ibn Raǧab sets side by side the three connected instructions of the Ḥadīṯ: fear of Allah in every place, following a bad deed with a good one that effaces its effect, and treating people with good character. The first two commands concern the relationship with Allah and dealing with one’s own misdeeds; the third concerns the relationship with other people. Ibn Raǧab also records differing chains in which Abū Ḏarr or Muʿāḏ ibn Ǧabal is named; the precise assessment of individual chains remains the subject of his critique of transmission. This entry cites only part of the shared Ḥadīṯ.

HAD-0538.narrator: Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0538.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0538.sharh: Ibn Raǧab comments on this sentence as the third component of a Ḥadīṯ in which fear of Allah and the following of a bad deed by a good one are commanded first. Treating other people well forms a duty of its own that complements personal piety. The sentence “Treat people with good character” is therefore not an independent second prophetic saying alongside HAD-0537, but part of the same transmission. In the transmission, various Isnād wordings through Abū Ḏarr and Muʿāḏ are transmitted.

HAD-0539.text: The most complete believer in Īmān is the one with the best character.
HAD-0539.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0539.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0539.sharh: Aṭ-Ṭaḥāwī cites, for the wording “The most complete of the believers in faith are those with the best character,” two independent chains through Abū Hurayrah. One wording additionally contains the statement that the best among the believers are those who treat their wives best. Aṭ-Ṭaḥāwī comments that “ḫuluq” means a trait of character rooted in people, which is present more strongly in some believers than in others and therefore constitutes a special virtue. According to this interpretation, the importance of good character for the completeness of faith follows from the wording; the differences of rank among individual persons are not to be determined solely by an outward manner of conduct.

HAD-0540.text: I guarantee a house at the edge of Paradise for the one who abandons dispute, even if he is in the right.
HAD-0540.narrator: Abū Umāmah al-Bāhilī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0540.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0540.sharh: An-Nawawī cites the transmission of Abū Umāmah with the three promising statements and expressly explains the Arabic word “zaʿīm” as a guarantor. The prophetic promise thereby becomes clear: a house at the edge of Paradise for one who refrains from quarrelsome dispute, even if he is in the right; a house in the middle for the one who leaves off lying even in jest; and a house in the upper part for a person of good character. Ibn al-Qayyim calls the transmission ṣaḥīḥ in his commentary on the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd. The explanation thus covers three distinct virtues and is not limited to abandoning dispute. The earlier Buḫārī HAD field contained only the first promise as a short version.

HAD-0541.text: Stop where the people stopped, for they stopped with knowledge.
HAD-0541.narrator: It is transmitted of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz رحمه الله:
HAD-0541.speaker: He said:

HAD-0542.text: Take for yourself the religion of the early ones, for they were upon the straight path.
HAD-0542.narrator: It is transmitted of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz رحمه الله:
HAD-0542.speaker: He said:

HAD-0543.text: If it is reported to you about a man in the East that he is upon the Sunnah, then send him Salām.
HAD-0543.narrator: It is transmitted of Sufyān aṯ-Ṯawrī رحمه الله:
HAD-0543.speaker: He said:

HAD-0544.text: Today the one who calls to the Sunnah is stranger than the Sunnah itself.
HAD-0544.narrator: It is transmitted of Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd رحمه الله:
HAD-0544.speaker: He said:

HAD-0545.text: Among the felicities of a young man is that Allah leads him to a scholar of the Sunnah.
HAD-0545.narrator: It is transmitted of Ayyūb as-Saḫtiyānī رحمه الله:
HAD-0545.speaker: He said:

HAD-0425.text: Because of intense heat, some placed, during Suǧūd, the end of their garment on the place of prostration.
HAD-0425.narrator: ʿAnas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0425.speaker: He said:
HAD-0425.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains the report of Anas that the Companions, in extreme heat, placed the ends of their garments on the place of prostration as protection from the hot ground. He distinguishes permission due to a real hardship from an unfounded abandonment of prostrating directly on the ground. He examines various fiqh views on touching a garment attached to the person praying and treats additional transmission wordings with an explicit examination of the continuity of their transmission; an addition that he describes as interrupted he does not present as an established prophetic wording.

HAD-0426.text: When asked whether the Prophet ﷺ had prayed in sandals, Anas رضي الله عنه answered: Yes.
HAD-0426.speaker: ʿAnas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-0426.sharh: Ibn Raǧab treats the question of Abū Maslamah Saʿīd ibn Yazīd al-Azdī to Anas, whether the Prophet ﷺ prayed in sandals. Anas confirmed this. The commentary presents the permission to pray in clean sandals and distinguishes between basic permissibility and regard for impurity as well as the conditions of the place of prayer. Ibn Raǧab points to the transmission paths of this short wording and also treats reservations expressed earlier against sandals in prayer.

HAD-0427.text: Jarīr رضي الله عنه wiped over the Ḫuff, then prayed, and explained that he had seen the Prophet ﷺ do the same.
HAD-0427.speaker: Jarīr ibn ʿAbdullāh رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-0427.sharh: Ibn Raǧab cites the statement of Ǧarīr ibn ʿAbdullāh, who after Wuḍūʾ wiped over his Ḫuff and then prayed. He justified his practice by the direct example of the Prophet ﷺ. The commentary stresses the time of Ǧarīr’s acceptance of Islam: because he became Muslim only later, his report was for the early scholars a strong argument against regarding the wiping over the Ḫuff as permanently abrogated by an earlier text. He expressly distinguishes wiping in Wuḍūʾ from the independent rules of praying in Ḫuff.

HAD-0428.text: He assisted the Prophet ﷺ with Wuḍūʾ; the Prophet ﷺ wiped over the Ḫuff and prayed.
HAD-0428.narrator: al-Muġīrah ibn Šuʿbah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0428.speaker: He said:
HAD-0428.sharh: Ibn Raǧab cites the further authentic report of al-Muġīrah ibn Šuʿbah in the chapter on prayer in Ḫuff: the Companion assisted the Prophet ﷺ with Wuḍūʾ; he wiped over the Ḫuff and then performed the prayer. The commentary attests prayer in such footwear as well as the legally permitted facilitation of wiping under the known conditions. The transmission is thematically related to HAD-0427, but it has an independent transmitter and must not be presented as the same chain.

HAD-0429.text: He saw a man who did not complete Rukūʿ and Suǧūd, and warned him against a prayer outside the Sunnah.
HAD-0429.speaker: He said:
HAD-0429.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl transmits in his commentary on the report of Ḥuḏayfah the explanation of al-Muhallab: the reproach “You have not prayed,” in this interpretation, denotes the serious lack of completeness in the acts of prayer. What is meant in particular is the absence of stillness and careful performance of Rukūʿ and Suǧūd. He compares this manner of expression with the statement that someone has not done a task at all if he performs it carelessly. He sets this linguistic and fiqh interpretation over against the report about the man whom the Prophet ﷺ commanded to repeat his incomplete prayer. The jurists further differ as to whether and when the deficiency invalidates the prayer; Ibn Baṭṭāl’s interpretation must not silently be called an undisputed Iǧmāʿ.

HAD-0430.text: When the Prophet ﷺ prayed, he kept his arms away from his body in Suǧūd until the brightness of his armpits became visible.
HAD-0430.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Mālik ibn Buḥaynah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0430.speaker: He said:
HAD-0430.sharh: Ibn al-Mulaqqin comments on the report of ʿAbdullāh ibn Mālik ibn Buḥaynah concerning the bodily posture of the Prophet ﷺ in prostration. The Prophet ﷺ kept his arms away from his body, so that the brightness of his armpits became visible. The commentator describes keeping the arms apart in prostration as a recommended posture; if someone does not observe this manner of holding the arms, his prayer is not invalidated by that alone. He cites earlier statements, among them those of ʿAlī, al-Barāʾ, Ibn Masʿūd, Abū Saʿīd and Ibn ʿUmar. The explanation expressly distinguishes the recommended bodily posture from the acts indispensable for the validity of the prayer.

HAD-0431.text: Whoever prays as we pray, accepts our Qiblah and eats our slaughter stands under the protection of Allah and of His Messenger.
HAD-0431.narrator: ʿAnas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0431.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-0431.sharh: Ibn Raǧab cites the prophetic report of Anas about praying as the Muslims pray, facing the Qiblah and eating their lawfully slaughtered animals. Central is the expressly assured inviolability of the person who is outwardly recognized as a Muslim; no one may break the granted duty of protection on his own authority. In his commentary Ibn Raǧab explains the mentioned signs as an expression of belonging to the visible obligations of faith. The Qiblah, according to him, makes clear conformity with the Islamic prayer, while eating the slaughtered animals together, in his argument at that time, stands for accepting the religious order of the community. His more extensive legal conclusions are not to be equated with the literal text of the Ḥadīṯ; classifying a particular person requires separate conditions and cannot be done from a shortened quotation alone.

HAD-0432.text: Whoever utters the testimony of faith, prays as we pray and accepts our Qiblah, his blood and property are protected, except by right.
HAD-0432.narrator: ʿAnas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0432.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0432.sharh: Ibn Raǧab treats the second transmission from Anas with the wording about the Schahādah, the Islamic prayer, facing the Qiblah and the recognition of Muslim slaughter. The report stresses the inviolability of life and property under the protection of the Islamic legal order, with the reservation, named in the authentic wording, of legally grounded claims. His commentary shows that al-Buḫārī cites this wording as an independent transmission path on the subject of outwardly recognizable belonging. The differing wordings of the transmission paths must not be fused into a single literal quotation. From a historical report about regulations of state and religion there follows no authority for private persons to use violence or to carry out judgments on individuals on their own authority.

HAD-0433.text: Maymūn ibn Siyāh asked Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه by what a person’s life and property are protected. Anas named the testimony that none is worthy of worship except Allah, facing the Qiblah, performing the prayer of the Muslims and taking part in their permitted slaughter. Whoever thus recognizably belongs to the community has, according to his statement, the rights and duties of the Muslims.
HAD-0433.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه answered the question of Maymūn ibn Siyāh:
