HAD-0433.speaker: Anas رضي الله عنه said:

HAD-0434.text: The Prophet ﷺ forbade facing directly toward the Qiblah or turning directly away from it when relieving oneself. He instructed the people of his region to turn instead toward the east or the west. Abū Ayyūb reported that in aš-Šām they found latrines already built facing the Qiblah; therefore they turned aside from them and asked Allah for forgiveness.
HAD-0434.narrator: Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0434.speaker: He reported:
HAD-0434.sharh: Ibn Raǧab here presents the report of Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī about the orientation when going to the toilet. The passage shows the special standing of the Qiblah in the practice of prayer and the distinction from everyday relieving oneself. The wording “toward the east or the west” is addressed to people whose Qiblah does not lie geographically in that direction; it is not a universal compass direction for every place. The sideways turn at existing latrines described by Abū Ayyūb makes clear the practical observance of the prohibition. The earlier HAD-0434 text about the change of the prayer Qiblah was a misattribution and does not belong to Buḫārī no. 394.

HAD-0435.text: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār asked Ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما whether a pilgrim, after the Ṭawāf of the ʿUmrah but before the Saʿy between aṣ-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, may approach his wife in marital intimacy. Ibn ʿUmar recalled the example of the Prophet ﷺ: he circumambulated the Kaʿbah seven times, performed two Rakʿah behind Maqām Ibrāhīm and then went between aṣ-Ṣafā and al-Marwah. Ibn ʿUmar pointed out that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is the model.
HAD-0435.narrator: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār reported from his question to Ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-0435.speaker: Ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما answered:
HAD-0435.sharh: Ibn Raǧab cites the question of ʿAmr ibn Dīnār to Ibn ʿUmar about the Saʿy not yet completed after the ʿUmrah-Ṭawāf. Ibn ʿUmar answered the question by the action of the Prophet ﷺ, who first circumambulated the Kaʿbah seven times, then prayed two Rakʿah behind Maqām Ibrāhīm and thereafter performed the Saʿy. The sequence attests the place of the prayer behind the Maqām in the course of the pilgrimage rite; the separate legal answer of Ǧābir concerning marital relations stands in the following transmission no. 396. The transmission is reported by ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, not by Muǧāhid.

HAD-0436.text: When asked whether a pilgrim, after the Ṭawāf of the ʿUmrah, may approach his wife before he has completed the Saʿy between aṣ-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdullāh رضي الله عنه answered: He should not approach her until he has finished the Saʿy.
HAD-0436.narrator: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār reported from their question to Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdullāh رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0436.speaker: Ǧābir رضي الله عنه answered:

HAD-0437.text: Ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما learned that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had entered the Kaʿbah. When Ibn ʿUmar arrived, the Prophet ﷺ had already come out. He asked Bilāl رضي الله عنه, who was standing by the door, whether the Prophet ﷺ had prayed in the Kaʿbah. Bilāl affirmed this and described two Rakʿah between the two columns to the left of the entrance. After going out, the Prophet ﷺ performed two Rakʿah again in front of the Kaʿbah.
HAD-0437.narrator: Muǧāhid reported about Ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما and his inquiry to Bilāl رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0437.speaker: Bilāl رضي الله عنه explained:
HAD-0437.sharh: Ibn Raǧab places the report about Ibn ʿUmar’s question to Bilāl concerning the prayer in the Kaʿbah among the transmissions on the direction of prayer and on Maqām Ibrāhīm. The report expressly records that Bilāl, as an eyewitness, confirmed that the Prophet ﷺ had performed two Rakʿah inside the Kaʿbah between two columns. After leaving, two Rakʿah followed facing the Kaʿbah. The distinction between Bilāl’s confirmed observation and Ibn ʿUmar’s later inquiry prevents falsely making Ibn ʿUmar an eyewitness of the prayer inside the Kaʿbah.

HAD-0438.text: The Prophet ﷺ entered the Kaʿbah, made Duʿāʾ in its sides and said after the prayer in front of it: This is the Qiblah.
HAD-0438.narrator: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-0438.speaker: He said:
HAD-0438.sharh: Ibn Raǧab cites the transmission of Ibn ʿAbbās, according to which the Prophet ﷺ made Duʿāʾ at various places inside the Kaʿbah and performed the prayer only after going out. After leaving, he prayed two Rakʿah toward the Kaʿbah and called it the Qiblah. The commentary places this wording in the same chapter as the report of Bilāl, according to which the Prophet ﷺ had prayed inside the Kaʿbah. Both reports must be examined according to their different transmitters and their level of knowledge; it is inadmissible in source criticism, from mere juxtaposition without additional evidence, to construct an invented chronological order of two events.

HAD-0439.text: The Prophet ﷺ first prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis; thereafter, after revelation, he turned toward the Kaʿbah.
HAD-0439.narrator: al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0439.speaker: He said:
HAD-0439.sharh: Ibn Raǧab treats, in the chapter on the obligatory facing of the Qiblah, the report of al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib. The Prophet ﷺ first prayed for sixteen or seventeen months toward Bayt al-Maqdis. After the revelation of the new Qiblah he turned toward the Kaʿbah. One of those praying with him then informed a group of the Anṣār who were just performing the ʿAṣr prayer; those praying changed their direction still during the prayer. The statement “sixteen or seventeen months” remains as a genuine uncertainty of the transmission. The action documents the implementation of the new instruction after a reliable report; the details of present-day legal cases are to be decided separately.

HAD-0440.text: The Prophet ﷺ prayed voluntary prayers on his mount, whichever way it turned; for the obligatory prayer he dismounted and faced the Qiblah.
HAD-0440.narrator: Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0440.speaker: He said:
HAD-0440.sharh: Ibn Raǧab places the report of Ǧābir about the direction of prayer on the mount in the chapter on facing the Qiblah. The Prophet ﷺ performed voluntary prayers on his mount even when it was not facing the Qiblah. For the obligatory prayers, by contrast, he dismounted and prayed facing the Qiblah. This distinction shows that the facilitation in voluntary prayer while traveling must not be transferred to all obligatory prayers without separate evidence. Other special circumstances, such as compelling danger or inability, must be examined separately according to their respective proofs.

HAD-0441.text: Abū Ḥumayd as-Sāʿidī رضي الله عنه described the prayer of the Prophet ﷺ: in prostration he set his hands upright without placing the forearms on the ground, and he directed the tips of his toes toward the Qiblah.
HAD-0441.narrator: Abū Ḥumayd as-Sāʿidī رضي الله عنه reported about the prayer of the Prophet ﷺ:
HAD-0441.speaker: He reported:
HAD-0441.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that al-Buḫārī cites in abbreviated form, in the chapter heading, the reference to Abū Ḥumayd’s description of the position of the toes toward the Qiblah, and reproduces the complete Ḥadīṯ later with a chain of transmission. It is a detail of the prostration (Suǧūd): the Prophet ﷺ directed the tips of the toes toward the Qiblah, while the position of his hands is described separately. The commentary is therefore not to be rendered as an independent opinion of a Companion or as an unevidenced new rule of prayer.

HAD-0442.text: al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī رحمه الله reported about the early Muslims: “They used to prostrate on their turban or their head covering, while their hands were in the sleeves.”
HAD-0442.narrator: It is transmitted from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī رحمه الله:
HAD-0442.speaker: He said:

HAD-0443.text: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه prayed on the roof of the mosque and thereby followed the Imām in prayer.
HAD-0443.narrator: It is transmitted from Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0443.speaker: He acted accordingly:

HAD-0444.text: It is reported of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما that he prayed on snow.
HAD-0444.narrator: It is transmitted from Ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-0444.speaker: He acted accordingly:

HAD-0546.text: Know that Islam is the Sunnah and the Sunnah is Islam.
HAD-0546.narrator: It is transmitted from al-Barbahārī رحمه الله:
HAD-0546.speaker: He said:

HAD-0547.text: If you see a man who loves the Āṯār, then hope good for him.
HAD-0547.narrator: It is transmitted from al-Barbahārī رحمه الله:
HAD-0547.speaker: He said:

HAD-0548.text: The earlier scholars said: Holding fast to the Sunnah is salvation.
HAD-0548.narrator: It is transmitted from Ibn Šihāb az-Zuhrī رحمه الله:
HAD-0548.speaker: He said:

HAD-0549.text: The Sunnah is like the ark of Nūḥ: whoever boards it is saved.
HAD-0549.narrator: It is transmitted from Mālik ibn Anas رحمه الله:
HAD-0549.speaker: He said:

HAD-0550.text: Be patient upon the Sunnah, and stop where the people before you stopped.
HAD-0550.narrator: It is transmitted from al-Awzāʿī رحمه الله:
HAD-0550.speaker: He said:

HAD-0551.text: Deeds are only according to intentions, and each person has only what he intended.
HAD-0551.narrator: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0551.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0551.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that the validity and the worth of deeds depend on the intention. He distinguishes the intention by which a deed is marked off as a particular act of worship, apart from another deed, from sincerity toward Allah. The emigration cited in the report shows that outwardly identical deeds acquire, through different aims, different legal meanings and meanings for the Hereafter. The statement does not make an outwardly forbidden deed lawful by a good intention alone.

HAD-0552.text: The lawful is clear and the forbidden is clear; between them lie doubtful things.
HAD-0552.narrator: an-Nuʿmān ibn Bašīr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0552.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0552.sharh: Ibn Raǧab cites the narration of an-Nuʿmān ibn Bašīr as the basis for distinguishing between what is clearly lawful, what is clearly forbidden, and doubtful matters. Whoever stays away from unclear borderline cases protects his religion and his honor. The comparison with the shepherd near a forbidden pasture explains the danger of gradually slipping into what is forbidden. The Ḥadīṯ joins this to the condition of the heart: its soundness is central to the soundness of action.

HAD-0553.narrator: Tamīm ad-Dārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0553.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0553.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains an-Naṣīḥah as sincere fidelity and a benevolent fulfillment of duties toward Allah, His Book, His Messenger, those in authority, and the rest of the Muslims. He distinguishes between obligatory and additional forms of this sincerity. Naṣīḥah for the Qurʾān comprises holding it in honor, striving to understand it, and acting according to it; toward people this includes conveying knowledge, warding off harm, and gently correcting errors. The short form “The religion is sincere counsel” therefore comprises more than occasional personal advice.

HAD-0554.text: Part of a person’s good Islam is that he leaves what does not concern him.
HAD-0554.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0554.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0555.text: Leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt.
HAD-0555.narrator: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-0555.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0555.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains the principle transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ by way of al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī: to leave a matter that carries justified doubt in favor of what does not give rise to such doubt. He sets this as a standard of truthfulness, of certainty, and of caution in dealing with questionable matters. The wording concerns a doubt that is to be taken seriously; it does not require that baseless whisperings or recurring Waswās be treated as binding legal doubts.

HAD-0556.text: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should honor his guest.
HAD-0556.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0556.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0556.sharh: Ibn Raǧab treats, in his fifteenth Ḥadīṯ, the connection between faith and conduct toward one’s fellow people. Showing honor to a guest is one of three instructions bound to belief in Allah and the Last Day; the same complete report mentions speaking well or remaining silent, and showing honor to the neighbor. The short excerpt on hospitality thus stands within a broader moral instruction. It matches the content already documented under HAD-0531 and is not presented as a new, independently transmitted saying of the Prophet.

HAD-0557.text: The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe.
HAD-0557.narrator: Abū Mūsā رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0557.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0557.sharh: Al-Baġawī presents the report of Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī with an explicit chain of transmission and calls it authentic by agreement. He explains the question “Which Islam is the best?” as a question about which qualities and deeds of Islam are the most excellent. The prophetic answer especially brings out that other Muslims must be safe from a person’s tongue and hand. This does not mean that the remaining duties of the religion would be without significance; the expression describes a particularly important quality of righteous Muslims.

HAD-0558.text: None of you believes completely until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
HAD-0558.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0558.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0558.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains the principle transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ through Anas: complete Īmān includes loving for one’s brother the good that one loves for oneself. The negation of Īmān uttered in the report denotes, according to his explicit interpretation, the lack of completeness of faith and does not here automatically mean departure from Islam. He brings in further authentic wordings that also mention the neighbor, and he distinguishes the obligatory principle of goodwill from envy and from the wish to withhold good from others.

HAD-0559.text: The strong one is not the wrestler; the strong one is he who controls himself when angry.
HAD-0559.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0559.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0559.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains the linguistic meaning of “ṣuraʿah”: what is meant is a man who can physically throw down many others. The Prophet ﷺ moved the measure of true strength from this outward ability to mastery of one’s own anger. Ibn Ḥaǧar compares further transmitted wordings and explains why self-control precisely at the moment of surging anger shows a greater inner strength. The Ḥadīṯ is not a blanket devaluation of physical strength, but a reweighting of the decisive quality.

HAD-0560.text: Gentleness is not found in anything except that it beautifies it.
HAD-0560.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0560.sharh: Al-Qurṭubī treats the statement of ʿĀʾišah, according to which gentleness adorns a matter and its removal disfigures it. The rule teaches a careful manner of dealing, especially where the same lawful aim can be reached without unnecessary harshness. Al-Qurṭubī sets reasoned address, fitting the person addressed, over against hasty, harsh action. The report is a repetition in substance of HAD-0521, and so no second independent narration is claimed here.

HAD-0561.text: Allah is gentle and loves gentleness.
HAD-0561.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0561.sharh: An-Nawawī discusses, with the authentic report of ʿĀʾišah, Allah’s love of gentleness and the special reward of a mild, deliberate deed. The same principle stands in connection with the report that gentleness beautifies a matter and harshness disfigures it. The short statement describes a virtue in dealing with people, without the necessary religious limits being set aside thereby. The content overlaps with HAD-0462, which contains the same saying under the same Muslim number.

HAD-0562.text: Whoever relieves a believer of one hardship among the hardships of this world, Allah relieves him of a hardship on the Day of Resurrection.
HAD-0562.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0562.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0562.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains the long report of Abū Hurayrah about help for believers: whoever relieves or removes a worldly distress of a believer, to him Allah promises relief in a distress of the Day of Resurrection. The special emphasis on that Day underscores how great is one’s need for divine help. The report mentions further kinds of help, among them relief for the needy, covering the faults of others, and the pursuit of knowledge. The HAD entry abbreviated here is thus only a part of the same longer narration as HAD-0512.

HAD-0563.text: Whoever covers a Muslim, Allah covers him in this world and in the Hereafter.
HAD-0563.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0563.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0563.sharh: Ibn Raǧab treats the covering of a Muslim’s faults as one of the deeds for which Allah promises covering and sparing in this world and the Hereafter. Covering does not mean that harmful deeds are to be continued, the rights of others violated, or wrong concealed without remedy; it is to be understood in connection with sincerity, the avoidance of exposure, and protection from harm. This entry is an excerpt from the same authentic Muslim narration as HAD-0514.

HAD-0564.text: Whoever points to something good receives the same reward as the one who does it.
HAD-0564.narrator: Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0564.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0564.sharh: Al-Qurṭubī explains the report in which a man pointed out a way to help a traveler whose mount had become unfit. The promise “Whoever points to good receives reward like the one who acts” covers participation through meaningful direction, even when the one who points does not himself perform the good deed. Al-Qurṭubī expressly discusses the extent of this equality of reward and leaves open the possibility that Allah recompenses both equally, since the reward is His favor. This interpretation is not to be presented as a deduction from the reward of the one who actually acts, nor as a guaranteed individual sum.

HAD-0565.narrator: Abū Mālik al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0565.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0565.sharh: Ibn Raǧab places the sentence transmitted from Abū Mālik al-Ašʿarī, “Purification is half of Īmān,” at the beginning of his explanation of the 23rd Ḥadīṯ. He examines differing earlier explanations of “purification” and “half,” and he sets outward ritual purification in connection with inward purification. The wording belongs to a longer report about Ḏikr, prayer, Ṣadaqah, patience, and the role of the Qurʾān. The entry is identical in content with HAD-0528; the repeated short form is not treated as an independent prophetic occurrence.

HAD-0506.text: The believer joins good action with fear, and the hypocrite joins bad action with a sense of security.
HAD-0506.narrator: It is transmitted from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī رحمه الله:
HAD-0506.speaker: He said:

HAD-0507.text: I met people who regarded the Duʿāʾ as the weapon of the believer.
HAD-0507.narrator: It is transmitted from Ṭāwūs ibn Kaysān رحمه الله:
HAD-0507.speaker: He said:

HAD-0508.text: The believer observes, reflects, and lets himself be awakened by admonition.
HAD-0508.narrator: It is transmitted from Wahb ibn Munabbih رحمه الله:
HAD-0508.speaker: He said:

HAD-0509.text: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib رحمه الله said: “The servants honor themselves by nothing more than by obedience to Allah, and they abase themselves by nothing more than by disobedience to Him.”
HAD-0509.narrator: It is transmitted from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib رحمه الله:
HAD-0509.speaker: He said:

HAD-0510.text: Be patient upon the Sunnah, and halt where the people before you halted.
HAD-0510.narrator: It is transmitted from al-Awzāʿī رحمه الله:
HAD-0510.speaker: He said:

HAD-0511.text: The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim. He does not wrong him and does not leave him unprotected to the one who harms him. Whoever attends to the needs of his brother, Allah fulfills his need; whoever removes a distress from a Muslim, Allah removes from him a distress on the Day of Resurrection; and whoever covers a Muslim, Allah covers him on the Day of Resurrection.
HAD-0511.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-0511.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0511.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains that Islamic brotherhood includes both the prohibition of wronging a Muslim and the duty not to leave him to those who harm him. The wording “lā yuslimuhu” means that he does not expose his brother to danger. Which support is specifically obligatory or recommended depends on the circumstances and on ability. Ibn Ḥaǧar also treats the help in needs and distresses mentioned in the same report. As an earlier interpretation, Ibn Baṭṭāl is cited by al-ʿAynī with the statement that helping the oppressed is in principle a collective duty, while with the competent authority it is a special task; this passage of Ibn Baṭṭāl is present here only as a reviewed secondary transmission.

HAD-0512.text: Whoever removes a worry of a believer from the worries of this world, Allah removes from him a worry of the Day of Resurrection.
HAD-0512.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0512.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0512.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains the severe distress (kurbah) and distinguishes its relief (tanfīs) from its complete removal (tafrīǧ). The report promises, for help given to a believer in a worldly hardship, a corresponding relief on the Day of Resurrection. The commentary places this under the principle that recompense corresponds to the kind of deed. The wording cited here is part of a longer authentic report in Muslim.

HAD-0513.text: Whoever grants relief to someone in need, Allah grants him relief in this world and in the Hereafter.
HAD-0513.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0513.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0513.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains the sentence about granting relief to a person in financial difficulty. He distinguishes two ways: giving the debtor respite until he is able to pay, and remitting the debt wholly or in part. He additionally grounds the required respite in Qurʾān 2:280; remission and further help are especially meritorious forms of relief. The statement concerns real hardships, not a demand to abandon legitimate claims in every situation.

HAD-0514.text: Whoever covers the faults of a Muslim, Allah covers his faults in this world and in the Hereafter.
HAD-0514.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0514.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0514.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains the covering of a Muslim’s faults and distinguishes the hidden lapse of an otherwise inconspicuous person from cases in which someone publicly and continually harms others. The unnecessary disclosure of private sins is disapproved. The rule, however, does not serve to conceal wrong against others; where warding off harm and safeguarding rights is required, the situation is to be judged differently.

HAD-0515.text: Allah helps the servant as long as the servant helps his brother.
HAD-0515.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0515.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0515.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains the prophetic promise that Allah helps the servant as long as he helps his brother, in connection with the related statement about support in the brother’s needs. He names help in legitimate concerns as a meritorious deed. The promise is not a license to help someone in wrongdoing. The sentence belongs to the longer authentic Ḥadīṯ in Muslim and repeats the principle that good is repaid with corresponding good.

HAD-0516.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ explained: Whoever calls others to right guidance receives a reward like the rewards of all who follow him in that, without their own reward being diminished.
HAD-0516.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0516.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0516.sharh: an-Nawawī explains that the call to right guidance is not limited to introducing something for the first time: whoever calls to right teaching or good action already known can likewise receive the reward that Allah grants to those who follow, without their reward being reduced. He gives as examples the conveying of knowledge, worship, and good conduct. Corresponding to this, in the same report, is the opposite warning about spreading misguidance. A mere call does not establish a license for invented religious practices.

HAD-0517.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ explained: Whoever calls others to misguidance bears sin corresponding to the sins of those who follow him in that, without their own responsibility becoming less.
HAD-0517.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0517.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0517.sharh: an-Nawawī discusses this second half of the same authentic report together with the call to right guidance. Whoever leads others into error or sinful action bears additional responsibility for the people who follow him; the personal guilt of those who follow is not thereby removed. The interpretation covers both failings spread for the first time and those already known. This wording and HAD-0516 come from the same longer prophetic statement; they are marked as two excerpts, not as two transmissions independent of each other.

HAD-0518.text: Whoever is not merciful to people, Allah is not merciful to him.
HAD-0518.narrator: Ǧarīr ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0518.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0518.sharh: an-Nawawī explains the saying “Whoever does not show mercy to people, Allah does not show mercy to him” as a general principle. According to the understanding of the scholars which he cites, the wording does not cover children alone, although the same chapter reports the loving conduct of the Prophet ﷺ toward children, but likewise other people. The Ḥadīṯ is transmitted from Ǧarīr ibn ʿAbdullāh in Muslim (no. 2319); the neighboring report of Abū Hurayrah about al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis is another wording of the principle, not the same chain of transmitters.

HAD-0519.text: Mercy is withdrawn only from one who is wretched.
HAD-0519.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0519.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0519.sharh: ʿAlī al-Qārī explains the phrase “Mercy is withdrawn only from one who is wretched” as a description of a person who has lost compassionate care for Allah’s creatures. He expressly counts gentle treatment of one’s own person as part of mercy as well. According to his explanation, kindness toward others benefits the one who acts, because it is a cause of Allah’s mercy toward him. He explains the expression “ša qī” as a wretched person or one who acts sinfully. This explanation of the word is a moral warning and not an individually applicable judgment declaring a specific person a Kāfir because of a lack of kindness.

HAD-0521.text: Gentleness enters no matter without adorning it, and it is removed from no matter without marring it.
HAD-0521.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0521.sharh: Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Qurṭubī explains this statement in connection with the conduct of the Prophet ﷺ and the reward for gentle action. What could be attained in a lawful manner both by harshness and by gentleness should preferably be sought with care; gentleness thereby improves the manner of dealing and the consequences of the action. Excessive harshness and hasty procedure can, by contrast, cause harm. The report does not teach a general prohibition of necessary, lawful firmness, but highlights the precedence of gentleness.

HAD-0522.text: Whoever is withheld gentleness is thereby withheld good.
HAD-0522.narrator: Ǧarīr ibn ʿAbdullāh رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0522.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0522.sharh: Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Qurṭubī interprets this report transmitted from Ǧarīr ibn ʿAbdullāh together with the statement about the adornment of gentleness. Whoever always lets himself be led by harshness and rash conduct misses good in dealing with people and, in some circumstances, reward in the Hereafter as well. The warning concerns missing the gentleness that is due, not the claim that a single harsh act irrevocably takes all good from a person. The name ʿĀʾišah, hitherto wrongly given as the female transmitter, was corrected on the basis of the source in Muslim.

HAD-0523.text: Wealth is not abundance of possessions; rather, true wealth is the wealth of the soul.
HAD-0523.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0523.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0523.sharh: an-Nawawī explains the word “ʿaraḍ” in the Ḥadīṯ as the perishable possession of this world. The praiseworthy “ġināʾ”, true wealth, consists according to his interpretation in the contentment of the heart, its satisfaction, and little desire for still more property. Whoever, despite wealth already present, continually seeks more does not, according to this explanation, possess the inner independence praised in the Ḥadīṯ. This is an interpretation of the authentic prophetic statement and not a blanket condemnation of material possession.

HAD-0525.text: The best Ṣadaqah is a gift after which the giver still has the necessary provision. Begin with those whose maintenance you are responsible for.
HAD-0525.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0525.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0525.sharh: Al-Bayhaqī sets the authentic statement about the best gift from a remaining sufficiency over against the other report about the special effort of a person with little property. He expressly explains that the assessment differs according to life circumstances and the ability to bear scarcity and poverty with patience. The principle of the Buḫārī report cited here is that after the voluntary gift enough remains for basic provision and that the maintenance of one’s own dependents has priority. The previous German text wrongly claimed that the gift in need was generally the best; this contradicted the phrase “عن ظهر غنى” and was corrected.

HAD-0726.text: Whoever shows people no mercy, to him no mercy is shown.
HAD-0726.narrator: Ǧarīr ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0726.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0727.text: Whoever points to good receives a reward like that of the one who does it.
HAD-0727.narrator: Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0727.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0728.text: Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most lying speech.
HAD-0728.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0728.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0729.text: Whoever is not grateful to people is not grateful to Allah.
HAD-0729.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0729.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0730.text: Allah has prescribed Iḥsān in every matter.
HAD-0730.narrator: Šaddād ibn Aws رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0730.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0731.text: Deeds are only according to intentions, and each person is due only what he intended.
HAD-0731.narrator: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0731.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0732.text: The lawful is clear and the forbidden is clear; between them lie doubtful matters.
HAD-0732.narrator: an-Nuʿmān ibn Bašīr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0732.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0733.narrator: Tamīm ad-Dārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0733.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0734.text: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or remain silent.
HAD-0734.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0734.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0735.text: The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe.
HAD-0735.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0735.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0736.text: None of you believes completely until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
HAD-0736.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0736.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0737.text: A strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than a weak one; in both there is good.
HAD-0737.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0737.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0738.text: A person should leave what does not concern him; that belongs to good Islām.
HAD-0738.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0738.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0739.text: Your smile in the face of your brother is a charity.
HAD-0739.narrator: Abū Dharr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0739.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0740.text: Purity is a part of Īmān.
HAD-0740.narrator: Abū Mālik al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0740.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0741.text: Hold to the Āṯār; whoever holds fast to them is upon salvation.
HAD-0741.narrator: It is transmitted of Sahl ibn ʿAbdillāh رحمه الله:
HAD-0741.speaker: He said:

HAD-0742.text: The people of the Sunnah examine the transmitters and preserve the religion.
HAD-0742.narrator: It is transmitted of Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān رحمه الله:
HAD-0742.speaker: He said:

HAD-0743.text: The Isnāds belong to the religion; without Isnāds everyone would say what he wants.
HAD-0743.narrator: It is transmitted of ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mubārak رحمه الله:
HAD-0743.speaker: He said:

HAD-0744.text: Hold to knowledge before it is lost and its bearers depart.
HAD-0744.narrator: It is transmitted of Ibn Šihāb az-Zuhrī رحمه الله:
HAD-0744.speaker: He said:

HAD-0745.text: People need knowledge more than food and drink, for it preserves their religion.
HAD-0745.narrator: It is transmitted of al-Layṯ ibn Saʿd رحمه الله:
HAD-0745.speaker: He said:

HAD-0846.text: When I am told of the death of a man of the Sunnah, it is as if I had lost one of my limbs.
HAD-0846.narrator: It is transmitted of Ayyūb as-Saḫtiyānī رحمه الله:
HAD-0846.speaker: He said:

HAD-0847.text: In earlier times people did not ask about the Isnād; when the Fitnah occurred, they said: Name your men to us.
HAD-0847.narrator: It is transmitted of Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn رحمه الله:
HAD-0847.speaker: He said:

HAD-0848.text: Knowledge was honorable as long as it was taken from the men; when it passed into books, people who did not belong to it also took it.
HAD-0848.narrator: It is transmitted of al-Awzāʿī رحمه الله:
HAD-0848.speaker: He said:

HAD-0849.text: Knowledge does not consist in many transmissions; knowledge is a light that Allah places in the heart.
HAD-0849.narrator: It is transmitted of Mālik ibn Anas رحمه الله:
HAD-0849.speaker: He said:

HAD-0850.text: Do not speak about any matter in which you have no Imām before you.
HAD-0850.narrator: It is transmitted of Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal رحمه الله:
HAD-0850.speaker: He said:

HAD-0851.text: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent.
HAD-0851.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0851.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0852.text: The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe.
HAD-0852.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-0852.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0853.text: None of you believes completely until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
HAD-0853.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0853.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0854.text: The lawful is clear and the forbidden is clear; between them lie doubtful matters.
HAD-0854.narrator: an-Nuʿmān ibn Bašīr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0854.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0855.narrator: Tamīm ad-Dārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0855.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0856.text: Purity is a part of Īmān.
HAD-0856.narrator: Abū Mālik al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0856.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0857.text: The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer; in both there is good.
HAD-0857.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0857.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0858.text: Allah is beautiful and loves beauty.
HAD-0858.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0858.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0859.text: Whoever travels a path on which he seeks knowledge, Allah thereby makes easy for him a path to Paradise.
HAD-0859.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0859.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0860.text: Make things easy and do not make them hard; give glad tidings and do not drive away.
HAD-0860.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0860.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0861.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0861.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0862.text: The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim; he does not wrong him and does not hand him over.
HAD-0862.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-0862.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0863.text: Modesty is a part of Īmān.
HAD-0863.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0863.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0864.text: Pray as you have seen me pray.
HAD-0864.narrator: Mālik ibn al-Ḥuwayriṯ رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0864.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0865.text: You will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you do not believe completely until you love one another.
HAD-0865.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0865.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0906.text: Know that Islām is the Sunnah and the Sunnah is Islām.
HAD-0906.narrator: It is transmitted from al-Barbahārī رحمه الله:
HAD-0906.speaker: He said:

HAD-0907.text: Salvation lies in holding fast to the community and abandoning division.
HAD-0907.narrator: It is transmitted from Ibn Baṭṭah رحمه الله:
HAD-0907.speaker: He said:

HAD-0908.text: The bearer of the Qurʾān is known by his night, when people are asleep.
HAD-0908.narrator: It is transmitted from al-Āǧurrī رحمه الله:
HAD-0908.speaker: He said:

HAD-0909.text: Do not sit with the people of desires and do not argue with them; I do not feel safe that they will draw you into their misguidance.
HAD-0909.narrator: It is transmitted from Abū Qilābah رحمه الله:
HAD-0909.speaker: He said:

HAD-0910.text: The foundation of the Sunnah is that upon which the Companions of the Messenger ﷺ agreed.
HAD-0910.narrator: It is transmitted from al-Ḥumaydī رحمه الله:
HAD-0910.speaker: He said:

HAD-0911.text: The Merciful shows mercy to the merciful; show mercy to the people on the earth.
HAD-0911.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-0911.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0912.text: Whoever is not grateful to people is not grateful to Allah.
HAD-0912.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0912.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0913.text: The believer is not stung twice from the same hole.
HAD-0913.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0913.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0914.text: Part of the beauty of a person's Islām is that he leaves what does not concern him.
HAD-0914.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0914.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0915.text: The strong one is not the wrestler, but the one who controls himself in anger.
HAD-0915.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0915.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0916.text: Truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise.
HAD-0916.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0916.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0917.text: Avoid suspicion, for suspicion is the most lying speech.
HAD-0917.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0917.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0918.text: Whoever is not merciful, to him no mercy is shown.
HAD-0918.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-0918.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0919.text: Whoever introduces into this affair of ours something that does not belong to it, that is rejected.
HAD-0919.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0920.text: Allah accepts only the good; He is good and accepts only the good.
HAD-0920.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0920.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0921.text: The world is a prison for the believer and a paradise for the disbeliever.
HAD-0921.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0921.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0922.text: Whoever guarantees me what is between his jaws and his legs, I guarantee him Paradise.
HAD-0922.narrator: Sahl ibn Saʿd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0922.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0923.text: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his neighbor.
HAD-0923.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0923.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0924.text: The best of you is the one from whom good is expected and from whose evil one is safe.
HAD-0924.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0924.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0925.text: The believer is neither a reviler nor a curser, neither obscene nor shameless.
HAD-0925.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0925.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0926.text: Whoever repents of a bad deed is like someone who has no sin.
HAD-0926.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0926.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0927.text: If one of you becomes angry, let him be silent.
HAD-0927.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0927.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0928.text: Preserve Allah, then Allah will preserve you.
HAD-0928.narrator: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-0928.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0929.text: Allah does not conceal a servant’s faults in the world without concealing them on the Day of Resurrection.
HAD-0929.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0929.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0930.text: The likeness of right guidance and knowledge is like abundant rain upon different soils.
HAD-0930.narrator: Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0930.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0931.text: Whoever removes a worldly distress from a believer, Allah removes from him a distress of the Day of Resurrection.
HAD-0931.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0931.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0932.text: The best of you is the one who learns the Qurʾān and teaches it.
HAD-0932.narrator: ʿUṯmān ibn ʿAffān رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0932.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0933.text: Whoever calls to right guidance has the reward of those who follow him.
HAD-0933.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0933.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0934.text: Whoever points to good has the reward of the one who does it.
HAD-0934.narrator: Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0934.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0935.text: Each of you is a shepherd, and each is responsible for his flock.
HAD-0935.narrator: Ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-0935.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0936.text: The deeds most beloved to Allah are the most constant ones, even if they are few.
HAD-0936.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0937.text: The servant speaks a word to which he pays no heed, and it makes him fall deep into the Fire.
HAD-0937.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0937.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0938.text: Whoever fasts the fasting month of Ramaḍān in faith and in hope of reward, his past sins are forgiven.
HAD-0938.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0938.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0939.text: Between the five prayers, from Jumuʿah to Jumuʿah and from Ramaḍān to Ramaḍān, lie expiations, so long as major sins are avoided.
HAD-0939.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0939.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0940.text: The strong person is the one who controls himself in anger.
HAD-0940.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0940.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0941.text: The truth is heavy, but its outcome is praiseworthy.
HAD-0941.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0941.speaker: He said:

HAD-0942.text: Seek knowledge before it is taken away.
HAD-0942.narrator: It is transmitted from Ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0942.speaker: He said:

HAD-0943.text: People are enemies of what they do not know.
HAD-0943.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0943.speaker: He said:

HAD-0944.text: They used not to ask about the Isnād; when the Fitnah came, they said: Name your men for us.
HAD-0944.narrator: It is transmitted from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn رحمه الله:
HAD-0944.speaker: He said:

HAD-0945.text: Be patient upon the Sunnah, and stop where the people stopped.
HAD-0945.narrator: It is transmitted from al-Awzāʿī رحمه الله:
HAD-0945.speaker: He said:

HAD-0946.text: Everyone may be accepted and rejected, except the occupant of this grave ﷺ.
HAD-0946.narrator: It is transmitted from Mālik ibn Anas رحمه الله:
HAD-0946.speaker: He said:

HAD-0947.text: All people depend on the Sunnah of the Messenger ﷺ.
HAD-0947.narrator: It is transmitted from aš-Šāfiʿī رحمه الله:
HAD-0947.speaker: He said:

HAD-0948.text: Whoever rejects the Ḥadīṯ of the Messenger ﷺ stands at the brink of ruin.
HAD-0948.narrator: It is transmitted from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal رحمه الله:
HAD-0948.speaker: He said:

HAD-0949.text: Treat people with that with which you yourself like to be treated.
HAD-0949.narrator: It is transmitted from Sufyān aṯ-Ṯawrī رحمه الله:
HAD-0949.speaker: He said:

HAD-0950.text: O son of Ādam, you are only days; when a day passes, a part of you passes.
HAD-0950.narrator: It is transmitted from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī رحمه الله:
HAD-0950.speaker: He said:

HAD-0951.text: The strong person is not the one in wrestling, but whoever controls himself when angry.
HAD-0951.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0951.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0952.text: The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe.
HAD-0952.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-0952.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0953.text: The believer to the believer is like a building: one part strengthens the other.
HAD-0953.narrator: Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0953.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0954.text: None of you believes completely until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
HAD-0954.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0954.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0955.text: Whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah.
HAD-0955.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0955.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0956.text: Part of the beauty of a person’s Islam is that he leaves what does not concern him.
HAD-0956.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0956.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0957.text: Allah is gentle and loves gentleness in all matters.
HAD-0957.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0958.text: Wealth is not an abundance of goods; true wealth is the wealth of the soul.
HAD-0958.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0958.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0959.text: Whoever removes from a believer one distress of the distresses of this world, from him Allah removes a distress of the Day of Resurrection.
HAD-0959.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0959.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0960.text: Truthfulness leads to piety, and piety leads to Paradise.
HAD-0960.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0960.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0961.text: Beware of envy; for envy consumes good deeds as fire consumes wood.
HAD-0961.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0961.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0962.text: Make things easy and do not make them difficult; give glad tidings and do not drive away.
HAD-0962.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0962.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0963.text: The best of you is the one from whom good is expected and from whose evil one is safe.
HAD-0963.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0963.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0964.text: The best of you is the one who learns the Qurʾān and teaches it.
HAD-0964.narrator: ʿUṯmān ibn ʿAffān رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0964.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0965.text: The All-Merciful shows mercy to the merciful; be merciful to those on the earth.
HAD-0965.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-0965.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0986.text: How many want the good, yet do not attain it.
HAD-0986.narrator: It is transmitted from Ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0986.speaker: He said:

HAD-0987.text: The Qurʾān explains one part by another; what is unclear to you, seek it in its context.
HAD-0987.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-0987.speaker: He said:

HAD-0988.text: The earth sanctifies no one; rather, only a person’s deed sanctifies him.
HAD-0988.narrator: It is transmitted from Salmān al-Fārisī رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0988.speaker: He said:

HAD-0989.text: Whoever purifies his intention, Allah purifies for him what is between him and the people.
HAD-0989.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0989.speaker: He said:

HAD-0990.text: The worth of every person lies in what he does well.
HAD-0990.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0990.speaker: He said:

HAD-0991.text: The believer is the one who examines himself and fears Allah.
HAD-0991.narrator: It is transmitted from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī رحمه الله:
HAD-0991.speaker: He said:

HAD-0992.text: This knowledge is religion; so look from whom you take your religion.
HAD-0992.narrator: It is transmitted from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn رحمه الله:
HAD-0992.speaker: He said:

HAD-0993.text: Nothing is harder for me to treat than my intention.
HAD-0993.narrator: It is transmitted from Sufyān aṯ-Ṯawrī رحمه الله:
HAD-0993.speaker: He said:

HAD-0994.text: The deed is not accepted until it is sincere and correct.
HAD-0994.narrator: It is transmitted from al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ رحمه الله:
HAD-0994.speaker: He said:

HAD-0995.text: Hold to the Āṯār of the Salaf, even if the people reject you.
HAD-0995.narrator: It is transmitted from al-Awzāʿī رحمه الله:
HAD-0995.speaker: He said:

HAD-0996.text: Nothing will improve the end of this Ummah except what improved its beginning.
HAD-0996.narrator: It is transmitted from Mālik ibn Anas رحمه الله:
HAD-0996.speaker: He said:

HAD-0997.text: The Isnād chain belongs to the religion; without the Isnād, anyone would say what he wishes.
HAD-0997.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mubārak رحمه الله:
HAD-0997.speaker: He said:

HAD-0998.text: The foundations of the Sunnah with us are holding fast to that upon which the Companions of the Messenger ﷺ were.
HAD-0998.narrator: It is transmitted from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal رحمه الله:
HAD-0998.speaker: He said:

HAD-0999.text: If the Ḥadīṯ is authentic, then it is my Maḏhab.
HAD-0999.narrator: It is transmitted from aš-Šāfiʿī رحمه الله:
HAD-0999.speaker: He said:

HAD-1000.text: Know that Islam is the Sunnah and the Sunnah is Islam.
HAD-1000.narrator: It is transmitted from al-Barbahārī رحمه الله:
HAD-1000.speaker: He said:

HAD-1001.text: The path of the believers is holding to the community and shunning innovation.
HAD-1001.narrator: It is transmitted from Ibn Baṭṭah رحمه الله:
HAD-1001.speaker: He said:

HAD-1002.text: The strongest means by which the servant draws near to Allah is holding fast to the Sunnah.
HAD-1002.narrator: It is transmitted from al-Lālakāʾī رحمه الله:
HAD-1002.speaker: He said:

HAD-1003.text: They detested it when a man changed his religion with every new opinion.
HAD-1003.narrator: It is transmitted from Ibrāhīm an-Naḫaʿī رحمه الله:
HAD-1003.speaker: He said:

HAD-1004.text: Take what they transmit to you from the Companions, and leave what they say from their own opinion.
HAD-1004.narrator: It is transmitted from aš-Šaʿbī رحمه الله:
HAD-1004.speaker: He said:

HAD-1005.text: The Ḥadīṯ is a trap except for the Fuqahāʾ.
HAD-1005.narrator: It is transmitted from Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah رحمه الله:
HAD-1005.speaker: He said:

HAD-1026.text: A servant speaks a word without heeding it and thereby falls into the Fire.
HAD-1026.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1026.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1027.text: Be in this world as a stranger or a wayfarer.
HAD-1027.narrator: Ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-1027.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1028.text: Whoever asks Allah for Paradise three times, Paradise says: O Allah, admit him into Paradise.
HAD-1028.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1028.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1029.text: The severest trials befall the prophets, then those nearest to them.
HAD-1029.narrator: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1029.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1030.text: Allah does not look at your bodies and your forms, but at your hearts and deeds.
HAD-1030.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1030.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1031.text: Whoever takes a path on which he seeks knowledge, Allah makes easy for him a path to Paradise.
HAD-1031.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1031.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1032.text: Whomever Allah wills good for, He grants him understanding in the religion.
HAD-1032.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1033.text: When a person dies, his work ends except in three things: ongoing Ṣadaqah, beneficial knowledge, or a righteous child who supplicates for him.
HAD-1033.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1033.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1034.text: Convey from me, even if it is only one verse.
HAD-1034.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-1034.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1035.text: Two words are light on the tongue, heavy on the Scale, and beloved to ar-Raḥmān.
HAD-1035.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1035.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1036.text: The happiest through my intercession is the one who says Lā ilāha illa Allah sincerely.
HAD-1036.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1036.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1037.text: The likeness of one who remembers his Lord and of one who does not remember Him is like the living and the dead.
HAD-1037.narrator: Abū Mūsā رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1037.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1038.text: The angels surround the people of Ḏikr, mercy covers them, and tranquility descends upon them.
HAD-1038.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1038.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1039.text: Whoever reads a letter from the Book of Allah receives for it a good deed.
HAD-1039.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1039.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1040.text: Allah has ninety-nine names; whoever preserves them enters Paradise.
HAD-1040.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1040.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1041.text: The Sunnah is like the ark of Nūḥ; whoever boards it is saved.
HAD-1041.narrator: It is reported from Mālik ibn Anas رحمه الله:
HAD-1041.speaker: He said:

HAD-1042.text: If you hear of a man in the East as an adherent of the Sunnah, send him Salām.
HAD-1042.narrator: It is reported from Sufyān aṯ-Ṯawrī رحمه الله:
HAD-1042.speaker: He said:

HAD-1043.text: Follow the paths of guidance; the small number of those who walk them does not harm you.
HAD-1043.narrator: It is reported from al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ رحمه الله:
HAD-1043.speaker: He said:

HAD-1044.text: Formerly they did not ask about the Isnād; when the Fitnah came, they said: Name your men for us.
HAD-1044.narrator: It is reported from Ibn Sīrīn رحمه الله:
HAD-1044.speaker: He said:

HAD-1045.text: Whoever rejects the Ḥadīṯ stands on the brink of destruction.
HAD-1045.narrator: It is reported from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal رحمه الله:
HAD-1045.speaker: He said:

HAD-0826.text: Allah extends His hand at night so that the sinner of the day may repent, and by day so that the sinner of the night may repent.
HAD-0826.narrator: Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0826.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0827.text: Whoever repents before the sun rises from the west, Allah accepts his repentance.
HAD-0827.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0827.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0828.text: Convey from me, even if it is only one verse.
HAD-0828.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-0828.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0829.text: May Allah make radiant the face of the one who hears a Ḥadīṯ from us, preserves it, and conveys it as he heard it.
HAD-0829.narrator: Zayd ibn Ṯābit رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0829.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0830.text: Whoever deliberately lies about me, let him take his place in the Hellfire.
HAD-0830.narrator: al-Muġīrah ibn Šuʿbah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0830.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0831.text: Whoever wishes that his provision be expanded and his life-trace be lengthened, let him maintain his ties of kinship.
HAD-0831.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0831.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0832.text: The one who severs the ties of kinship does not enter Paradise.
HAD-0832.narrator: Ǧubayr ibn Muṭʿim رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0832.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0833.text: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his guest.
HAD-0833.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0833.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0834.text: Give the road its right: lowering the gaze, withholding harm, returning the Salām, enjoining good, and forbidding evil.
HAD-0834.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0834.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0835.text: Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most lying speech.
HAD-0835.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0835.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0836.text: Do not envy one another, do not hate one another, do not turn away from one another, and be servants of Allah as brothers.
HAD-0836.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0836.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0837.text: Taqwā is here — and he pointed to his chest.
HAD-0837.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0837.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0838.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-0838.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0839.text: Your smile in the face of your brother is Ṣadaqah for you.
HAD-0839.narrator: Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0839.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0840.text: Truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise.
HAD-0840.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0840.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0841.text: There is no excuse for the one who chose misguidance while holding it to be guidance.
HAD-0841.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0841.speaker: He said:

HAD-0842.text: You are in a time with many scholars and few orators; after you comes a time with many orators and few scholars.
HAD-0842.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0842.speaker: He said:

HAD-0843.text: Knowledge does not consist in many transmissions; knowledge is fear of Allah.
HAD-0843.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0843.speaker: He said:

HAD-0844.text: Learn before knowledge is taken away; for the taking away of knowledge occurs through the death of the scholars.
HAD-0844.narrator: It is transmitted from Abū ad-Dardāʾ رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0844.speaker: He said:

HAD-0845.text: The knowledgeable one is he whose deed confirms his statement; and he whose deed contradicts his statement is blameworthy.
HAD-0845.narrator: It is transmitted from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī رحمه الله:
HAD-0845.speaker: He said:

HAD-0966.text: Whoever among you sees something reprehensible, let him change it with his hand.
HAD-0966.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0966.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0967.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0967.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0968.text: Help your brother, whether he is an oppressor or is oppressed.
HAD-0968.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0968.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0969.text: The believer is not bitten twice from the same hole.
HAD-0969.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0969.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0970.text: The lawful is clear and the forbidden is clear; between them are doubtful things.
HAD-0970.narrator: an-Nuʿmān ibn Bašīr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0970.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0971.text: Obedience to Allah is salvation, and disobedience to Him is ruin.
HAD-0971.narrator: It is transmitted from Abū Bakr aṣ-Ṣiddīq رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0971.speaker: He said:

HAD-0972.text: Call yourselves to account before you are called to account.
HAD-0972.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0972.speaker: He said:

HAD-0973.text: Were your hearts pure, they would never be sated with the word of Allah.
HAD-0973.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿUṯmān ibn ʿAffān رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0973.speaker: He said:

HAD-0974.text: Knowledge calls to action; if action does not answer it, it departs.
HAD-0974.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0974.speaker: He said:

HAD-0975.text: Follow and do not invent anew; you have already been sufficed.
HAD-0975.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0975.speaker: He said:

HAD-0976.text: Every innovation is misguidance, even if the people see it as good.
HAD-0976.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-0976.speaker: He said:

HAD-0977.text: Learn knowledge, for learning it for the sake of Allah is fear of Him.
HAD-0977.narrator: It is transmitted from Muʿāḏ ibn Ǧabal رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0977.speaker: He said:

HAD-0978.text: You will not be a knower until you are a learner; and you will not be knowing by knowledge until you act upon it.
HAD-0978.narrator: It is transmitted from Abū ad-Dardāʾ رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0978.speaker: He said:

HAD-0979.text: The people asked about the good, and I asked about the evil, for fear that it would reach me.
HAD-0979.narrator: It is transmitted from Ḥuḏayfah ibn al-Yamān رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0979.speaker: He said:

HAD-0980.text: There is no scholar but that from his statement one takes and rejects, except from the Prophet ﷺ.
HAD-0980.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-0980.speaker: He said:

HAD-0981.text: Whoever claims that Muḥammad ﷺ concealed something of the revealed knowledge has gravely slandered Allah.
HAD-0981.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها:
HAD-0981.speaker: She said:

HAD-0982.text: Preserve from me two vessels of knowledge; one I spread, and if I spread the other, this throat would be cut.
HAD-0982.narrator: It is transmitted from Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0982.speaker: He said:

HAD-0983.text: We are a people whom Allah has honored through Islam.
HAD-0983.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0983.speaker: He said:

HAD-0984.text: I leave nothing that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did except that I do it.
HAD-0984.narrator: It is transmitted from Abū Bakr aṣ-Ṣiddīq رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0984.speaker: He said:

HAD-0985.text: The world is passing away, and the Hereafter is drawing near; be among the children of the Hereafter.
HAD-0985.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0985.speaker: He said:

HAD-1106.text: Know that Islām is the Sunnah and the Sunnah is Islām.
HAD-1106.narrator: It is transmitted of al-Barbahārī رحمه الله:
HAD-1106.speaker: He said:

HAD-1107.text: Whoever does not recognize the blessing of Allah through the Qurʾān recognizes no blessing.
HAD-1107.narrator: It is transmitted of Qatādah رحمه الله:
HAD-1107.speaker: He said:

HAD-1108.text: They disliked wearing conspicuous clothing by which one becomes known.
HAD-1108.narrator: It is transmitted of Ibrāhīm an-Naḫaʿī رحمه الله:
HAD-1108.speaker: He said:

HAD-1109.text: Whoever worships Allah without knowledge, his harm is greater than his benefit.
HAD-1109.narrator: It is transmitted of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz رحمه الله:
HAD-1109.speaker: He said:

HAD-1110.text: The Isnād belongs to the religion; without the Isnād, everyone would have said what he wished.
HAD-1110.narrator: It is transmitted of Ibn al-Mubārak رحمه الله:
HAD-1110.speaker: He said:

HAD-1111.text: The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer; in both there is good.
HAD-1111.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1111.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1112.text: Strive for what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not be incapable.
HAD-1112.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1112.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1113.text: A believer is not stung twice from one hole.
HAD-1113.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1113.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1114.text: Whoever calls to right guidance receives a reward like those who follow him.
HAD-1114.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1114.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1115.text: Whoever calls to misguidance bears sin like those who follow him.
HAD-1115.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1115.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1116.text: Make things easy and do not make them hard; give glad tidings and do not drive people away.
HAD-1116.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1116.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1117.text: Whoever introduces into this matter of ours something that does not belong to it, it is rejected.
HAD-1117.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1118.text: Whoever meets Allah without associating anything with Him enters Paradise.
HAD-1118.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1119.text: The world is a prison for the believer and a paradise for the kāfir.
HAD-1119.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1119.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1120.text: People will keep asking until it is said: Who created Allah?
HAD-1120.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1120.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1121.text: If you ask, then ask Allah; if you seek help, then seek help from Allah.
HAD-1121.narrator: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-1121.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1122.text: Deeds are only according to intentions.
HAD-1122.narrator: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1122.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1123.text: The religion is easy, and no one goes to excess in the religion except that it overwhelms him.
HAD-1123.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1123.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1124.text: Wealth does not consist in much possession, but wealth is contentment of the soul.
HAD-1124.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1124.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1125.text: Whoever relieves a hardship of a believer, Allah relieves for him a hardship on the Day of Resurrection.
HAD-1125.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1125.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0746.text: Seek help in memorization by abandoning sins.
HAD-0746.narrator: It is transmitted from Wakīʿ ibn al-Ǧarrāḥ رحمه الله:
HAD-0746.speaker: He said:

HAD-0747.text: Knowledge consists of fear of Allah and acting according to the Sunnah.
HAD-0747.narrator: It is transmitted from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī رحمه الله:
HAD-0747.speaker: He said:

HAD-0748.text: Whoever takes knowledge should begin with humility; arrogance extinguishes benefit.
HAD-0748.narrator: It is transmitted from Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah رحمه الله:
HAD-0748.speaker: He said:

HAD-0749.text: Follow the Āṯār of the Salaf, even if the people reject you.
HAD-0749.narrator: It is transmitted from al-Awzāʿī رحمه الله:
HAD-0749.speaker: He said:

HAD-0750.text: Everyone can accept and reject, except the occupant of this grave ﷺ.
HAD-0750.narrator: It is transmitted from Mālik ibn Anas رحمه الله:
HAD-0750.speaker: He said:

HAD-0751.text: Īmān is to believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and the divine decree.
HAD-0751.narrator: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0751.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0752.text: Purity is half of Īmān, and al-ḥamdu lillāh fills the scale.
HAD-0752.narrator: Abū Mālik al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0752.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0753.text: Had it not been a hardship for my Ummah, I would have commanded them the Siwāk at every prayer.
HAD-0753.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0753.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0754.text: Whoever performs the Wuḍūʾ well, his sins leave his body, even from beneath his nails.
HAD-0754.narrator: ʿUṯmān ibn ʿAffān رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0754.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0755.text: Prayer is light, Ṣadaqah is a proof, and patience is illumination.
HAD-0755.narrator: Abū Mālik al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0755.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0756.text: Whoever builds a mosque for Allah, Allah builds for him something comparable in Paradise.
HAD-0756.narrator: ʿUṯmān ibn ʿAffān رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0756.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0757.text: The places most beloved to Allah are the mosques, and the places most hateful to Allah are the markets.
HAD-0757.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0757.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0758.text: When the call is made to prayer, the Šayṭān flees until he no longer hears the Āḏān.
HAD-0758.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0758.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0759.text: Between a person and Širk and Kufr lies the abandonment of the prayer.
HAD-0759.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-0759.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0760.text: The covenant between us and them is the prayer; whoever leaves it commits Kufr.
HAD-0760.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0761.text: Whoever performs the Fajr prayer stands under Allah's protection.
HAD-0761.narrator: Ǧundub ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0761.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0762.text: The heaviest prayers for the hypocrites are ʿIšāʾ and Fajr.
HAD-0762.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0762.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0763.text: Prayer in congregation surpasses the individual prayer by twenty-seven degrees.
HAD-0763.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-0763.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0764.text: Whoever performs the two cool prayers — Fajr and ʿAṣr — will enter Paradise.
HAD-0764.narrator: Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0764.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0765.text: Whoever prays twelve voluntary Rakʿāt daily, a house in Paradise will be built for him.
HAD-0765.narrator: Umm Ḥabībah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-0765.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0786.text: A house in which Allah’s Book is read becomes spacious for its inhabitants, its angels are present, and the Šayāṭīn leave it.
HAD-0786.narrator: It is narrated from Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0786.speaker: He said:

HAD-0787.text: Hold fast to the path and to the Sunnah; for whoever is upon it and remembers Allah, his eyes weep out of fear of Allah.
HAD-0787.narrator: It is narrated from ʿUbayy ibn Kaʿb رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0787.speaker: He said:

HAD-0788.text: Do not perform any act of worship that the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ did not perform; for the first ones left the later ones no room for innovation.
HAD-0788.narrator: It is narrated from Ḥuḏayfah ibn al-Yamān رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0788.speaker: He said:

HAD-0789.text: The earth is not a sanctuary for anyone; rather, a person's deed sanctifies him.
HAD-0789.narrator: It is narrated from Salmān al-Fārisī رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0789.speaker: He said:

HAD-0790.text: The one who seeks knowledge must not be arrogant; for knowledge does not remain with an arrogant person.
HAD-0790.narrator: It is narrated from Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0790.speaker: He said:

HAD-0791.text: O son of Ādam, you are only days; when a day passes, a part of you passes.
HAD-0791.narrator: It is narrated from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī رحمه الله:
HAD-0791.speaker: He said:

HAD-0792.text: This knowledge is religion; so look from whom you take your religion.
HAD-0792.narrator: It is narrated from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn رحمه الله:
HAD-0792.speaker: He said:

HAD-0793.text: Hold fast to the Āṯār of those who were before you, even if the people reject you; and beware of the opinions of men, even if they embellish them for you.
HAD-0793.narrator: It is narrated from al-Awzāʿī رحمه الله:
HAD-0793.speaker: He said:

HAD-0794.text: Be patient upon the Sunnah, stop where they stopped, and say what they said.
HAD-0794.narrator: It is narrated from al-Awzāʿī رحمه الله:
HAD-0794.speaker: He said:

HAD-0795.text: A Bidʿah is dearer to Iblīs than a sin; for one repents from a sin, but from a Bidʿah one often does not repent.
HAD-0795.narrator: It is narrated from Sufyān aṯ-Ṯawrī رحمه الله:
HAD-0795.speaker: He said:

HAD-0796.text: If you hear of a man of the Sunnah in the East and of a man of the Sunnah in the West, then send them Salām and make Duʿāʾ for them.
HAD-0796.narrator: It is narrated from Sufyān aṯ-Ṯawrī رحمه الله:
HAD-0796.speaker: He said:

HAD-0797.text: Follow the paths of guidance, and let not the small number of those who walk it harm you.
HAD-0797.narrator: It is narrated from al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ رحمه الله:
HAD-0797.speaker: He said:

HAD-0798.text: If a deed is sincere but not correct, it is not accepted; and if it is correct but not sincere, it is not accepted.
HAD-0798.narrator: It is narrated from al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ رحمه الله:
HAD-0798.speaker: He said:

HAD-0799.text: The Sunnah is like the ark of Nūḥ: whoever boards it is saved, and whoever remains behind perishes.
HAD-0799.narrator: It is narrated from Mālik ibn Anas رحمه الله:
HAD-0799.speaker: He said:

HAD-0800.text: What was not religion then is not religion today either.
HAD-0800.narrator: It is narrated from Mālik ibn Anas رحمه الله:
HAD-0800.speaker: He said:

HAD-0801.text: The Muslims are agreed upon this: the one to whom the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ becomes clear may not abandon it because of the statement of any person.
HAD-0801.narrator: It is narrated from Muḥammad ibn Idrīs aš-Šāfiʿī رحمه الله:
HAD-0801.speaker: He said:

HAD-0802.text: The foundations of the Sunnah with us are: holding fast to that upon which the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were, and following them.
HAD-0802.narrator: It is narrated from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal رحمه الله:
HAD-0802.speaker: He said:

HAD-0803.text: Do not sit with the people of Kalām, even if they defend the Sunnah.
HAD-0803.narrator: It is narrated from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal رحمه الله:
HAD-0803.speaker: He said:

HAD-0804.text: The Isnād belongs to the religion; were it not for the Isnād, everyone would say whatever he wished.
HAD-0804.narrator: It is narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mubārak رحمه الله:
HAD-0804.speaker: He said:

HAD-0805.text: Between us and the people stands the Isnād; without it anyone could claim whatever he wishes.
HAD-0805.narrator: It is narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mubārak رحمه الله:
HAD-0805.speaker: He said:

HAD-0866.text: Allah is gentle and loves gentleness in all matters.
HAD-0866.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0867.text: Whoever relieves a believer of a burden in this world, Allah will relieve him of a burden on the Day of Resurrection.
HAD-0867.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0867.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0868.text: The believer to the believer is like a building whose parts strengthen one another.
HAD-0868.narrator: Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0868.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0869.text: Allah does not look at your bodies and forms, but at your hearts and deeds.
HAD-0869.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0869.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0870.text: Whoever among you sees something objectionable should change it with his hand.
HAD-0870.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0870.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-0871.text: Follow the Qurʾān and ask Allah for steadfastness.
HAD-0871.narrator: It is transmitted from Abū Bakr aṣ-Ṣiddīq رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0871.speaker: He said:

HAD-0872.text: Call yourselves to account before you are called to account.
HAD-0872.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0872.speaker: He said:

HAD-0873.text: If our heart were pure, it would never be sated with the word of Allah.
HAD-0873.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿUṯmān ibn ʿAffān رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0873.speaker: He said:

HAD-0874.text: People are asleep; when they die, they awaken.
HAD-0874.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0874.speaker: He said:

HAD-0875.text: Follow and do not innovate; you have already been given what suffices.
HAD-0875.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0875.speaker: He said:

HAD-0876.text: Every innovation is an error, even if people find it good.
HAD-0876.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-0876.speaker: He said:

HAD-0877.text: You will not be learned until you learn; and you will not be knowledgeable until you act upon the knowledge.
HAD-0877.narrator: It is transmitted from Abū ad-Dardāʾ رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0877.speaker: He said:

HAD-0878.text: Learn knowledge, for learning it for the sake of Allah is fear of Him.
HAD-0878.narrator: It is transmitted from Muʿāḏ ibn Ǧabal رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0878.speaker: He said:

HAD-0879.text: The heart is a king, and the parts of the body are its soldiers.
HAD-0879.narrator: It is transmitted from Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0879.speaker: He said:

HAD-0880.text: Whoever tells you that Muḥammad ﷺ concealed anything of the revelation has lied about Allah.
HAD-0880.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها:
HAD-0880.speaker: She said:

HAD-0881.text: The people asked about the good; I asked about the evil, out of fear that it would befall me.
HAD-0881.narrator: It is transmitted from Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0881.speaker: He said:

HAD-0882.text: Every innovation is misguidance, even if people see it as good.
HAD-0882.narrator: It is transmitted from Ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-0882.speaker: He said:

HAD-0883.text: Knowledge is abundant, but life is short; take from knowledge what you need for your religion.
HAD-0883.narrator: It is transmitted from Salman al-Fārisī رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0883.speaker: He said:

HAD-0884.text: Whoever is silent is saved; and whoever speaks good, gains.
HAD-0884.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-0884.speaker: He said:

HAD-0885.text: The Qurʾān is either a proof for you or a proof against you.
HAD-0885.narrator: It is transmitted from Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0885.speaker: He said:

HAD-0886.text: Knowledge does not consist of many narrations, but of Ḫašyah.
HAD-0886.narrator: It is transmitted of Ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0886.speaker: He said:

HAD-0887.text: Hold fast to the Sunnah; it is a protective wall for you.
HAD-0887.narrator: It is transmitted of ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0887.speaker: He said:

HAD-0888.text: The worth of every person lies in what he masters well.
HAD-0888.narrator: It is transmitted of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0888.speaker: He said:

HAD-0889.text: Obey me as long as I obey Allah and His Messenger.
HAD-0889.narrator: It is transmitted of Abū Bakr رضي الله عنه:
HAD-0889.speaker: He said:
