HAD-1812.text: When a person dies, his deeds come to an end except in three things: ongoing Ṣadaqah, knowledge from which benefit is drawn, or a righteous child who prays for him.
HAD-1812.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1812.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1813.text: Whoever calls to guidance receives the same reward as those who follow it, without their reward being diminished thereby.
HAD-1813.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1813.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1814.text: Whoever introduces a good practice in Islam receives its reward and the reward of those who act according to it, without anything being diminished from their reward.
HAD-1814.narrator: Ǧarīr ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1814.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1815.text: When people gather in one of the houses of Allah, read the Book of Allah and study it together, the Sakīnah descends upon them, mercy envelops them, the angels surround them, and Allah mentions them among those who are with Him.
HAD-1815.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1815.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1816.text: Allah raises people by this Book and abases others by it.
HAD-1816.narrator: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1816.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1817.text: The best among you are those who learn the Qurʾān and teach it.
HAD-1817.narrator: ʿUṯmān ibn ʿAffān رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1817.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1818.text: Whoever recites the Qurʾān skillfully is with the noble and obedient scribes; and whoever recites it with difficulty receives two rewards.
HAD-1818.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1819.text: Recite the Qurʾān, for it will come on the Day of Resurrection as an intercessor for its companions.
HAD-1819.narrator: Abū Umāmah al-Bāhilī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1819.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1820.text: Do not make your houses graves. The Šayṭān flees from the house in which Sūrat al-Baqarah is recited.
HAD-1820.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1820.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1821.text: Recite the two luminous ones – al-Baqarah and Āl ʿImrān –, for they will come on the Day of Resurrection and intercede for their companions.
HAD-1821.narrator: Abū Umāmah al-Bāhilī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1821.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1822.text: Qul huwa Allahu aḥad corresponds to one third of the Qurʾān.
HAD-1822.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1822.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1823.text: Hold fast to the Qurʾān; by the One in Whose hand is my soul, it slips away faster than camels from their fetters.
HAD-1823.narrator: Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1823.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1824.text: The likeness of the believer who reads the Qurʾān is like the citrus fruit: its fragrance is good and its taste is good.
HAD-1824.narrator: Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1824.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1825.text: The congregational prayer surpasses the prayer of the individual by twenty-seven degrees.
HAD-1825.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-1825.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1826.text: Between a person and Širk and Kufr stands the abandonment of the prayer.
HAD-1826.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-1826.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1827.text: The first matter about which judgment is passed among people on the Day of Resurrection concerns shed blood.
HAD-1827.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1827.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1828.text: The bankrupt one of my Ummah comes on the Day of Resurrection with prayer, fasting and Zakāh, but he has insulted this one, slandered that one, taken another’s wealth, shed blood and struck. Then his good deeds are distributed to those who were harmed.
HAD-1828.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1828.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1829.text: Seven will Allah shade on the day when there is no shade except His: a just Imām; a youth who grew up in the worship of Allah; a man whose heart is attached to the mosques; two people who love one another for the sake of Allah; a man who refuses an invitation to sin with the words: I fear Allah; one who gives in secret; and one who remembers Allah alone, so that his eyes shed tears.
HAD-1829.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1829.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1830.text: The places most beloved to Allah are the mosques, and the places most hateful to Allah are the markets.
HAD-1830.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1830.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1831.text: The world is the prison of the believer and the paradise of the disbeliever.
HAD-1831.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1831.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1832.text: Be in this world like a stranger or a traveler.
HAD-1832.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-1832.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1833.text: Wealth does not consist in the abundance of possessions; true wealth is the wealth of the soul.
HAD-1833.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1833.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1834.text: Look at the one who is below you, and not at the one who is above you; that is more apt so that you do not belittle Allah’s favor.
HAD-1834.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1834.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1835.text: The son of Ādam says: My wealth, my wealth. Of his wealth, only what he consumed, what he wore until it wore out, or what he gave and sent ahead for himself belongs to him.
HAD-1835.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn aš-Šiḫḫīr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1835.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1836.text: Two gifts in which many people suffer loss: health and free time.
HAD-1836.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-1836.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1837.text: If the son of Ādam had a valley full of gold, he would wish for a second; and nothing fills his mouth except earth. Allah accepts the repentance of the one who repents.
HAD-1837.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1837.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1838.text: The heart of an old person remains young in two things: in the love of long life and in the love of wealth.
HAD-1838.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1838.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1839.text: The world is sweet and green, and Allah appoints you as successors in it in order to see how you act.
HAD-1839.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1839.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1840.text: None of you should wish for death because of a misfortune. If he absolutely must do it, he should say: O Allah, let me live as long as life is better for me, and let me die when death is better for me.
HAD-1840.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1840.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1841.text: I know that you are only a stone that neither harms nor benefits. Had I not seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ kiss you, I would not have kissed you.
HAD-1841.narrator: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1841.speaker: He said:

HAD-1842.text: If the religion were according to mere opinion, the underside of the leather sock would be more fitting to wipe than its upper side. But I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wipe over the upper side of his leather socks.
HAD-1842.narrator: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1842.speaker: He said:

HAD-1843.text: Allah looked into the hearts of the servants and found the heart of Muḥammad ﷺ to be the best; then He looked into the hearts of the servants after him and found the hearts of his Companions to be the best hearts.
HAD-1843.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1843.speaker: He said:

HAD-1844.text: A sign of the people of innovation is their attack on the people of transmission.
HAD-1844.narrator: Abū Ḥātim ar-Rāzī رحمه الله said:
HAD-1844.speaker: He said:

HAD-1845.text: If you see a person who is quarrelsome and contentious and impressed by his own opinion, then his loss is complete.
HAD-1845.narrator: Bilāl ibn Saʿd رحمه الله said:
HAD-1845.speaker: He said:

HAD-1766.text: Allah has prescribed Iḥsān for everything.
HAD-1766.narrator: Šaddād ibn Aws رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1766.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1767.text: Protect yourselves from the Fire, even with half a date.
HAD-1767.narrator: ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1767.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1768.text: A good word is a Ṣadaqah.
HAD-1768.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1768.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1769.text: Every joint of a person owes a Ṣadaqah each day: to mediate justly between two people is Ṣadaqah, to help a person with his mount is Ṣadaqah, a good word is Ṣadaqah, every step toward the prayer is Ṣadaqah, and to remove something harmful from the path is Ṣadaqah.
HAD-1769.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1769.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1770.text: A man saw on the path something that harmed people and removed it. For that he was forgiven.
HAD-1770.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1770.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1771.text: Speak to the people with what they understand. Do you want Allah and His Messenger ﷺ to be taken for liars?
HAD-1771.narrator: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1771.speaker: He said:

HAD-1772.text: Instruct the people once every week; if you want more, then twice, at most three times. Do not make this Qurʾān burdensome for them.
HAD-1772.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما said:
HAD-1772.speaker: He said:

HAD-1773.narrator: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1773.speaker: He said:

HAD-1774.text: If you relate to people something that their minds do not reach, it becomes a temptation for some of them.
HAD-1774.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1774.speaker: He said:

HAD-1775.text: Follow and invent nothing new; you have already been sufficed.
HAD-1775.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1775.speaker: He said:

HAD-1776.text: Moderation in the Sunnah is better than great zeal in an innovation.
HAD-1776.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1776.speaker: He said:

HAD-1777.text: Learn; and when you have learned, then act.
HAD-1777.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1777.speaker: He said:

HAD-1778.text: People remain in good as long as they take knowledge from their elders and their trustworthy ones.
HAD-1778.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1778.speaker: He said:

HAD-1779.text: Allah has not placed your cure in what He has forbidden you.
HAD-1779.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1779.speaker: He said:

HAD-1780.text: We would learn ten verses at a time from the Prophet ﷺ and would not move on to the next until we had learned the knowledge and the practice that were in them.
HAD-1780.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1780.speaker: He said:

HAD-1781.text: When you are placed before a decision, judge according to Allah’s Book; if you do not find it there, then according to what the Prophet ﷺ decided; if you do not find that either, then according to the judgment of the righteous; and if you find nothing, strive to reach a judgment.
HAD-1781.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1781.speaker: He said:

HAD-1782.text: A person’s rank is his religion, his Muruʾah is his character, and his origin is his intellect.
HAD-1782.narrator: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1782.speaker: He said:

HAD-1783.text: If the Īmān of Abū Bakr were weighed against the Īmān of this Ummah, the Īmān of Abū Bakr would outweigh it.
HAD-1783.narrator: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1783.speaker: He said:

HAD-1784.text: Be Rabbānīyūn: forbearing and learned in the sacred law. The Rabbānī is the one who raises people with the small questions of knowledge before the great ones.
HAD-1784.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما said:
HAD-1784.speaker: He said:

HAD-1785.text: You will surely adorn the mosques as the Jews and the Christians adorned them.
HAD-1785.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما said:
HAD-1785.speaker: He said:

HAD-1786.text: For every community there are Magians; the Magians of this Ummah are those who say: There is no Qadar.
HAD-1786.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما said:
HAD-1786.speaker: He said:

HAD-1787.text: Knowledge comes through learning, and forbearance through practicing forbearance. Whoever seeks the good, it is given to him; and whoever guards himself against evil is protected from it.
HAD-1787.narrator: Abū ad-Dardāʾ رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1787.speaker: He said:

HAD-1788.text: Īmān is pure and far from sins. If someone commits fornication, Īmān leaves him; if he reproaches himself and turns back, Īmān returns to him.
HAD-1788.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1788.speaker: He said:

HAD-1789.text: When three are on a journey, they should appoint one of them as their leader.
HAD-1789.narrator: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1789.speaker: He said:

HAD-1790.text: Whoever newly acquires wealth, no Zakāh is due on it until a year has passed with its owner.
HAD-1790.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما said:
HAD-1790.speaker: He said:

HAD-1791.text: Formerly they did not ask about the Isnād. But when the Fitnah occurred, they said: Name your transmitters to us. Then one would look at the people of the Sunnah and take their Ḥadīṯs, and one would look at the people of innovation and not take their Ḥadīṯs.
HAD-1791.narrator: Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn رحمه الله said:
HAD-1791.speaker: He said:

HAD-1792.text: The Isnād belongs to the religion. Were there no Isnād, anyone could say what he wished.
HAD-1792.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mubārak رحمه الله said:
HAD-1792.speaker: He said:

HAD-1793.text: Between us and the people stand the chains of transmission.
HAD-1793.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mubārak رحمه الله said:
HAD-1793.speaker: He said:

HAD-1794.text: The shy and the arrogant do not attain knowledge.
HAD-1794.narrator: Muǧāhid ibn Ǧabr رحمه الله said:
HAD-1794.speaker: He said:

HAD-1795.text: While the Tābiʿūn were still numerous, we said: Allah is above His Throne, and we believe in what has been transmitted in the Sunnah concerning His attributes.
HAD-1795.speaker: He said:

HAD-1796.text: Let the transmissions concerning the attributes stand as they have come, without how.
HAD-1796.narrator: al-Walīd ibn Muslim رحمه الله reported concerning al-Awzāʿī, Sufyān aṯ-Ṯawrī, Mālik and al-Layṯ:
HAD-1796.speaker: They said:

HAD-1797.text: Everything with which Allah has described Himself in the Qurʾān: its recitation is its explanation, without how and without likeness.
HAD-1797.narrator: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah رحمه الله said:
HAD-1797.speaker: He said:

HAD-1798.text: The Istiwāʾ is not unknown, the how is not comprehensible, the message is from Allah, the conveyance was incumbent upon the Messenger, and faith is incumbent upon us.
HAD-1798.speaker: He said:

HAD-1799.text: The Istiwāʾ is known, the how is unknown, believing in it is obligatory, and asking about the how is an innovation.
HAD-1799.narrator: Mālik ibn Anas رحمه الله said:
HAD-1799.speaker: He said:

HAD-1800.text: All the Imāms whom I reached said: Īmān is word and deed, and it increases and decreases.
HAD-1800.narrator: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān رحمه الله said:
HAD-1800.speaker: He said:

HAD-1801.text: Among the Ṣaḥābah, the Tābiʿūn and those after them whom we reached, there was agreement: Īmān is word, deed and intention; none of the three suffices without the others.
HAD-1801.speaker: He said:

HAD-1802.text: The Sunnah with us, which we have taken from the scholars, is: Īmān consists of intention, word and deed.
HAD-1802.narrator: Abū ʿUbayd al-Qāsim ibn Sallām رحمه الله said:
HAD-1802.speaker: He said:

HAD-1803.narrator: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal رحمه الله said:
HAD-1803.speaker: He said:

HAD-1804.text: I met more than a thousand scholars; none of them disagreed that Īmān is word and deed and that it increases and decreases.
HAD-1804.narrator: Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl al-Buḫārī رحمه الله said:
HAD-1804.speaker: He said:

HAD-1805.text: The jurists from the East to the West agreed to believe in the attributes mentioned in the Qurʾān and in reliably transmitted reports, without altering them, determining their how, or equating them with creation.
HAD-1805.narrator: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan aš-Šaybānī رحمه الله said:
HAD-1805.speaker: He said:

HAD-1886.text: When the prayer was first prescribed, it was two Rakʿah; the travel prayer remained so, and to the prayer at the place of residence an addition was made.
HAD-1886.speaker: She said:

HAD-1887.text: None of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ transmitted more from him than I, except ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr; for he wrote, while I did not write.
HAD-1887.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1887.speaker: He said:

HAD-1888.text: As for the Qurʾān, it is a waymark like a waymark on the road. What you recognize clearly of it, ask no one about it; what is unclear to you, return its knowledge to a scholar or to Allah.
HAD-1888.narrator: Muʿāḏ ibn Ǧabal رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1888.speaker: He said:

HAD-1889.text: What destroys Islam? The slip of the scholar, the hypocrite’s disputing by means of the Book, and the judgment of misleading leaders.
HAD-1889.narrator: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1889.speaker: He said:

HAD-1890.text: If you love a brother, then do not dispute with him.
HAD-1890.narrator: Muʿāḏ ibn Ǧabal رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1890.speaker: He said:

HAD-1891.text: Recognize the Muhāǧirūn for their merit, follow their traces, and beware of what people newly introduce into their religion; for the worst of things are the innovations.
HAD-1891.speaker: He said:

HAD-1892.text: Do not sit with the people of inclinations, do not debate with them, and do not listen to them.
HAD-1892.speaker: He said:

HAD-1893.text: Hold patiently to the Sunnah, remain standing where the people before you remained standing, say what they said, be silent about that about which they were silent, and travel the path of your righteous predecessors.
HAD-1893.speaker: He said:

HAD-1894.text: Hold to the transmissions of those who went before, even if people reject you; and beware of the opinions of men, even if they adorn their words.
HAD-1894.speaker: He said:

HAD-1895.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and those responsible after him laid down paths. Whoever follows them is rightly guided; whoever strengthens himself by them is given support.
HAD-1895.narrator: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz رحمه الله said:
HAD-1895.speaker: He said:

HAD-1896.text: Hold fast to the Sunnah; by Allah’s permission it is a protection for you. No innovation was introduced without there already having been something that serves as proof against it.
HAD-1896.narrator: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz رحمه الله said:
HAD-1896.speaker: He said:

HAD-1897.text: Learn Islam; when you have learned it, do not turn away from it. Hold to the straight path and to the Sunnah of your Prophet ﷺ and to that upon which his Companions were.
HAD-1897.narrator: Abū al-ʿĀliyah ar-Riyāḥī رحمه الله said:
HAD-1897.speaker: He said:

HAD-1898.text: When something from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is reliably established, it is binding; nothing else weakens it.
HAD-1898.speaker: He said:

HAD-1899.text: Whoever rejects a Ḥadīṯ of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stands on the brink of ruin.
HAD-1899.narrator: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal رحمه الله said:
HAD-1899.speaker: He said:

HAD-1900.text: Whoever equates Allah with His creation commits Kufr; and whoever denies that with which Allah has described Himself commits Kufr. In that with which Allah has described Himself, or with which His Messenger ﷺ has described Him, there is no equating.
HAD-1900.narrator: Nuʿaym ibn Ḥammād رحمه الله said:
HAD-1900.speaker: He said:

HAD-1901.text: It does not befit the Muslims to seek to fathom the Qadar through probing questions and investigation. The Qadar belongs to Allah’s secrets; what is binding is faith in what has been decreed of good and of evil.
HAD-1901.narrator: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Āǧurrī رحمه الله said:
HAD-1901.speaker: He said:

HAD-1902.text: From Allah is the message, upon the Messenger lies the conveyance, and upon us lies submission.
HAD-1902.narrator: Muḥammad ibn Šihāb az-Zuhrī رحمه الله said:
HAD-1902.speaker: He said:

HAD-1903.text: Do not sit with the people of inclinations and do not debate with them; I am not secure against their drawing you into their misguidance or confusing you about what you have recognized.
HAD-1903.speaker: He said:

HAD-1904.text: If Allah wills good for a servant, He opens for him the door to action and closes for him the door to dispute; if He wills evil for him, the opposite occurs.
HAD-1904.speaker: He said:

HAD-1905.text: If it reached me that the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ did not go beyond a fingernail in Wuḍūʾ, I would not go beyond that. It suffices as a burden to contradict their deeds.
HAD-1905.speaker: He said:

HAD-2006.text: The Sunnah explains the Qurʾān and points to it.
HAD-2006.narrator: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal رحمه الله said:
HAD-2006.speaker: He said:

HAD-2007.text: Know that Islām is the Sunnah and the Sunnah is Islām.
HAD-2007.speaker: He said:

HAD-2008.text: Follow the paths of right guidance, and the small number of those who walk them does not harm you.
HAD-2008.narrator: al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ رحمه الله said:
HAD-2008.speaker: He said:

HAD-2009.text: When a person loves innovation, Allah takes the light of the Sunnah out of his heart.
HAD-2009.narrator: al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ رحمه الله said:
HAD-2009.speaker: He said:

HAD-2010.text: They detested it when a man made himself conspicuous and came forward with his knowledge.
HAD-2010.speaker: He said:

HAD-2011.text: The strong one is not the one who wins in wrestling; the strong one is the one who controls himself in anger.
HAD-2011.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2011.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-2012.text: Wealth is not the abundance of possessions; wealth is the wealth of the soul.
HAD-2012.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2012.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-2013.text: Look at the one who is below you, and do not look at the one who is above you; that is better, so that you do not belittle Allah’s grace.
HAD-2013.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2013.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-2014.text: A good word is a Ṣadaqah.
HAD-2014.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2014.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-2015.text: Do not belittle anything of the good, even if you meet your brother with a friendly face.
HAD-2015.narrator: Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2015.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-2016.text: The smile into your brother’s face is Ṣadaqah for you.
HAD-2016.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2016.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-2017.text: Whoever is not merciful, to him no mercy is shown.
HAD-2017.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2017.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-2018.text: Whoever is not merciful to people, Allah is not merciful to him.
HAD-2018.narrator: Ǧarīr ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2018.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-2019.text: The All-Merciful has mercy on the merciful; have mercy on those on the earth, then the One above the heaven will have mercy on you.
HAD-2019.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2019.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-2020.text: Gentleness is in nothing except that it adorns it, and it is taken from nothing except that it disfigures it.
HAD-2020.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-2021.text: Allah is gentle and loves gentleness in all matters.
HAD-2021.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-2022.text: Whoever keeps a dog, except a hunting dog, a livestock dog or a field dog, his reward decreases each day by one Qīrāṭ.
HAD-2022.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2022.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-2023.text: A woman was punished because of a cat: she locked it up until it died.
HAD-2023.narrator: Ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2023.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-2024.text: While a man was on the way and became very thirsty, he found a well and drank; then he gave a dog water, and Allah thanked him for that.
HAD-2024.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2024.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-2025.text: In every living being with a moist liver there is reward.
HAD-2025.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2025.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-2026.text: A person is upon the Dīn of his close friend; so each of you should look at whom he takes as a friend.
HAD-2026.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2026.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-2027.text: The likeness of the good and the bad companion is like the carrier of musk and the bellows of the blacksmith.
HAD-2027.narrator: Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2027.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-2028.text: A person follows the path of his friend; so he should pay attention to whom he befriends.
HAD-2028.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2028.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-2029.text: Whoever guarantees me what is between his jaws and what is between his legs, I guarantee him Paradise.
HAD-2029.narrator: Sahl ibn Saʿd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2029.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-2030.text: Hold back your tongue, let your house suffice you, and weep over your sin.
HAD-2030.narrator: ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2030.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-2031.text: Whoever supplicates for his brother in his absence, the angel says to him: Āmīn, and the same for you.
HAD-2031.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2031.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-2032.text: The supplication of a Muslim for his brother in his absence is answered.
HAD-2032.narrator: Abū ad-Dardāʾ رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2032.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-2033.text: The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim: he does him no wrong and does not hand him over.
HAD-2033.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2033.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-2034.text: The believer is a mirror to the believer, and the believer is a brother to the believer.
HAD-2034.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2034.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-2035.text: Help your brother, whether he does wrong or wrong is done to him.
HAD-2035.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2035.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-2036.text: The believer is not stung twice from the same hole.
HAD-2036.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2036.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-2037.text: Whoever deceives us does not belong to us.
HAD-2037.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2037.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-2038.text: Four qualities: whoever has them is a pure hypocrite; and whoever has one of them has a quality of hypocrisy until he leaves it.
HAD-2038.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2038.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-2039.text: The signs of the hypocrite are three: when he speaks, he lies; when he promises, he breaks it; and when he is trusted, he betrays.
HAD-2039.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2039.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-2040.text: Shall I not name to you the greatest of the great sins? Associating something with Allah, disobedience toward the parents, and false testimony.
HAD-2040.narrator: Abū Bakrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2040.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-2041.text: Whoever worships Allah without knowledge, his ruin is greater than his benefit.
HAD-2041.narrator: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz رحمه الله said:
HAD-2041.speaker: He said:

HAD-2042.text: Hold fast to the Sunnah; for it is, with Allah’s permission, a protection for you.
HAD-2042.narrator: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz رحمه الله said:
HAD-2042.speaker: He said:

HAD-2043.text: From Allah comes the message, upon the Messenger lies the conveyance, and upon us lies the submission.
HAD-2043.speaker: He said:

HAD-2044.text: If a Ḥadīṯ is authentic, then it is my school of law.
HAD-2044.speaker: He said:

HAD-2045.text: The Muslims are agreed: whoever clearly recognizes the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, it is not permitted for him to leave it because of the statement of someone else.
HAD-2045.speaker: He said:

HAD-1926.text: The believer is not bitten twice from the same hole.
HAD-1926.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1926.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1927.text: Souls are assembled hosts: those among them that recognize one another come together; those that are strangers to one another part.
HAD-1927.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1927.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1928.text: None of you believes completely until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
HAD-1928.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1928.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1929.text: Do not envy one another, do not hate one another, do not turn your backs on one another, and be brothers as servants of Allah.
HAD-1929.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1929.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1930.text: Whoever points to something good receives the same reward as the one who does it.
HAD-1930.narrator: Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1930.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1931.text: Paradise is closer to one of you than his shoelace, and the Hellfire likewise.
HAD-1931.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1931.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1932.text: Paradise is surrounded by hardships, and the Hellfire by desires.
HAD-1932.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1932.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1933.text: His deed alone will not bring any of you into Paradise. Nor me – except that Allah encompasses me with mercy.
HAD-1933.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1933.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1934.text: Allah says: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and what has not come to any human heart.
HAD-1934.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1934.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1935.text: Death will be brought on the Day of Resurrection in the form of a white-and-black ram and then slaughtered; thereafter it will be said: Inhabitants of Paradise, eternity without death; inhabitants of the Fire, eternity without death.
HAD-1935.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1935.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1936.text: Visit the graves, for they remind you of the Hereafter.
HAD-1936.narrator: Buraydah ibn al-Ḥuṣayb رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1936.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1937.text: Three things follow the deceased: his family, his wealth, and his deeds. Two return and one remains: his deeds remain.
HAD-1937.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1937.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1938.text: Be in this world like a stranger or a traveler.
HAD-1938.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-1938.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1939.text: When the human being dies, his work ends except in three things: ongoing Ṣadaqah, knowledge from which benefit is drawn, or a righteous child who asks for him.
HAD-1939.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1939.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1940.text: The world is an enjoyment, and the best enjoyment of the world is the righteous woman.
HAD-1940.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-1940.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1941.text: Do not dispute with your brother, for dispute brings no good.
HAD-1941.narrator: Ibn Abī Laylā رحمه الله said:
HAD-1941.speaker: He said:

HAD-1942.text: It suffices you as a sin that you constantly dispute.
HAD-1942.narrator: Abū ad-Dardāʾ رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1942.speaker: He said:

HAD-1943.text: Successful is the one who is preserved from dispute, anger, and greed.
HAD-1943.narrator: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz رحمه الله said:
HAD-1943.speaker: He said:

HAD-1944.text: If you love a brother, then do not dispute with him, do not joke with him hurtfully, and do not give him a promise that you break.
HAD-1944.narrator: Muʿāḏ ibn Ǧabal رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1944.speaker: He said:

HAD-1945.text: Whoever makes his religion the object of disputes frequently changes his position.
HAD-1945.narrator: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz رحمه الله said:
HAD-1945.speaker: He said:

HAD-1966.text: The Dīn is easy, and no one exaggerates in the Dīn except that he is overwhelmed.
HAD-1966.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1966.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1967.text: When I forbid you something, avoid it; and when I command you something, then do of it what you are able.
HAD-1967.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1967.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1968.text: Allah does not look at your bodies and does not look at your forms, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds.
HAD-1968.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1968.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1969.text: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or remain silent.
HAD-1969.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1969.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1970.text: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should honor his neighbor.
HAD-1970.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1970.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1971.text: Call yourselves to account before you are called to account.
HAD-1971.narrator: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1971.speaker: He said:

HAD-1972.text: The world is departing and the Hereafter is drawing near; so be children of the Hereafter and not children of the world.
HAD-1972.narrator: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1972.speaker: He said:

HAD-1973.text: Follow and do not invent anew; for you have already been sufficed.
HAD-1973.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1973.speaker: He said:

HAD-1974.text: How many there are who want good and do not attain it.
HAD-1974.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1974.speaker: He said:

HAD-1975.text: The community is that which accords with the truth, even if you are alone.
HAD-1975.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1975.speaker: He said:

HAD-1976.text: Whoever among you wishes to follow should follow those who have already died; for the living is not safe from Fitnah.
HAD-1976.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1976.speaker: He said:

HAD-1977.text: The people asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the good; I asked him about the evil, out of fear that it would befall me.
HAD-1977.narrator: Ḥuḏayfah ibn al-Yamān رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1977.speaker: He said:

HAD-1978.text: We are a people whom Allah has honored through Islam; if we seek honor through something else, Allah humiliates us.
HAD-1978.narrator: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1978.speaker: He said:

HAD-1979.text: Stones would almost have fallen upon you from the sky: I tell you, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, and you say: Abū Bakr and ʿUmar said.
HAD-1979.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما said:
HAD-1979.speaker: He said:

HAD-1980.text: Learn knowledge; for learning it for the sake of Allah is fear, seeking it is worship, and studying it is praise.
HAD-1980.narrator: Muʿāḏ ibn Ǧabal رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1980.speaker: He said:

HAD-1981.text: Be a scholar, a learner, a listener, or a lover; and do not be the fifth, otherwise you perish.
HAD-1981.narrator: Abū ad-Dardāʾ رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1981.speaker: He said:

HAD-1982.text: Knowledge is not attained through the comfort of the body.
HAD-1982.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما said:
HAD-1982.speaker: He said:

HAD-1983.text: May Allah have mercy on the first women of the Muhāǧirāt; when the verse about covering was revealed, they tore their cloths and covered themselves with them.
HAD-1983.speaker: She said:

HAD-1984.text: Everything new is misguidance, even if the people regard it as good.
HAD-1984.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما said:
HAD-1984.speaker: He said:

HAD-1985.text: Speak to the people according to what they recognize; do you want Allah and His Messenger to be denied?
HAD-1985.narrator: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1985.speaker: He said:

HAD-2166.text: Allah is good and accepts only what is good.
HAD-2166.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2166.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2166.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that Allah is here called “ṭayyib” in the sense of being free and exalted above defects, close to the meaning of al-Quddūs. The origin of ṭayyib comprises purity, soundness, and being free from evil; therefore Allah accepts only what is itself pure, lawful, and free of corruption.

HAD-2167.text: Allah commanded the believers what He commanded the messengers.
HAD-2167.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2167.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2167.sharh: The explanation of Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ makes clear: if Allah accepts only the ṭayyib, then the instruction to the believers to take from the ṭayyib is not a mere dietary recommendation, but a basis for the acceptance of deed, Ṣadaqah, and Duʿāʾ. The believers are joined in this with the messengers, because purity of food and purity of action belong together.

HAD-2168.text: A man stretches his hands toward the sky and calls: O Lord, O Lord – yet his food is forbidden.
HAD-2168.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2168.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ mentioned:
HAD-2168.sharh: From the explanation of Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ it follows: if Allah accepts only what is pure, then forbidden food stands against acceptance. The man gathers outward grounds for the answering of Duʿāʾ – travel, need, raised hands, and repeated calling – yet the Ḥarām in food, drink, and provision contradicts the ṭayyib that is required for acceptance.

HAD-2169.text: Leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt.
HAD-2169.narrator: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2169.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2169.sharh: Ibn al-ʿArabī treats the Ḥadīṯ, within the Tirmiḏī passage, as a basis for leaving what is doubtful and moving to what is clearer. The measure is not mere whim, but what brings calm and certainty in the heart and protects the religion from Rayb and Šubuhāt.

HAD-2170.text: Part of a person’s good Islam is that he leaves what does not concern him.
HAD-2170.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2170.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2170.sharh: Ibn al-ʿArabī explains the statement as part of the completeness of Islam: the servant leaves words, actions, and occupations that do not concern him religiously and bring no benefit. What is meant is not a withdrawal from duty and benefit, but the leaving of what is superfluous, harmful, and what diminishes the goodness of Islam.

HAD-2171.text: None of you believes completely until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
HAD-2171.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2171.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2171.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that what is meant here is the completeness of Īmān. The believer should wish for his brother the good that he loves for himself, and in rights and claims prefer the truth even when this means hardship for himself.

HAD-2172.text: The blood of a Muslim who testifies that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah is not lawful – except in one of three cases.
HAD-2172.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2172.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2172.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl treats the Ḥadīṯ in the chapter on the cases in which the inviolability of blood is lifted by an established right. The principle remains the inviolability of Muslim life; the cases named are legally bound exceptions and not a private permission for taking the law into one’s own hands.

HAD-2173.text: Among these three cases is: life for life.
HAD-2173.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2173.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2173.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl assigns “life for life” to the legally established Qiṣāṣ. What is meant is not retaliation by individuals, but the retaliation for intentional killing that is bound by proof, conditions, and the competent judicial authority.

HAD-2174.text: Among these three cases is: the fornicator who is married or has already been married.
HAD-2174.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2174.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2174.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains “aṯ-ṯayyib az-zānī” in connection with Iḥṣān: the legal consequence named in the Ḥadīṯ does not concern every act of unlawful intercourse without distinction, but the one in whom the legal conditions of Iḥṣān are fulfilled and whose deed has been established in a legally valid manner.

HAD-2175.text: Among these three cases is: the one who leaves his religion and separates from the community.
HAD-2175.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2175.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2175.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl treats the expression in connection with the established grounds by which the original inviolability of a Muslim’s blood can be legally lifted. “Leaving the religion” denotes Ridda; “leaving the community” describes separation from the community of the Muslims. Carrying out legal sanctions does not belong in the hands of individual persons.

HAD-2176.text: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should not inflict harm upon his neighbor.
HAD-2176.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2176.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2176.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl stresses the strong right of the neighbor: harm by word or deed contradicts the completeness of Īmān. The link with belief in Allah and the Last Day is meant to move the believer to self-examination and to refraining from harm.

HAD-2177.text: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should honor his guest.
HAD-2177.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2177.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2177.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl counts the honoring of the guest among the prophetic ways of conduct. These include a good reception, provision according to one’s means, and a manner of dealing that does not leave the guest isolated or humiliate him; the honoring is understood as a fruit of a complete Īmān.

HAD-2178.text: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or remain silent.
HAD-2178.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2178.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2178.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains: what is meant is the complete Īmān. Its strength moves a person to call himself to account already in this world for his words and to be silent about what would bring him regret on the Last Day. The good is spoken; harmful speech is withheld.

HAD-2179.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2179.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2179.sharh: al-Ḫaṭṭābī explains: what is meant is to avoid the causes of anger and not to expose oneself to things that kindle it. Since the feeling of anger belongs to human nature, the prohibition also includes not following what anger urges in words or deeds.

HAD-2180.text: Allah has prescribed Iḥsān for every thing.
HAD-2180.narrator: Šaddād ibn Aws رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2180.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2180.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ shows by the following examples how far Iḥsān extends: even where killing or slaughter is legally permissible, unnecessary torment remains forbidden. Iḥsān means carrying out the permitted act in the most gentle and most correct manner.

HAD-2181.text: If you kill, then kill in a good manner; and if you slaughter, then slaughter in a good manner.
HAD-2181.narrator: Šaddād ibn Aws رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2181.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2181.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the instruction applies generally to legally permissible killing, Qiṣāṣ, fixed punishments, and slaughter: creatures must not be tormented in this; the act is to be carried out without unnecessary prolongation or added torment.

HAD-2182.text: One of you should sharpen his blade and grant relief to his animal for slaughter.
HAD-2182.narrator: Šaddād ibn Aws رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2182.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2182.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ expressly explains these words as an interpretation of Iḥsān in slaughter: a sharp blade shortens the process and eases the animal. Iḥsān also includes preventing additional fear and avoidable suffering.

HAD-2183.narrator: Abū Ḏarr al-Ġifārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2183.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2183.sharh: Ibn al-ʿArabī treats this Ḥadīṯ directly. The first instruction obliges to Taqwā in every condition and in every place: the servant does not shape his conduct toward Allah according to whether people see him, but preserves the fear of Allah constantly.

HAD-2184.text: Let a good deed follow a bad deed; it erases it.
HAD-2184.narrator: Abū Ḏarr al-Ġifārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2184.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2184.sharh: Ibn al-ʿArabī explains that a good deed should follow the bad deed, one that erases its trace. The immediate following of the good is especially fitting: the bad choice is broken by a good choice and should not harden through repetition.

HAD-2185.narrator: Abū Ḏarr al-Ġifārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2185.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2185.sharh: Ibn al-ʿArabī treats the entire Ḥadīṯ directly. The concluding instruction places dealings with people under good character: to Taqwā toward Allah is joined good conduct toward His creatures.

HAD-2066.text: Whoever says this Tahlīl one hundred times, one hundred good deeds are written for him and one hundred bad deeds are erased.
HAD-2066.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2066.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2066.sharh: The Sharḥ shows that the repeated Tahlīl is not only a confession of Tawḥīd, but is linked to a concrete reward: good deeds are written and sins are erased. This shows the breadth of Allah’s grace in an easy yet meaningful Ḏikr.

HAD-2067.text: Whoever says this Tahlīl one hundred times, it is for him a protection from the Šayṭān on this day.
HAD-2067.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2067.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2067.sharh: The explanation points to the protective character of this Ḏikr: the Tahlīl is, on the day of the one who says it, a Ḥirz, that is, protection, from the Šayṭān. This shows that Tawḥīd and constant Ḏikr are among the strongest means by which the servant is preserved from temptation and whispering.

HAD-2068.text: No one comes with something better than the one who says this Tahlīl, except someone who does more than he does.
HAD-2068.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2068.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2068.sharh: The explanation shows that this Ḏikr has a very high rank. Whoever says it with the mentioned number attains a tremendous reward; he is surpassed only by someone who performs still more of this act of worship or of a comparable one.

HAD-2069.text: That I say: Subḥānallāh, al-Ḥamdu lillāh, lā ilāha illa-llāh and Allahu Akbar, is dearer to me than that over which the sun rises.
HAD-2069.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2069.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2069.sharh: The Sharḥ explains that these four words were dearer to the Prophet ﷺ than everything over which the sun rises, that is, the world and its goods. What is meant is the tremendous excellence of this Ḏikr over worldly possession; at the same time it does not mean that it absolutely precedes every Qurʾān recitation or every situation-bound Ḏikr.

HAD-2070.text: The words most beloved to Allah are four: Subḥānallāh, al-Ḥamdu lillāh, lā ilāha illa-llāh and Allahu Akbar.
HAD-2070.narrator: Samurah ibn Ǧundub رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2070.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2070.sharh: The explanation shows that these four words are among the statements most beloved to Allah, because they unite the basic meanings of Ḏikr: Allah’s perfect purity from deficiency, His praise, His uniqueness in worship, and His greatness. Therefore they are among the most excellent words of the servant.

HAD-2071.text: Deeds are only according to intentions, and each person is due only what he intended.
HAD-2071.narrator: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2071.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2071.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains that the intention is the scale of the deed: the same outward action can, according to the Niyyah, be worship, habit, or sin. The Ḥadīṯ is therefore a basis for the acceptance and evaluation of actions.

HAD-2072.text: The Ḥalāl is clear and the Ḥarām is clear, and between the two lie doubtful matters.
HAD-2072.narrator: an-Nuʿmān ibn Bašīr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2072.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2072.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that this Ḥadīṯ is a great foundation of the Dīn: the servant protects his religion and his honor by avoiding doubtful things, because they can lead to the forbidden.

HAD-2073.narrator: Tamīm ad-Dārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2073.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2073.sharh: an-Nawawī explains Naṣīḥah as comprehensive sincerity: toward Allah through Tawḥīd and obedience, toward the Messenger ﷺ through following, and toward the Muslims through counsel, loyalty, and help.

HAD-2074.text: Leave what makes you doubt for that which does not make you doubt.
HAD-2074.narrator: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2074.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2074.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that the believer leaves doubtful things and chooses that in which certainty and calm of the heart lie. Thus he protects his Dīn and distances himself from suspicion and inner unrest.

HAD-2075.text: There shall be neither harm nor mutual harm.
HAD-2075.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2075.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2075.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that the Ḥadīṯ is a great legal rule: it is forbidden to inflict harm on others in the first place or to respond with unlawful counter-harm. Harm is removed in the Dīn and is not newly produced.

HAD-2076.text: Fear Allah wherever you are, and let a good deed follow the bad deed, then it erases it.
HAD-2076.narrator: Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2076.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2076.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that Taqwā is required both in private and in public. Good deeds erase bad ones when the servant repents, improves himself, and lets obedience follow the sin.

HAD-2077.text: Allah does not look at your bodies and does not look at your forms, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds.
HAD-2077.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2077.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2077.sharh: an-Nawawī explains that a person’s worth does not arise from outward appearance, but from the heart and the deeds. What is meant is sincerity, Īmān, right intention, and righteous action.

HAD-2078.text: A sense of shame is a branch of Īmān.
HAD-2078.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2078.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2078.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains that Ḥayāʾ belongs to Īmān, because true shame keeps the servant from evil and leads him to obedience. Therefore it is not merely character, but a religious effect of faith.

HAD-2079.text: The strong believer is more beloved to Allah and better than the weak believer; in both there lies good.
HAD-2079.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2079.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2079.sharh: an-Nawawī explains that strength here means especially strength in Īmān, in resolve, in patience, and in benefit for the Dīn. Nevertheless the weak believer remains in the good because of his Īmān.

HAD-2080.text: Strive for what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not be incapable.
HAD-2080.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2080.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2080.sharh: an-Nawawī explains that the servant must join two things: actively taking up beneficial means and seeking help from Allah. Laziness, incapacity, and mere regret are thereby rejected.

HAD-2081.text: Whoever introduces into this matter of ours something that does not belong to it, his deed is rejected.
HAD-2081.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2081.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that this Ḥadīṯ is a scale for outward actions: everything that is introduced into the Dīn without a basis is rejected, even if the one who does it means it well.

HAD-2082.text: If I forbid you something, then avoid it; and if I command you something, then do of it what you are able.
HAD-2082.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2082.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2082.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that prohibitions are in principle to be avoided completely, while commands are fulfilled according to ability. In this there is mercy, and the rule that Allah does not burden the servant beyond his strength.

HAD-2083.narrator: Abū Mālik al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2083.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2083.sharh: an-Nawawī explains that Ṭahārah has a tremendous standing: outward purification prepares for worship, and inward purification from Širk, sins, and bad traits belongs to the core of Īmān.

HAD-2084.text: The Qurʾān is a proof for you or against you.
HAD-2084.narrator: Abū Mālik al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2084.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2084.sharh: an-Nawawī explains that the Qurʾān benefits the one who recites it, understands it, and follows it; but it testifies against the one who reads it and contradicts its guidance.

HAD-2085.text: Every person goes out in the morning and sells his soul: he frees it or he ruins it.
HAD-2085.narrator: Abū Mālik al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2085.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2085.sharh: an-Nawawī explains that every day brings a new situation of action: whoever obeys Allah frees his soul; whoever follows sin sells it to its ruin.

HAD-2086.text: Astonishing is the affair of the believer: his whole affair is good.
HAD-2086.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2086.sharh: an-Nawawī explains that the believer gives thanks in joy and is patient in suffering. Thereby both well-being and trial become a good for him, because both states lead him back to Allah.

HAD-2087.text: Patience is only at the first shock.
HAD-2087.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2087.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2087.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains that true patience shows itself especially in the first moment of the affliction, when the pain is fresh and the soul is pressed toward complaining.

HAD-2088.text: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or remain silent.
HAD-2088.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2088.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2088.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that the tongue should be opened only for good. Whoever is not sure that his speech is good protects his Dīn by silence.

HAD-2089.text: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should honor his guest.
HAD-2089.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2089.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2089.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that honoring the guest belongs to the visible fruits of Īmān. Faith shows itself not only in words, but also in good conduct toward Allah’s creatures.

HAD-2090.text: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should honor his neighbor.
HAD-2090.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2090.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2090.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that the neighbor’s right belongs to the signs of complete Īmān. This includes refraining from harm, kindness, consideration, and preserving his right.

HAD-2091.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2091.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2091.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar and an-Nawawī explain that these five pillars are the most visible foundations of Islam. The Ḥadīṯ names the supporting pillars upon which the outward order of the Dīn stands.

HAD-2092.narrator: Abū Mālik al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2092.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2092.sharh: an-Nawawī explains that the prayer is light because it leads the servant to guidance, restrains him from what is shameful, and can be light and proof for him on the Day of Resurrection.

HAD-2093.text: The servant is nearest to his Lord while he is in suǧūd.
HAD-2093.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2093.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2093.sharh: an-Nawawī explains that suǧūd has a particularly honored station because of complete humility, lowliness before Allah, and nearness to worship. For this reason, abundant duʿāʾ is recommended in it.

HAD-2094.text: Between the human being and Širk and Kufr stands the abandonment of the prayer.
HAD-2094.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2094.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2094.sharh: an-Nawawī explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the immense danger of abandoning the Ṣalāh. He cites the known interpretations of the scholars: either as Kufr that takes one out of the religion, or as the severest threat for a deed that resembles the acts of Kufr.

HAD-2095.text: The prayer in congregation surpasses the prayer alone by twenty-seven degrees.
HAD-2095.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2095.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2095.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains that the merit of the congregation comes from its many meanings: the gathering of the Muslims, the open display of the Šaʿāʾir, mutual reminder, and the greater completeness of the prayer.

HAD-2096.text: Whoever performs the morning prayer stands in the protection of Allah.
HAD-2096.narrator: Ǧundub ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2096.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2096.sharh: an-Nawawī explains that the protection of Allah here contains a tremendous warning: whoever attacks the one who prays or violates his right exposes himself to Allah’s claim. At the same time it shows the special station of the morning prayer.

HAD-2097.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2097.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2097.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar and an-Nawawī explain that fasting is a shield: it protects from sins, breaks the desires, and is a protection from the Fire when it is performed with sincerity and guarding of the tongue.

HAD-2098.text: Whoever fasts Ramaḍān out of Īmān and out of hope of reward, what preceded of his sins is forgiven him.
HAD-2098.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2098.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2098.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains that “out of Īmān” means: in belief in Allah’s duty and promise; and “out of hope of reward” means: sincerely for Allah, not out of habit, reputation, or mere conformity.

HAD-2099.text: Ṣadaqah does not diminish any possession.
HAD-2099.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2099.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2099.sharh: an-Nawawī explains that Ṣadaqah does not truly diminish possession: Allah replaces it, blesses what remains, and raises the servant thereby. The visible decrease is surpassed by blessing and reward.

HAD-2100.text: The upper hand is better than the lower hand.
HAD-2100.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2100.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2100.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains that the upper hand is the giving hand and the lower is the taking one. The Ḥadīṯ educates toward generosity, self-sufficiency, and dignity instead of unnecessary asking.

HAD-2101.text: Protect yourselves from the Fire, even with half a date.
HAD-2101.narrator: ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2101.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2101.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains that even a small Ṣadaqah should not be belittled. A small gift can, because of sincerity and need, have a great reward and be a protection from the Fire.

HAD-2102.text: Upon every joint of the human being there lies each day a Ṣadaqah.
HAD-2102.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2102.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2102.sharh: an-Nawawī explains that the human being owes thanks for the gifts of his body. This thanks takes place through manifold good deeds, not only through gifts of money, but also through reconciliation, help, and a good word.

HAD-2103.text: To remove a harmful object from the path is Ṣadaqah.
HAD-2103.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2103.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2103.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains that good deeds also lie in seemingly small services. Removing harm from the path protects people and shows that Ṣadaqah is not only money, but can be every beneficial act of obedience.

HAD-2104.text: The best of you is the one who learns the Qurʾān and teaches it.
HAD-2104.narrator: ʿUṯmān ibn ʿAffān رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2104.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2104.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains that the merit arises from the joining of learning and teaching. Whoever learns the Qurʾān acts for himself; whoever teaches it lets the benefit pass on to others.

HAD-2105.text: The knowledgeable reciter of the Qurʾān is with the noble, righteous scribes.
HAD-2105.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2105.sharh: an-Nawawī explains that the knowledgeable reciter receives a high station because of his completeness in reciting and preserving the Qurʾān. Whoever strives despite difficulty likewise receives an immense reward.

HAD-2266.text: Everything of the Muslim is inviolable for the Muslim: his blood, his property, and his honor.
HAD-2266.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2266.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2266.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the three protected domains comprehensively: blood stands for body and life, property for material possessions, and honor for protection from degrading or injurious speech. The Ḥadīṯ thus summarizes fundamental rights of the Muslim.

HAD-2267.text: Whoever removes from a believer one of the hardships of this world, from him Allah removes one of the hardships of the Day of Resurrection.
HAD-2267.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2267.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2267.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains »naffasa« as the removal and easing of a hardship. The Ḥadīṯ sets the help given to the believer in this world over against a corresponding relief from Allah on the Day of Resurrection.

HAD-2268.text: Whoever grants relief to a person in need, Allah grants him relief in this world and in the Hereafter.
HAD-2268.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2268.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2268.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats relief for the one who is in hardship or in difficulty of payment as part of the comprehensive principle of mutual help. Whoever lawfully grants relief to another, to him the Ḥadīṯ promises corresponding relief from Allah.

HAD-2269.text: Whoever covers a Muslim, Allah covers him in this world and in the Hereafter.
HAD-2269.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2269.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2269.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ places the covering of the Muslim among the deeds that are answered with a divine recompense of the same kind. What is meant is the covering of faults whose disclosure has no legally required benefit, not the concealment of ongoing wrong that endangers others.

HAD-2270.text: Allah helps the servant as long as the servant helps his brother.
HAD-2270.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2270.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2270.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats the sentence as a comprehensive principle of mutual support. As long as the servant helps his brother in what is lawful and good, he stands under the promise of divine help; the wording joins service to people with hope in Allah’s aid.

HAD-2271.text: Whoever travels a path on which he seeks knowledge, Allah thereby eases for him a path to Paradise.
HAD-2271.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2271.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2271.sharh: Ibn al-ʿArabī explains that the path of knowledge is not only the physical path to a teacher, but includes every serious effort for beneficial religious knowledge. Allah thereby eases for the seeker the paths of obedience that lead to Paradise.

HAD-2272.text: No people gather in a house of Allah to recite the Book of Allah and study it together except that special gifts are granted to them.
HAD-2272.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2272.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2272.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that the Ḥadīṯ expressly praises the shared recitation and mutual study of the Qurʾān in the houses of Allah. Shared learning thus belongs to the special gatherings for which the subsequent promises are named.

HAD-2273.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2273.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2273.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains the descending Sakīnah as a special tranquility and firmness that Allah grants to those gathered. Occupation with the Qurʾān thus brings not only knowledge, but also inner calm and steadfastness.

HAD-2274.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2274.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2274.sharh: Ibn Raǧab places the enveloping by mercy among the special consequences of the Qurʾān gathering. Those assembled are thereby under a special divine Raḥmah as long as they occupy themselves with Allah’s Book.

HAD-2275.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2275.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2275.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains the presence of the angels as a special honoring of the gathering of the Qurʾān and of knowledge. The angels surround the people who occupy themselves with Allah’s Book as a sign of the excellence of this sitting.

HAD-2276.text: Allah mentions them with those who are with Him.
HAD-2276.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2276.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2276.sharh: Ibn Raǧab emphasizes the greatness of this promise: whoever remembers Allah together with others through the Qurʾān and knowledge is mentioned by Allah in a higher assembly. This is a special form of honoring.

HAD-2277.text: Whomever his deeds hold back, his lineage does not bring him forward more quickly.
HAD-2277.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2277.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2277.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that the ranks in the Hereafter are attained through Īmān and righteous deeds, not through lineage. Whoever falls behind in his action is not raised, by a noble genealogy alone, to the ranks of those who act.

HAD-2278.text: Allah has recorded the good deeds and the bad deeds and then explained this.
HAD-2278.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2278.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported from his Lord عز وجل:
HAD-2278.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl treats the Ḥadīṯ as an expression of Allah’s immense favor toward the servants: good and bad deeds are not treated alike; rather, the following explanation shows a clear preference for the good and a limitation of the bad.

HAD-2279.text: Whoever intends a good deed and does not carry it out, Allah records it for him as a complete good deed.
HAD-2279.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2279.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported from his Lord عز وجل:
HAD-2279.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that even the serious intention toward the good is a deed of the heart and is therefore rewarded. That it is recorded as a complete good deed shows Allah’s special favor, although the outward act has not yet taken place.

HAD-2280.text: Whoever intends a good deed and carries it out, Allah records for him from ten up to seven hundred good deeds and many further multiples besides.
HAD-2280.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2280.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported from his Lord عز وجل:
HAD-2280.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl highlights the multiplication of the good deed as a special favor of Allah. The reward begins at tenfold and can be increased up to seven-hundredfold and beyond.

HAD-2281.text: Whoever intends a bad deed and does not carry it out, Allah records for him a complete good deed; if he carries it out, only a single bad deed is recorded against him.
HAD-2281.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2281.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported from his Lord عز وجل:
HAD-2281.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl highlights the mercy of Allah: good deeds are multiplied, whereas bad deeds are not. Abstaining from the intended sin can be recorded as a good deed, while the sin actually committed is at first counted only once.

HAD-2282.text: Whoever shows enmity to a Walī of Mine, I have declared war on him.
HAD-2282.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2282.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported from his Lord عز وجل:
HAD-2282.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl shows the immense standing of the Awliyāʾ of Allah: enmity toward a servant because of his nearness to Allah and his obedience is a grave matter. Wilāyah rests on Īmān, Taqwā, and obedience, not on mere claim.

HAD-2283.text: My servant does not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than what I have made obligatory upon him.
HAD-2283.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2283.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported from his Lord عز وجل:
HAD-2283.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Farāʾiḍ take precedence over voluntary deeds. The basis of nearness to Allah is first the careful fulfillment of what Allah has prescribed as binding.

HAD-2284.text: My servant continues to draw near to Me through voluntary deeds until I love him.
HAD-2284.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2284.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported from his Lord عز وجل:
HAD-2284.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that Nawāfil, on the basis of fulfilled obligations, carry the servant further forward in nearness to Allah. Continued voluntary ʿIbādah is thus a path to the special love of Allah.

HAD-2285.text: When I love him, I am his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he grasps, and his foot with which he walks.
HAD-2285.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2285.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported from his Lord عز وجل:
HAD-2285.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl understands the statement as a special divine preservation and guidance: the beloved servant is led, in his senses and actions, to what Allah loves and permits, and is protected from using his limbs in disobedience.

HAD-2046.text: Whoever is reached by an authentic Ḥadīṯ from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and does not accept it stands on the brink of ruin.
HAD-2046.narrator: Isḥāq ibn Rāhawayh رحمه الله said:
HAD-2046.speaker: He said:

HAD-2047.text: The defense of the Sunnah is better than fighting with the sword.
HAD-2047.narrator: Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn رحمه الله said:
HAD-2047.speaker: He said:

HAD-2048.text: I met more than a thousand men of the scholars, and I saw none of them differing in this: that Īmān is word and deed.
HAD-2048.speaker: He said:

HAD-2049.text: The sign of the people of innovation is that they revile the people of transmission.
HAD-2049.narrator: Abū Ḥātim ar-Rāzī رحمه الله said:
HAD-2049.speaker: He said:

HAD-2050.text: If you see a man who belittles a Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then know that he is a heretic.
HAD-2050.narrator: Abū Zurʿah ar-Rāzī رحمه الله said:
HAD-2050.speaker: He said:

HAD-2051.text: Whoever grants relief to someone in distress, Allah grants him relief in this world and in the Hereafter.
HAD-2051.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2051.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2051.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that the principle here is: Recompense is of the same kind as the deed. A kurbah is a severe distress; to relieve it means to remove the constriction from the one afflicted or to ease it. Thus, whoever relieves a believer of a worldly distress, Allah relieves for him a far greater distress on the Day of Resurrection.

HAD-2052.text: Whoever covers a Muslim’s fault, Allah covers his fault in this world and in the Hereafter.
HAD-2052.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2052.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2052.sharh: The explanation indicates that covering a Muslim means not exposing his faults and slips, but treating him with Naṣīḥah and protection from public disgrace. This does not count as support of the sin, but as a moral covering, so long as no harm and no continuing injustice are thereby protected.

HAD-2053.text: Allah helps the servant as long as the servant helps his brother.
HAD-2053.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2053.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2053.sharh: The statement sums up the reward for helping: whoever stands by his brother in permitted and good matters remains under Allah’s help. The servant’s help to his brother is thereby a cause for Allah Himself to grant him help, relief, and support.

HAD-2054.text: Whoever travels a path on which he seeks knowledge, Allah thereby eases for him a path to Paradise.
HAD-2054.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2054.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2054.sharh: The explanation shows the high station of beneficial knowledge: the path may be the actual path to a gathering of knowledge, or every path by which knowledge is sought. This knowledge is a means to right guidance and thereby a cause for Allah to ease for the servant the path to Paradise.

HAD-2055.text: No people gather in a house among the houses of Allah, recite the Book of Allah and study it together, except that calm descends upon them.
HAD-2055.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2055.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2055.sharh: The explanation mentions the special merit of gathering for recitation and shared occupation with the Qurʾān. Whoever gathers in a house of Allah for Tilāwah and Tadārus receives a special gift: Sakīnah, that is, calm, firmness, and inner reassurance.

HAD-2056.text: The angels surround them, mercy covers them, and Allah mentions them among those who are with Him.
HAD-2056.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2056.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2056.sharh: Among the fruits of this Qurʾān gathering are several honors: mercy envelops the participants, angels surround them, and Allah mentions them among the angels. The explanation thereby stresses that occupation with the Qurʾān brings not only knowledge, but also nearness, protection, and praise with Allah.

HAD-2057.text: Whomever his deed holds back, his lineage does not advance him.
HAD-2057.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2057.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2057.sharh: The explanation makes clear: before Allah, origin, standing, or lineage does not count, but righteous deed. Whoever falls behind through insufficient deed is not brought forward by his nasab; the measure of nearness to Allah is thus obedience and ʿAmal, not mere belonging.

HAD-2058.text: The likeness of the one who remembers his Lord and of the one who does not remember his Lord is like the likeness of the living and the dead.
HAD-2058.narrator: Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2058.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2058.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains that the one who remembers resembles the living: his outward is adorned by life and obedience, and his inward is illuminated by knowledge. The one who does not remember Allah resembles the dead, because benefit, light, and spiritual vitality are absent in him.

HAD-2059.text: Allah has angels who roam the roads and seek the people of Ḏikr.
HAD-2059.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2059.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2059.sharh: An-Nawawī explains concerning the angels that they are described as roaming angels who deliberately seek the gatherings of Ḏikr. From this the special honor of such sittings becomes visible: they are not hidden, but are sought out and surrounded by angels.

HAD-2060.text: Allah says: I am at My servant’s opinion of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me.
HAD-2060.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2060.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2060.sharh: The explanation of the scholars shows: good thinking about Allah means hoping for His mercy, forgiveness, and acceptance while remaining obedient to Him. The statement “I am with him when he remembers Me” points to special nearness, support, and acceptance for the servant who mentions Allah.

HAD-2061.text: Two words are light on the tongue, heavy on the scale, and beloved to the Most Merciful.
HAD-2061.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2061.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2061.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains the contrast between lightness and weight: the words are easy to say and can be repeated without effort, but their reward is heavy on the scale. That they are beloved to the Most Merciful shows their special station among the forms of Tasbīḥ and Ḏikr.

HAD-2062.text: These two words are: Subḥānallāhi wa-bi-ḥamdihī, Subḥānallāhi l-ʿAẓīm.
HAD-2062.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2062.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2062.sharh: The sharḥ explains that these two formulas declare Allah free of every deficiency and at the same time describe Him with praise and greatness. They therefore join Tanzīh, Ḥamd, and the acknowledgment of Allah’s greatness in a few words that are easy to pronounce.

HAD-2063.text: Whoever says a hundred times a day: Subḥānallāhi wa-bi-ḥamdihī, his sins are forgiven, even if they are like the foam of the sea.
HAD-2063.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2063.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2063.sharh: The explanation shows the vastness of Allah’s forgiveness: the comparison with the sea foam stands for a great quantity of sins. Whoever regularly says this Ḏikr receives forgiveness of sins, and the scholars understand this within the known rules of repentance and of the distinction between minor and major sins.

HAD-2064.text: Whoever says: Lā ilāha illa-llāhu waḥdahū lā šarīka lah, receives a mighty reward and protection.
HAD-2064.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2064.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2064.sharh: The sharḥ explains that this formula contains pure Tawḥīd: Allah alone possesses worship, dominion, praise, and full power. The rewards named in the Ḥadīṯ, good deeds, the erasure of sins, and protection from the Šayṭān, show the special station of the Tahlīl and of its repetition.

HAD-2065.text: Whoever says this Tahlīl a hundred times, it is for him equal to the freeing of ten slaves.
HAD-2065.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2065.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2065.sharh: The sharḥ explains that the reward of the Tahlīl is here compared with the freeing of ten slaves, in order to show the greatness of its reward. The formula contains pure Tawḥīd: Allah alone has worship, dominion, praise, and perfect power.

HAD-2226.text: Removing what is harmful from the path is a Ṣadaqah.
HAD-2226.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2226.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2226.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl counts the removal of harm from the path among the good deeds by which the servant gives thanks for the gifts of his body. The benefit is directed immediately to other people, by the removal of a cause of injury or obstruction.

HAD-2227.narrator: an-Nawwās ibn Samʿān رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2227.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
