HAD-2227.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains Birr as the opposite of sin and iniquity. In this context, Birr comprises what the Šarīʿah requires as obligatory or as recommended, and good character gathers many of these forms of good into one comprehensive quality.

HAD-2228.text: Sin is that which stirs unrest in your soul and of which you do not wish people to know.
HAD-2228.narrator: an-Nawwās ibn Samʿān رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2228.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2228.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains Iṯm as that which the Šarīʿah forbids. The inner unrest and the unease at righteous people coming to know of it are a warning sign in matters whose prohibition the servant does not already know from a clear text; clear revelation is not thereby annulled.

HAD-2229.text: I counsel you to Taqwā toward Allah and to hearing and obeying.
HAD-2229.narrator: al-ʿIrbāḍ ibn Sāriyah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2229.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2229.sharh: Al-Ḫaṭṭābī cites the Ḥadīṯ in the chapter on holding fast to the Sunnah. The prophetic farewell exhortation begins with Taqwā and with orderly hearing and obeying; thereby fear of Allah and the preservation of the communal order are placed at the beginning of the guidance.

HAD-2230.text: Whoever of you lives after me will see many differences of opinion.
HAD-2230.narrator: al-ʿIrbāḍ ibn Sāriyah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2230.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2230.sharh: Al-Ḫaṭṭābī places this prediction directly in connection with the following instruction to hold fast to the Sunnah. The multitude of later differences thereby does not become an occasion for arbitrariness, but for a stronger bond to the transmitted prophetic guidance.

HAD-2231.text: Hold to my Sunnah and to the Sunnah of the rightly guided, rightly led caliphs; hold fast to it and bite onto it with the molars.
HAD-2231.narrator: al-ʿIrbāḍ ibn Sāriyah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2231.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2231.sharh: Al-Ḫaṭṭābī explains the biting with the molars as an image of the utmost resolve in holding fast to the Sunnah: like one who holds something so firmly between the teeth that it cannot be wrested from him. He sees in it at the same time the command to remain patient with the difficulties of holding fast to the Sunnah.

HAD-2232.text: Beware of newly introduced matters; for every newly introduced matter is a Bidʿah, and every Bidʿah is misguidance.
HAD-2232.narrator: al-ʿIrbāḍ ibn Sāriyah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2232.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2232.sharh: Al-Ḫaṭṭābī explains the condemned newly introduced matter as that which is introduced without a basis in the foundations of the religion and without being traced back to its standard. What, by contrast, rests on recognized principles and is traced back to them does not, according to his explanation, fall under the Bidʿah and misguidance condemned here.

HAD-2233.text: You have asked about something great; yet it is easy for the one for whom Allah makes it easy.
HAD-2233.narrator: Muʿāḏ ibn Ǧabal رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2233.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2233.sharh: Ibn al-ʿArabī treats the Ḥadīṯ as a connected guidance to the foundations and the means of protection of the religion. The answer makes clear: the goal — entry into Paradise and removal from the Fire — is immense, yet it becomes attainable through Allah’s making it easy, by the way of obedience.

HAD-2234.text: Serve Allah and associate nothing with Him.
HAD-2234.narrator: Muʿāḏ ibn Ǧabal رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2234.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2234.sharh: Ibn al-ʿArabī places this instruction at the beginning of the answer: the foundation of all following deeds is exclusive ʿIbādah for Allah without Širk. Without this foundation, the subsequent pillars do not bear the meaning that belongs to them in the Ḥadīṯ.

HAD-2235.narrator: Muʿāḏ ibn Ǧabal رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2235.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2235.sharh: Ibn al-ʿArabī treats the prayer as one of the central obligatory pillars that follow immediately upon Tawḥīd. In the later image of the same Ḥadīṯ, the Prophet ﷺ expressly designates the prayer as the supporting pillar of the religious edifice.

HAD-2236.narrator: Muʿāḏ ibn Ǧabal رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2236.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2236.sharh: Ibn al-ʿArabī mentions the Zakāh among the obligatory foundations by which the servant walks the path to Paradise. It joins obedience to Allah with the right that has been fixed in wealth.

HAD-2237.narrator: Muʿāḏ ibn Ǧabal رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2237.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2237.sharh: Ibn al-ʿArabī places the fasting of Ramaḍān among the obligatory foundational acts. Later in the same Ḥadīṯ the fast is described as a shield, whereby its role both as a duty and as a protection against sin is brought out.

HAD-2238.text: Perform the Ḥaǧǧ to the House.
HAD-2238.narrator: Muʿāḏ ibn Ǧabal رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2238.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2238.sharh: Ibn al-ʿArabī mentions the Ḥaǧǧ as part of the obligatory answer to Muʿāḏ’s question about the path to Paradise. Here it stands together with Tawḥīd, prayer, Zakāh and the fast of Ramaḍān as a foundational duty of Islam.

HAD-2239.narrator: Muʿāḏ ibn Ǧabal رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2239.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2239.sharh: Ibn al-ʿArabī explains the Ṣawm as protection: it shields the servant against the causes of the Fire by restraining desires and strengthening obedience. The image of the Ǧunnah thereby denotes protection and screening.

HAD-2240.text: Ṣadaqah extinguishes sin as water extinguishes fire.
HAD-2240.narrator: Muʿāḏ ibn Ǧabal رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2240.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2240.sharh: Ibn al-ʿArabī explains the image thus: the reward of Ṣadaqah removes the effect of the sin and protects the servant from its punishment, just as water sensibly extinguishes fire. The statement describes the expiating effect of the good deed.

HAD-2241.text: The prayer of a person in the depth of the night also belongs to the gates of good.
HAD-2241.narrator: Muʿāḏ ibn Ǧabal رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2241.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2241.sharh: Ibn al-ʿArabī links the night prayer with the special gates of good and refers to its already known excellence. The Ḥadīṯ places it alongside fasting and Ṣadaqah as a special voluntary deed with a strong character of protection and of drawing near.

HAD-2242.text: The head of the matter is Islam.
HAD-2242.narrator: Muʿāḏ ibn Ǧabal رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2242.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2242.sharh: Ibn al-ʿArabī explains the image of the head by the fact that a human being cannot subsist bodily without a head; correspondingly, the religious matter has no existence without Islam. Islam is thus the foundational prerequisite upon which the remaining works are built.

HAD-2243.narrator: Muʿāḏ ibn Ǧabal رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2243.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2243.sharh: Ibn al-ʿArabī explains the prayer as that upon which the religious edifice stands and on which it rests, just as a building rests on its supporting pillar. Thereby the special central position of the prayer among the practical acts is brought out.

HAD-2244.text: The tip of its hump is the Ǧihād.
HAD-2244.narrator: Muʿāḏ ibn Ǧabal رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2244.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2244.sharh: Ibn al-ʿArabī explains the «tip of the hump» as an image of the highest and most prominent place. The Ḥadīṯ thereby describes the high standing of the lawfully conducted Ǧihād within the religious duties and efforts.

HAD-2245.text: Hold back your tongue. Are people then cast into the Fire upon their faces because of anything other than the harvest of their tongues?
HAD-2245.narrator: Muʿāḏ ibn Ǧabal رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2245.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2245.sharh: Ibn al-ʿArabī sets forth the restraint of the tongue as the comprehensive means of protection after the deeds mentioned before. The «harvest of the tongues» denotes the consequences of what people acquire by their speech; unrestrained words can therefore become a cause of severe punishment.

HAD-2246.text: Allah has imposed obligations; so do not neglect them.
HAD-2246.narrator: Abū Ṯaʿlabah al-Ḫušanī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2246.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2246.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that the imposed obligations must be preserved and carried out. Neglecting them means abandoning what Allah has made binding; the first category of the Ḥadīṯ therefore concerns holding fast to the Farāʾiḍ.

HAD-2247.text: Allah has set limits; so do not transgress them.
HAD-2247.narrator: Abū Ṯaʿlabah al-Ḫušanī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2247.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2247.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains the Ḥudūd here as the limits set by Allah for what is permitted and what is commanded, which must not be transgressed. The expression is broader than the penal meaning of the word and includes stopping at what Allah has laid down.

HAD-2248.text: Allah has forbidden things; so do not violate these prohibitions.
HAD-2248.narrator: Abū Ṯaʿlabah al-Ḫušanī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2248.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2248.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that the forbidden things must neither be touched nor violated. The believer thereby distinguishes between what is commanded as obligatory, the limits that have been set, and what has been expressly forbidden, and treats each category accordingly.

HAD-2249.text: Allah has remained silent about things out of mercy — not out of forgetfulness; so do not inquire into them.
HAD-2249.narrator: Abū Ṯaʿlabah al-Ḫušanī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2249.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2249.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains the things that are not expressly regulated as a domain of pardon and mercy, so long as no other proof determines their ruling. The silence does not rest on forgetfulness; rather, it means that the servant should not seek new hardship through unnecessary inquiry.

HAD-2250.text: Renounce the world, and Allah will love you.
HAD-2250.narrator: Sahl ibn Saʿd as-Sāʿidī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2250.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2250.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains Zuhd not as a prohibition of permitted things, but as a slight attachment of the heart to the fleeting world. Whoever prefers what remains with Allah to what passes away directs his desire more strongly toward Allah and His reward.

HAD-2251.text: Renounce what people possess, and people will love you.
HAD-2251.narrator: Sahl ibn Saʿd as-Sāʿidī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2251.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2251.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains: Whoever does not look with desire at what is in people’s hands preserves himself from rivalry, asking, and dependence. People thereby feel secure from his claim, and their hearts incline to him more readily.

HAD-2252.text: Neither may harm be inflicted nor may harm be repaid with harm.
HAD-2252.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2252.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2252.sharh: Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr cites several explanations: harm may neither be inflicted on another from the outset nor returned as an unlawful counter-reaction. He emphasizes that the sentence applies as a general principle in a great many worldly legal questions.

HAD-2253.text: If people were given on the basis of their mere claims, people would claim the blood and the property of others.
HAD-2253.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2253.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2253.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains the legal reason: a mere claim is not sufficient, because otherwise blood and property would be left unprotected and exposed to the claims of others. Procedural law therefore requires a stronger basis than the mere presentation of a claim.

HAD-2254.text: The oath lies with the defendant.
HAD-2254.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2254.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2254.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains that the defendant’s side is supported by the original legal state: as a rule, the non-existence of additional claims is presumed. The oath strengthens this side when the plaintiff does not prove his claim in the required manner.

HAD-2255.text: Whoever among you sees something reprehensible should change it with his hand.
HAD-2255.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2255.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2255.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the Ḥadīṯ as a foundational text on the manner of changing what is reprehensible. Changing it with the hand applies where there is actual ability and within lawful authority; it must not lead to something still more reprehensible.

HAD-2256.text: If he is not able to do that, then with his tongue.
HAD-2256.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2256.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2256.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the degrees according to ability. If an actual change by the hand is not possible, or if it would cause greater harm, verbal admonition and explanation remain, within the limits of what is possible.

HAD-2257.text: If he is not able to do that either, then with his heart.
HAD-2257.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2257.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2257.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains: If the tongue also cannot be used, the rejection of what is reprehensible remains in the heart. This inner rejection does not lapse so long as the person recognizes the reprehensible as such.

HAD-2258.text: That is the weakest degree of Īmān.
HAD-2258.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2258.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2258.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ connects the degrees with the servant’s ability. Mere rejection in the heart is the last and weakest remaining form when the hand and the tongue cannot be used; the Ḥadīṯ thereby also shows gradations in Īmān.

HAD-2259.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2259.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2259.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats the Ḥadīṯ in the chapter on the rights of the Muslim. The prohibition of envy protects brotherhood from a person begrudging his brother’s gift or wishing for its disappearance.

HAD-2260.text: Do not practice Naǧaš against one another.
HAD-2260.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2260.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2260.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ places Naǧaš among the forbidden acts that produce mistrust and enmity. In a sale it means in particular artificially driving up a price without a genuine intention to buy, in order to deceive another.

HAD-2261.text: Do not hate one another, and do not turn your backs on one another.
HAD-2261.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2261.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2261.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains Tadābur as mutual turning away and enmity, in which one, so to speak, turns his back on the other. The Ḥadīṯ thereby forbids modes of conduct that destroy Islamic brotherhood.

HAD-2262.text: None of you should place his own sale upon the sale of his brother.
HAD-2262.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2262.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2262.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats the prohibition in connection with the preservation of mutual rights. An existing concluded purchase, or a serious initiation of a purchase, must not be undermined by a competing offer in a way that produces dispute and harm.

HAD-2263.text: Be servants of Allah as brothers.
HAD-2263.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2263.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2263.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ connects the preceding prohibitions with their positive aim: the servants of Allah should live together in religious brotherhood. Avoiding envy, deception, hatred, and turning away protects precisely this bond.

HAD-2264.text: The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim: he does him no wrong, does not abandon him, and does not despise him.
HAD-2264.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2264.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2264.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains: Not abandoning the Muslim brother means standing by him with help and support in a lawful need. Likewise, wrong and contempt are incompatible with the brotherhood that is owed.

HAD-2265.text: Taqwā is here — and he pointed three times to his chest. It is enough evil for a person that he despises his Muslim brother.
HAD-2265.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2265.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2265.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ connects the warning against contempt with the inner state of the heart. Outward rank, possession, or appearance does not justify belittling a Muslim; what is decisive is Taqwā, whose true reality Allah knows.

HAD-2126.text: Four qualities: whoever possesses them is a pure hypocrite.
HAD-2126.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2126.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2126.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains that what is meant here is practical hypocrisy, when these qualities appear persistently in conduct. The threat is meant to deter the believer from lying, betrayal, faithlessness, and an immoderate eagerness to quarrel.

HAD-2127.text: The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe.
HAD-2127.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2127.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2127.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the perfection of Islam in one’s dealings. Whoever harms others with tongue or hand has lost a quality that belongs to perfect Islam.

HAD-2128.text: The emigrant is the one who abandons what Allah has forbidden.
HAD-2128.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2128.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2128.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains that the true Hiǧrah is not merely a change of place. A lasting meaning of the Hiǧrah is to abandon sins and prohibitions for the sake of Allah.

HAD-2129.text: Whoever points to something good receives reward like the one who does it.
HAD-2129.narrator: Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2129.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2129.sharh: an-Nawawī explains that the one who guides to good, reminds of it, or opens the way to it receives a share of the reward. This includes teaching, giving counsel, mediating, and every permitted help toward obedience.

HAD-2130.text: Whoever calls to right guidance receives reward like the rewards of those who follow him.
HAD-2130.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2130.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2130.sharh: an-Nawawī explains that the call to right guidance brings ongoing reward as long as people follow the good. The doers’ own reward is not diminished by this.

HAD-2131.text: Say: I believe in Allah; then remain steadfast.
HAD-2131.narrator: Sufyān ibn ʿAbdillāh aṯ-Ṯaqafī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2131.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2131.sharh: an-Nawawī explains that this Ḥadīṯ sums up the Dīn: correct Īmān in Allah and thereafter steadfastness in obedience. Istiqaāmah means remaining on the straight path and not deviating from it knowingly.

HAD-2132.text: Three qualities: whoever possesses them finds through them the sweetness of Īmān.
HAD-2132.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2132.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2132.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains that the sweetness of Īmān means the inner joy, calm, and strength that the servant experiences through love of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ, love for the sake of Allah, and aversion to Kufr.

HAD-2133.text: The deeds most beloved to Allah are the most constant, even if they are few.
HAD-2133.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2133.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains that constancy shows that the deed rests on resolve, love, and sincerity. A few lasting deeds are better than much that soon breaks off and wearies the servant.

HAD-2134.text: Whomever Allah wants good for, He gives him understanding in the Dīn.
HAD-2134.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2134.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains that Fiqh in the Dīn is a sign of Allah’s good for the servant. What is meant is understanding of the Qurʾān, the Sunnah, faith, Ḥalāl and Ḥarām, so that the servant worships Allah correctly.

HAD-2135.text: Guard Allah, then Allah will guard you.
HAD-2135.narrator: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2135.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2135.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that ‘guarding Allah’ means guarding His limits, commands, and prohibitions. Whoever does this, Allah guards him in his Dīn, his world, and in what is truly beneficial for him.

HAD-2136.text: When you ask, ask Allah; and when you seek help, seek help from Allah.
HAD-2136.narrator: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2136.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2136.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that these words contain the Tawḥīd in Duʿāʾ and Istiʿānah. The heart, in asking, hope, and help, should be bound first and in truth to Allah.

HAD-2137.text: Allah recorded the good and bad deeds and then explained them.
HAD-2137.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2137.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2137.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that this Ḥadīṯ shows Allah’s immense mercy: an intended good deed is already recorded, while a bad deed is not recorded until it is committed.

HAD-2138.text: O My servants, I have forbidden injustice to Myself and made it forbidden among you.
HAD-2138.narrator: Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2138.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ narrated from his Lord:
HAD-2138.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that this Ḥadīṯ shows the perfection of Allah’s justice. Allah is free of injustice, and He forbids His servants mutual injustice in blood, property, honor, and all rights.

HAD-2139.text: Allah stretches out His hand in the night so that the sinner of the day may repent.
HAD-2139.narrator: Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2139.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2139.sharh: an-Nawawī explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the vastness of Allah’s acceptance of repentance. The door of Tawbah remains open, and Allah calls His servants to return despite their sins.

HAD-2140.text: Allah rejoices over the repentance of His servant more than one of you who finds his lost mount again.
HAD-2140.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2140.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2140.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar and an-Nawawī explain that the Ḥadīṯ illustrates Allah’s immense acceptance of Tawbah. The joy is understood in a manner that befits Allah’s transcendence, without equating Him with creation.

HAD-2141.text: The master of the Istighfār petitions is that the servant confesses his guilt and asks Allah for forgiveness.
HAD-2141.narrator: Šaddād ibn Aws رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2141.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2141.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains that this petition joins Tawḥīd, acknowledgment of Allah’s grace, confession of one’s own sin, and hope of forgiveness. For this reason it was described as the most excellent form of Istighfār.

HAD-2142.text: In the body there is a piece of flesh: if it is good, the whole body is good.
HAD-2142.narrator: an-Nuʿmān ibn Bašīr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2142.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2142.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that the heart is the king of the limbs. When the heart is sound through Īmān, sincerity, and Taqwā, the limbs follow it in good; when it is corrupted, corruption appears in the deeds.

HAD-2143.text: Paradise is nearer to one of you than the strap of his shoe, and the Fire likewise.
HAD-2143.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2143.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2143.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the nearness of salvation and ruin. A small deed can be a cause of great mercy, and a sin can endanger the person; therefore the servant should remain vigilant.

HAD-2144.text: Deeds are according to their endings.
HAD-2144.narrator: Sahl ibn Saʿd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2144.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2144.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains that the outcome of a deed and the end of life are decisive. The Ḥadīṯ calls one to remain steadfast until death and not to rely on earlier deeds.

HAD-2145.text: Every servant will be raised according to that upon which he died.
HAD-2145.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2145.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2145.sharh: an-Nawawī explains that the person will be raised on the Day of Resurrection according to his state at death. In this lies a strong admonition to live upon good and to seek a good end.

HAD-2146.text: Remember frequently the destroyer of pleasures: death.
HAD-2146.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2146.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2146.sharh: al-Mubārakfūrī explains that frequent remembrance of death weakens attachment to the world, impels one to tawbah, and prepares the servant for meeting Allah.

HAD-2147.narrator: an-Nuʿmān ibn Bašīr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2147.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2147.sharh: al-Mubārakfūrī explains that Duʿāʾ itself is ʿIbādah, because in it lie neediness, humility, hope, and turning toward Allah. Whoever asks Allah testifies to His power, His nearness, and His uniqueness in answering.

HAD-2148.text: Whoever dies knowing that there is none rightfully worshipped except Allah enters Paradise.
HAD-2148.narrator: ʿUṯmān ibn ʿAffān رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2148.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2148.sharh: an-Nawawī explains that knowledge of lā ilāha illa-llāh does not mean mere utterance, but knowledge, acknowledgment, and holding fast to Tawḥīd. The Ḥadīṯ shows the immense merit of Tawḥīd and its end in Paradise.

HAD-2149.text: Whoever testifies that none is rightfully worshipped except Allah and that Muḥammad is His Messenger, Allah makes the Fire forbidden for him.
HAD-2149.narrator: ʿUbādah ibn aṣ-Ṣāmit رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2149.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2149.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar and an-Nawawī explain that the Šahādah is joined with knowledge, truthfulness, and acceptance. Its promise applies to the one who fulfills Tawḥīd and does not destroy it by what contradicts it.

HAD-2150.text: The best speech is the Book of Allah, and the best guidance is the guidance of Muḥammad ﷺ.
HAD-2150.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2150.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2150.sharh: an-Nawawī explains that the Ḥadīṯ shows the perfection of the revelation and of the prophetic guidance. The best speech is Allah’s Book, and every guidance is measured by the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ.

HAD-2151.text: Deeds are judged only according to intentions.
HAD-2151.narrator: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2151.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2151.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl transmits from al-Muhallab that al-Buḫārī placed the Ḥadīṯ of intentions at the beginning of his work in order to indicate that reading, writing, and acting likewise receive their due worth only with a sincere intention for Allah. The deed is therefore not valued merely according to its outward form, but according to its Niyyah.

HAD-2152.text: Each person is entitled only to what he intended.
HAD-2152.narrator: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2152.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2152.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl’s explanation of the beginning of Ṣaḥīḥ al-Buḫārī shows that a person’s share in an action depends on his intention: the same outward path or the same outward action receives its religious worth only through what the doer intends by it.

HAD-2153.text: Whoever performed his Hiǧrah for Allah and His Messenger, his Hiǧrah is for Allah and His Messenger.
HAD-2153.narrator: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2153.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2153.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl mentions, regarding the Hiǧrah passage, that in the Ḥadīṯ the intention determines the ruling of the action. The particular mention of the woman shows that an outwardly religious movement loses its rank when it in fact takes place for worldly aims.

HAD-2154.text: Islam was built upon five pillars.
HAD-2154.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2154.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2154.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that al-Buḫārī brings this Ḥadīṯ in the Kitāb al-Īmān because the pillars mentioned belong to the foundations upon which the visible Islam is built. The image of the structure shows: these foundation pillars carry the building, while further obligations and Sunan complete it.

HAD-2155.text: Among the pillars is the testimony that there is no god worthy of worship except Allah and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah.
HAD-2155.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2155.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2155.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl makes clear that the testimony is the first and load-bearing pillar. It stands at the beginning because the other visible acts of worship are validly built only upon Tawḥīd and the acknowledgment of the messengership of Muḥammad ﷺ.

HAD-2156.text: Among the pillars are the prayer, the Zakāh, the Ḥaǧǧ, and the fast in Ramaḍān.
HAD-2156.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2156.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2156.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the Ḥadīṯ in the context of the foundations of Īmān: prayer, Zakāh, Ḥaǧǧ, and fasting are not merely individual acts, but load-bearing outward pillars of Islam. Whoever heeds these pillars holds fast to the visible structure of the religion.

HAD-2157.text: The lawful is clear and the forbidden is clear.
HAD-2157.narrator: an-Nuʿmān ibn Bašīr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2157.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2157.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains this Ḥadīṯ as a division of matters into clear Ḥalāl, clear Ḥarām, and an intermediate area of Šubuhāt. The clear lawful and the clear forbidden remain recognizable by the proof; the problem lies in the intermediate cases, in which the servant needs knowledge and Warāʿ.

HAD-2158.text: Between them there are doubtful matters that many people do not know.
HAD-2158.narrator: an-Nuʿmān ibn Bašīr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2158.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2158.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Šubuhāt are intermediate cases between clear Ḥalāl and clear Ḥarām. Many people do not know their ruling; it does not follow from this, however, that no one knows them, for those firmly grounded in knowledge can, by proofs, assign some of these cases.

HAD-2159.text: Whoever avoids the doubtful matters thereby protects his religion and his honor.
HAD-2159.narrator: an-Nuʿmān ibn Bašīr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2159.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2159.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that avoiding the Šubuhāt is an act of protection: whoever stops at unclear intermediate cases preserves his religion from diminishment and his honor from suspicion. This is Warāʿ, not baseless whispering; for what is meant are cases in which there is a genuine doubt about the proof or about classification.

HAD-2160.text: In the body there is a piece of flesh: if it is sound, the whole body is sound; if it is corrupted, the whole body is corrupted. It is the heart.
HAD-2160.narrator: an-Nuʿmān ibn Bašīr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2160.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2160.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl adduces the heart passage in the same chapter as an indication of the central place of the heart: if it is sound, the other limbs become ordered; if it is corrupted, the corruption appears in the body. Therefore, avoiding Šubuhāt and Ḥarām depends not only on outward knowledge, but also on the inner vigilance of the heart.

HAD-2161.narrator: Tamīm ad-Dārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2161.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2161.sharh: al-Māzirī explains, regarding the statement «The religion is Naṣīḥah», that Naṣīḥah is linguistically derived either from the purifying of honey—thus sincerity and purification—or from sewing, because the advisor closes by his counsel the rift of his brother. The Ḥadīṯ thereby indicates that religion rests upon sincere purification and healing solicitude.

HAD-2162.text: Naṣīḥah applies to Allah, His Book, His Messenger, the leaders of the Muslims, and their general body.
HAD-2162.narrator: Tamīm ad-Dārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2162.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2162.sharh: al-Māzirī’s explanation makes clear that Naṣīḥah is not merely a single piece of counsel, but sincerity and healing solicitude: toward Allah through pure obedience, toward His Book and His Messenger through acceptance and following, and toward the Muslims through seeking their religious and worldly benefit.

HAD-2163.text: What I have forbidden you, avoid.
HAD-2163.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2163.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2163.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains this Ḥadīṯ in the context of holding fast to the Sunnah: prohibitions are fulfilled by complete avoidance. Whoever leaves what is forbidden remains within the safe boundary of the revelation and does not make the religion harder by his own questioning or by evasion.

HAD-2164.text: What I have commanded you, do of it what you are able.
HAD-2164.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2164.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2164.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl sets forth that commands are carried out within the limits of ability. This shows the mercy of the Šarīʿah: what is forbidden is avoided, while what is commanded is fulfilled according to capacity; incapacity lifts only what truly lies out of reach.

HAD-2165.text: Those before you perished because of their much questioning and their opposition to their prophets.
HAD-2165.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2165.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2165.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the warning against excessive questioning and opposition as a protection of the Ummah from hardship and fragmentation. What is blamed is not the learning of necessary religion, but questioning out of obstinacy, exaggeration, or a search for unnecessary hardship.

HAD-2286.text: If he asks Me, I will certainly give him.
HAD-2286.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2286.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported from his Lord عز وجل:
HAD-2286.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl connects the promise with the state of the servant who preserves the obligations and draws near to Allah through Nawāfil. His Duʿāʾ thereby stands under a special promise of being answered.

HAD-2287.text: If he seeks protection with Me, I will certainly grant him protection.
HAD-2287.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2287.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported from his Lord عز وجل:
HAD-2287.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the promise of protection as part of Allah’s special care for the obedient servant who is near to Him. Whoever turns sincerely to Allah and seeks refuge with Him stands under this special promise of protection.

HAD-2288.text: Allah has excused for my Ummah what it does by mistake.
HAD-2288.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2288.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2288.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that an unintended error is not placed on the same level as deliberate action. The lifting concerns in particular the sinfulness; whether worldly legal consequences remain alongside it depends on the respective legal question and on further evidence.

HAD-2289.text: Allah has excused for my Ummah what it does out of forgetfulness.
HAD-2289.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2289.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2289.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that forgetfulness is not treated like conscious and intentional action. The sin is lifted; possible compensatory, repetitive, or other legal consequences must, however, each be determined from the specific evidence of the act in question.

HAD-2290.text: Allah has excused for my Ummah that to which it is compelled.
HAD-2290.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2290.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2290.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that a genuine state of compulsion can lessen or remove responsibility for compelled action. Whether Ikrāh is actually present and which legal consequences fall away depends on the kind and strength of the compulsion and on the concrete act; the Ḥadīṯ is therefore not a blanket license.

HAD-2291.text: Be in this world like a stranger or like a traveler who moves on.
HAD-2291.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2291.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2291.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the prophetic instruction as a call not to bind oneself permanently to the world. The stranger, and especially the one passing through, does not direct his main aim toward the place of stay, but toward the destination of his journey; likewise the believer should make the Āḫirah his true goal.

HAD-2292.text: When you reach the evening, do not expect the morning; and when you reach the morning, do not expect the evening.
HAD-2292.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما said:
HAD-2292.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما said:
HAD-2292.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl understands the statement as a practical application of the prophetic parable: the servant should not treat his lifetime as though the next portion were guaranteed to him. Thereby he is spurred to immediate action and does not postpone obedience to a supposedly secure future.

HAD-2293.text: Take from your health for your illness and from your life for your death.
HAD-2293.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما said:
HAD-2293.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما said:
HAD-2293.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl understands the statement as an exhortation to use existing strength and lifetime for obedience before illness or death restricts the possibility of doing so. Health and life are thus treated as a temporally limited opportunity for action.

HAD-2294.text: O son of Adam, so long as you call upon Me and hope in Me, I forgive you what has occurred from you, and it does not concern Me.
HAD-2294.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2294.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported from his Lord تبارك وتعالى:
HAD-2294.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that Duʿāʾ and hope in Allah are among the great causes of forgiveness. The magnitude or multitude of sins does not exceed Allah’s forgiveness so long as the servant turns to Him sincerely and does not despair of forgiveness.

HAD-2295.text: O son of Adam, if your sins reach the clouds of the sky and you then ask Me for forgiveness, I forgive you.
HAD-2295.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2295.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported from his Lord تبارك وتعالى:
HAD-2295.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that even extraordinarily great sins do not exceed the vastness of Allah’s forgiveness. The statement joins acknowledgment of one’s own sin with Istighfār and hope, and thereby warns at the same time against despairing of Allah’s mercy.

HAD-2296.text: O son of Adam, if you come to Me with sins that nearly fill the earth, yet you associate nothing with Me, I come to you with forgiveness just as great.
HAD-2296.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2296.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported from his Lord تبارك وتعالى:
HAD-2296.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that the promise is bound to remaining free of Širk. Even immense sins remain under Allah’s forgiveness when the servant meets Him with Tawḥīd; this is at the same time one of the strongest statements about the greatness of Tawḥīd and the vastness of forgiveness.

HAD-2297.text: A servant utters a word without considering its gravity, and thereby plunges into the Fire deeper than the East is distant.
HAD-2297.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2297.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2297.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the tongue is among the most dangerous limbs, because an unconsidered word can have great consequences. The Ḥadīṯ therefore requires examination and restraint before speaking, especially when the servant does not know the religious import of his words.

HAD-2298.text: A servant speaks a word that pleases Allah, without attaching great importance to it, and Allah thereby raises him by degrees of rank.
HAD-2298.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2298.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2298.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl shows that a sincere good word can have a reward far greater than the speaker himself expects. The servant should therefore not belittle the opportunity for speech that is true, beneficial, and pleasing to Allah.

HAD-2299.text: A servant speaks a word that angers Allah, without attaching great importance to it, and thereby falls into Ǧahannam.
HAD-2299.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2299.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2299.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the other side of the same rule: a word can be regarded as slight by the speaker and yet, because of its content, be a grave sin. Therefore guarding the tongue is part of guarding the religion.

HAD-2300.text: By the One in Whose hand is my soul: if you did not sin, Allah would take you away and bring people who sin.
HAD-2300.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2300.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2300.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the statement not as an invitation to sin. It rather shows human fallibility and the importance of divine forgiveness: Allah loves Tawbah and Istighfār and did not create human beings like sinless angels.

HAD-2301.text: They would sin, ask Allah for forgiveness, and He would forgive them.
HAD-2301.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2301.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2301.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ highlights the connection between sin, Istighfār, and forgiveness. The promise applies to the one who returns to Allah after the lapse; it is not a license to persist in sin.

HAD-2302.text: Help your brother, whether he is the oppressor or the oppressed.
HAD-2302.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2302.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2302.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that Nuṣrah means help and support. In the case of the oppressed, the help consists in defending his right; in the case of the oppressor, help is realized precisely by restraining him from wrong and preserving him from its consequences.

HAD-2303.text: Help for the oppressor consists in restraining him from wrong.
HAD-2303.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2303.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2303.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that stopping the oppressor is itself a form of support for him, because it protects him from further sin and from the consequences of his wrong. The Ḥadīṯ thereby turns the pre-Islamic slogan of blind tribal loyalty into a principle of just help.

HAD-2304.text: Do you think that this woman would throw her child into the fire?
HAD-2304.narrator: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2304.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2304.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl treats the scene as a vivid parable: the natural mercy of a mother toward her child makes clear how remote it is that she would knowingly throw it into the fire. The Prophet ﷺ uses this visible example in order then to point to Allah’s still greater mercy.

HAD-2305.text: Allah is more merciful to His servants than this woman is to her child.
HAD-2305.narrator: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2305.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2305.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ clarifies the vastness of divine mercy through an example immediately understandable to people. The mother’s mercy is created and limited; Allah’s mercy toward His servants is more comprehensive.

HAD-2306.text: Allah made mercy into one hundred parts.
HAD-2306.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2306.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2306.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the one hundred parts mentioned in the Ḥadīṯ concern the created mercy that belongs to creatures. The text makes clear the immense vastness of the mercy Allah has appointed for His servants.

HAD-2307.text: Allah sent down one part of mercy upon the earth; through it creatures are merciful to one another.
HAD-2307.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2307.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2307.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that all forms of compassion, affection, and protection among creatures come from this single part that was sent down. Even an animal’s care for its young belongs to this one mercy distributed in the world.

HAD-2308.text: Allah withheld ninety-nine parts of mercy, with which He treats His servants mercifully on the Day of Resurrection.
HAD-2308.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2308.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2308.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ understands the statement as a great hope for the Day of Resurrection: what creatures know of mercy in this world is only a small share compared with what Allah has withheld for the Hereafter.

HAD-2309.text: A servant may, in the eyes of people, perform the deeds of the people of Paradise while he belongs to the people of the Fire.
HAD-2309.narrator: Sahl ibn Saʿd as-Sāʿidī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2309.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2309.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the outward appearance of a deed alone is not enough to judge a person’s final state. What is decisive is that upon which a person ends and what Allah knows of his inward condition.

HAD-2310.text: A servant may, in the eyes of people, perform the deeds of the people of the Fire while he belongs to the people of Paradise.
HAD-2310.narrator: Sahl ibn Saʿd as-Sāʿidī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2310.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2310.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the opposite half as a warning against hasty judgments based solely on visible snapshots. A person may change, make Tawbah, or end upon something that does not correspond to his earlier outward state.

HAD-2311.text: Deeds are judged according to their endings.
HAD-2311.narrator: Sahl ibn Saʿd as-Sāʿidī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2311.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2311.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the concluding formula as a principle: the final worth of a life’s course depends essentially on how the servant ends. The Ḥadīṯ therefore joins hope with fear and warns against self-assurance on account of earlier good deeds.

HAD-2312.text: Is one of you unable to acquire a thousand good deeds every day? He says one hundred Tasbīḥāt; thereby a thousand good deeds are recorded for him, or a thousand faults are erased from him.
HAD-2312.narrator: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2312.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2312.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the immense multiplication of Ḏikr: one hundred Tasbīḥāt produce a thousand good deeds through a recompense of at least tenfold. The variants of transmission mention either the recording of the good deeds or the erasing of the corresponding faults; the text shows the great reward of an easy, constant form of Ḏikr.

HAD-2313.text: Allah loves gentleness in all matters.
HAD-2313.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2313.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains gentleness as a fundamental disposition of adab that avoids harshness so long as no legal ground requires harshness. The context shows that even provocative words should be answered with composure and without unnecessary excess.

HAD-2314.text: Allah has angels who roam about, seeking gatherings of Ḏikr.
HAD-2314.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2314.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2314.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains these special angels as those who, in addition to the angels appointed for other tasks, seek out the gatherings of remembrance. The Ḥadīṯ thereby shows the special standing of communal Ḏikr.

HAD-2315.text: When the angels find a gathering in which Allah is remembered, they sit with them and surround one another with their wings up to the lowest heaven.
HAD-2315.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2315.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2315.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ understands the surrounding with the wings as a special honoring and accompanying of this gathering. The angels remain with the people of Ḏikr and fill the space between them and the heaven.

HAD-2316.text: The angels report: We came from Your servants on the earth; they glorify You, they utter the Takbīr, the Tahlīl and the Taḥmīd, and they ask You.
HAD-2316.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2316.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2316.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ shows that the gathering is marked by various forms of Ḏikr: Tasbīḥ, Takbīr, Tahlīl, Taḥmīd and Duʿāʾ. The Ḥadīṯ thereby joins praise and petition in one shared sitting.

HAD-2317.text: They ask Allah for Paradise. Although they have not seen it, they would long for it even more strongly if they had seen it.
HAD-2317.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2317.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2317.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains Allah’s question, although He knows all things, as a highlighting and honoring of the servants before the angels. That they seek Paradise without having seen it shows the strength of their Īmān in the unseen.

HAD-2318.text: They seek refuge with Allah from the Fire. Although they have not seen it, they would flee from it even more strongly if they had seen it.
HAD-2318.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2318.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2318.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the juxtaposition of hope and fear: the servants long for Paradise and at the same time seek protection from the Fire. Both rest on Īmān in the unseen and are strengthened by certainty.

HAD-2319.text: Allah says about this gathering: I have forgiven them, given them what they asked for, and protected them from that from which they sought refuge.
HAD-2319.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2319.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2319.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ emphasizes the special favor of these gatherings: forgiveness, being answered, and protection are named together. The statement is one of the strongest prophetic encouragements to sincere Ḏikr in a righteous company.

HAD-2320.text: Among them there may be someone who only happened to pass by and sat down with them. Allah says: I have forgiven him too; they are people whose sitting companion does not become unhappy.
HAD-2320.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2320.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2320.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the concluding statement as a pointer to the Barakah of good company: even the one who did not originally come for the Ḏikr receives a share in the special favor of this sitting. This underscores the effect of righteous company and of its surroundings.

HAD-2321.text: You will not enter Paradise until you believe.
HAD-2321.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2321.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2321.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the statement as an indication that entry into Paradise is bound to Īmān. The Ḥadīṯ then leads on to the practical means by which the community strengthens this Īmān and makes its fruits visible.

HAD-2322.text: You will not believe completely until you love one another.
HAD-2322.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2322.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2322.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ links mutual love with the completeness and the visible effect of Īmān. What is meant is a love for Allah’s sake that strengthens brotherhood, mutual rights, and the avoidance of enmity.

HAD-2323.text: Shall I not point you to something by which you love one another? Spread the Salām among you.
HAD-2323.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2323.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2323.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the spreading of the Salām as a practical means for mutual love to arise. The greeting makes brotherhood visible, removes estrangement, and helps to join hearts together.

HAD-2324.text: Among the best qualities of Islam is that you give food.
HAD-2324.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2324.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2324.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains feeding others as an especially comprehensive form of good conduct, because it relieves need and creates affection among people. The Ḥadīṯ thereby shows a concrete social fruit of Islam.

HAD-2325.text: Greet with the Salām those whom you know and those whom you do not know.
HAD-2325.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2325.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2325.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Salām is not limited to acquaintances. Giving it also to the Muslim one does not know prevents the greeting from becoming a mere habit among friends, and instead strengthens general Islamic brotherhood.

HAD-1986.text: There is no Islam without community, no community without leadership, and no leadership without obedience.
HAD-1986.narrator: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1986.speaker: He said:

HAD-1987.text: Obey me so long as I obey Allah and His Messenger; if I disobey Allah and His Messenger, then there is no obedience toward me.
HAD-1987.narrator: Abū Bakr aṣ-Ṣiddīq رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1987.speaker: He said:

HAD-1988.text: No one may hold a false opinion and say: I am free in that.
HAD-1988.narrator: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1988.speaker: He said:

HAD-1989.text: The measure of your knowledge is not the abundance of transmission, but the measure of knowledge is the fear of Allah.
HAD-1989.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1989.speaker: He said:

HAD-1990.text: The heart is king, and the limbs are its soldiers.
HAD-1990.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-1990.speaker: He said:

HAD-1991.text: The believer joins good action with fear, and the hypocrite joins bad action with security.
HAD-1991.speaker: He said:

HAD-1992.text: Turning toward the Dunyā and turning away from the Hereafter comes from the weakness of certainty.
HAD-1992.speaker: He said:

HAD-1993.text: This knowledge is Dīn; so look from whom you take your Dīn.
HAD-1993.narrator: Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn رحمه الله said:
HAD-1993.speaker: He said:

HAD-1994.text: Formerly one did not ask about the Isnād; but when the Fitnah came, one said: Name your men to us.
HAD-1994.speaker: He said:

HAD-1995.text: From everyone one can take and reject, except from the possessor of this grave.
HAD-1995.narrator: Mālik ibn Anas رحمه الله said:
HAD-1995.speaker: He said:

HAD-1996.text: Knowledge is not taken from four: from a fool, a liar, a follower of desires, and someone who does not know what he transmits.
HAD-1996.narrator: Mālik ibn Anas رحمه الله said:
HAD-1996.speaker: He said:

HAD-1997.text: Innovation is dearer to Iblīs than sin, for from sin one repents, but from innovation one rarely repents.
HAD-1997.speaker: He said:

HAD-1998.text: Hold to the transmissions of the Salaf, even if the people reject you.
HAD-1998.speaker: He said:

HAD-1999.text: Be patient upon the Sunnah, halt where the people halted, and say what they said.
HAD-1999.speaker: He said:

HAD-2000.text: When I am told of the death of a man of the Sunnah, it is as if I had lost one of my limbs.
HAD-2000.speaker: He said:

HAD-2001.text: The more an innovator exerts himself, the further he moves away from Allah.
HAD-2001.speaker: He said:

HAD-2002.text: The Isnād belongs to the Dīn; without the Isnād everyone would say what he wants.
HAD-2002.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mubārak رحمه الله said:
HAD-2002.speaker: He said:

HAD-2003.text: We have greater need of a little Adab than of much knowledge.
HAD-2003.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mubārak رحمه الله said:
HAD-2003.speaker: He said:

HAD-2004.text: Whoever seeks Ḥadīṯ as it came is a man of the Sunnah.
HAD-2004.narrator: Wakīʿ ibn al-Ǧarrāḥ رحمه الله said:
HAD-2004.speaker: He said:

HAD-2005.text: The foundations of the Sunnah with us are: holding fast to that upon which the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were, and following them.
HAD-2005.narrator: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal رحمه الله said:
HAD-2005.speaker: He said:

HAD-2186.text: Preserve Allah, then He will preserve you.
HAD-2186.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2186.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2186.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains “Preserve Allah” as preserving His limits, rights, commands and prohibitions. Whoever preserves this, Allah preserves him; this preservation especially comprises the religion and the Īmān of the servant and, according to Allah’s wisdom, his affairs in this world.

HAD-2187.text: Preserve Allah, then you will find Him opposite you.
HAD-2187.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2187.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2187.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that the one who preserves Allah’s limits finds Allah before him: with His special care, preservation, support and right guidance. The meaning is not spatial nearness, but the special divine companionship of the obedient servant.

HAD-2188.text: If you ask, then ask Allah; and if you seek help, then seek help from Allah.
HAD-2188.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2188.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2188.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains the instruction as the realization of Tawḥīd, trust and neediness toward Allah: the heart directs its request and its true trust to Allah. Permissible help from people in matters they are capable of does not contradict this; the heart remains dependent on Allah in that.

HAD-2189.text: If the whole community gathered to benefit you with something, it could benefit you only with something that Allah has determined for you.
HAD-2189.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2189.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2189.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that the benefit and harm of creation stand entirely under Allah’s prior knowledge and His determination. No creature can bring the servant a benefit that Allah has not determined for him; this strengthens Tawakkul and dissolves the heart’s dependence on people.

HAD-2190.text: If they gathered to harm you with something, they could harm you only with something that Allah has determined for you. The reed pens are raised and the leaves are dried.
HAD-2190.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2190.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2190.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains: Harm too reaches the servant only within what Allah has determined. “The reed pens are raised and the leaves are dried” indicates that the determination has already been written; the creatures do not step outside Allah’s Qadar.

HAD-2191.text: Among what has reached the people from the words of the earlier prophecy is: If you feel no shame, then do what you want.
HAD-2191.narrator: Abū Masʿūd ʿUqbah ibn ʿAmr al-Anṣārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2191.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2191.sharh: al-Ḫaṭṭābī explains that the sense of shame has been transmitted since the earlier prophets as praiseworthy and obligatory. “Then do what you want,” according to his explanation, is not a free pass, but in meaning a statement: whoever has no Ḥayāʾ is no longer held back by it from what is ugly and does what his soul drives him to.

HAD-2192.text: Say: I believe in Allah — and then remain steadfast.
HAD-2192.narrator: Sufyān ibn ʿAbdillāh aṯ-Ṯaqafī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2192.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2192.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains this statement as one of the comprehensive prophetic instructions: first Allah is acknowledged as the only Lord and the One worthy of worship, and He is believed in; then follows steadfastness, without departing from Tawḥīd, and holding fast to obedience until death.

HAD-2193.text: If I perform the prescribed prayers, fast Ramaḍān, hold the permissible as permissible, hold the forbidden as forbidden, and do nothing beyond that — will I enter Paradise? He said: Yes.
HAD-2193.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2193.speaker: A man asked the Prophet ﷺ; he replied:
HAD-2193.sharh: al-Qurṭubī explains that “holding the permissible as permissible” here comprises using or acquiring the permissible, and “holding the forbidden as forbidden” comprises refraining from the forbidden. That the questioner did not want to do anything beyond that can refer to additional voluntary deeds; the answer confirms entry into Paradise upon fulfilling the obligatory foundations and avoiding the forbidden.

HAD-2194.narrator: Abū Mālik al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2194.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2194.sharh: al-Māzirī names several lines of explanation for “purity is half of Īmān.” Among them is that purification effaces sins, while Īmān effaces the preceding sins, as well as the special standing of Ṭahārah as a foundational devotional purification. What is decisive is the extraordinary importance of purity within Īmān and the acts of worship.

HAD-2195.text: Al-ḥamdu li-llāh fills the scale pan.
HAD-2195.narrator: Abū Mālik al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2195.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2195.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that “Al-ḥamdu li-llāh” fills the scale pan with the reward granted for it. He connects the Ḥamd with the complete acknowledgment of Allah’s gifts and one’s own neediness toward Him; precisely this meaning explains the greatness of its weight.

HAD-2196.text: Subḥān Allāh and al-ḥamdu li-llāh fill — or one of the two fills — what is between the heavens and the earth.
HAD-2196.narrator: Abū Mālik al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2196.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2196.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the immense reward of Tasbīḥ and Ḥamd: the wording describes the greatness of what these words bring forth in reward and weight. Ḏikr is thus not a slight act of the tongue, but possesses with Allah an extraordinary weight.

HAD-2197.narrator: Abū Mālik al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2197.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2197.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the light metaphor as an indication of the effect of prayer: it leads and illuminates the path of the servant. Prayer is thus a cause of right guidance and clarity and also possesses in the Hereafter an effect that brings light.

HAD-2198.narrator: Abū Mālik al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2198.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2198.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains Ṣadaqah as proof of the genuineness of Īmān: whoever gives out his beloved wealth in obedience to Allah thereby shows the truthfulness of his inner faith and distinguishes himself from the attitude of hypocrisy and stinginess.

HAD-2199.narrator: Abū Mālik al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2199.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2199.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ distinguishes between Nūr and Ḍiyāʾ: Ḍiyāʾ denotes a stronger shining connected with exertion. This fits patience, because Ṣabr requires holding fast to obedience and bearing toil.

HAD-2200.text: The Qurʾān is a proof for you or against you.
HAD-2200.narrator: Abū Mālik al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2200.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2200.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains: The Qurʾān is a proof for the one who follows it and acts according to it; otherwise it becomes a proof against him. Revelation is therefore not only information, but obligates the one whom it reaches.

HAD-2201.text: Every person sets out in the morning and sells his soul: either he frees it or he ruins it.
HAD-2201.narrator: Abū Mālik al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2201.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2201.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the daily striving of the person as a trade with his own soul: whoever sells it to Allah through obedience frees it; whoever leaves it to disobedience brings it to ruin. Every day is thus a new path either to the salvation or to the harm of one’s own soul.

HAD-2202.text: O My servants, I have forbidden injustice to Myself and I have made it forbidden among you; so do not wrong one another.
HAD-2202.narrator: Abū Ḏarr al-Ġifārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2202.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported from his Lord عز وجل:
HAD-2202.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains that Allah is exalted above injustice. With “I have forbidden injustice to Myself” it is expressed that He has excluded it from Himself; among the servants injustice is expressly forbidden. No one may transgress the limits toward another.

HAD-2203.text: O My servants, all of you are going astray except the one whom I guide aright; so ask Me for right guidance, then I will guide you aright.
HAD-2203.narrator: Abū Ḏarr al-Ġifārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2203.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported from his Lord عز وجل:
HAD-2203.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains that right guidance comes from Allah. Without Allah’s guidance the human being remains exposed to error; therefore he is instructed to ask Allah for right guidance and to acknowledge his neediness for it.

HAD-2204.text: O My servants, all of you are hungry except the one whom I feed; so ask Me for food, then I will feed you.
HAD-2204.narrator: Abū Ḏarr al-Ġifārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2204.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported from his Lord عز وجل:
HAD-2204.sharh: Ibn Raǧab sums up right guidance, food, clothing and forgiveness as an expression of the complete neediness of creatures. The servant does not possess these things independently from himself; he takes the permissible means, yet knows that provision ultimately comes from Allah and asks Him for it.

HAD-2205.text: O My servants, all of you are unclothed except the one whom I clothe; so ask Me for clothing, then I will clothe you.
HAD-2205.narrator: Abū Ḏarr al-Ġifārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2205.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported from his Lord عز وجل:
HAD-2205.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains the provision of clothing likewise as part of the comprehensive poverty of the servant toward Allah. The human being uses the means available to him, yet the possibility of attaining provision, and the provision itself, rest upon Allah’s granting.

HAD-2106.text: Read the Qurʾān, for it comes on the Day of Resurrection as an intercessor for its companions.
HAD-2106.narrator: Abū Umāmah al-Bāhilī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2106.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2106.sharh: an-Nawawī explains that the Qurʾān intercedes for those who recite it, preserve it, and act according to it. What is meant is not mere reading without regard for its rights, but accompanying the Qurʾān with Īmān and following.

HAD-2107.text: There is no envy except in two cases: in a man to whom Allah gave the Qurʾān and who recites it by day and by night.
HAD-2107.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2107.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2107.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains that what is meant here is not blameworthy envy, but the permissible wishing for an equal blessing. The merit lies with the one who receives the Qurʾān and uses it constantly in recitation and action.

HAD-2108.text: Allah raises peoples by this Book and abases others by it.
HAD-2108.narrator: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2108.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2108.sharh: an-Nawawī explains that elevation through the Qurʾān concerns the one who believes it, learns it, teaches it, and follows it. Abasement befalls the one who neglects it or opposes its guidance.

HAD-2109.text: The likeness of the believer who reads the Qurʾān is like a citrus fruit: its fragrance is good and its taste is good.
HAD-2109.narrator: Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2109.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2109.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains that the good taste points to the benefit of Īmān, and the good fragrance points to the visible benefit of the recitation. The Qurʾān makes the believer beneficial to himself and to others.

HAD-2110.text: Hold fast to the Qurʾān, for it escapes faster than camels from their fetters.
HAD-2110.narrator: Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2110.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2110.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains that the Ḥadīṯ directs one to constant repetition and care of the Qurʾān. Whoever neglects it forgets it quickly; whoever repeats it regularly preserves this gift.

HAD-2111.text: The strong one is not the one who wins in wrestling; the strong one is the one who controls himself in anger.
HAD-2111.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2111.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2111.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains that true strength is not mere bodily power, but mastery over the soul when anger seeks to drive it into transgression. The Ḥadīṯ transfers strength to self-control and Taqwā.

HAD-2112.text: A person is upon the Dīn of his close friend; so each one should look at whom he takes as a close friend.
HAD-2112.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2112.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2112.sharh: The explanations of the Ḥadīṯ mention that close friendship influences a person in belief, conduct, and habits. Therefore it is commanded to choose companions carefully and to seek nearness to the people of good.

HAD-2113.text: Whoever is not merciful to people, Allah is not merciful to him.
HAD-2113.narrator: Ǧarīr ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2113.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2113.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains that mercy toward created beings is a cause of attaining Allah’s mercy. Whoever chooses harshness and cruelty deprives himself of a great gate of grace.

HAD-2114.text: Gentleness is in nothing except that it beautifies it.
HAD-2114.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2114.sharh: an-Nawawī explains that Rifq is a praiseworthy trait, because gentleness orders things, opens hearts, and leads to a good outcome. Harshness often spoils what gentleness would beautify.

HAD-2115.text: Allah is gentle and loves gentleness in all matters.
HAD-2115.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2115.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar and an-Nawawī explain that Allah loves gentleness because it leads to wisdom, justice, and a good effect. What is meant is not weakness, but calm, just, and measured treatment.

HAD-2116.text: A good word is a Ṣadaqah.
HAD-2116.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2116.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2116.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains that Ṣadaqah is not limited to money. A good word can gladden hearts, guide to the good, lessen dispute, and therefore be counted as a benefaction.

HAD-2117.text: Do not belittle anything of the good, even if you meet your brother with a friendly face.
HAD-2117.narrator: Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2117.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2117.sharh: an-Nawawī explains that the Ḥadīṯ trains one not to regard small good deeds as insignificant. A friendly face belongs to good conduct, opens hearts, and can carry weight with Allah.

HAD-2118.text: The believer is not stung twice from the same hole.
HAD-2118.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2118.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2118.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains that the believer learns from experience and does not let himself be led repeatedly into the same harm, the same deception, or the same sin. The Ḥadīṯ joins caution with insight.

HAD-2119.text: None of you believes completely until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
HAD-2119.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2119.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2119.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that the completeness of the obligatory Īmān requires loving for the Muslim brother the good in the Dīn and in this world, and wishing for him what one loves for oneself.

HAD-2120.text: The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim: he does not oppress him and does not abandon him.
HAD-2120.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2120.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2120.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains that brotherhood in Islam produces concrete rights: refraining from wrong, help, protection, and not handing the Muslim over to harm, insofar as one is able to do so.

HAD-2121.text: Help your brother, whether he does wrong or wrong is done to him.
HAD-2121.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2121.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2121.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains that help for the oppressed takes place through support, while help for the oppressor consists in restraining him from the wrong. Thus help does not become partisanship for falsehood.

HAD-2122.text: Whoever deceives us does not belong to us.
HAD-2122.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2122.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2122.sharh: an-Nawawī explains that deception in sale, counsel, dealings, and all rights is forbidden. The wording is a strong threat and shows that fraud contradicts the way of the Muslims.

HAD-2123.text: The signs of the hypocrite are three: when he speaks, he lies.
HAD-2123.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2123.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2123.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains that these traits are signs of practical hypocrisy. They show an inward corruption in conduct, even though the person is not, by that alone, judged to be outside Islam.

HAD-2124.text: When he promises something, he breaks his promise.
HAD-2124.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2124.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2124.sharh: Ibn Ḥaǧar explains that breaking promises belongs to the traits of the hypocrites, because it damages the truthfulness of the heart and faithfulness in dealings. The believer should keep his word.

HAD-2125.text: When something is entrusted to him, he commits betrayal.
HAD-2125.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2125.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2125.sharh: an-Nawawī explains that betrayal in matters entrusted belongs to the grave signs of bad religion and bad character traits. The Amānah comprises property, words, rights, and duties.

HAD-2206.text: O My servants, you sin by night and by day, and I forgive all the sins; so ask Me for forgiveness, then I forgive you.
HAD-2206.narrator: Abū Ḏarr al-Ġifārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2206.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported from his Lord عز وجل:
HAD-2206.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that the servant, because of his recurring faults, is constantly dependent on Istighfār and Tawbah. The call to ask Allah for forgiveness joins the recognition of one's own sin with hope in Allah's comprehensive forgiveness.

HAD-2207.text: O My servants, you will never reach the point of harming Me such that you harm Me, and you will never reach the point of benefiting Me such that you benefit Me.
HAD-2207.narrator: Abū Ḏarr al-Ġifārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2207.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported from his Lord عز وجل:
HAD-2207.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains Allah's complete independence from created beings: obedience does not benefit Allah, and sin does not harm Him. The benefit and harm of deeds return to the servants themselves; Allah is the perfectly Rich, while created beings are in need.

HAD-2208.text: O My servants, if the first and the last of you, your humans and your Ǧinn, were upon the most Allah-fearing heart of a single man among you, that would add nothing to My dominion.
HAD-2208.narrator: Abū Ḏarr al-Ġifārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2208.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported from his Lord عز وجل:
HAD-2208.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that Allah's dominion is perfect and is not increased by the obedience of all created beings. The fruit of Taqwā returns entirely to the servants; Allah gains nothing through their obedience.

HAD-2209.text: O My servants, if the first and the last of you, your humans and your Ǧinn, were upon the most wicked heart of a single man among you, that would take nothing away from My dominion.
HAD-2209.narrator: Abū Ḏarr al-Ġifārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2209.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported from his Lord عز وجل:
HAD-2209.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains the opposite half of the same principle: the sins of all created beings do not diminish Allah's dominion. The harm of sin strikes the sinner himself, not the Lord of the worlds.

HAD-2210.text: O My servants, if the first and the last of you, your humans and your Ǧinn, stood in one place, asked Me, and I gave each one his request, that would diminish what is with Me only as much as a needle that is dipped into the sea.
HAD-2210.narrator: Abū Ḏarr al-Ġifārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2210.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported from his Lord عز وجل:
HAD-2210.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the image as the utmost illustration that Allah's gifts and stores do not decrease through giving. Just as practically nothing of the sea remains clinging to a smooth needle when it is dipped into the sea, the fulfillment of all requests does not diminish what is with Allah.

HAD-2211.text: O My servants, it is only your deeds that I record for you and then repay to you in full.
HAD-2211.narrator: Abū Ḏarr al-Ġifārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2211.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported from his Lord عز وجل:
HAD-2211.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that Allah records the deeds of His servants completely and causes the recompense for them to reach them. Nothing is lost or forgotten; the statement joins complete knowledge, justice, and the servant's responsibility for his actions.

HAD-2212.text: Whoever finds good, let him praise Allah.
HAD-2212.narrator: Abū Ḏarr al-Ġifārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2212.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported from his Lord عز وجل:
HAD-2212.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains: whoever finds good at the end recognizes that success, right guidance, and the possibility of good deeds come from Allah, and praises Him for that. One's own action does not become self-admiration, but an occasion for Ḥamd.

HAD-2213.text: Whoever finds something else, let him blame no one but himself.
HAD-2213.narrator: Abū Ḏarr al-Ġifārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2213.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported from his Lord عز وجل:
HAD-2213.sharh: Ibn Raǧab explains that, in the case of a bad outcome, the servant recognizes the responsibility for his own sins and omissions. Allah has shown him the way and is not unjust toward him; therefore the blame falls back upon his own misconduct.

HAD-2214.text: Some Companions said: O Messenger of Allah, the wealthy have taken the rewards; they pray as we pray, they fast as we fast, and they give Ṣadaqah from their surplus wealth.
HAD-2214.narrator: Abū Ḏarr al-Ġifārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2214.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2214.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains »Ahl ad-duṯūr« as people with much wealth. The poor Ṣaḥābah did not envy them for worldly things, but wanted to vie with them in good deeds and reward, because these were able, in addition, to give from their wealth.

HAD-2215.text: Has Allah not given you things with which you can give Ṣadaqah?
HAD-2215.narrator: Abū Ḏarr al-Ġifārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2215.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2215.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that Ṣadaqah is not limited to wealth. Allah has also opened, for those without surplus money, ways to attain the reward of a Ṣadaqah through various forms of obedience and of good.

HAD-2216.text: In every Tasbīḥ there is a Ṣadaqah, in every Takbīr a Ṣadaqah, in every Taḥmīd a Ṣadaqah, and in every Tahlīl a Ṣadaqah.
HAD-2216.narrator: Abū Ḏarr al-Ġifārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2216.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2216.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that these forms of Ḏikr are called Ṣadaqah because they correspond in reward to a Ṣadaqah, or because they indicate the truthfulness of Īmān. Good deeds can thus become Ṣadaqah even without the expenditure of wealth.

HAD-2217.text: Enjoining the good is a Ṣadaqah, and forbidding the reprehensible is a Ṣadaqah.
HAD-2217.narrator: Abū Ḏarr al-Ġifārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2217.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2217.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ also places enjoining the good and forbidding the reprehensible among the acts of Ṣadaqah: the good that reaches another person through this act possesses a rewardable benefit like a gift.

HAD-2218.text: In the marital intercourse of one of you there lies a Ṣadaqah.
HAD-2218.narrator: Abū Ḏarr al-Ġifārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2218.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2218.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains »buḍʿ« here as marital sexual intercourse. The Ḥadīṯ shows that even a permitted natural act can be rewarded through the right orientation and the permitted frame.

HAD-2219.text: If he were to satisfy his desire in what is forbidden, would there not then be a sin upon him?
