HAD-2219.narrator: Abū Ḏarr al-Ġifārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2219.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2219.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains that the Prophet ﷺ made the connection clear to the Ṣaḥābah by an argument from the contrary: the same natural desire leads to sin on the forbidden path. This shows that it is not the desire itself that decides, but the lawful or forbidden path of its fulfillment.

HAD-2220.text: Likewise he receives reward when he satisfies it in what is permitted.
HAD-2220.narrator: Abū Ḏarr al-Ġifārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2220.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2220.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains that the sin on the forbidden path shows the intelligibility of the reward on the permitted path. The reward is connected especially with the intention of protecting oneself from the forbidden by means of the permitted; the Prophet ﷺ made this vivid to the Ṣaḥābah through the comparison.

HAD-2221.text: Upon every joint of the human being there lies every day a Ṣadaqah.
HAD-2221.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2221.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2221.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that every joint and every part of the healthy body is a gift from Allah, for which thanks are owed daily. Obedience and good deeds are in this context called Ṣadaqah, because the servant thanks with them for the bodily favors granted to him.

HAD-2222.text: To mediate justly between two people is a Ṣadaqah.
HAD-2222.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2222.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2222.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that just mediation between people belongs to the righteous deeds whose acceptance with Allah is hoped for. The expression includes in particular the just settling and resolving of disputes.

HAD-2223.text: To help a man with his mount, to seat him upon it, or to lift his luggage onto it, is a Ṣadaqah.
HAD-2223.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2223.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2223.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl places practical help for others among the daily forms of Ṣadaqah. The Ḥadīṯ thereby extends the concept of Ṣadaqah beyond money to concrete bodily support and relief.

HAD-2224.text: A good word is a Ṣadaqah.
HAD-2224.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2224.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2224.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that a good word, like a monetary gift, can bring joy and benefit into the heart of the recipient. Therefore good speech is called Ṣadaqah: it produces good, removes hardness from hearts, and belongs to the significant deeds of Birr.

HAD-2225.text: Every step that you take toward the prayer is a Ṣadaqah.
HAD-2225.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2225.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2225.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl also places the steps toward the prayer among the acts of Ṣadaqah. Bodily movement toward obedience thus itself becomes a form of thanks for the health and the ability to move that Allah has given to the human being.

HAD-1946.text: Beware of quarreling, debates and disputes; through this a person can become unjust, disloyal and sinful. Hold fast to patience, for patience leads to righteousness.
HAD-1946.speaker: He said:

HAD-1947.text: Beware of quarreling and debates in religion; discuss neither with a scholar nor with an ignorant person. The scholar can withhold his knowledge from you, and the ignorant person hardens your heart.
HAD-1947.narrator: Maymūn ibn Mihrān رحمه الله said:
HAD-1947.speaker: He said:

HAD-1948.text: The sign of the people of innovation is their attack on the people of transmission.
HAD-1948.narrator: Abū Ḥātim ar-Rāzī رحمه الله said:
HAD-1948.speaker: He said:

HAD-1949.text: The believer deals tactfully with people and does not quarrel. He spreads Allah's wisdom; if it is accepted, he praises Allah, and if it is rejected, he praises Allah.
HAD-1949.speaker: He said:

HAD-1950.text: Among the foundations of the Sunnah is to abandon disputes in religion and not to sit with the people of inclinations.
HAD-1950.narrator: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal رحمه الله said:
HAD-1950.speaker: He said:

HAD-1951.text: Whoever removes for a believer one distress from the distresses of this world, from him Allah removes one distress from the distresses of the Day of Resurrection.
HAD-1951.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1951.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1952.text: Allah helps the servant as long as the servant helps his brother.
HAD-1952.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1952.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1953.text: Whoever takes a path on which he seeks knowledge, Allah thereby makes easy for him a path to Paradise.
HAD-1953.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1953.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1954.text: Whoever walks a path in order to seek knowledge, Allah makes easy for him a path to Paradise.
HAD-1954.narrator: Abū ad-Dardāʾ رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1954.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1955.text: None of you believes completely until I am more beloved to him than his father, his child and all people.
HAD-1955.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1955.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1956.text: None of you believes completely until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
HAD-1956.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1956.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1957.text: The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe.
HAD-1957.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-1957.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1958.text: The believer is for the believer like a building: one part strengthens the other.
HAD-1958.narrator: Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1958.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1959.text: The believers, in their love, mercy and affection, are like one body.
HAD-1959.narrator: Nuʿmān ibn Bašīr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1959.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1960.text: A strong limb is more beloved to Allah and better than a weak limb; in both there is good.
HAD-1960.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1960.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1961.text: Strive for what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not be incapable.
HAD-1961.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1961.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1962.text: If something befalls you, do not say: If only I had done this; rather say: Allah has decreed, and what He wanted, He has done.
HAD-1962.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1962.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1963.text: Deeds are only according to intentions, and each person is due only what he intended.
HAD-1963.narrator: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-1963.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1964.text: Whoever introduces into this affair of ours something that does not belong to it, his deed is rejected.
HAD-1964.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-1965.text: The best speech is Allah's Book, and the best guidance is the guidance of Muḥammad ﷺ; the worst things are the newly introduced matters.
HAD-1965.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-1965.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:

HAD-2406.text: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from cowardice.
HAD-2406.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2406.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-2406.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ understands cowardice as blameworthy weakness where steadfastness and courage are required. The supplication seeks protection from a state that holds the servant back from duty and truth.

HAD-2407.text: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from decrepit old age.
HAD-2407.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2407.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-2407.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains al-haram as an age in which strength and the senses decline so severely that the person returns to a state of great weakness. The supplication concerns especially the burdensome consequences of this state.

HAD-2408.text: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from stinginess.
HAD-2408.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2408.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-2408.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains stinginess as withholding what is owed in rights over wealth or in necessary spending. It can both violate religious duties and foster need and harshness toward others.

HAD-2409.text: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave.
HAD-2409.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2409.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-2409.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ presents seeking refuge from the punishment of the grave as part of the prophetic supplications for protection. By it the servant asks to be preserved from the consequences of sin after death.

HAD-2410.text: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the Fitnah of life and of death.
HAD-2410.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2410.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-2410.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the Fitnah of life as trials that endanger faith and obedience, and the Fitnah of death as the trials at the end of life and thereafter. The supplication is therefore a more comprehensive protection for the servant’s entire path.

HAD-2411.text: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from severe distress.
HAD-2411.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2411.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to seek refuge:
HAD-2411.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains ǧahd al-balāʾ as a severe trial that brings a person to the limit of what he can bear. Seeking refuge covers great distresses in religion, body, family, and circumstances of life.

HAD-2412.text: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from being overtaken by misfortune.
HAD-2412.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2412.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to seek refuge:
HAD-2412.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains darak aš-šaqāʾ as the reaching or being overtaken by misery and severe misfortune. The supplication is directed against states that lead a person to ruin in worldly or otherworldly respect.

HAD-2413.text: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from a bad outcome of what is decreed.
HAD-2413.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2413.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to seek refuge:
HAD-2413.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that Allah’s Qadar itself is not called bad, but the event that befalls the servant and pains or harms him. The Duʿāʾ is therefore a request for protection from the burdensome consequences of what might befall him.

HAD-2414.text: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the gloating of enemies.
HAD-2414.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2414.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to seek refuge:
HAD-2414.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains šamātat al-aʿdāʾ as an enemy’s joy over a misfortune that strikes the servant. The supplication therefore covers both protection from the misfortune itself and from the added humiliation of hostile gloating.

HAD-2415.text: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done.
HAD-2415.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-2415.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ understands the supplication as refuge from the bad consequences of deeds already committed. It includes repentance, protection from their punishment, and the request not to remain upon the consequences of earlier faults.

HAD-2416.text: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have not yet done.
HAD-2416.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-2416.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the second half as protection from future evil and from deeds into which the servant might later fall. The Ḥadīṯ thereby joins past and future in a comprehensive request for preservation.

HAD-2417.narrator: Ṭāriq ibn Ašyam al-Ašǧaʿī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2417.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ taught a man to say:
HAD-2417.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ places the request for forgiveness at the beginning, because the removal of sins opens the way for further divine favor. Maghfirah includes the covering and the pardoning of sin.

HAD-2418.text: O Allah, have mercy on me.
HAD-2418.narrator: Ṭāriq ibn Ašyam al-Ašǧaʿī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2418.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ taught a man to say:
HAD-2418.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ understands the request for Raḥmah as a request to attain good after purification from sin. Forgiveness removes evil; mercy brings benefit and divine favor.

HAD-2419.narrator: Ṭāriq ibn Ašyam al-Ašǧaʿī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2419.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ taught a man to say:
HAD-2419.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the request for Hudā as guidance to the right way and firmness upon it. It includes knowledge of what is right and help to act accordingly.

HAD-2420.narrator: Ṭāriq ibn Ašyam al-Ašǧaʿī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2420.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ taught a man to say:
HAD-2420.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ understands Rizq comprehensively: lawful provision for the body as well as what sustains the heart and religion. The short Duʿāʾ thus gathers central needs of this world and the next.

HAD-2421.text: O Allah, grant my soul its Taqwā.
HAD-2421.narrator: Zayd ibn Arqam رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2421.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-2421.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the supplication as a request that Allah grant the soul fear of God, obedience, and protection from sin. Taqwā is not only knowledge of what is right, but a state that shapes action.

HAD-2422.text: Purify my soul; You are the Best who purifies it.
HAD-2422.narrator: Zayd ibn Arqam رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2422.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-2422.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ understands the purification of the soul as cleansing from sin, bad traits, and corrupt inclinations. The servant at the same time acknowledges that true Tazkiyah succeeds only with Allah’s help.

HAD-2423.text: You are its Walī and its Mawlā.
HAD-2423.narrator: Zayd ibn Arqam رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2423.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-2423.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the words as an acknowledgment of complete need toward Allah: He is the Protector, Helper, and Lord of the soul. Therefore its right guidance and purification are sought from Him.

HAD-2424.text: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from knowledge that brings no benefit.
HAD-2424.narrator: Zayd ibn Arqam رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2424.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-2424.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains useless knowledge as knowledge that leads the servant neither to right guidance nor to righteous action. The benefit of religious knowledge therefore appears in understanding, fear of God, and putting it into practice.

HAD-2425.text: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from a heart that feels no humility.
HAD-2425.narrator: Zayd ibn Arqam رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2425.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-2425.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ understands a heart without Ḫušūʿ as a heart that is not moved in a fitting way by remembrance, admonition, and revelation. The supplication is therefore directed toward a living, receptive heart.

HAD-2566.text: In Paradise there is a tent made of a single hollowed pearl, whose expanse is sixty miles.
HAD-2566.narrator: Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2566.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2566.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats the description as part of the actual size and beauty of dwelling in Paradise. The measurements make clear an expanse that surpasses worldly notions.

HAD-2567.text: In the various sections of this tent dwell relatives who do not see one another; the believer visits them.
HAD-2567.narrator: Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2567.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2567.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the great spatial expanse as the reason that the dwellers of different sections do not perceive one another directly, while the believer moves freely among them.

HAD-2568.text: Sayḥān, Ǧayḥān, the Euphrates and the Nile are among the rivers of Paradise.
HAD-2568.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2568.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2568.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ mentions various classical explanations of the connection of these well-known rivers with Paradise. What is certain is the prophetic attribution of their special origin or relation to Paradise, without establishing further details that are not attested.

HAD-2569.text: People will enter Paradise whose hearts are like the hearts of birds.
HAD-2569.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2569.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2569.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ mentions as meanings the special tenderness and fearfulness of their hearts as well as strong Tawakkul. The various interpretations do not necessarily contradict one another and describe praiseworthy states of the heart.

HAD-2570.text: The fire that people kindle in this world is only one part of seventy parts of the heat of Ǧahannam.
HAD-2570.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2570.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2570.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the comparison as a warning of the extraordinary intensity of the fire of Hell. Even the strongest known worldly fire conveys only a very limited impression of it.

HAD-2571.text: None of you will be brought into Paradise by his deed alone.
HAD-2571.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2571.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2571.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that deeds do not compel entry into Paradise by their own power. Guidance, the acceptance of deeds and the actual entry rest on Allah’s grace; the deeds are a cause of ranks and an expression of obedience.

HAD-2572.text: Not even you, O Messenger of Allah? He said: Not even I, except that Allah envelops me with His grace and mercy.
HAD-2572.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2572.speaker: The Companions asked the Prophet ﷺ:
HAD-2572.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl emphasizes that even the Prophet ﷺ attributes his entry into Paradise to Allah’s grace. This does not exclude the worth of deeds, but prevents the servant from relying on his achievement instead of Allah’s favor.

HAD-2573.text: Strive to hit what is right, and draw near to it.
HAD-2573.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2573.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2573.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains saddidū as seeking the right and balanced path. Whoever does not attain perfection should draw near to it, without overburdening himself through excess and then abandoning the deed.

HAD-2574.text: None of you should wish for death.
HAD-2574.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2574.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2574.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the prohibition by the benefit of continued life for the servant. As long as he lives, he still has the possibility to increase good, to make up what he missed and to correct faults through Tawbah.

HAD-2575.text: If he is one who does good, he can increase in good; if he is an evildoer, he can ask Allah for His pleasure through Tawbah.
HAD-2575.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2575.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2575.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains both possibilities as an argument for patience with the life that remains: the obedient one can increase his reward; the one who falls short can return, repent and seek Allah’s good pleasure.

HAD-2576.text: No lasting pain strikes the believer without sins being erased from him thereby.
HAD-2576.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī and Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2576.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2576.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains waṣab as lasting or continuing pain. The Ḥadīṯ shows that even such bodily burdens become for the believer a cause of the erasure of sins.

HAD-2577.text: No fatigue strikes the believer without sins being erased from him thereby.
HAD-2577.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī and Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2577.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2577.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains naṣab as fatigue and bodily exhaustion. Such everyday burdens are not lost for the believer, but can contribute to the erasure of sins.

HAD-2578.text: No illness strikes the believer without sins being erased from him thereby.
HAD-2578.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī and Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2578.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2578.sharh: Al-Māzirī expressly includes illness among the burdens that bring expiation for the believer. The Ḥadīṯ makes clear that bodily weakness does not remain religiously meaningless.

HAD-2579.text: No sadness strikes the believer without sins being erased from him thereby.
HAD-2579.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī and Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2579.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2579.sharh: Al-Māzirī treats, besides bodily pain, also the burden of the soul. Sadness and inner distress can serve the believer as expiation and thus belong to the trials whose effect Allah does not let go to waste.

HAD-2580.text: Even worry that occupies the believer becomes for him a cause of the erasure of sins.
HAD-2580.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī and Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2580.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2580.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains the mentioned hamm as worry and inner burden. The Ḥadīṯ thereby extends the expiation even to worries that occupy a person, although they need not be outwardly visible.

HAD-2581.text: All these burdens become for the believer an expiation for his bad deeds.
HAD-2581.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī and Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2581.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2581.sharh: Al-Māzirī understands the closing formula as a comprehensive promise: various bodily and spiritual trials can become for the believer an erasure of sins. The text turns unavoidable burden into a source of hope and purification.

HAD-2582.text: The expiation covers both the bodily and the spiritual distresses of the believer.
HAD-2582.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī and Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2582.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2582.sharh: Al-Māzirī’s explanations of the terms show that the Ḥadīṯ deliberately names different forms of trial: lasting pain, fatigue, illness, sadness and worry. The promise of expiation is therefore not limited to a single kind of suffering.

HAD-2583.text: You kiss your children? We do not kiss them.
HAD-2583.speaker: A Bedouin said to the Prophet ﷺ:
HAD-2583.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl treats affection toward children as part of the permitted and praised mercy. Bodily tenderness such as kissing small children does not contradict dignity or manliness, but is an expression of Raḥmah.

HAD-2584.text: What can I do for you if Allah has removed mercy from your heart?
HAD-2584.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2584.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl understands the reply as a rebuke of harshness toward children. Mercy is a gift of Allah and shows itself in conduct; whoever loses it from the heart loses an essential basis of good dealings.

HAD-2585.text: Allah is gentle and loves gentleness.
HAD-2585.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2585.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains Rifq as mildness, calm proceeding and the avoidance of needless harshness. That Allah loves Rifq makes it a fundamental Islamic attitude in dealings and in carrying out permitted aims.

HAD-2326.text: Beware of sitting on the roads.
HAD-2326.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2326.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2326.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the warning by the fact that sitting on public roads can easily lead to glances, speech, or actions that harm passers-by. Where such sitting is unnecessary, avoiding it is safer; where it is necessary, the rights mentioned afterwards apply.

HAD-2327.text: If you must sit there, then give the road its right.
HAD-2327.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2327.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2327.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that permission to sit on public roads is bound to observing the rights of those who pass by. Use of public space does not release one from consideration, protection, and the duties that arise there.

HAD-2328.text: Part of the right of the road is to lower the gaze.
HAD-2328.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2328.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2328.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl places lowering the gaze among the first rights of those who pass by. The one sitting should guard his eyes from what is not permitted to him, and should not violate people's privacy or honor through curious watching.

HAD-2329.text: Part of the right of the road is to keep harm away.
HAD-2329.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2329.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2329.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl understands keeping harm away in a comprehensive sense: the one sitting may not harm passers-by either by words or by actions. The right of the road thereby protects body, honor, and the undisturbed use of public space.

HAD-2330.text: Part of the right of the road is to return the Salām.
HAD-2330.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2330.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2330.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl counts returning the Salām among the rights that arise from meeting those who pass by. Whoever takes a public seat must not neglect the social duties connected with it.

HAD-2331.text: Part of the right of the road is to enjoin the good and forbid the reprehensible.
HAD-2331.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2331.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2331.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the one who uses the public road and perceives something reprehensible there upholds the known duties of enjoining the good and forbidding the reprehensible within his ability. The Ḥadīṯ makes this a right of public space, not a permission for uncontrolled intervention.

HAD-2332.text: It is not permitted for a Muslim to shun his brother for longer than three nights.
HAD-2332.narrator: Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2332.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2332.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that groundless personal shunning beyond three days is forbidden. The short period takes account of human nature in anger; afterwards the Muslim should end the enmity and restore brotherhood.

HAD-2333.text: The better of the two is the one who begins with the Salām first.
HAD-2333.narrator: Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2333.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2333.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the greater merit belongs to the one who overcomes his own reserve and begins the reconciliation with the Salām. Taking the initiative to restore brotherhood is thereby itself a good deed.

HAD-2334.text: The gates of Paradise are opened on Mondays and Thursdays.
HAD-2334.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2334.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2334.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the two days as times of special divine favor and forgiveness. The Ḥadīṯ, however, links this regular opportunity directly with a warning against persisting enmity.

HAD-2335.text: On these days every servant who associates nothing with Allah is forgiven, except a man between whom and his brother there is enmity.
HAD-2335.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2335.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2335.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the text first names the foundation of Tawḥīd and then highlights persisting personal enmity as an obstacle to this special forgiveness. What is meant is groundless or sinful enmity, not a lawfully grounded distancing.

HAD-2336.text: It is said: Let these two wait until they reconcile.
HAD-2336.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2336.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2336.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ understands the postponement as a serious warning against holding on to personal enmity. The repetition strengthens the call to reconciliation and shows how much mutual bitterness can keep the servant away from special favor.

HAD-2337.text: Buyer and seller have the right of choice as long as they have not yet separated from each other.
HAD-2337.narrator: Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2337.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2337.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the right of choice in a sale as protection of both contracting parties against haste and incomplete consent. As long as the sale session continues, there remains, according to the rule named in the Ḥadīṯ, room to confirm the contract or to dissolve it.

HAD-2338.text: If buyer and seller are truthful and disclose everything, Barakah is given to them in their transaction; if they lie and conceal something, the Barakah of their transaction is wiped out.
HAD-2338.narrator: Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2338.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2338.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that truthfulness and disclosure of defects belong to the causes of Barakah in trade. Deception may outwardly bring profit, but it destroys the blessed effect of the transaction and violates the rights of the other contracting party.

HAD-2339.text: No one has ever eaten anything better than what he has earned by the work of his own hands.
HAD-2339.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2339.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains earning from one's own work as a particularly honorable and safe form of livelihood. The Ḥadīṯ praises self-reliance, lawful earning, and the readiness to provide one's own livelihood through actual work.

HAD-2340.text: The Prophet of Allah, Dāwūd عليه السلام, ate from the work of his own hands.
HAD-2340.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2340.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl cites the example of Dāwūd عليه السلام as a special proof that one's own work is compatible with prophetic dignity. High rank does not release one from lawful earning; rather, honest work is expressly praised.

HAD-2341.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the one who takes Ribā, the one who pays it, the scribe of the contract, and his two witnesses.
HAD-2341.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2341.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2341.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats the Ḥadīṯ as a strong warning against all participation in a Ribā transaction. Not only the immediate recipient, but also the parties who knowingly take part are named, because their participation makes the forbidden contract possible or confirms it.

HAD-2342.text: He said about those involved in Ribā: They are equal in it.
HAD-2342.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2342.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2342.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the equating in the Ḥadīṯ with regard to participation in the forbidden act and the warning pronounced for it. It does not necessarily mean that every participant possesses in every respect the same individual degree of sin; what is decisive is their knowing cooperation in the Ribā transaction.

HAD-2343.text: Shall I not inform you about the greatest of the major sins? Associating something with Allah.
HAD-2343.narrator: Abū Bakrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2343.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2343.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains Širk as the gravest of the major sins mentioned, because it violates Allah's exclusive right to ʿIbādah. The Ḥadīṯ therefore begins with this offense, before the weighty rights of people are named.

HAD-2344.text: Among the greatest major sins is disobedience toward the parents.
HAD-2344.narrator: Abū Bakrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2344.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2344.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl emphasizes the gravity of ʿUqūq al-wālidayn, because Allah in the revelation repeatedly names the right of the parents immediately after His own right. Ingratitude, offense, and culpable violation of their rights therefore belong among the greatest sins.

HAD-2345.text: And beware of false statement and false testimony.
HAD-2345.narrator: Abū Bakrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2345.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2345.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the repeated warning against false statement as an indication of its extraordinary danger and of how easily the tongue can fall into it. False testimony joins lying with the violation of others' rights and can thereby cause great harm.

HAD-2426.text: O Allah, I seek refuge with You from a soul that is never satisfied.
HAD-2426.narrator: Zayd ibn Arqam رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2426.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-2426.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the insatiable soul as one whose desire for worldly things finds no end. Seeking refuge from it is a request for qanāʿah, restraint of desires, and contentment with lawful provision.

HAD-2427.text: O Allah, I seek refuge with You from a Duʿāʾ that is not answered.
HAD-2427.narrator: Zayd ibn Arqam رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2427.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-2427.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the request as refuge from causes that stand against being answered, and from a supplication lacking the required sincerity and turning toward Allah. It teaches the servant to ask both for what is sought and for the acceptance of his Duʿāʾ.

HAD-2428.text: We have entered the evening, and dominion in the evening belongs to Allah; all praise belongs to Allah.
HAD-2428.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2428.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say in the evening:
HAD-2428.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the formula as a conscious acknowledgment that, with the coming of evening, dominion and praise belong to Allah alone. The servant thereby begins the evening with tawḥīd, gratitude, and turning toward Allah.

HAD-2429.text: My Lord, I ask You for the good of this night and the good of what comes after it.
HAD-2429.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2429.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say in the evening:
HAD-2429.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ understands the request comprehensively: it includes every good that lies in the night or proceeds from it, especially obedience, protection, rest, and righteous opportunities.

HAD-2430.text: I seek refuge with You from the evil of this night and from the evil of what comes after it.
HAD-2430.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2430.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say in the evening:
HAD-2430.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the refuge as a comprehensive request against the visible and hidden evil of the night and the events that follow from it. The servant entrusts his protection to Allah.

HAD-2431.text: When morning came, the Prophet ﷺ said correspondingly: We have entered the morning, and dominion in the morning belongs to Allah.
HAD-2431.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2431.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say in the evening:
HAD-2431.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the same meaning is renewed in the morning: with the beginning of a new day the servant again affirms Allah’s dominion and begins his time with Ḏikr and acknowledgment of his dependence on Allah.

HAD-2432.text: There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone.
HAD-2432.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2432.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-2432.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the formula as a pure affirmation of tawḥīd after the hostile armies turned away. Victory is not ascribed to human strength, but to Allah alone.

HAD-2433.text: Allah strengthened His army and granted His servant victory.
HAD-2433.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2433.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-2433.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl emphasizes that the victory of the believers and the strengthening of their army ultimately come from Allah. The wording joins the military outcome with tawakkul and acknowledgment of divine help.

HAD-2434.text: Allah alone defeated the allied armies; after Him there is nothing.
HAD-2434.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2434.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-2434.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl understands the statement as a complete attribution of the final victory to Allah. The allies were driven back without a human force matching them; thereby Allah’s power and the nullity of created strength before Him are emphasized.

HAD-2435.text: The Prophet ﷺ left her early after the Ṣubḥ prayer, while she sat at her place of prayer; when he returned later in the forenoon, she was still sitting there in Ḏikr.
HAD-2435.narrator: Ǧuwayriyah bint al-Ḥāriṯ رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2435.speaker: Ǧuwayriyah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2435.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ understands the context as evidence for the excellence of continuous Ḏikr, while also showing that short, comprehensive formulas can possess extraordinary weight.

HAD-2436.text: After I left, I said four words three times; if they were weighed against everything you have said since morning, they would equal it.
HAD-2436.narrator: Ǧuwayriyah bint al-Ḥāriṯ رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2436.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2436.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the statement as an indication of Ǧawāmiʿ al-Kalim in Ḏikr: few words can, because of their comprehensive meaning, surpass a very great quantity of other formulations.

HAD-2437.text: Subḥān Allāh wa-bi-ḥamdih – according to the number of His creation.
HAD-2437.narrator: Ǧuwayriyah bint al-Ḥāriṯ رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2437.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2437.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the number of creation as an expression of a quantity that the human being cannot grasp. The Ḏikr is thereby bound to an immeasurable magnitude.

HAD-2438.text: Subḥān Allāh wa-bi-ḥamdih – according to His good pleasure.
HAD-2438.narrator: Ǧuwayriyah bint al-Ḥāriṯ رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2438.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2438.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ understands the wording as Ḏikr in a measure that pleases Allah and corresponds to His good pleasure. It joins tasbīḥ and taḥmīd with the servant’s highest aim: riḍā Allāh.

HAD-2439.text: Subḥān Allāh wa-bi-ḥamdih – according to the weight of His Throne.
HAD-2439.narrator: Ǧuwayriyah bint al-Ḥāriṯ رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2439.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2439.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the mention of the Throne as an expression of immense greatness. The Ḏikr is verbally bound to something whose actual weight only Allah knows.

HAD-2440.text: Subḥān Allāh wa-bi-ḥamdih – according to the ink of His words.
HAD-2440.narrator: Ǧuwayriyah bint al-Ḥāriṯ رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2440.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2440.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ understands the ink of Allah’s words as an image of something inexhaustible. The words of Allah have no end; accordingly, the unlimitedness of praise is here expressed in words.

HAD-2441.text: Fāṭimah رضي الله عنها complained of the hard work with the hand mill and asked the Prophet ﷺ for a servant.
HAD-2441.narrator: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2441.speaker: ʿAlī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2441.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the domestic context as the starting point of the prophetic instruction. The bodily burden was real, yet the Prophet ﷺ pointed to a spiritual benefit that was even better for her.

HAD-2442.text: Shall I not direct you to something that is better for you than a servant?
HAD-2442.narrator: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2442.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2442.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl understands the statement as an indication that the taught Ḏikr is a help for body and soul and at the same time brings lasting reward. The Prophet ﷺ replaced the desired material relief with a greater religious gift.

HAD-2443.text: When you go to bed, say thirty-three times: Subḥān Allāh.
HAD-2443.narrator: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2443.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2443.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the tasbīḥ as declaring Allah free of every deficiency. Its fixed number of repetitions makes the Ḏikr a constant nightly sunnah.

HAD-2444.text: And say thirty-three times: al-ḥamdu li-llāh.
HAD-2444.narrator: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2444.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2444.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the taḥmīd as praise and thanks for Allah’s blessings. The sleep-Ḏikr thereby joins tanzīh and gratitude immediately before the end of the day.

HAD-2445.text: And say thirty-four times: Allāhu akbar.
HAD-2445.narrator: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2445.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2445.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the takbīr as magnifying Allah above everything else. With thirty-four takbīrāt the total number of the nightly Ḏikr is completed at one hundred.

HAD-2526.text: A Šayṭān reports that he did not leave a man until he had separated him from his wife; thereupon Iblīs draws him close to himself and praises him.
HAD-2526.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2526.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2526.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ emphasizes the particular gravity of deliberately destroying a marriage. The separation of spouses causes far-reaching harm to the family, the children, and social relationships.

HAD-2527.text: Each one of you is assigned a companion from among the Ǧinn.
HAD-2527.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2527.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2527.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the Qarīn as an accompanying Šayṭān who seeks to move the human being toward sin and toward evil. This does not release the human being from his own responsibility.

HAD-2528.text: The Companions asked: Even you, O Messenger of Allah? He said: Even me.
HAD-2528.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2528.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2528.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the Prophet ﷺ also had a Qarīn; the distinction does not lie in the absence of such a companion, but in Allah’s special help and protection.

HAD-2529.text: But Allah helped me against him, so that he commands me only to good.
HAD-2529.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2529.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2529.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ mentions the well-known discussion of reading and meaning concerning »fa-aslama«. What is certain is the core: Allah granted His Prophet ﷺ special help and protection, so that no prompting to evil any longer came from this Qarīn.

HAD-2530.text: Strive for what is right, and draw as near as possible to what is perfectly right.
HAD-2530.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2530.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2530.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the instruction as a joining of earnest striving and realistic steadfastness. The servant should want to hit the truth and, when imperfection is unavoidable, remain as close to it as possible.

HAD-2531.text: None of you will be saved by his deeds alone or enter Paradise by them.
HAD-2531.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2531.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2531.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that deeds are causes of reward, yet they establish no independent claim upon Allah. Entry into Paradise occurs ultimately through Allah’s mercy and favor.

HAD-2532.text: The Companions asked: Not even you, O Messenger of Allah? He said: Not even I, except that Allah envelops me with mercy and favor.
HAD-2532.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2532.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2532.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that even the highest human ʿIbādah does not outweigh the gifts of Allah. The Prophet ﷺ names himself in order to make clear the complete dependence of all human beings upon Allah’s Raḥmah.

HAD-2533.text: And rejoice in the good news.
HAD-2533.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2533.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2533.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the good news as a protection against despair: knowledge of dependence upon Allah’s mercy should not lead to inactivity, but to balanced action with hope.

HAD-2534.text: The Prophet ﷺ stood in prayer so long that his feet swelled.
HAD-2534.narrator: al-Muġīrah ibn Šuʿbah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2534.speaker: al-Muġīrah ibn Šuʿbah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2534.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the extraordinary length of the prayer as an expression of gratitude and voluntary ʿIbādah. The report shows the strong connection between recognizing grace and increased obedience.

HAD-2535.text: Should I not then be a grateful servant?
HAD-2535.narrator: al-Muġīrah ibn Šuʿbah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2535.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2535.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that forgiveness does not lead to slackening in ʿIbādah. With the Prophet ﷺ, certainty of Allah’s favor led rather to still greater gratitude.

HAD-2536.text: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reminded the people regularly on certain days, and not every day.
HAD-2536.narrator: Abū Wāʾil reported about ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-2536.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه used to:
HAD-2536.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ places the practice of Ibn Masʿūd as an application of the prophetic method of teaching: knowledge and admonition are to be conveyed so that the capacity to receive and attentiveness remain.

HAD-2537.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ chose fitting days for our admonition, because he wanted to avoid our becoming weary of it.
HAD-2537.narrator: Abū Wāʾil reported from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-2537.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه said about the Prophet ﷺ:
HAD-2537.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ draws from this a principle of good teaching: frequency alone is not the aim. The teacher takes account of the people’s condition and their capacity to receive, so that useful admonition does not lose its effect through overload.

HAD-2538.text: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen.
HAD-2538.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2538.speaker: Allah عز وجل said:
HAD-2538.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the statement as evidence that the reality of Paradise surpasses everything that human beings know from this-worldly experience. Descriptions convey truth, but not the complete reality that can be experienced.

HAD-2539.text: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no ear has heard.
HAD-2539.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2539.speaker: Allah عز وجل said:
HAD-2539.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that even all the descriptions and accounts that have been heard do not fully grasp the actual beauty and greatness of Paradise.

HAD-2540.text: I have prepared for My righteous servants what has never occurred to any human heart.
HAD-2540.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2540.speaker: Allah عز وجل said:
HAD-2540.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that even human imagination remains bound to this-worldly experience. The hidden reward in Paradise therefore surpasses every measure that can be fully imagined.

HAD-2541.text: Allah calls the inhabitants of Paradise and asks them: Are you content?
HAD-2541.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2541.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-2541.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the question not as a search for unknown information, but as an honoring of the inhabitants of Paradise and as an introduction to a still greater gift.

HAD-2542.text: How should we not be content, O Lord, when You have given us what You have not given to any other of Your creatures?
HAD-2542.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2542.speaker: The inhabitants of Paradise say:
HAD-2542.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains their answer as an expression of perfect gratitude. They recognize the uniqueness and the greatness of what Allah has granted them from His favor.

HAD-2543.text: I let My good pleasure rest upon you, and never again thereafter shall I be angry with you.
HAD-2543.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2543.speaker: Allah عز وجل says:
HAD-2543.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains Allah’s enduring good pleasure as a gift still greater than the delights of Paradise already received. It guarantees complete security from every future wrath and every punishment.

HAD-2544.text: The inhabitants of Paradise see the inhabitants of the high chambers above them like a shining star on the distant horizon.
HAD-2544.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2544.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2544.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the likeness as a depiction of great differences of rank within Paradise. Despite a shared salvation, the degrees differ according to Īmān, sincerity, and deeds.

HAD-2545.text: These high degrees are not only for prophets; they are also reached by men who believed in Allah and truly affirmed the Messenger.
HAD-2545.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2545.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2545.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that high ranks in Paradise are attainable through true Īmān and sincere affirmation of the Messenger. The Ḥadīṯ opens to the believers hope of high degrees, without abolishing the special rank of the prophets.

HAD-2626.text: Allah is gentle and loves gentleness.
HAD-2626.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2626.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the prophetic instruction as praise of mildness and restraint, even in tense situations. Rifq belongs to the qualities that Allah loves, and its effect becomes visible in speech and action.

HAD-2627.text: Allah gives for gentleness what He does not give for harshness and what He does not give for anything else.
HAD-2627.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2627.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that gentleness often reaches aims that harshness thwarts. The special reward therefore includes both the religious recompense and the good consequences in interpersonal affairs.

HAD-2628.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2628.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2628.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that constant truthfulness leads a person to comprehensive good and obedience. Ṣidq is thus not only a single virtue, but a path to further righteous qualities.

HAD-2629.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2629.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2629.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains Birr as a comprehensive term for obedience and good deeds. Because truthfulness leads to this path, it leads indirectly to the deeds that ground entry into Paradise.

HAD-2630.text: A person continually speaks the truth and strives for truthfulness, until he is written before Allah as a Ṣiddīq.
HAD-2630.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2630.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2630.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that repeated truthful speech and the conscious cultivation of Ṣidq finally become a firmly established quality. The rank of the Ṣiddīq is the result of constant practice and sincerity.

HAD-2631.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2631.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2631.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that lying opens a person to further forms of disobedience. Kaḏib rarely remains isolated; it weakens the inner restraint toward other misconduct.

HAD-2632.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2632.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2632.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains Fuǧūr as transgression and continued disobedience. Because lying leads there, the Ḥadīṯ warns against its endpoint: a path that can lead a person to the punishment of the Fire.

HAD-2633.text: A person continually lies and strives in lying, until he is written before Allah as a liar.
HAD-2633.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2633.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2633.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that repeated lying can finally become a firmly established character trait. The Ḥadīṯ therefore warns not only against single falsehoods, but against the conscious habituation to Kaḏib.

HAD-2634.text: Allah will punish those who torment people in this world.
HAD-2634.narrator: Hišām ibn Ḥakīm رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2634.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2634.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the Ḥadīṯ as a severe warning against unjust physical mistreatment. Whoever torments people without right exposes himself to a corresponding divine retribution; power and office do not remove this responsibility.

HAD-2635.text: There is many a disheveled person, turned away from the doors, who, if he swore by Allah, would be confirmed by Allah.
HAD-2635.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2635.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2635.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that outward standing and social esteem are no reliable measure of nearness to Allah. A servant little regarded among people can, because of his Taqwā and sincerity, hold a high rank with Allah.

HAD-2636.text: When a man says: «The people have perished», then he himself is the most perished among them.
HAD-2636.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2636.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2636.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the blame for the one who, out of self-exaltation, despises others wholesale and holds himself to be better. Whoever, by contrast, speaks from concern about religious disorders, without arrogance and without depriving people of their hope, does not fall under the same blame.

HAD-2637.text: When you cook broth, increase its water.
HAD-2637.narrator: Abū Ḏarr al-Ġifārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2637.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2637.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the instruction as a practical way to make beneficence possible even with small means. By increasing the broth, the benefit of a meal can be extended to neighbors, without great wealth being required.

HAD-2638.text: Be mindful of your neighbors and give them some of it in a good manner.
HAD-2638.narrator: Abū Ḏarr al-Ġifārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2638.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2638.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ understands the instruction as a concrete right of the neighbor. Even small gifts strengthen affection, notice need, and prevent neighborhood from becoming mere spatial closeness without mutual care.

HAD-2639.text: A needy woman came to me with two daughters; I found nothing except a single date and gave it to her.
HAD-2639.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2639.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats the report as an example that even a very small gift has significance when it benefits a needy person at the right moment. The action of ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها forms the starting point for the following prophetic promise.

HAD-2640.text: The woman divided the date between her two daughters and ate nothing of it herself.
HAD-2640.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2640.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ highlights the mother’s selflessness: despite her own need, she preferred her two daughters. The report joins motherly love, Īṯār and care for daughters with the subsequent promise of protection from the Fire.

HAD-2641.text: Whoever is tested with daughters and is good to them, they will be for him a protection from the Fire.
HAD-2641.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2641.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the promise as a great incentive to good care, upbringing and provision for daughters. The expression of being tested points to the responsibility and the effort; precisely patient and good treatment becomes a ground of protection from the Fire.

HAD-2642.text: There is no woman whose three children die before her, except that they will be a protection for her from the Fire.
HAD-2642.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2642.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2642.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the promise as a reward for patiently bearing an especially heavy loss. The child who died before becomes thereby a ground of special mercy and a protection for the parent who hopes with patience.

HAD-2643.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2643.speaker: When a woman asked: «And two?», the Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2643.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the answer expressly extends the promise also to the loss of two children. The brevity of the prophetic answer strengthens the consolation and shows the breadth of the divine reward for patient endurance.

HAD-2644.text: The small children of the Muslims belong to the small inhabitants of Paradise.
HAD-2644.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2644.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2644.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the expression as a clear message of consolation about the deceased small children of the Muslims. They are in Paradise and stand there under special care and security.

HAD-2645.text: One of these children meets his father or his parents, holds him fast and does not let go, until Allah lets him and his father enter Paradise.
HAD-2645.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2645.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2645.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the figurative scene as further consolation for patient parents: the deceased child will not be lost to them in the hereafter, but will become a ground of special mercy and of entry into Paradise.

HAD-2346.text: Whoever has in his heart even the weight of a speck of dust of arrogance will not enter Paradise.
HAD-2346.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2346.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2346.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains arrogance as a grave disease of the heart that shows itself in the rejection of the truth and the belittling of others. The warning concerns not merely outward clothing or a groomed appearance, but the corrupted inner state.

HAD-2347.text: Allah is beautiful and loves beauty.
HAD-2347.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2347.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2347.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that beautiful clothing and a clean appearance are not to be equated with Kibr. The Ḥadīṯ clearly separates lawful beauty from arrogance and makes plain that the blame concerns inner pride.

HAD-2348.text: Arrogance is to reject the truth and to belittle people.
HAD-2348.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2348.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2348.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the two core elements of Kibr: not accepting the truth out of pride, and treating other people with contempt. Thereby the Prophet ﷺ defines arrogance by concrete inner and outward effects.

HAD-2349.text: The complete Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe.
HAD-2349.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2349.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2349.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the Ḥadīṯ links the completeness of Islam with protecting others from verbal and bodily harm. The tongue and the hand are mentioned in particular because many forms of wrong occur through them.

HAD-2350.text: The true Muhāǧir is the one who leaves what Allah has forbidden.
HAD-2350.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2350.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2350.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the praised Hiǧrah, besides spatial emigration, also has an enduring religious meaning: the servant leaves what Allah has forbidden. This inner Hiǧrah remains relevant in every age.

HAD-2351.text: The upper hand is better than the lower hand.
HAD-2351.narrator: Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2351.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2351.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the upper hand as the giving hand and the lower as the taking hand. The Ḥadīṯ trains one in generosity and self-reliance, and in giving benefit, as far as possible, rather than depending on others.

HAD-2352.text: Begin with those whose maintenance you are responsible for.
HAD-2352.narrator: Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2352.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2352.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the order of spending: the obligatory provision of those one is bound to maintain takes precedence over voluntary Ṣadaqah. Generosity therefore does not begin by neglecting existing duties.

HAD-2353.text: The best Ṣadaqah is that which is given from an existing sufficiency.
HAD-2353.narrator: Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2353.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2353.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that voluntary Ṣadaqah is ideally given after one’s own necessary needs and those of one’s family have been secured. The Ḥadīṯ orders generosity and responsibility, rather than setting the two against each other.

HAD-2354.text: Whoever strives for abstinence, Allah preserves him from asking.
HAD-2354.narrator: Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2354.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2354.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the one who earnestly guards himself from unnecessary asking and dependence receives help from Allah in this inner independence. The Ḥadīṯ joins one’s own effort with divine help.

HAD-2355.text: Whoever seeks contentment, Allah grants him contentment.
HAD-2355.narrator: Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2355.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2355.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains contentment as the inner independence of the heart from what people possess. Whoever seeks this attitude and uses the lawful means, Allah helps him to preserve satisfaction and self-reliance.

HAD-2356.text: Whoever guarantees me what is between his jaws and what is between his legs, I guarantee him Paradise.
HAD-2356.narrator: Sahl ibn Saʿd as-Sāʿidī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2356.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2356.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that many grave sins arise through the tongue and the private parts. Whoever guards both from what is forbidden thereby protects a great part of his religion; that is why the extraordinary promise of Paradise is mentioned.

HAD-2357.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was neither obscene in his speech nor did he strive for obscenity.
HAD-2357.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2357.speaker: He described the Prophet ﷺ:
HAD-2357.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl understands the statement as part of the perfect character of the Prophet ﷺ: he neither used shameless or hurtful speech of his own accord nor deliberately sought such a manner of expression. The Ḥadīṯ presents purity of language as a mark of good character.

HAD-2358.text: Among the best of you are those with the best character.
HAD-2358.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2358.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2358.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains good character as a broad collection of praiseworthy manners: patience, gentleness, beneficence, refraining from harm, and good conduct. The Ḥadīṯ makes Ḥusn al-Ḫuluq a measure of special excellence.

HAD-2359.text: I served the Prophet ﷺ for ten years; he never said to me: «Uff», nor: «Why did you do that?», nor: «Why did you not do that?»
HAD-2359.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2359.speaker: Anas رضي الله عنه described the Prophet ﷺ:
HAD-2359.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl highlights in this the extraordinary gentleness and patience of the Prophet ﷺ in daily dealings. The report shows that good character becomes visible especially in recurring everyday situations, not only in extraordinary moments.

HAD-2360.text: Whoever looks after a widow and a needy person is like someone who fights in the path of Allah — or like someone who stands the night in prayer and fasts the day.
HAD-2360.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2360.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2360.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the immense reward by the lasting benefit of this care. Whoever continuously strives for the weak and the needy combines the use of wealth, time, and personal effort, and therefore receives a reward that resembles great forms of ʿIbādah.

HAD-2361.text: That I say Subḥān Allāh, al-ḥamdu li-llāh, lā ilāha illā Allāh and Allāhu akbar is dearer to me than everything over which the sun rises.
HAD-2361.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2361.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2361.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ understands the four formulas as a comprehensive Ḏikr of Tanzīh, praise, Tawḥīd, and the glorification of Allah. That they are more valuable than the world shows the superiority of lasting reward in the hereafter over perishable possession.

HAD-2362.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2362.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2362.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains Fisq here as a grave departure from the obedience that is required, through violating a Muslim’s honor. The expression shows that reviling is not merely bad manners, but a religiously serious sin.

HAD-2363.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2363.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2363.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the expression as an extremely strong warning against the forbidden fighting of Muslims. The term Kufr is used here for an act that resembles the traits and ways of the Kuffār, or that constitutes a grave branch of Kufr; it does not automatically mean Kufr akbar for every single perpetrator.

HAD-2364.text: None of you should point a weapon at his brother.
HAD-2364.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2364.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2364.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the prohibition as protection against carelessly endangering life and bodily integrity. Even without intent to kill, pointing with a weapon can, through a wrong movement or other causes, turn into grave harm.

HAD-2365.text: For he does not know whether the Šayṭān causes his hand to go astray and he thereby falls into a pit of the Fire.
HAD-2365.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2365.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2365.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl understands the reason as a warning against situations in which a person does not fully control the consequences. The Šayṭān can turn play, a threat, or carelessness into an actual injury; therefore the dangerous initial act itself is already forbidden.

HAD-2466.text: When Allah decreed the creation, He wrote in a book with Himself: My mercy outweighs My wrath.
HAD-2466.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2466.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2466.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ understands the statement as a tremendous hope in the vastness of Allah’s Raḥmah. The authentic text affirms Raḥmah and Ġaḍab for Allah in a manner befitting Him and brings out that His mercy outweighs His wrath.

HAD-2467.text: Allah created one hundred portions of mercy.
HAD-2467.narrator: Salmān al-Fārisī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2467.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2467.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the portions counted in the Ḥadīṯ concern the created mercy which Allah distributes among His creatures. This is to be distinguished from Allah’s own attribute of Raḥmah.

HAD-2468.text: Each of these portions is of tremendous magnitude; Allah placed one portion of them upon the earth.
HAD-2468.narrator: Salmān al-Fārisī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2468.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2468.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the wording as an illustration of the immense vastness of the created mercy. Even the single portion appointed for this world suffices for the countless forms of compassion among creatures.

HAD-2469.text: Through this one portion the mother is merciful to her child, and animals and birds are merciful to one another.
HAD-2469.narrator: Salmān al-Fārisī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2469.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2469.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that even the natural compassion among humans and animals comes from this one worldly portion. The Ḥadīṯ thereby makes the vastness of the mercy reserved for the Hereafter especially clear.

HAD-2470.text: Ninety-nine portions remain for the Day of Resurrection; then Allah completes them with the portion that He had distributed in this world.
HAD-2470.narrator: Salmān al-Fārisī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2470.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2470.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the concluding statement as a great hope for the Day of Resurrection: the greater part of the created mercy is reserved for the Hereafter. This encourages hope without removing the duty of Tawbah and obedience.

HAD-2471.text: If the believer knew what punishment there is with Allah, no one would feel secure about his Paradise.
HAD-2471.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2471.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2471.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the statement as a balance between hope and fear. Knowing the severity of Allah’s punishment prevents false security and negligence; it is meant to lead the believer to Taqwā and Tawbah, not to despair.

HAD-2472.text: If the Kāfir knew how great the mercy with Allah is, no one would despair of His Paradise.
HAD-2472.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2472.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2472.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the second half as the counterpart to the believer’s fear: Allah’s mercy is so vast that even one who truly knew it ought not to despair of it. The Ḥadīṯ thereby joins Ḫawf and Raǧāʾ, without making light of Kufr or sin.

HAD-2473.text: A man from earlier communities, to whom Allah had given wealth and children, feared greatly at his death what awaited him with Allah.
HAD-2473.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2473.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-2473.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the starting point of the story as a strong fear of Allah despite a life in which the man saw hardly any good deeds for himself. This fear later became the cause of the mercy shown to him, not his unusual instruction itself.

HAD-2474.text: He instructed his family to burn him after his death, to grind him, and to scatter his ashes in the wind.
HAD-2474.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2474.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-2474.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ makes clear that the man’s instruction is not taught as correct ʿAqīdah. The story describes his state of great fear and ignorance; the forgiveness occurred because of his sincere fear of Allah.

HAD-2475.text: His family carried out the instruction; Allah gathered him again and brought him before Himself.
HAD-2475.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2475.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-2475.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ cites the report as a clear proof of Allah’s complete power over recreation. The scattering of the body parts changes nothing about the fact that Allah can fully restore the human being.

HAD-2476.text: What led you to do this? He answered: The fear of You.
HAD-2476.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2476.speaker: Allah asked him:
HAD-2476.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the man’s sincere Ḫašyah is the key to understanding the story. His faulty action did not arise from defiance toward Allah, but from overwhelming fear of His punishment.

HAD-2477.text: Allah met him, because of this fear, with mercy and forgave him.
HAD-2477.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2477.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-2477.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the outcome as proof of the vastness of Allah’s mercy toward the one whose heart is sincerely filled with fear of Him. The story justifies neither false beliefs nor self-appointed forms of burial.

HAD-2478.text: A servant sinned and said: My Lord, I have sinned; forgive me.
HAD-2478.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2478.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported from his Lord:
HAD-2478.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that admitting the sin and returning to Allah are essential marks of sincere Tawbah. The servant does not excuse his sin; he acknowledges it and asks his Lord for forgiveness.

HAD-2479.text: My servant knows that he has a Lord who forgives the sin and calls to account for the sin; I have forgiven My servant.
HAD-2479.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2479.speaker: Allah says in the Ḥadīṯ qudsī:
HAD-2479.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ emphasizes that the servant brings together two truths: hope in Allah’s forgiveness and fear of His reckoning. Precisely this knowledge leads him back to Tawbah after the lapse.

HAD-2480.text: Even when the servant sinned again and again sincerely asked for forgiveness, Allah forgave him again; the sin must not keep him from renewed Tawbah.
HAD-2480.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2480.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported from his Lord:
HAD-2480.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the Ḥadīṯ as proof that a repeated relapse does not close the door of Tawbah, provided that each Tawbah is truly sincere. The text encourages returning to Allah and not persisting in the sin.

HAD-2481.text: The statement «I have forgiven My servant; so let him do what he wills» does not mean permission to sin, but the continuing forgiveness with ever-renewed sincere Tawbah.
HAD-2481.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2481.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported from his Lord:
HAD-2481.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains: As long as the servant, after a sin, truly repents, does not declare it lawful, and returns to Allah, the door of forgiveness remains open. The sentence justifies neither planned sin nor persistence without Tawbah.

HAD-2482.text: No one has greater Ġayrah than Allah; therefore He has forbidden the open and the hidden indecencies.
HAD-2482.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2482.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2482.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ connects the divine Ġayrah with the prohibition of the Fawāḥiš. The authentic text affirms the attribute for Allah in a manner befitting Him; it is not to be equated with created Ġayrah.

HAD-2483.text: No one loves praise more than Allah; therefore He has praised Himself.
HAD-2483.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2483.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2483.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that Allah is worthy of all perfect praise and teaches His servants to praise Him with the praise that befits Him. Here too it holds: Allah’s attributes are understood without equating them with the attributes of creatures.

HAD-2484.text: No one loves the excuse and the establishing of the proof more than Allah; therefore He sent the messengers and revealed the books.
HAD-2484.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2484.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2484.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that Allah makes the truth clear to people through revelation and messengers and thereby establishes the Ḥuǧǧah. Punishment does not occur on the basis of hidden or unexplained demands, but after the message has been made clear.

HAD-2485.text: Three men stood at the House of Allah and asked themselves whether Allah hears their words.
HAD-2485.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2485.speaker: The report states:
HAD-2485.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the report as a warning against deficient knowledge of Allah’s perfect hearing and knowledge. Nothing of open or hidden speech escapes Him.

HAD-2486.text: One person thought: Allah hears us only when we speak aloud; another said: If He hears what is loud, He also hears what is hidden.
HAD-2486.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2486.speaker: The report states:
HAD-2486.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ highlights the error of judging Allah’s hearing by human limits. Allah hears the open and the hidden in a perfect manner befitting Him.

HAD-2487.text: Thereupon it was revealed that the people could not hide from the fact that their hearing, their eyes and their skin would testify against them, and that their false thought about Allah brought them to ruin.
HAD-2487.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2487.speaker: The report states:
HAD-2487.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the false thought that Allah does not know much of hidden action was itself a cause of ruin. The text confirms Allah’s all-encompassing knowledge and the testimony of the limbs on the Day of Resurrection.

HAD-2488.text: Some hypocrites stayed behind from the campaigns of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and rejoiced at having remained behind him.
HAD-2488.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2488.speaker: The report states:
HAD-2488.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the report as a description of a concrete nifāq behavior: remaining behind in violation of duty was not regretted, but made an occasion for one’s own joy.

HAD-2489.text: When the Prophet ﷺ returned, they excused themselves, swore oaths and wanted to be praised for something they had not done; concerning this, the warning in Āl ʿImrān 188 was revealed.
HAD-2489.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2489.speaker: The report states:
HAD-2489.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the combination of a false excuse and the desire for undeserved praise as especially reprehensible: besides the good that was omitted, there is the deception about one’s own state.

HAD-2490.text: Ibn ʿAbbās explained regarding Āl ʿImrān 188: The Prophet ﷺ asked people among the People of the Scripture about a matter; they concealed the truth from him, gave a different answer and still wanted to be praised for it.
HAD-2490.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2490.speaker: The report states:
HAD-2490.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ places the explanation of Ibn ʿAbbās in the context of the revelation: what is censured is the deliberate concealment of the truth, the pretense of correct information and the desire for praise for something that was not done.

HAD-2491.text: During a journey in great hardship, ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy said to his people that they should spend nothing for those with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so that they would disperse from him.
HAD-2491.narrator: Zayd ibn Arqam رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2491.speaker: The report states:
HAD-2491.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the statement as an attempt to weaken the community around the Prophet ﷺ through economic pressure. The report shows a concrete manifestation of nifāq.

HAD-2492.text: ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy also said: When we return to Madīnah, the mightier will drive the more humiliated out of it.
HAD-2492.narrator: Zayd ibn Arqam رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2492.speaker: The report states:
HAD-2492.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the statement as an arrogant reversal of true honor: true ʿIzzah belongs to Allah, His Messenger and the believers, not to the one who deems himself superior by lineage or worldly rank.

HAD-2493.text: Zayd conveyed the statements to the Prophet ﷺ. ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy denied them under oath, and Zayd thereby at first fell under grave suspicion.
HAD-2493.narrator: Zayd ibn Arqam رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2493.speaker: The report states:
HAD-2493.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ highlights Zayd’s trial: he reported what he had heard, but at first was not confirmed because of the other’s oath. The report shows the burden that truthful testimony can at times bring with it.

HAD-2494.text: Allah revealed Sūrat al-Munāfiqūn and thereby confirmed Zayd’s report.
HAD-2494.narrator: Zayd ibn Arqam رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2494.speaker: The report states:
HAD-2494.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the revelation as a clear exoneration of Zayd and a disclosure of the hypocrites’ actual statements. Truth can be contested for a time, yet it does not remain hidden before Allah.

HAD-2495.text: The Prophet ﷺ then called those concerned to ask forgiveness for them; they, however, turned their heads away.
HAD-2495.narrator: Zayd ibn Arqam رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2495.speaker: The report states:
HAD-2495.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ connects the turning away with the arrogance of the hypocrites described in the Qurʾān. Even after their fault was disclosed, they lacked the humble return that would have been required for genuine Tawbah.

HAD-2496.text: Allah will fold up the heavens on the Day of Resurrection.
HAD-2496.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2496.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2496.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the statement as a description of a real act of Allah on the Day of Resurrection, as it is transmitted in the authentic text. The Ḥadīṯ sets forth Allah’s complete dominion over the whole creation.

HAD-2497.text: Then He takes them with His right hand.
HAD-2497.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2497.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2497.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats the wording as part of the transmitted description of the Last Day. It is affirmed without equating Allah with creation or recasting the transmitted statement into a created attribute.

HAD-2498.text: Then Allah says: I am the King. Where are the tyrants? Where are the arrogant?
HAD-2498.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2498.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
