HAD-2498.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the words as a disclosure of Allah’s perfect and undisputed dominion on the Day of Resurrection. Worldly power, coercion and arrogance vanish completely before His dominion.

HAD-2499.text: Then Allah folds up the earths and says again: I am the King. Where are the tyrants? Where are the arrogant?
HAD-2499.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2499.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2499.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ connects the folding up of the earths with the same demonstration of divine dominion. A divergent transmission regarding the designation of the Hand is not made the core of the record; what remains decisive is the secure common meaning of the Ṣaḥīḥ text.

HAD-2500.text: The people will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection upon a white earth, slightly reddish, like a loaf of pure flour.
HAD-2500.narrator: Sahl ibn Saʿd as-Sāʿidī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2500.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2500.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the description as an indication of the complete change of the known surface of the earth on the Day of Resurrection. The new ground is level, clear and without the familiar features of this world.

HAD-2501.text: On this earth there is for no one a recognizable mark or a point of orientation.
HAD-2501.narrator: Sahl ibn Saʿd as-Sāʿidī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2501.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2501.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the place of gathering bears no buildings, mountains, marks of ownership or other points of orientation of the former world. Thereby the complete equality of people before Allah becomes visible.

HAD-2502.text: The moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ into two parts.
HAD-2502.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2502.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2502.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats the splitting of the moon as an authentically transmitted visible sign and miracle of the Prophet ﷺ. The majority of the Ṣaḥīḥ paths confirm the event from different lines of transmission.

HAD-2503.text: One part of the moon was on one side of the mountain and the other part on the other.
HAD-2503.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2503.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2503.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ understands the description of place as a clarification that the splitting was sensorily perceptible to those present and was not transmitted merely as an abstract statement.

HAD-2504.text: The inhabitants of Makkah asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for a sign; thereupon he showed them the splitting of the moon.
HAD-2504.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2504.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2504.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ places the transmission among the clear prophetic signs. The request for a visible sign is answered in the report directly by the observed splitting of the moon.

HAD-2505.text: No one bears injurious statements with more patience than Allah.
HAD-2505.narrator: Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2505.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2505.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the statement as a highlighting of Allah’s immense Ḥilm and forbearance toward His servants. Despite the gravest false statements about Him, He grants them time and continues to provide for them.

HAD-2666.text: Then his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Magian.
HAD-2666.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2666.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2666.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl understands the statement as an indication of the strong influence of upbringing and environment on the child. The text distinguishes between the original Fiṭrah and later external imprintings.

HAD-2667.text: Just as an animal gives birth to a complete young: do you see any mutilation on it before you yourselves cause it?
HAD-2667.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2667.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2667.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the animal simile as an illustration: the newborn first comes forth unharmed; the later change is brought about from outside. Likewise the Ḥadīṯ distinguishes between the original Fiṭrah and a later imprinting.

HAD-2668.text: If his parents are Muslims, he is a Muslim.
HAD-2668.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2668.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2668.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl treats the outward legal status of the child in connection with Fiṭrah and parental affiliation. The statement is understood within the framework of the transmitted rulings concerning children and their classification, and not as an independent statement about every conceivable special case.

HAD-2669.text: Every child is touched by the Šayṭān at its birth, except Maryam and her son.
HAD-2669.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2669.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2669.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl treats this statement as a special exception, established by authentic transmission, for Maryam and ʿĪsā عليهما السلام. It is received as a report about the unseen, without going beyond the wording.

HAD-2670.text: Concerning those who die as small children, the Prophet ﷺ said: Allah knows best what they would have done.
HAD-2670.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2670.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2670.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the reply as referring back to Allah the hidden knowledge of future actions that did not occur. The text forbids speculative certainty about what a child who died early would later have done.

HAD-2671.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2671.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2671.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the mentioned offenses as especially grave sins with destructive consequences for religion and the Hereafter. The number seven names here concrete, especially dangerous offenses, and does not mean that major sins as a whole would be limited to seven.

HAD-2672.text: Among the seven destructive sins is to associate something with Allah.
HAD-2672.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2672.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2672.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats Širk as the gravest of the offenses named in this Ḥadīṯ. It concerns Allah’s exclusive right to ʿIbādah and therefore stands at the beginning of the enumeration.

HAD-2673.text: Among the seven destructive sins is Siḥr.
HAD-2673.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2673.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2673.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ counts Siḥr among the destructive major sins and distinguishes its legal assessment according to the actual content and the form employed. The Ḥadīṯ in any case makes clear the extraordinary danger of Siḥr.

HAD-2674.text: Among the seven destructive sins is to kill, without right, a soul that Allah has made inviolable.
HAD-2674.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2674.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2674.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ emphasizes the inviolability of life. The addition «without right» shows that forbidden killing is meant, and that cases established as rightful do not fall under this wording.

HAD-2675.text: Among the seven destructive sins is to consume Ribā.
HAD-2675.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2675.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2675.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ places Ribā among the major destructive offenses. The wording about «eating» thereby denotes the forbidden economic benefit and stands for taking and using up the proceeds of Ribā.

HAD-2676.text: Among the seven destructive sins is to devour the property of an orphan.
HAD-2676.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2676.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2676.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ classifies the unlawful devouring of an orphan’s property among the destructive major sins. The particular gravity lies in exploiting someone in need of protection and in violating an entrusted property right.

HAD-2677.text: Among the seven destructive sins is to turn one’s back on the day of battle.
HAD-2677.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2677.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2677.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ counts unlawful flight from the ordered battle line among the destructive sins. What is meant is culpable withdrawal in a situation in which holding one’s ground is obligatory; the known šarʿī exceptions remain unaffected by this.

HAD-2678.text: Among the seven destructive sins is to accuse chaste, unsuspecting believing women of fornication.
HAD-2678.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2678.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2678.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ places the Qadhf of chaste believing women among the destructive major sins. The gravity lies in the violation of honor and in a grave unsubstantiated accusation with far-reaching social and legal consequences.

HAD-2679.text: Īmān has more than seventy – or more than sixty – branches.
HAD-2679.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2679.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2679.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that Īmān in the Šarīʿah does not denote only a single inner statement, but comprises numerous branches. Among them are convictions, words, and deeds, and their diversity shows the degrees of Īmān.

HAD-2680.text: The highest branch of Īmān is the statement: Lā ilāha illā Allāh.
HAD-2680.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2680.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2680.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains Tawḥīd as the highest branch, because the remaining branches of Īmān are valid only on its foundation. Without the soundness of Lā ilāha illā Allāh, the subsequent deeds do not bear their actual religious meaning.

HAD-2681.text: The lowest branch of Īmān is to remove what is harmful from the path.
HAD-2681.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2681.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2681.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the removal of harm from the path as the lowest branch mentioned, because it contains immediate benefit for Muslims, even if the deed appears slight outwardly. The Ḥadīṯ thereby shows that practical kindness is part of Īmān.

HAD-2682.text: Al-Ḥayāʾ is a branch of Īmān.
HAD-2682.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2682.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2682.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains praiseworthy Ḥayāʾ as a trait of character that holds a person back from what is shameful and moves him to fulfill duty. A supposed «Ḥayāʾ» that keeps someone from truth or duty does not belong to this praised branch.

HAD-2683.narrator: Tamīm ad-Dārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2683.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2683.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains Naṣīḥah as a comprehensive expression for sincerity and wanting good for the one to whom Naṣīḥah is due. That the religion is summed up by it shows the extraordinary breadth of this principle.

HAD-2684.narrator: Tamīm ad-Dārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2684.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2684.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains Naṣīḥah toward Allah as sincerity in Tawḥīd, Īmān, and obedience, and as purifying ʿIbādah from opposites and defects. Allah needs no benefit from the servant; the Naṣīḥah returns to the servant himself as sincere obedience.

HAD-2685.text: Naṣīḥah applies to the Book of Allah.
HAD-2685.narrator: Tamīm ad-Dārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2685.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2685.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains Naṣīḥah toward the Book of Allah through belief in its revelation, reverent acceptance, understanding, recitation, and acting according to its directives. The Book is not merely honored verbally, but is made the standard.

HAD-2546.text: Among the people of my Ummah who love me most strongly are people after me; one of them would wish to see me, even if he had to give up family and wealth for that.
HAD-2546.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2546.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2546.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the statement as praise for strong, sincere Īmān in the Prophet ﷺ among people who did not experience him personally. Love shows itself in longing, following, and valuing his Sunnah.

HAD-2547.text: In Paradise there is a gathering place that its inhabitants regularly visit.
HAD-2547.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2547.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2547.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the so-called market of Paradise not as a place of need and trade as in this world, but as a place of gathering and delight for the inhabitants of Paradise.

HAD-2548.text: There a wind blows over their faces and their clothing.
HAD-2548.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2548.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2548.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the wind as part of the renewed delight in Paradise. It brings no hardship, but additional beauty and a pleasant fragrance.

HAD-2549.text: Thereby the inhabitants of Paradise increase in beauty and grace.
HAD-2549.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2549.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2549.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the delight of Paradise does not diminish or stand still, but is continually renewed and increased.

HAD-2550.text: When they return to their relatives, these say: By Allah, you have become even more beautiful in beauty; and they answer them with the same.
HAD-2550.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2550.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2550.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ understands the mutual observation as part of the constantly increasing joy and beauty in Paradise. No one experiences envy or loss there through the increase of another.

HAD-2551.text: The first group that enters Paradise will be, in its beauty, like the full moon.
HAD-2551.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2551.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2551.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the likeness of the full moon as an image of the extraordinary brightness, beauty, and perfection of the first group that enters.

HAD-2552.text: The group after them will be like the brightest shining star in the sky.
HAD-2552.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2552.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2552.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the different images of light as an indication of differing ranks, while all the inhabitants of Paradise live in perfect joy and beauty.

HAD-2553.text: Every man among them has two wives.
HAD-2553.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2553.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2553.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats the statement as part of the transmitted description of paradisiacal life. It describes a gift of Allah in the Hereafter, whose complete reality is not measured by the conditions of this world.

HAD-2554.text: In Paradise there is no unmarried person.
HAD-2554.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2554.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2554.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the statement as an indication of the completeness of delight and the absence of worldly forms of loneliness or lack in Paradise.

HAD-2555.text: The inhabitants of Paradise eat and drink there.
HAD-2555.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2555.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2555.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains eating and drinking in Paradise as pure delight, not as the removal of hunger or weakness. Paradisiacal needs do not follow the burdensome bodily processes of this world.

HAD-2556.text: There they neither defecate nor urinate, and they do not have to clean their noses.
HAD-2556.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2556.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2556.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the absence of such excretions as part of the perfect purity of the paradisiacal body. Delight there is separated from every unpleasant bodily accompaniment.

HAD-2557.text: Their food becomes a belch and sweat whose fragrance is like musk.
HAD-2557.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2557.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2557.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that even the bodily processing of food in Paradise is pleasant, pure, and fragrant. None of it bears the impurity or the hardship of worldly excretions.

HAD-2558.text: Tasbīḥ and Taḥmīd are given to them as a matter of course, as breathing is given to you.
HAD-2558.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2558.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2558.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that Ḏikr in Paradise takes place without effort and burden. It becomes a natural joy of the inhabitants, as light and constant as breathing.

HAD-2559.text: Whoever enters Paradise lives in lasting delight and will never be wretched.
HAD-2559.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2559.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2559.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that delight in Paradise is free of every interruption, worry, and hardship. There is no change there from happiness to distress.

HAD-2560.text: The clothing of the inhabitants of Paradise never wears out.
HAD-2560.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2560.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2560.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the permanence of the clothing as part of the complete lastingness of paradisiacal delight. Nothing there is subject to the decay that marks this world.

HAD-2561.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2561.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2561.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that aging, weakness, and bodily decay are completely lifted in Paradise. The inhabitants remain in lasting strength and beauty.

HAD-2562.text: It is called out to the inhabitants of Paradise: You will remain healthy and will never become ill.
HAD-2562.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2562.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2562.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the proclamation as final security from illness. Health in Paradise is not a passing state, but lasting.

HAD-2563.text: You will live and will never die.
HAD-2563.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2563.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2563.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the statement as the final lifting of death for the inhabitants of Paradise. Their life thereafter has no end.

HAD-2564.text: You will remain young and will never age.
HAD-2564.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2564.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2564.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains lasting youth as part of the perfect paradisiacal creation. The weakness of old age and bodily decline are excluded there.

HAD-2565.text: You will delight and will never experience need or wretchedness.
HAD-2565.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2565.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2565.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that paradisiacal well-being is never interrupted by worry, loss, poverty, or pain. The statement sums up the lastingness of delight.

HAD-2706.text: Whoever claims something that does not belong to him does not belong to us, and he shall take his place in the Fire.
HAD-2706.narrator: Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2706.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2706.sharh: The wording warns with the utmost severity against a knowingly false arrogation of what one is not entitled to. In the context of the chapter it concerns especially false claims of lineage and belonging and the violation of the rights of others connected with them.

HAD-2707.text: Whoever designates a man as a Kāfir or as an enemy of Allah, although he is not, upon him this statement returns.
HAD-2707.narrator: Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2707.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2707.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains «ḥāra ʿalayhi» as: the statement returns upon the speaker. If the accused person is not so, the blame of the false attribution falls upon the speaker; the text is therefore a warning against unfounded Takfīr and a false attribution of enmity.

HAD-2708.text: Do not turn away from your fathers; whoever turns away from his father, this is designated as Kufr in his case.
HAD-2708.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2708.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2708.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains the wording in two ways: actual Kufr, when the forbidden is declared lawful, or linguistic Kufr in the sense of denying and concealing the right of one’s own father. Therefore the wording must not be understood without distinction as automatic Kufr akbar.

HAD-2709.text: Whoever knowingly attributes himself to someone other than his father, Paradise is denied to him.
HAD-2709.narrator: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ and Abū Bakrah رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2709.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2709.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ contains an extraordinarily grave threat against the knowingly false attribution to another father. Decisive is the knowingness named in the text itself; the context treats the deliberate denial of the actual lineage and of the right connected with it.

HAD-2710.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2710.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2710.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains «Fisq» as departing from obedience and from what the Šarīʿah obliges. Insulting a Muslim thereby violates his protected honor and is a forbidden transgression.

HAD-2711.text: Fighting against a Muslim is Kufr.
HAD-2711.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2711.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2711.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ distinguishes expressly: whoever fights a Muslim because of his Islam and holds this to be lawful falls under actual Kufr. For other cases he names interpretations such as an act of the Kuffār, Kufr of favor or of right, or Kufr by the deed, not automatically Kufr of conviction.

HAD-2712.text: Do not return after me as Kuffār, by some of you striking the necks of the others.
HAD-2712.narrator: Ǧarīr ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2712.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2712.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the warning in connection with the inviolability of Muslim blood. He prefers the interpretation that the Muslims should not fall back into the manner of the Kuffār, of fighting and killing one another; alongside this he names Kufr of the deed or of favor. The text is therefore not a blanket judgment of Kufr akbar upon every single fighter.

HAD-2713.text: Two things among the people are Kufr.
HAD-2713.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2713.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2713.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the designation here as a sharp warning: these are deeds and customs of the people of Kufr and of the Ǧāhiliyyah. In a broader sense he also describes in it the denial of a favor; the wording is not understood blanket-wise as Kufr akbar of every doer.

HAD-2714.text: Disparaging and contesting the lineage of others.
HAD-2714.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2714.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2714.sharh: Contesting lineage belongs, according to Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, to the forbidden customs of the Ǧāhiliyyah. Lineage serves to recognize and connect kinship; disparaging or damaging it without cause violates this right and the favor that lies in it.

HAD-2715.text: The Niyāḥah — the loud lamenting mourning — over a deceased person.
HAD-2715.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2715.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2715.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ assigns Niyāḥah to the forbidden practices of the Ǧāhiliyyah. The warning is directed against the loud lament that expresses discontent with destiny and contradicts the enjoined Ṣabr; the designation as Kufr is not understood here blanket-wise as Kufr akbar.

HAD-2716.text: Whichever slave flees from his masters, this is designated as Kufr in his case until he returns to them.
HAD-2716.narrator: Ǧarīr ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2716.speaker: Ǧarīr رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-2716.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ first explains the designation as Kufr linguistically as denying and concealing a right that is owed. As a further possibility he names actual Kufr in the case of Istiḥlāl. Thus the wording is expressly differentiated even in the early Šarḥ and is not an automatic judgment of Kufr akbar from the deed alone.

HAD-2717.text: Whichever slave flees, the Ḏimmah has disavowed itself from him.
HAD-2717.narrator: Ǧarīr ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2717.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2717.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ first explains «Ḏimmah» as covenant or obligation and cites several interpretations for the wording, among them the loss of a relationship of protection and guarantee. The statement is a grave warning in the historical legal context; the early Šarḥ itself does not restrict it to only a single interpretation.

HAD-2718.text: When the slave flees, his prayer is not accepted.
HAD-2718.narrator: Ǧarīr ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2718.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2718.sharh: Al-Māzirī names several possibilities for «his prayer is not accepted». One concerns the case of Istiḥlāl; another connects the threat with the fugitive persisting in the forbidden remaining away. The wording is therefore not set forth without differentiation as a general judgment on the validity of every single prayer.

HAD-2719.text: Whoever says: «We received rain through Allah’s favor and mercy» believes in Me and rejects the attribution to the star.
HAD-2719.narrator: Zayd ibn Ḫālid al-Ǧuhanī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2719.speaker: Allah said, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reported:
HAD-2719.sharh: The correct attribution traces the rain back to Allah’s favor and mercy. Al-Māzirī distinguishes from this the notion that a star creates or causes the rain independently; precisely this causal attribution is the central point of the Kufr warning in the chapter.

HAD-2720.text: Whoever says: «We received rain through such-and-such a star» denies Me and believes in the star.
HAD-2720.narrator: Zayd ibn Ḫālid al-Ǧuhanī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2720.speaker: Allah said, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reported:
HAD-2720.sharh: Al-Māzirī relates the actual Kufr warning to the belief that the star creates or causes the rain instead of Allah. Whoever, by contrast, acknowledges Allah alone as Creator and understands a stellar position merely as a temporal sign is distinguished from this in the early explanation. The mere wording must therefore not be equated blanket-wise without examining the intended attribution.

HAD-2721.text: Allah grants His servants no gift without a group of them becoming ungrateful toward it.
HAD-2721.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2721.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported from Allah تعالى:
HAD-2721.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the Kufr mentioned here can designate the denial or the ingratitude toward the gift, when it is not attributed to Allah and He is not thanked for it.

HAD-2722.text: They say about the gift of the rain: «The stars — and through the stars.»
HAD-2722.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2722.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported from Allah تعالى:
HAD-2722.sharh: The reprehensible attribution consists in ascribing the rain to a heavenly body as an independently acting cause or creator. Whoever acknowledges Allah alone as Creator and designates only a time or a sign does not fall under the same verdict of faith.

HAD-2723.text: Allah sends down rain; thereafter a group of the people attributes it to this or that star.
HAD-2723.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2723.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2723.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ makes clear that the assessment of faith depends on the intended attribution: Allah is the Creator of the rain; an independent efficacy of the stars is rejected.

HAD-2724.text: After the rain some people became grateful and others ungrateful.
HAD-2724.narrator: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2724.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-2724.sharh: The juxtaposition of «grateful» and «kāfir» shows here Kufr toward the gift: the Niʿmah is not attributed to its Giver and the due thanks fail to appear.

HAD-2725.text: The grateful said about the rain: «This is Allah’s mercy.»
HAD-2725.narrator: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2725.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-2725.sharh: The correct attitude connects the gift with Allah, acknowledges His mercy, and thanks Him. Thereby the Niʿmah is attributed to its real Giver.

HAD-2366.text: Paradise is surrounded by things that weigh heavily on the soul.
HAD-2366.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2366.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2366.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the path to Paradise often leads through things that weigh heavily on the nafs: patience in obedience, refraining from forbidden desires, and steadfastness in trials. The difficulty does not lie in Paradise itself, but in the duties and efforts on the way there.

HAD-2367.text: The Fire is surrounded by desires.
HAD-2367.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2367.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2367.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that many paths to the Fire appear attractive through unrestrained desires. The Ḥadīṯ therefore warns against merely following the immediate wish of the nafs without examining it by the standard of revelation.

HAD-2368.text: Whoever loves the meeting with Allah, Allah loves his meeting.
HAD-2368.narrator: ʿUbādah ibn aṣ-Ṣāmit رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2368.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2368.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the love of meeting Allah in connection with the moment when the believing servant is given tidings of Allah's pleasure and the coming honor. Then what lies before him becomes beloved to him, and he longs for the meeting with his Lord.

HAD-2369.text: Whoever detests the meeting with Allah, Allah detests his meeting.
HAD-2369.narrator: ʿUbādah ibn aṣ-Ṣāmit رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2369.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2369.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the opposite side by the one who, at death, is given tidings of punishment and harm. Because he fears and detests what is coming, he detests the meeting; the Ḥadīṯ thereby describes the state at the passage into the Hereafter.

HAD-2370.text: What is meant is not the natural aversion to death. When the believer, at his death, is given tidings of Allah's pleasure and honor, nothing is dearer to him than what lies before him.
HAD-2370.narrator: ʿUbādah ibn aṣ-Ṣāmit رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2370.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ explained:
HAD-2370.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl expressly explains that the Ḥadīṯ does not blame the inborn wariness of death. What is decisive is the state after the message about what is coming: the believer then loves the meeting with Allah because of the announced grace.

HAD-2371.text: O Allah, set right for me my religion, which is the safeguard of my affairs.
HAD-2371.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2371.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-2371.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the Prophet ﷺ begins with religion because its state decides the salvation of the person. Religion protects and orders his affairs; setting it right includes sincerity, obedience, and steadfastness.

HAD-2372.text: O Allah, set right for me my world, in which is my livelihood.
HAD-2372.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2372.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-2372.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ does not understand the request as love of the world for its own sake. What is meant is an ordered, lawful basis of life that supports the servant in obedience and preserves him from forbidden means.

HAD-2373.text: O Allah, set right for me my Hereafter, to which is my return.
HAD-2373.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2373.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-2373.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the setting right of the Āḫirah as a request for righteous deeds, a good end, and salvation after death. The Ḥadīṯ thereby joins religion, the world, and the Hereafter in an ordered Duʿāʾ.

HAD-2374.text: Make life for me an increase in every good.
HAD-2374.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2374.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-2374.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that a longer life is a good when it opens to the servant additional opportunities for obedience, repentance, and good deeds. The request is therefore directed not merely toward prolonging life, but toward an increase of good.

HAD-2375.text: Make death for me a rest from every evil.
HAD-2375.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2375.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-2375.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that death, after a good end, can be for the believing servant a deliverance from the evils, trials, and opportunities for sin of this world. The request is bound to a righteous end, not to a longing for death out of mere distress.

HAD-2376.text: This world is sweet and green.
HAD-2376.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2376.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2376.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the image of the sweet, green world as a pointer to its attraction for the eye and the soul. Precisely its beauty makes it a trial, because a person is easily taken in by it.

HAD-2377.text: Allah sets you in it one after another and watches how you act.
HAD-2377.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2377.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2377.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains succession in the world as a trial of responsibility. Generations succeed one another, and what is decisive is not possession in itself, but how the servant acts with what is entrusted to him.

HAD-2378.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2378.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2378.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ understands the warning not as a prohibition of lawful worldly means, but as protection from delusion, excess, and the loss of the Hereafter through the attraction of the world.

HAD-2379.text: And beware of the Fitnah of women; for the first Fitnah of the Banū Isrāʾīl was with regard to women.
HAD-2379.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2379.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2379.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the special mention as a warning against a strong worldly temptation. What is meant is protection from unlawful desire, blameworthy transgression of limits, and situations that turn a person away from his religious duty.

HAD-2380.text: A man had killed ninety-nine people and asked for the most knowledgeable person on earth.
HAD-2380.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2380.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-2380.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ emphasizes that even a perpetrator of enormous sins can seek the door of Tawbah. That the man specifically asks for the most knowledgeable shows the necessity of returning, in grave religious questions, to real knowledge.

HAD-2381.text: He was directed to a monk. When this one said that there was no Tawbah for him, he killed him and completed one hundred.
HAD-2381.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2381.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-2381.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ makes clear how dangerous an answer without sufficient knowledge can be. The monk was known for piety, but he was not the suitable scholar for this legal question; his false message of despair made the situation worse.

HAD-2382.text: Then he asked again for the most knowledgeable person and was directed to a scholar. This one said: Who could stand between you and Tawbah?
HAD-2382.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2382.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-2382.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains in this the breadth of Tawbah: even very great sins do not exclude the possibility of a sincere return to Allah. The scholar therefore answers the question with knowledge and opens the door of hope, without denying the gravity of the deed.

HAD-2383.text: The scholar instructed him to leave his bad land and to go to a land in which people serve Allah.
HAD-2383.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2383.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-2383.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the change of place as part of genuine Tawbah: the man was to leave the surroundings that could draw him back to sin, and to join a righteous community. Tawbah therefore also includes removing the causes of relapse.

HAD-2384.text: On the way to the land of the righteous people, death overtook him.
HAD-2384.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2384.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-2384.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ stresses that the man had not yet reached the righteous surroundings he sought. His sincere intention and his actual setting out show, however, that his Tawbah did not remain a mere claim, but turned into action.

HAD-2385.text: The angels of mercy and the angels of punishment disputed over who should receive him.
HAD-2385.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2385.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-2385.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the dispute of the angels by the two visible sides of his state: a past full of grave sins and a present sincere movement toward Tawbah. The outcome shows the importance of his actual will to repent.

HAD-2506.text: People associate partners with Allah and attribute a child to Him; yet He grants them health and provision.
HAD-2506.narrator: Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2506.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2506.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ highlights Allah’s extraordinary forbearance: even toward people who assert the gravest untruth about Him, He continues worldly provision and well-being. This is no sign of His pleasure in their belief, but of His Ḥilm.

HAD-2507.text: To the person with the lightest punishment in the Fire it is said: If everything on earth belonged to you, would you ransom yourself with it? He says: Yes.
HAD-2507.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2507.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2507.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the scene as a depiction of the despair of the one punished: in the face of the punishment, every conceivable worldly possession would be worthless to him if only he could save himself with it.

HAD-2508.text: Allah says to him: I asked of you something far easier than that: that you associate nothing with Me.
HAD-2508.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2508.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2508.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the Ḥadīṯ brings out the central importance of Tawḥīd. The foundation demanded was not material effort, but exclusive ʿIbādah for Allah without Širk.

HAD-2509.text: But he refused this easier demand and persisted in Širk.
HAD-2509.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2509.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2509.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the closing statement as a warning against Širk: despite the simple and fundamental demand of Tawḥīd, the person concerned chose association. The scene makes clear the gravity of this offense.

HAD-2510.text: On the Day of Resurrection, the person with the most pleasant life among the people of the Fire is dipped once into the Fire.
HAD-2510.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2510.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2510.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that even a single moment of the otherworldly punishment makes every earlier worldly comfort appear meaningless. The Ḥadīṯ thereby puts the value of passing ease of life into proportion.

HAD-2511.text: Then he is asked: Did you ever experience anything good or any enjoyment? He says: No, by Allah, my Lord.
HAD-2511.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2511.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2511.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the answer as an expression of the overwhelming effect of the otherworldly punishment. Beside it, even an entire life full of worldly comforts loses its weight.

HAD-2512.text: And the person with the hardest life among the people of Paradise is dipped once into Paradise.
HAD-2512.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2512.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2512.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the other side of the parable: already the first immediate enjoyment of Paradise makes the hardships of the entire worldly life fade.

HAD-2513.text: Then he is asked: Did you ever experience need or hardship? He says: No, by Allah, my Lord; I never experienced need and I never saw hardship.
HAD-2513.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2513.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2513.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the perfection of otherworldly happiness completely surpasses the memory of worldly distress. The Ḥadīṯ strengthens patience and hope amid passing trials.

HAD-2514.text: Allah lets no good deed of the believer go lost.
HAD-2514.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2514.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2514.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the statement as evidence of Allah’s perfect justice: no good deed of the believer is diminished or passed over.

HAD-2515.text: The believer receives good in this world for his good deeds and is rewarded for them in the Hereafter.
HAD-2515.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2515.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2515.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that Allah can give the believer, from one good deed, both worldly benefit and otherworldly reward. The kind of worldly benefit lies in Allah’s wisdom.

HAD-2516.text: The Kāfir may be given something in this world for good deeds; in the Hereafter, however, he has no good deed for them by which he is rewarded.
HAD-2516.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2516.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2516.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that worldly recompense for individual good deeds must not be equated with otherworldly acceptance. For the otherworldly reward, Īmān is the fundamental condition.

HAD-2517.text: The parable of the believer is like a young, pliant plant: the winds bend it at times and set it upright again, until its end comes.
HAD-2517.narrator: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2517.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2517.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the parable as an image of the believer’s trials: he is moved and tested by distresses, yet he remains standing through Īmān and return to Allah until his appointed lifetime ends.

HAD-2518.text: The parable of the hypocrite is like a rigid tree that remains standing until it is all at once completely uprooted.
HAD-2518.narrator: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2518.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2518.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the rigid tree as a contrasting image: the hypocrite does not receive the same purifying consequence of ongoing trials; then his end can come suddenly and completely.

HAD-2519.text: Among the trees there is a tree whose leaves do not fall and whose likeness resembles the Muslim.
HAD-2519.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2519.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2519.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the parable through lasting usefulness: the Muslim should, like this tree, bring forth benefit, constancy, and good fruit in various states.

HAD-2520.text: The Prophet ﷺ explained: It is the date palm.
HAD-2520.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2520.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2520.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the date palm as an especially fitting parable for the Muslim: it is constant, useful, and brings forth manifold benefit. The scene also shows the permitted use of riddles and parables in teaching.

HAD-2521.text: The Šayṭān has given up hope that those who pray on the Arabian Peninsula will worship him as a deity.
HAD-2521.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2521.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2521.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the Šayṭān no longer expects the return of the entire praying community of the Arabian Peninsula to his worship. The Ḥadīṯ does not mean that individual people could never fall into Širk.

HAD-2522.text: Yet he continues to strive to sow discord and enmity among them.
HAD-2522.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2522.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2522.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains at-taḥrīš as incitement against one another: dispute, hatred, enmity, and Fitnah remain central paths of the Šayṭān, even when he does not attain his greater aim.

HAD-2523.text: Iblīs sets his throne upon the water.
HAD-2523.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2523.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2523.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats the statement as an authentic report about Iblīs and his order. It belongs to the matters of the unseen that are affirmed on the basis of the Ṣaḥīḥ transmission.

HAD-2524.text: Then Iblīs sends out his troops to lead the people into temptation.
HAD-2524.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2524.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2524.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the dispatched troops as helpers of the Šayṭān in various forms of seduction. The Ḥadīṯ describes an organized effort toward Fitnah and sin.

HAD-2525.text: The one among them who causes the greatest Fitnah stands nearest to Iblīs.
HAD-2525.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2525.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2525.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that rank with Iblīs is measured by the extent of the corruption caused. The greater the harm to religion and relationships, the greater his recognition.

HAD-2606.text: Shall I tell you what al-ʿAḍh is? It is Namīmah: the carrying onward of speech between people.
HAD-2606.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2606.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2606.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains Namīmah as the carrying of statements with the result or the intention of spoiling relationships and sowing discord. The Ḥadīṯ makes clear that harmful retelling is not merely social awkwardness.

HAD-2607.text: A person speaks the truth until he is written with Allah as a truthful one.
HAD-2607.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2607.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2607.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that repeated truthfulness becomes a fixed quality of the person. Lasting Ṣidq shapes character and religious rank until the servant is marked as especially truthful.

HAD-2608.text: A person lies until he is written with Allah as a liar.
HAD-2608.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2608.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2608.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that repeated lying shapes the character until Kiḏb becomes a fixed quality. The Ḥadīṯ thereby warns against gradually accustoming the tongue to untruth.

HAD-2609.text: The strong one is not the one who defeats others in wrestling.
HAD-2609.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2609.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2609.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that bodily superiority is not the highest form of strength. The Ḥadīṯ shifts the measure from outward force to mastery of one's own nafs in the moment of strong agitation.

HAD-2610.text: The truly strong one is the one who controls himself when he is angry.
HAD-2610.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2610.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2610.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains self-control in anger as true strength, because the person then struggles precisely against a strong inner impulse. Control here does not mean denying anger, but preventing unjust words and deeds.

HAD-2611.text: I know a word; if he were to say it, that would depart from him.
HAD-2611.narrator: Sulaymān ibn Ṣurad رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2611.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2611.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the Prophet ﷺ names for the visibly angry man a concrete means against the influence of Šayṭān. The Ḥadīṯ thereby joins inner self-control with immediate Ḏikr and Istiʿāḏah.

HAD-2612.text: I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Šayṭān.
HAD-2612.narrator: Sulaymān ibn Ṣurad رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2612.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2612.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the Istiʿāḏah as a prophetic means against whispering that arises from anger. The servant turns thereby to Allah, instead of following the first impulse of anger.

HAD-2613.text: Beware of unfounded suspicion; for suspicion is the most deceptive speech.
HAD-2613.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2613.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2613.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ understands the forbidden ẓann as an unfounded negative assumption about others for which no solid proof is present. Such suspicion becomes a source of false judgments and poisons relationships.

HAD-2614.text: Do not search into the hidden matters of others.
HAD-2614.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2614.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2614.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains taḥassus as deliberate inquiry into the private or hidden affairs of others. The Ḥadīṯ thereby protects the personal sphere from curious and harmful investigation.

HAD-2615.text: Do not spy on one another.
HAD-2615.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2615.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2615.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains taǧassus as the active search for hidden faults and secrets. The distinction of the terms strengthens the general prohibition of spying on the Muslim without right.

HAD-2616.text: Do not compete against one another in a way that produces enmity and ill will.
HAD-2616.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2616.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2616.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that not every striving is blameworthy; what is blamed is the competitive pursuit that sets hearts against one another and leads to envy, unfair advantage, or enmity.

HAD-2617.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2617.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2617.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains ḥasad as ill will toward a gift that Allah has granted to another. The Ḥadīṯ thereby forbids a state of the heart that damages brotherhood and contentment with Allah's decree.

HAD-2618.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2618.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2618.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ understands the prohibition as protection from groundless or sinful mutual enmity. Religiously grounded rejection of a forbidden act is to be distinguished from this; the Ḥadīṯ is directed against personal relationships of hatred.

HAD-2619.text: Do not turn your backs on one another and do not break off the relationships.
HAD-2619.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2619.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2619.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains tadābur as mutual turning away that makes enmity visible and tears relationships apart. The Ḥadīṯ requires that such personal ruptures not become a lasting state.

HAD-2620.text: Be servants of Allah as brothers.
HAD-2620.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2620.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2620.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the instruction of brotherhood as the aim of the preceding prohibitions. Suspicion, spying, envy, and enmity are forbidden because they destroy the bond of the believers that Allah requires.

HAD-2621.text: On the Day of Resurrection you will give the rights back to their owners in full.
HAD-2621.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2621.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2621.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the statement as a comprehensive warning against injustice: no right of another is lost. On the Day of Resurrection settlement is made, even if a claim seemed small or unnoticed in this world.

HAD-2622.text: Even for the hornless sheep, requital is taken from the horned sheep.
HAD-2622.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2622.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2622.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the example as an especially strong proof of the perfection of divine justice. When settlement is shown even among animals, the warning to people against violating the rights of others is all the more pressing.

HAD-2623.text: Let him enter; what a bad man of his tribe.
HAD-2623.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said about a man who asked for admission:
HAD-2623.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that naming a known harmful character can be permissible when warning is thereby given or a justified benefit is reached. It is not to be equated with forbidden backbiting when a legitimate warning is necessary.

HAD-2624.text: Among the people with the worst standing with Allah on the Day of Resurrection is the one whom people avoid out of fear of his wounding speech.
HAD-2624.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2624.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that people may avoid someone out of fear of his bad conduct without this raising his standing. The very fact that others must protect themselves from his tongue is a severe warning about character.

HAD-2625.text: Whoever is denied gentleness is denied the good.
HAD-2625.narrator: Ǧarīr ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2625.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2625.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains Rifq as mildness, composure, and the avoidance of needless harshness. Because many good results are reached only through calm and fitting action, the loss of Rifq means the loss of large parts of the good.

HAD-2646.text: People are like mines of silver and gold.
HAD-2646.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2646.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2646.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains people as differing original dispositions and qualities, comparable to mines of differing value. From these dispositions different character traits emerge.

HAD-2647.text: The best of them in the Ǧāhiliyyah are the best of them in Islam, when they attain understanding in the religion.
HAD-2647.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2647.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2647.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that praiseworthy natural qualities receive, through Islam and Fiqh, their proper measure and their complete direction. Origin or former standing alone does not suffice; what is decisive is understanding of the religion.

HAD-2648.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2648.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2648.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains “assembled armies” as groups and kinds with differing qualities. The Ḥadīṯ describes differences and agreements among the souls, without removing individual responsibility.

HAD-2649.text: Those of the souls that recognize one another and agree find one another.
HAD-2649.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2649.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2649.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ offers as a near explanation that agreement of qualities and character dispositions can lead to affection and familiarity. Similar traits find one another more readily.

HAD-2650.text: Those of the souls that are strange to one another and do not agree go apart.
HAD-2650.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2650.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2650.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that opposing qualities and character traits can lead to distance and a lack of familiarity. The text describes an observable effect of differing dispositions.

HAD-2651.text: The creation of one of you is gathered in his mother's womb for forty days.
HAD-2651.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2651.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2651.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl treats the Ḥadīṯ as evidence for the staged creation of the human being and for the prior divine decree. The wording is taken as a report about a hidden matter, without extending it beyond the text.

HAD-2652.text: Then he is in it a ʿAlaqah in a corresponding manner.
HAD-2652.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2652.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2652.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl places the ʿAlaqah as one of the stages of development named in the Ḥadīṯ. The statement remains bound to the transmitted wording and is not replaced by later speculations.

HAD-2653.text: Then he is in it a Muḍġah in a corresponding manner.
HAD-2653.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2653.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2653.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl cites the Muḍġah as a further one of the stages named in the text. The emphasis of the Ḥadīṯ then lies on the work of the angel and on the written decree.

HAD-2654.text: Then the angel is sent and breathes the soul into him.
HAD-2654.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2654.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2654.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl treats the sending of the angel and the breathing in of the soul as part of the hidden events that the Prophet ﷺ conveyed through revelation. The text shows the connection between creation and the divine decree.

HAD-2655.text: The angel is commanded to write down the person's Rizq.
HAD-2655.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2655.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2655.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl cites the written Rizq as part of the Qadar. That it is written does not remove the person's duty to take lawful means for earning; the writing belongs to the prior knowledge and to the decree of Allah.

HAD-2656.text: The angel is commanded to write down the person's term of life.
HAD-2656.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2656.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2656.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl places the written term of life under the Qadar. The servant does not know his fixed term and therefore remains obliged to use his time in obedience and to take lawful means to preserve life.

HAD-2657.text: The angel is commanded to write down the person's deeds.
HAD-2657.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2657.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2657.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl treats the writing of the deeds as part of the prior divine decree. This does not remove the servant's responsibility; rather, the Ḥadīṯ joins the Qadar with the person's later actual deed.

HAD-2658.text: The angel is commanded to write down whether the person will be wretched or happy.
HAD-2658.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2658.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2658.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl understands Šaqāwah and Saʿādah as part of the written Qadar. The text is not meant to lead the servant into inactivity, but to fear, hope, and holding to the revealed paths of obedience.

HAD-2659.text: A person may perform the deeds of the people of Paradise until only an ell remains between him and it; then what was written overtakes him, and he performs the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters there.
HAD-2659.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2659.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2659.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the statement as a warning against relying on the visible state so far. What decides is the end; the servant should therefore constantly ask for steadfastness and not feel secure in his own deeds.

HAD-2660.text: A person may perform the deeds of the people of the Fire until only an ell remains between him and it; then what was written overtakes him, and he performs the deeds of the people of Paradise and enters there.
HAD-2660.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2660.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2660.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the other side as an opening of hope: a person's earlier outward state does not decide his end on its own. Tawbah, guidance, and a good end remain of central importance until the close.

HAD-2661.text: What of a person who performs a good deed and is praised by people for it?
HAD-2661.narrator: Abū Ḏarr al-Ġifārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2661.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ was asked:
HAD-2661.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that unplanned praise for a good deed performed sincerely is not equated with Riyāʾ. What is decisive is that the deed was originally performed for Allah and not in order to obtain people's praise.

HAD-2662.text: That is the advance glad tiding for the believer.
HAD-2662.narrator: Abū Ḏarr al-Ġifārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2662.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2662.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ understands a good standing among people that was not sought as a possible early glad tiding of the acceptance of a righteous deed. It replaces neither sincerity nor the final reckoning in the Hereafter.

HAD-2663.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2663.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2663.sharh: Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr explains the statement as a comprehensive evidence for the Qadar: nothing falls outside the prior knowledge, the decree, and the will of Allah. At the same time, command, prohibition, and human responsibility remain.

HAD-2664.text: Even incapacity and competence occur according to Qadar.
HAD-2664.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2664.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2664.sharh: Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr explains that human ability, prudence, and their opposite also do not lie outside the Qadar. The Ḥadīṯ does not thereby take from the person the charge to act; it places his abilities too under the decree of Allah.

HAD-2665.text: Every newborn is born upon the Fiṭrah.
HAD-2665.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2665.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2665.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the Fiṭrah as the original state upon which the child is created, before external influences and conscious decisions come in. The Ḥadīṯ thereby brings out the original creational disposition.

HAD-2386.text: When it was measured, he was closer to the land of the righteous people; thus he was forgiven.
HAD-2386.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2386.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-2386.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the outcome as evidence for the acceptance of sincere Tawbah even after extraordinarily grave sins. What was decisive was that the man actually turned away from his former surroundings and his former path and sought Allah.

HAD-2387.text: The believer sees his sins as though he were sitting beneath a mountain and feared that it would fall upon him.
HAD-2387.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-2387.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-2387.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl understands the statement as a mark of living fear of Allah: the believer does not belittle his sins, but views them in the light of Allah's greatness and fears their consequences. This attitude drives him to Tawbah and correction.

HAD-2388.text: The wrongdoer sees his sins like a fly that flies past his nose.
HAD-2388.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-2388.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-2388.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the contrast as a warning against belittling sin. The wrongdoer attaches hardly any weight to his transgression; precisely this indifference more easily prevents him from sincere repentance.

HAD-2389.text: Allah rejoices more over the Tawbah of His believing servant than a man who, in a deadly wilderness, finds again his lost mount together with food and water.
HAD-2389.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2389.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2389.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the parable as an extraordinary encouragement to Tawbah. The Ḥadīṯ describes, with a maximally understandable human image of joy, how greatly Allah loves the return of His servant, without equating Allah's attribute with created joy.

HAD-2390.text: The son of Adam says: My wealth, my wealth.
HAD-2390.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn aš-Šiḫḫīr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2390.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2390.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ understands the statement as a criticism of the deception through possession. The human being calls wealth «mine», although his actual benefit from it is limited and a large part passes to others after his death.

HAD-2391.text: Of your wealth, only what you have eaten and consumed truly belongs to you.
HAD-2391.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn aš-Šiḫḫīr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2391.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2391.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the immediately consumed portion of the wealth has already fulfilled its worldly benefit. Possession that is merely accumulated, by contrast, does not remain permanently with the human being.

HAD-2392.text: Or what you have worn and worn out.
HAD-2392.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn aš-Šiḫḫīr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2392.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2392.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ places clothing among the passing immediate benefits of possession: it is used and perishes. The Ḥadīṯ thereby relativizes the notion of lasting ownership.

HAD-2393.text: Or what you have given as Ṣadaqah and thereby sent ahead for your Hereafter.
HAD-2393.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn aš-Šiḫḫīr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2393.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2393.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains this portion as the lasting benefit of wealth: what is spent sincerely for Allah does outwardly leave the servant's possession, yet remains for him as reward for the Āḫirah.

HAD-2394.text: Three things follow the deceased: his family, his wealth, and his deeds.
HAD-2394.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2394.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2394.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the three companions as a vivid summary of the passage from this world to the next. Family and possession belong to the worldly surroundings; the deeds, by contrast, are directly bound to the servant's responsibility.

HAD-2395.text: Two return and one remains: family and wealth return, his deeds remain with him.
HAD-2395.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2395.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2395.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the concluding statement as a call to give priority to the companion who remains. Family and possession end at the grave as immediate companions; good or bad deeds, by contrast, remain the basis of what awaits the servant thereafter.

HAD-2396.text: O Allah, I ask You for right guidance.
HAD-2396.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2396.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-2396.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ understands al-Hudā as a request for guidance to the right path, firmness upon it, and protection from error. The Duʿāʾ begins with this, because right guidance is the basis of the other good states.

HAD-2397.text: O Allah, I ask You for Taqwā.
HAD-2397.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2397.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-2397.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains Taqwā as guarding against Allah's displeasure through obedience and avoiding the forbidden. The request joins outward actions with inward fear of Allah.

HAD-2398.text: O Allah, I ask You for chastity.
HAD-2398.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2398.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-2398.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains al-ʿAfāf as restraint from the forbidden and from shameful desire. The request especially includes guarding desire, the tongue, and conduct from what is unlawful.

HAD-2399.text: O Allah, I ask You for contentment.
HAD-2399.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2399.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-2399.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ understands al-Ġinā here as contentment and independence of the heart from what is with people. What is meant is not mere possession, but inner satisfaction with Allah's provision.

HAD-2400.text: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the disappearance of Your favor.
HAD-2400.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2400.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-2400.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the request as protection against granted favors being withdrawn because of sin, ingratitude, or trial. It teaches the servant not to regard favor as a matter of course.

HAD-2401.text: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the change of Your granted health and well-being.
HAD-2401.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2401.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-2401.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ understands the change of the ʿĀfiyah as a passage from protection and well-being to illness, distress, or another trial. The Duʿāʾ joins gratitude with a request for the continuance of the good.

HAD-2402.text: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the sudden arrival of Your punishment.
HAD-2402.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2402.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-2402.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the suddenness as an arrival without preceding warning signs. The request teaches fear of an unexpected reversal and constant need of Allah's protection.

HAD-2403.text: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from all Your wrath.
HAD-2403.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2403.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-2403.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the concluding request as a comprehensive refuge from everything that brings Allah's displeasure. It gathers the previous specific requests for protection into one general request.

HAD-2404.text: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from incapacity.
HAD-2404.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2404.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-2404.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains ʿaǧz as the lack of ability to carry out a required action. Seeking refuge from it includes protection from states that hinder the servant in duties, earning, and good works.

HAD-2405.text: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from sluggishness.
HAD-2405.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2405.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
HAD-2405.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains kasal as a lack of inner drive toward the good, although the ability is present. Seeking refuge from it protects against postponing duties and missing good opportunities.

HAD-2446.text: No Muslim servant asks for his brother in his absence without his Duʿāʾ being especially accepted.
HAD-2446.narrator: Abū ad-Dardāʾ رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2446.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2446.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the special excellence of the Duʿāʾ for an absent brother by its greater nearness to sincerity. Since the one benefited does not hear the request, it is further removed from flattery and recompense.

HAD-2447.text: The commissioned angel says thereupon: Āmīn – and for you the same.
HAD-2447.narrator: Abū ad-Dardāʾ رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2447.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2447.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the one who asks is favored twice through his selfless Duʿāʾ: the angel confirms the request with Āmīn and at the same time asks for the one who supplicates the same good.

HAD-2448.text: One of you is answered so long as he does not become impatient.
HAD-2448.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2448.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2448.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that constancy in the Duʿāʾ is itself ʿIbādah. Impatience means breaking off the request, because the servant expects the answer according to his own measure of time.

HAD-2449.text: The servant's Duʿāʾ remains under the promise of being answered so long as he does not ask for a sin or for the severing of ties of kinship.
HAD-2449.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2449.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2449.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that a request for something sinful or for the destruction of kinship that is rightfully protected is not a permitted aim of Duʿāʾ. The promise of being answered refers to lawful requests.

HAD-2450.text: He says: I have called upon my Lord again and again, but He has not answered me.
HAD-2450.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2450.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ explained impatience:
HAD-2450.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains impatience as an inner displeasure that the answer does not become visible at once. The servant should not limit Allah by his own measure of time, nor belittle the Duʿāʾ because an immediate effect is absent.

HAD-2451.text: Then he becomes disappointed, abandons the Duʿāʾ and ceases to ask.
HAD-2451.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2451.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2451.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ makes clear that the real problem is not merely a passing feeling, but the breaking off of the Duʿāʾ that follows from it. Steadfastness and a good expectation of Allah therefore belong to the Adab of asking.

HAD-2452.text: I stood at the gate of Paradise and saw that most of those who had entered were poor.
HAD-2452.narrator: Usāmah ibn Zayd رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2452.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2452.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the statement as an indication of the excellence of many of the needy, who can enter earlier because of fewer worldly attachments and a shorter reckoning of wealth. Poverty in itself, however, guarantees no salvation; what remains decisive is Īmān and obedience.

HAD-2453.text: The owners of great wealth were held back – except those for whom the Fire had already been decreed.
HAD-2453.narrator: Usāmah ibn Zayd رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2453.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2453.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the delay of the wealthy by the additional reckoning of how they acquired and used their wealth. Possession is thereby a responsibility; the Ḥadīṯ does not blame lawful wealth as such.

HAD-2454.text: I stood at the gate of the Fire and saw that many of its inhabitants were women.
HAD-2454.narrator: Usāmah ibn Zayd رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2454.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2454.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ places the report together with other prophetic warnings in which specific sins and modes of conduct are addressed. The statement is therefore an admonition to Tawbah and to obedience, not a devaluation of the female sex.

HAD-2455.text: I have left behind me no Fitnah more harmful to men than the Fitnah of women.
HAD-2455.narrator: Usāmah ibn Zayd رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2455.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2455.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ understands the statement as a warning against unlawful desire and the religious consequences that can arise from it. The Ḥadīṯ does not blame women as a sex, but warns against a strong form of worldly temptation.

HAD-2456.text: Three men from earlier peoples sought shelter at night in a cave; a boulder fell and closed the way out upon them.
HAD-2456.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2456.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-2456.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the account as evidence for the permissibility of calling upon Allah in distress while mentioning righteous deeds performed with sincerity. The distress at the same time makes visible that Allah alone can open the way out.

HAD-2457.text: The first man mentioned his special obedience toward his elderly parents: he gave them their evening milk before his family, even while his children waited hungry.
HAD-2457.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2457.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-2457.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ highlights the exceptional Birr toward the parents. Out of sincere fear of Allah the man placed their customary right before his own immediate wishes and made precisely this hidden sincerity the subject of his Duʿāʾ.

HAD-2458.text: The second man had the opportunity for a forbidden relationship with a woman whom he greatly desired; when she reminded him of Allah, he refrained from her out of fear of Allah.
HAD-2458.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2458.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-2458.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the deed as a strong example of sincere Taqwā: the man left a desired sin in a moment of real opportunity solely out of fear of Allah. Precisely the refraining while the ability was present makes the deed especially weighty.

HAD-2459.text: The third man preserved a worker's wage, increased it in trust and later returned to him the entire property that had arisen from it.
HAD-2459.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2459.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-2459.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ highlights Amānah and the complete safeguarding of another's rights. The man did not use the abandoned payment for himself, but preserved its economic value and later handed everything to the owner without deduction.

HAD-2460.text: Each of the three asked Allah by his deed performed with sincerity; the rock moved aside piece by piece until they could leave the cave.
HAD-2460.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2460.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-2460.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the outcome as evidence for the benefit of sincere deeds in the utmost distress and for Allah's answering of the Duʿāʾ. What was decisive was not the mere recounting of the deeds, but their sincerity for Allah.

HAD-2461.text: Ḥanẓalah said to Abū Bakr رضي الله عنه: «Ḥanẓalah has become a hypocrite.»
HAD-2461.narrator: Ḥanẓalah al-Usaydī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2461.speaker: Ḥanẓalah رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-2461.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that Ḥanẓalah did not attribute actual nifāq to himself, but out of strong fear of Allah feared the change of his inner state between the prophetic gathering and daily life. His statement shows self-examination, not a confirmed diagnosis of hypocrisy.

HAD-2462.text: When we are with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he reminds us of the Fire and Paradise, it is as if we see them with our own eyes.
HAD-2462.narrator: Ḥanẓalah al-Usaydī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2462.speaker: Ḥanẓalah رضي الله عنه explained:
HAD-2462.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the strong presence of the Āḫirah in the prophetic admonition as the effect of intense Ḏikr and living certainty. The statement describes an especially high state of attentiveness and fear.

HAD-2463.text: When we then go away and occupy ourselves with wives, children and possessions, we forget much of that.
HAD-2463.narrator: Ḥanẓalah al-Usaydī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2463.speaker: Ḥanẓalah رضي الله عنه explained:
HAD-2463.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the change as part of human nature: lawful everyday tasks take up attention, and the exceptional state of the admonition does not remain constantly equally strong. That is not automatically nifāq.

HAD-2464.text: If you remained constantly in the state in which you are with me and in Ḏikr, the angels would extend their hands to you upon your beds and upon your paths.
HAD-2464.narrator: Ḥanẓalah al-Usaydī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2464.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2464.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that a permanently equally high state of Ḏikr and inner presence would be exceptional. The statement shows the excellence of this state without declaring it the constantly attainable normal state of every person.

HAD-2465.text: But, O Ḥanẓalah: a time for this and a time for that – and he said it three times.
HAD-2465.narrator: Ḥanẓalah al-Usaydī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2465.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2465.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the wording as a recognition of a natural fluctuation between intense Ḏikr and lawful worldly occupations. It is not a permission to allow sin at times; rather, it places legitimate needs of daily life alongside times of special spiritual gathering.

HAD-2586.text: Allah gives for gentleness what He does not give for harshness and for anything else.
HAD-2586.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2586.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that mildness often leads to results that harshness does not reach. The Ḥadīṯ therefore highlights not only the moral worth of Rifq, but also its special effect and reward.

HAD-2587.text: By Allah, he does not believe. By Allah, he does not believe. By Allah, he does not believe.
HAD-2587.narrator: Abū Šurayḥ al-ʿAdawī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2587.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2587.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the threefold repetition as an especially strong warning. What is meant is not a blanket cancellation of the أصل of Īmān, but the absence of its required completeness in someone who does not protect his neighbor from his harm.

HAD-2588.text: What is meant is the one whose neighbor is not safe from his harm.
HAD-2588.narrator: Abū Šurayḥ al-ʿAdawī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2588.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2588.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains «bawāʾiq» as harms, evils, and aggressions. The Ḥadīṯ links the completeness of Īmān to the neighbor being able to be safe from verbal, physical, and other injury.

HAD-2589.text: For every illness there is a remedy.
HAD-2589.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
