HAD-2589.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2589.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the Ḥadīṯ as confirmation that Allah has created fitting remedies for illnesses. This supports the permission and the recommendation to use lawful medical means.

HAD-2590.text: When the fitting remedy meets the illness, healing takes place by Allah's permission.
HAD-2590.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2590.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2590.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that not every means employed heals automatically: the remedy must fit the illness, and the actual healing remains bound to Allah's permission. The Ḥadīṯ links medical means with Tawakkul.

HAD-2591.text: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should honor his guest.
HAD-2591.narrator: Abū Šurayḥ al-ʿAdawī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2591.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2591.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains hospitality as a visible fruit of Īmān and good character. Honoring includes a kind welcome, fitting entertainment, and refraining from what lowers or shames the guest.

HAD-2592.text: The special honoring of the guest covers one day and one night.
HAD-2592.narrator: Abū Šurayḥ al-ʿAdawī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2592.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2592.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl distinguishes the especially emphasized first period of hospitality from the general hospitality of the following days. The first day and the first night thus have a highlighted claim to a good reception.

HAD-2593.narrator: Abū Šurayḥ al-ʿAdawī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2593.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2593.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the three days as the regular period of the guest's right. The rule protects the guest from neglect and the host from an unlimited burden.

HAD-2594.text: What goes beyond the three days counts for the host as Ṣadaqah.
HAD-2594.narrator: Abū Šurayḥ al-ʿAdawī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2594.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2594.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that further hospitality after the regular guest-right has ended is voluntary good. Additional generosity thus remains expressly rewarded, without being treated as an unlimited duty.

HAD-2595.text: The guest may not stay with the host so long that he puts him into hardship.
HAD-2595.narrator: Abū Šurayḥ al-ʿAdawī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2595.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2595.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains that the guest also has duties: he may not misuse hospitality nor put the host into financial or personal hardship. The Ḥadīṯ therefore orders the rights of both sides.

HAD-2596.text: By Allah, he does not believe! By Allah, he does not believe! By Allah, he does not believe!
HAD-2596.narrator: Abū Šurayḥ رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2596.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2596.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the threefold repetition as an especially strong warning. The statement does not automatically negate the أصل of Īmān in every doer, but shows the severe impairment of his Īmān through the continued harming of the neighbor.

HAD-2597.text: What is meant is the one whose neighbor is not safe from his evil.
HAD-2597.narrator: Abū Šurayḥ رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2597.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2597.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains bawāʾiq as harms and evils from which the neighbor may expect safety. The Ḥadīṯ makes protection of the neighbor a serious measure of religious conduct.

HAD-2598.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ kissed al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī رضي الله عنهما.
HAD-2598.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2598.speaker: He reported about the Prophet ﷺ:
HAD-2598.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains kissing and embracing children as an expression of natural, permitted mercy. The prophetic conduct contradicts a harshness that regards affection toward children as weakness.

HAD-2599.text: Whoever shows no mercy, to him no mercy is shown.
HAD-2599.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2599.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2599.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl understands the statement as a principle of corresponding requital: whoever shows mercy to creatures may hope for mercy; whoever hardens his heart against permitted mercy exposes himself to a severe warning.

HAD-2600.text: A Bedouin said to the Prophet ﷺ: Do you kiss your children? We do not kiss them.
HAD-2600.speaker: She reported:
HAD-2600.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl brings out the contrast between prophetic mercy and unnecessary harshness. Visibly showing affection toward children belongs to good character and to the care of the family bond.

HAD-2601.text: What can I do for you if Allah has taken mercy out of your heart?
HAD-2601.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2601.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl understands the reply as a sharp rebuke of a hardened heart. Lack of mercy toward one's own children is not a sign of strength, but a lack of a basic good quality.

HAD-2602.text: When Allah had created creation, the bond of kinship rose and sought protection from the severing of kinship.
HAD-2602.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2602.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2602.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the personification of the kinship bond as a strong highlighting of its rights. The Ḥadīṯ makes clear that severing family bonds is not a minor social discourtesy, but a grave religious offense.

HAD-2603.text: Are you not content that I maintain the bond with the one who maintains you?
HAD-2603.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2603.speaker: Allah said about the bond of kinship:
HAD-2603.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl explains the promise as a special divine care for the one who upholds his duties of kinship. Ṣilat ar-Raḥim is thereby expressly linked with Allah's own kindness and support.

HAD-2604.text: And that I sever the bond with the one who severs you?
HAD-2604.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2604.speaker: Allah said about the bond of kinship:
HAD-2604.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl understands the threat as a severe warning against deliberately severing kinship. Whoever culpably destroys the family bonds laid upon him thereby exposes himself to the withdrawal of a special divine connection and favor.

HAD-2605.text: If you wish, read: «If you turn away, will you then not spread corruption on the earth and sever your bonds of kinship?»
HAD-2605.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2605.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2605.sharh: Ibn Baṭṭāl links the Ḥadīṯ with the Qurʾān passage about فساد and the severing of kinship. It is thereby shown that qaṭīʿat ar-raḥim belongs to the clearly condemned social and religious harms.

HAD-2686.text: Naṣīḥah applies to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
HAD-2686.narrator: Tamīm ad-Dārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2686.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2686.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains Naṣīḥah toward the Messenger ﷺ as sincere belief in him, acceptance of his message, obedience to his Sunnah, and protection of his station from distortion or belittlement.

HAD-2687.text: Naṣīḥah applies to the leaders of the Muslims.
HAD-2687.narrator: Tamīm ad-Dārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2687.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2687.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains Naṣīḥah toward the leaders of the Muslims as a sincere wish for their right guidance and righteousness, support in obedience to Allah, and honest, fitting counsel without deception or betrayal.

HAD-2688.text: Naṣīḥah applies to the general body of the Muslims.
HAD-2688.narrator: Tamīm ad-Dārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2688.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2688.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains Naṣīḥah toward the Muslims as a sincere wish for their religious and worldly good: to teach them what is good, to protect them from harm, to respect their rights, and to want for them the good that one wants for oneself.

HAD-2689.text: I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to perform the prayer.
HAD-2689.narrator: Ǧarīr ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2689.speaker: Ǧarīr رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-2689.sharh: Al-Māzirī's explanation of the chapter shows that Naṣīḥah is not only an inner attitude, but is joined to the fundamental duties of Islam. Ǧarīr's Bayʿah therefore names first the constant performance of the prayer.

HAD-2690.text: I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to pay the Zakāh.
HAD-2690.narrator: Ǧarīr ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2690.speaker: Ǧarīr رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-2690.sharh: The mention of the Zakāh alongside the prayer shows that the Bayʿah comprises both the rights of Allah and the duties concerning wealth. Sincere practice of the religion therefore includes the proper fulfillment of the obligatory Zakāh.

HAD-2691.text: I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to Naṣīḥah for every Muslim.
HAD-2691.narrator: Ǧarīr ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2691.speaker: Ǧarīr رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-2691.sharh: Al-Māzirī's explanation of Naṣīḥah comprises sincere care without fraud: to wish the Muslim his good, to help him in what is good, to warn him of harm, and not to cheat him of his rights. Ǧarīr's Bayʿah makes this a binding religious attitude.

HAD-2692.text: I pledged allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ to hearing and obeying; he then said to me: as far as you are able to do so – and to Naṣīḥah for every Muslim.
HAD-2692.narrator: Ǧarīr ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2692.speaker: Ǧarīr رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-2692.sharh: The prophetic addition «as far as you are able to do so» binds hearing and obeying to actual ability and accords with the general principle that Allah does not obligate the servant beyond his capacity. At the same time, Naṣīḥah for every Muslim remains part of the Bayʿah.

HAD-2693.text: Four qualities: whoever has all of them bears qualities of complete Nifāq in these actions; whoever has one of them bears a quality of Nifāq until he gives it up.
HAD-2693.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2693.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2693.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains that these traits can occur in a Muslim without the greater Nifāq of faith thereby being present automatically. The Ḥadīṯ warns against adopting conduct that resembles the qualities of the Munāfiqūn; it is especially dangerous when they become a fixed habit.

HAD-2694.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2694.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2694.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains lying as a quality in which the person outwardly shows something other than what is actually present. Precisely this separation of outward presentation and inner truth establishes the resemblance to a quality of Nifāq.

HAD-2695.text: When he enters a covenant, he acts treacherously.
HAD-2695.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2695.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2695.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains betrayal of a covenant as a form of Khiyānah: the person outwardly shows commitment and obligation, yet deliberately violates them. The Ḥadīṯ warns against this likeness of character to the Munāfiqūn and requires truthfulness also in agreements and obligations.

HAD-2696.text: When he promises something, he breaks his promise.
HAD-2696.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2696.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2696.sharh: Breaking a promise belongs to the expressly named qualities of Nifāq. The warning is directed against unreliability that has become deliberate and part of character; from the mere presence of this single quality, Nifāq akbar does not follow automatically.

HAD-2697.text: When he disputes, he departs from the truth and transgresses the bounds.
HAD-2697.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2697.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2697.sharh: By «faǧara» in dispute it is explained that the disputant departs from the truth and lets himself be carried into falsehood or lying. The Ḥadīṯ warns against this quality as a quality of Nifāq, without deriving from it Nifāq akbar automatically for every doer.

HAD-2698.text: The sign of the Munāfiq is three.
HAD-2698.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2698.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2698.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains «Āyah of the Munāfiq» as his sign. That three traits are named here and four in the previous Ḥadīṯ is no contradiction: the reports highlight different traits.

HAD-2699.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2699.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2699.sharh: Deliberate lying is one of the signs of Nifāq named in the Ḥadīṯ. The explanation of the chapter treats such traits as warning qualities of character; the mere single sin is not, without further grounds, a judgment of Nifāq akbar.

HAD-2700.text: When he promises something, he breaks his promise.
HAD-2700.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2700.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2700.sharh: The deliberate breaking of commitments is named as a sign of Nifāq. The warning concerns moral unreliability; it is not the same as a blanket judgment that every single doer has Nifāq akbar.

HAD-2701.text: When something is entrusted to him, he commits betrayal.
HAD-2701.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2701.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2701.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains Khiyānah regarding an Amānah together in meaning with betrayal of a covenant: in both cases an obligation that was taken on is faithlessly violated. This is a sign of Nifāq in conduct.

HAD-2702.text: The sign of the Munāfiq is three – even if he fasts, prays, and claims to be a Muslim.
HAD-2702.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2702.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2702.sharh: The added wording shows that outward acts of worship do not render harmless the danger of deeply rooted qualities such as lying, breach of covenant, and betrayal. The chapter's Šarḥ nevertheless distinguishes between such qualities of Nifāq and the greater Nifāq of faith.

HAD-2703.text: When a man declares his brother a Kāfir, this statement falls back upon one of the two.
HAD-2703.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2703.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2703.sharh: The wording is a grave warning against unfounded Takfīr. If a Muslim is wrongly called a Kāfir, the guilt, or the dangerous statement, returns upon the speaker; it does not follow that every false Takfīr would automatically itself be Kufr akbar.

HAD-2704.text: If the person concerned is in fact as he was called, the statement applies to him; otherwise it returns upon the speaker.
HAD-2704.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2704.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2704.sharh: If the attribution of Kufr is unfounded, its guilt returns upon the one who uttered it. The Ḥadīṯ thereby sharpens the warning against rash Takfīr; it does not establish the rule that every false Takfīr is for its part automatically Kufr akbar.

HAD-2705.text: No man knowingly attributes himself to someone other than his father without this being designated as Kufr.
HAD-2705.narrator: Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2705.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2705.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains the designation as Kufr in this topic in a differentiated way: in the case of Istiḥlāl, actual Kufr can be meant; otherwise «Kufr» can linguistically denote the denial and concealment of the right of one's own father. The mere act is therefore not treated wholesale as Kufr akbar of every doer.

HAD-2726.text: Others said about the rain: «Such-and-such a star was in the right.»
HAD-2726.narrator: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2726.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-2726.sharh: The Šarḥ warns against ascribing Allah’s gift to a star. If only a temporal sign is meant and Allah alone is acknowledged as Creator, this is not the same as the claim of an independent effect of the stars.

HAD-2727.text: A sign of Nifāq is hatred of the Anṣār.
HAD-2727.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2727.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2727.sharh: Whoever recognizes the standing of the Anṣār, their commitment to the Prophet ﷺ, and their early support of Islām loves them on that account. Hatred directed precisely at this religious standing is therefore a sign of Nifāq.

HAD-2728.text: A sign of Īmān is love for the Anṣār.
HAD-2728.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2728.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2728.sharh: Love for the Anṣār follows from love for the Prophet ﷺ, for Islām, and for those who supported him in a difficult time. Therefore this love is a sign of sound Īmān.

HAD-2729.text: Only a Muʾmin loves the Anṣār.
HAD-2729.narrator: al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2729.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2729.sharh: The particular love for the Anṣār springs from the recognition of their help to the Prophet ﷺ and of their service to Islām. This religiously grounded love belongs to the signs of Īmān.

HAD-2730.text: Only a Munāfiq hates the Anṣār.
HAD-2730.narrator: al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2730.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2730.sharh: The hatred that is meant is connected with the religious standing of the Anṣār. Whoever loathes their merits precisely because of their support of the Prophet ﷺ and of Islām thereby shows a mark of Nifāq.

HAD-2731.text: Whoever loves the Anṣār, Allah loves him.
HAD-2731.narrator: al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2731.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2731.sharh: Love for the Anṣār is praised because it proceeds from love for the Prophet ﷺ, for Islām, and for their merits in the service of the religion.

HAD-2732.text: Whoever hates the Anṣār, Allah hates him.
HAD-2732.narrator: al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2732.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2732.sharh: The severe censure concerns hatred directed against the Anṣār because of their merits for the Prophet ﷺ and the religion.

HAD-2733.text: A man who believes in Allah and the Last Day does not hate the Anṣār.
HAD-2733.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2733.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2733.sharh: True faith leads to recognition of the merits of the Anṣār. Therefore religiously motivated hatred of them contradicts the stance of a Muʾmin.

HAD-2734.narrator: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2734.speaker: ʿAlī رضي الله عنه said about the bequest of the Prophet ﷺ:
HAD-2734.sharh: Whoever acknowledges the standing of ʿAlī رضي الله عنه with the Prophet ﷺ and his merits in Islām loves him for a religious reason. This love is therefore a sign of Īmān.

HAD-2735.narrator: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2735.speaker: ʿAlī رضي الله عنه said about the bequest of the Prophet ﷺ:
HAD-2735.sharh: What is meant is hatred directed against ʿAlī رضي الله عنه on account of his religious merits, his nearness to the Prophet ﷺ, and his commitment to Islām. Such hatred is a mark of Nifāq.

HAD-2736.text: O you women, give Ṣadaqah and ask Allah frequently for forgiveness.
HAD-2736.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2736.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2736.sharh: The call to Ṣadaqah and Istighfār is a way to the effacement of sins. Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ emphasizes that the Prophet ﷺ here guides to good deeds and repentance.

HAD-2737.text: The Prophet ﷺ said to the women: «I saw you as the majority of the inhabitants of the Fire.»
HAD-2737.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2737.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2737.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ immediately names concrete sinful behaviors and links the warning with Ṣadaqah and Istighfār. It is a moral warning with a way to repentance and not a statement about the worth of a sex.

HAD-2738.text: Among the causes mentioned are frequent cursing and ingratitude toward the husband.
HAD-2738.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2738.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2738.sharh: «Kufr al-ʿašīr» here means ingratitude toward the kindness and the right of the husband. Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ expressly emphasizes that this notion of Kufr here does not mean Kufr toward Allah.

HAD-2739.text: The Prophet ﷺ described a form, mentioned in the Ḥadīṯ, of «deficiency in ʿAql and Dīn» and afterwards explained it himself.
HAD-2739.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2739.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2739.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the expression by means of the examples that the Prophet ﷺ himself named. It must not be understood in isolation as a statement about human dignity or as a blanket devaluation.

HAD-2740.text: As an explanation of the deficiency in ʿAql mentioned here, the Prophet ﷺ referred to the rule of testimony in which two women correspond to the testimony of one man.
HAD-2740.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2740.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2740.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ explains the expression used here through a concrete rule of testimony. Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ thereby refers to Qurʾān 2:282 and its reasoning that one reminds the other when one errs.

HAD-2741.text: As an explanation of the deficiency in Dīn mentioned here, the Prophet ﷺ referred to the fact that the menstruating woman does not pray during this time and does not fast in Ramaḍān.
HAD-2741.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2741.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2741.sharh: The «deficiency in Dīn» mentioned here denotes the temporarily smaller number of certain acts of worship performed, because of a šarʿī prescribed exception. No blame attaches to the woman for this; omitting the Ṣalāh during menstruation is itself obedience.

HAD-2742.text: When Ibn Ādam reads an Āyah of prostration and prostrates, the Šayṭān withdraws weeping.
HAD-2742.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2742.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2742.sharh: The believer’s prostration is obedience and submission toward Allah. The Šayṭān then remembers his own refusal of the commanded Suǧūd and withdraws full of regret.

HAD-2743.text: Ibn Ādam was called to Suǧūd, he prostrated — Paradise is for him.
HAD-2743.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2743.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported about the words of the Šayṭān:
HAD-2743.sharh: The sentence brings out the reward of obedience and of Suǧūd. Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ at the same time makes clear that not every deed for which Paradise is promised is thereby alone proven to be obligatory.

HAD-2744.text: I was commanded the Suǧūd, but I refused it — the Fire is for me.
HAD-2744.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2744.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported about the words of the Šayṭān:
HAD-2744.sharh: The statement sets the obedience of Ibn Ādam over against the arrogant refusal of Iblīs. The core is the warning against pride and disobedience toward Allah.

HAD-2745.text: Between the human being and Širk and Kufr stands the abandonment of the Ṣalāh.
HAD-2745.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2745.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2745.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ names two classical lines of interpretation: one group of the Salaf and of Ahl al-Ḥadīṯ explained the deliberate relinquishment of the Ṣalāh, despite acknowledgment of its obligation, as Kufr; other scholars assessed it as a grave sin and Fisq, not as an exit from Islām. Over the denial of the known obligation of the Ṣalāh, by contrast, there is no such dispute. The Ḥadīṯ must therefore not be shortened, in the case of a particular doer, without the relevant conditions and the documented Ikhtilāf.

HAD-2746.text: When the Prophet ﷺ was asked about the best deeds, he mentioned first the Īmān in Allah.
HAD-2746.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2746.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2746.sharh: Tawḥīd and affirming Īmān are the foundation and condition of the remaining deeds; therefore they are mentioned here as the best deeds.

HAD-2747.text: Thereafter the Prophet ﷺ mentioned the Ǧihād in Allah's path.
HAD-2747.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2747.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2747.sharh: The order of the answers about the best deeds can vary according to situation and need; here the Ǧihād follows the Īmān.

HAD-2748.text: Thereafter the Prophet ﷺ mentioned an accepted Ḥaǧǧ.
HAD-2748.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2748.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2748.sharh: A mabrūr Ḥaǧǧ is explained as free from sin and fault, accepted and performed sincerely for Allah.

HAD-2749.text: Among the best deeds are the Īmān in Allah and the Ǧihād in His path.
HAD-2749.narrator: Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2749.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2749.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ joins the foundation of Īmān with an especially weighty outward deed; differing ranks are understood according to context and need.

HAD-2750.text: The most excellent manumission is that of a person who is especially valuable among his people and of high price.
HAD-2750.narrator: Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2750.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2750.sharh: A greater personal expenditure and a greater benefit for the one set free can make the manumission especially meritorious.

HAD-2751.text: Whoever is not able to do that should help a craftsman or work for someone who himself possesses no skill.
HAD-2751.narrator: Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2751.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2751.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains al-aḫraq as someone without craft skill. Whoever cannot manage a great deed finds a door of good in helping others with his ability.

HAD-2752.text: Whoever is not able to do that either should keep his evil away from the people; that is Ṣadaqah for himself.
HAD-2752.narrator: Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2752.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2752.sharh: Consciously keeping one's own harm away from others is itself a form of kindness and Ṣadaqah.

HAD-2753.text: Among the best deeds is the Ṣalāh at its appointed time.
HAD-2753.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2753.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2753.sharh: The Ṣalāh is singled out through its tie to the time set by Allah.

HAD-2754.text: Thereafter the Prophet ﷺ mentioned Birr toward the parents.
HAD-2754.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2754.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2754.sharh: Birr toward the parents includes kindness, good conduct and fulfilling their rightful claims; doors of Birr remain even after their death.

HAD-2755.text: Thereafter the Prophet ﷺ mentioned the Ǧihād in Allah's path.
HAD-2755.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2755.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2755.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ mentions the Ǧihād after the Ṣalāh and Birr al-wālidayn; ranks of such answers can vary according to circumstances.

HAD-2756.text: The gravest sin is to associate an equal with Allah, although He created you.
HAD-2756.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2756.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2756.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains nidd as an equal counterpart. The particular ugliness of Širk lies in giving another a share in what belongs to the Creator alone.

HAD-2757.text: Thereafter, among the gravest sins is to kill one's own child out of fear that it would have to share the livelihood with one.
HAD-2757.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2757.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2757.sharh: The act is motivated by fear of poverty and at the same time violates the natural duty of care and the protection of a soul made inviolable by Allah.

HAD-2758.text: Thereafter, among the gravest sins is Zinā with the wife of the neighbor.
HAD-2758.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2758.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2758.sharh: The sin is aggravated by the neighbor's additional right: besides Zinā, trust, neighborliness and protected family rights are violated.

HAD-2759.text: Among the greatest of the great sins is to associate something with Allah.
HAD-2759.narrator: Abū Bakrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2759.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2759.sharh: Širk stands at the head of the Kabāʾir mentioned; the enumerations of great sins are not limited to a few fixed single points.

HAD-2760.text: Among the greatest of the great sins is ʿUqūq toward the parents.
HAD-2760.narrator: Abū Bakrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2760.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2760.sharh: ʿUqūq is the grave violation of the obligatory kindness and the rights of the parents; its mention shows the exceptional standing of their rights.

HAD-2761.text: Among the greatest of the great sins is a false statement or false testimony.
HAD-2761.narrator: Abū Bakrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2761.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2761.sharh: A false statement and false testimony can destroy rights and secure injustice through a seemingly lawful means; the repetition underscores their danger.

HAD-2762.text: The Prophet ﷺ named among the Kabāʾir: Širk toward Allah, killing a soul, ʿUqūq toward the parents and a false statement.
HAD-2762.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2762.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2762.sharh: The enumeration names important Kabāʾir without excluding all the remaining great sins.

HAD-2763.text: Among the Kabāʾir is that a man has his own parents insulted.
HAD-2763.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2763.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2763.sharh: Whoever knowingly creates the occasion for his parents to be insulted bears responsibility for that cause, even if he does not utter the insult himself.

HAD-2764.text: That happens in that he insults the father or the mother of another, and that one then insults the parents of the one who insulted.
HAD-2764.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2764.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2764.sharh: A forbidden outcome can also be incurred by knowingly setting its foreseeable cause.

HAD-2765.text: Whoever carries in the heart even the weight of a smallest particle of Kibr does not simply enter Paradise.
HAD-2765.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2765.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2765.sharh: The threat can point to a prior punishment if Allah punishes because of the Kibr; it is no proof of a blanket eternal damnation of every sinful Muslim.

HAD-2806.text: Allah can support this Dīn even through a sinful person.
HAD-2806.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2806.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2806.sharh: The benefit that arises for the Dīn through a person does not by itself prove either that person’s inner righteousness or that person’s final outcome. Allah can bring benefit to His religion through people who are themselves sinful.

HAD-2807.text: A person can, according to the outward impression, perform the deeds of the people of Paradise, while his end turns out otherwise.
HAD-2807.narrator: Sahl ibn Saʿd as-Sāʿidī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2807.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2807.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ warns against deriving a person’s final state from a momentary outward impression alone. What is decisive is the actual close of his life, which Allah knows.

HAD-2808.text: Deeds are judged according to their conclusion.
HAD-2808.narrator: Sahl ibn Saʿd as-Sāʿidī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2808.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2808.sharh: The outcome of a life is of particular importance. A present outward state must therefore not lead to a self-assured statement about the final judgment of the hereafter of a particular person.

HAD-2809.text: A man from earlier communities took his own life in severe suffering; upon that a grave threat of the hereafter was issued.
HAD-2809.narrator: Ǧundab ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Baǧalī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2809.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2809.sharh: The report serves to deter from suicide. It relates a divine judgment about a particular earlier case and must not be understood as a general human authority to fix the same final outcome for every single person affected.

HAD-2810.narrator: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2810.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2810.sharh: The Prophet ﷺ had this statement proclaimed publicly. In the context there is also a warning against hastily designating a person as a martyr with a certain verdict of Paradise solely on account of his outward exertion.

HAD-2811.text: Ġulūl — the unlawful taking from the spoils of war before their lawful distribution — is connected with a grave threat of the Fire.
HAD-2811.narrator: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2811.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2811.sharh: The report corrects the hasty designation of a man as a martyr after an unlawfully taken piece of spoils had become known. It shows the gravity of Ġulūl and the danger of certain judgments of the hereafter based on mere outward impressions.

HAD-2812.text: Even a seemingly slight item of property taken unlawfully from the spoils can be the occasion of a grave punishment in the hereafter.
HAD-2812.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2812.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2812.sharh: Muslim 115 sharpens the warning against Ġulūl: not the material value alone determines the gravity, but the violation of the entrusted right. Even seemingly slight objects must not be appropriated unlawfully.

HAD-2813.text: The one who kills himself does not thereby automatically become a Kāfir.
HAD-2813.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2813.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2813.sharh: Muslim’s own chapter presents the Ḥadīṯ as proof that suicide is not automatically Kufr. The man received forgiveness because of his Hiǧrah; this joins the grave sin with the fundamental possibility of divine forgiveness.

HAD-2814.text: The Prophet ﷺ asked Allah for forgiveness for the hands of the man who had harmed himself.
HAD-2814.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2814.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2814.sharh: The Duʿāʾ of the Prophet ﷺ confirms that the person affected was not treated as outside Islam. The report is therefore a central counterweight to the severe Waʿīd texts of the preceding chapter.

HAD-2815.text: Shortly before the Resurrection, Allah sends a gentle wind that takes the soul of every person in whose heart there is even the slightest measure of Īmān.
HAD-2815.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2815.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2815.sharh: The report describes an event of the end of time: the people who have even a little Īmān are taken before the last events of the Hour. The differing words of the transmissions each time describe a very small measure of Īmān.

HAD-2816.text: Hasten ahead with righteous deeds before Fitnah breaks in like pieces of a dark night.
HAD-2816.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2816.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2816.sharh: The Prophet ﷺ calls for the times of clarity to be used for obedience before a confusing Fitnah makes steadfastness difficult. The image of the dark night describes the strong obscurity of these trials.

HAD-2817.text: In a severe Fitnah a person can be believing in the morning and unbelieving in the evening — or believing in the evening and unbelieving in the morning.
HAD-2817.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2817.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2817.sharh: The text warns against a rapid religious reversal in times of great Fitnah. It is a call to steadfastness and must not serve as a basis for accusing particular people of Kufr across the board without concrete proofs.

HAD-2818.text: Among the dangers of the Fitnah is that a person sells his Dīn for a perishable share of the Dunyā.
HAD-2818.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2818.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2818.sharh: The cause of the falling away described is expressed as a worldly exchange: temporary benefit is placed above the Dīn. The Ḥadīṯ therefore urges that Īmān be made firm before such trials set in.

HAD-2819.text: Ṯābit ibn Qays رضي الله عنه feared, because of the revelation about raising the voice above the voice of the Prophet ﷺ, that his deeds might be nullified; the Prophet ﷺ gave him instead the glad tidings of Paradise.
HAD-2819.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2819.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2819.sharh: Ṯābit’s fear shows the believers’ concern for the acceptance of their deeds. The Prophet ﷺ expressly corrected his assessment of himself and testified Paradise for him; the variants 119b–d are not multiplied as new cards.

HAD-2820.text: Whoever realizes his Islam well is not called to account for the deeds of his Ǧāhiliyyah.
HAD-2820.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2820.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2820.sharh: Muslim 120a–c transmits the same core in several chains. Good Islam here means becoming sincere in Islam and not holding fast to the earlier rejection; the earlier deeds are lifted by entry into Islam.

HAD-2821.text: Islam wipes away what was before it.
HAD-2821.narrator: ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2821.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2821.sharh: Entry into Islam wipes away the person’s previous sins. ʿAmr رضي الله عنه received this assurance when he wanted to make forgiveness a condition of his Bayʿah.

HAD-2822.text: The Hiǧrah wipes away what was before it.
HAD-2822.narrator: ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2822.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2822.sharh: The sincere Hiǧrah is named in the Ḥadīṯ as a cause by which earlier sins are wiped away.

HAD-2823.text: The Ḥaǧǧ wipes away what was before it.
HAD-2823.narrator: ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2823.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2823.sharh: The Ḥaǧǧ performed with sincerity is named, together with Islam and the Hiǧrah, as a cause of the wiping away of earlier sins.

HAD-2824.text: The best upon which we build is the testimony: Lā ilāha illā Allah and Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah.
HAD-2824.narrator: ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2824.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2824.sharh: ʿAmr رضي الله عنه placed at the end of his life the testimony of faith above the changing phases of his life. The basis of his hope was the Tawḥīd and the confirmation of the Risālah.

HAD-2825.text: For people who had committed grave sins before their Islam, the way of Tawbah and forgiveness was opened.
HAD-2825.narrator: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2825.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2825.sharh: Muslim 122 joins the question of earlier deeds of Širk, killing and Zinā with the revelation texts about Tawbah and Allah’s forgiveness. The earlier state does not close the door to sincere entry into Islam.

HAD-2846.text: That a believer loathes a certain waswasah so much that he hardly wishes to utter it is a sign of living Īmān.
HAD-2846.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2846.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2846.sharh: The Prophet ﷺ did not call the content of the whispering Īmān, but the loathing, the distress, and the rejection that the believer feels toward it. 132b is only another chain.

HAD-2847.text: The Prophet ﷺ called the warding off and the loathing of waswasah pure Īmān.
HAD-2847.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2847.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2847.sharh: The short wording is understood in the chapter on waswasah thus: the bad thought itself is not Īmān, but that the heart rejects it and finds it heavy.

HAD-2848.text: If the waswasah leads to the question of who created Allah, the believer should say: I believe in Allah.
HAD-2848.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2848.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2848.sharh: The Prophet ﷺ did not teach endless occupation with the whispering, but the affirmation of Īmān. Muslim 134b is a report with the same answer and an additional mention of the messengers.

HAD-2849.text: If the waswasah reaches the question “Who created your Lord?”, one should seek refuge with Allah.
HAD-2849.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2849.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2849.sharh: The prophetic treatment is istiʿāḏah: seeking protection with Allah from the Šayṭān. The report does not make the unwanted whispering itself a falling away from faith.

HAD-2850.text: With such waswasah one should end it and not follow it any further.
HAD-2850.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2850.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2850.sharh: Along with the istiʿāḏah, the Prophet ﷺ commands that the chain of thoughts be cut off. That guards against feeding a compulsive whispering further by continued occupation with it.

HAD-2851.text: People will keep on asking until it is said: Allah created the creation—but who created Allah? Whoever finds this within himself should say: I believe in Allah.
HAD-2851.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2851.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2851.sharh: The prophetic treatment of waswasah is to affirm the Īmān and not to follow the endless chain of thoughts. The unwanted whispering itself is not treated as kufr accepted by one’s will.

HAD-2852.text: Whoever reaches such waswasah should seek refuge with Allah and stop with it.
HAD-2852.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2852.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2852.sharh: Istiʿāḏah and ending the chain of thoughts are the response expressly transmitted. The variants of this ḥadīṯ are recorded only according to an independent core of the statement.

HAD-2853.text: Whoever claims that Muḥammad ﷺ saw his Lord has uttered a tremendous claim about Allah.
HAD-2853.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2853.sharh: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها expressly denied the claim of a vision of Allah with the eyes and brought Qurʾān evidences. The report is preserved as her transmitted explanation, without concealing the other authentic wordings of Ibn ʿAbbās.

HAD-2854.text: The Prophet ﷺ saw Ǧibrīl عليه السلام in his real form twice.
HAD-2854.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2854.sharh: ʿĀʾišah explained the verses about the seeing as referring to Ǧibrīl عليه السلام. Thereby she determines the object of these two vision events as the angel in his original form.

HAD-2855.text: Whoever claims that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concealed something of the revelation has brought a grave false claim.
HAD-2855.narrator: Masrūq reported from ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها:
HAD-2855.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2855.sharh: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها grounded this in the Qurʾān’s command to the Messenger ﷺ to convey the revelation completely. The report confirms the complete conveyance of the risālah.

HAD-2856.text: Whoever claims that the Prophet ﷺ knows of himself what will happen tomorrow has brought a false claim.
HAD-2856.speaker: It was transmitted:
HAD-2856.sharh: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها pointed out that knowledge of the unseen belongs to Allah. The Messenger ﷺ knows of it only what Allah makes known to him through revelation.

HAD-2857.text: To the question whether the Prophet ﷺ had seen his Lord, he answered: Light—how could I see Him?
HAD-2857.narrator: Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2857.speaker: It was transmitted:
HAD-2857.sharh: The report describes the Prophet’s ﷺ answer to Abū Ḏarr’s direct question. It is understood together with the other authentic reports on the ruʾyah and is not extended beyond its wording.

HAD-2858.text: The Prophet ﷺ said about the vision of his Lord: I saw light.
HAD-2858.narrator: Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2858.speaker: It was transmitted:
HAD-2858.sharh: This authentic wording variant is “I saw light.” It is documented as its own transmitted formulation, without deriving from it an untransmitted claim about a vision with the eyes.

HAD-2859.text: The Prophet ﷺ saw his Lord with his heart.
HAD-2859.narrator: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2859.speaker: It was transmitted:
HAD-2859.sharh: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما expressly describes the ruʾyah as a vision of the heart. Thereby his authentic transmission remains precisely preserved alongside ʿĀʾišah’s denial of the vision with the eyes.

HAD-2860.text: The vision of the heart is mentioned twice in the report.
HAD-2860.narrator: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2860.speaker: It was transmitted:
HAD-2860.sharh: The second wording of Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما emphasizes the ruʾyah with the heart twice. It must not be silently reworded into a bodily vision with the eyes.

HAD-2861.text: The verses “Then he drew near and came closer” were related by ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها to Ǧibrīl عليه السلام.
HAD-2861.narrator: Masrūq reported from ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها:
HAD-2861.speaker: It was transmitted:
HAD-2861.sharh: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها explained that the Prophet ﷺ saw Ǧibrīl عليه السلام in his actual form. In her explanation the Qurʾān passage is related to this vision of the angel.

HAD-2862.text: Abū Ḏarr expressly asked the Prophet ﷺ about the ruʾyah of his Lord.
HAD-2862.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Šaqīq reported from Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه:
HAD-2862.speaker: It was transmitted:
HAD-2862.sharh: The significance of this report lies in the direct prophetic answer to a direct question. Therefore it is not replaced by later speculation, but preserved in its wording alongside the other ṣaḥīḥ reports.

HAD-2863.text: Allah does not sleep, and sleep does not befit Him.
HAD-2863.narrator: Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2863.speaker: It was transmitted:
HAD-2863.sharh: The ḥadīṯ expressly negates sleep of Allah. This is a prophetic negation of a deficiency, and it is understood without taʿṭīl of the other affirmed attributes.

HAD-2864.text: Allah lowers the Scale and raises it.
HAD-2864.narrator: Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2864.speaker: It was transmitted:
HAD-2864.sharh: The wording describes Allah’s disposal and His just determination over His creation. The text is affirmed without fixing a manner that goes beyond what was transmitted from the Prophet.

HAD-2865.text: The deed of the night ascends to Allah before the deed of the day, and the deed of the day before the deed of the night.
HAD-2865.narrator: Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2865.speaker: It was transmitted:
HAD-2865.sharh: The ḥadīṯ describes the ascent of deeds in the transmitted temporal order. It belongs to the connected report about the perfection of Allah’s sovereignty and His knowledge.

HAD-2986.text: Among them there are people whom the Fire reaches up to the hip, or to the place of the hip-belt.
HAD-2986.narrator: Samurah ibn Ǧundub رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2986.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2986.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains “al-ḥuǧzah” as the place where the trousers or the undergarment are tied. Another transmitted wording uses “ḥaqwayhi” at this point, that is, the region of the hip and the waist.

HAD-2987.text: Among them there are people whom the Fire reaches up to the collarbone, or up to the neck.
HAD-2987.narrator: Samurah ibn Ǧundub رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2987.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2987.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains “at-tarquwah” as the bone between the hollow of the neck and the shoulder. Together with the wording “up to his neck,” this describes the highest of the degrees mentioned in this report.

HAD-2988.text: Jahannam and Paradise disputed with one another. Jahannam said: The arrogant and the violent will enter me.
HAD-2988.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2988.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2988.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats the dispute described in the Ḥadīṯ as real speech made possible by Allah; he also mentions the interpretation that it depicts what distinguishes each of the two places. The text especially highlights arrogance and violence for Jahannam.

HAD-2989.text: Paradise said: Why is it that those who enter me are above all the weak, the modest, and those little regarded by people?
HAD-2989.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2989.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2989.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the weak mentioned here not as people without strength of faith, but as humble people who lower themselves before Allah and do not raise themselves above others. The transmitted words describe their low worldly standing, not a lack of Īmān.

HAD-2990.text: You, Jahannam, are My punishment; through you I punish whom I will of My servants.
HAD-2990.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2990.speaker: Allah says in the Ḥadīṯ:
HAD-2990.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ cites this statement as part of Allah’s reply to both places: Jahannam is named as the place and the means of punishment. The record stays with the transmitted wording and adds no statement about the how of the divine act.

HAD-2991.text: You are My mercy; through you I show mercy to whom I will of My servants.
HAD-2991.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2991.speaker: Allah says in the Ḥadīṯ to Paradise:
HAD-2991.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ cites the statement as the counterpart to naming Jahannam a punishment. In the transmitted wording Paradise is called a mercy through which Allah grants favor to whom He will of His servants.

HAD-2992.text: Both Paradise and Jahannam will receive their fill.
HAD-2992.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2992.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2992.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats the following wordings as a mutual explanation of how the filling of Paradise and the Fire promised in the Ḥadīṯ is described. The statement is therefore not read in isolation from the variants that follow immediately.

HAD-2993.text: Jahannam keeps saying: Is there still more? Until the Lord of Power places His foot into it; then it says: Enough, enough. Its parts draw together.
HAD-2993.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2993.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2993.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ places the wordings of this section side by side and uses them to explain the wording mutually. For the presentation, the transmitted statement therefore remains decisive; nothing is added here about the nature or the how of what the text ascribes to Allah.

HAD-2994.text: In Paradise there still remains free space. Allah creates for it a further creation and has them dwell in that free space of Paradise.
HAD-2994.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2994.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2994.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the transmitted wordings complete one another: Paradise still has free space, and Allah creates a creation for it. He stresses at the same time that Allah creates no one for punishment without a deed having preceded by which punishment would be deserved.

HAD-2995.text: On the Day of Resurrection death will be brought in the form of a whitish-black ram and placed between Paradise and Jahannam.
HAD-2995.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2995.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2995.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains that death is not an independent body, but is the opposite of life. The form of the ram visible in the Ḥadīṯ serves to make the final end of death plain to the inhabitants of Paradise and the Fire.

HAD-2996.text: The inhabitants of Paradise and the inhabitants of the Fire raise their heads and look; they recognize death, for they have all known it.
HAD-2996.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2996.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2996.sharh: The scene makes the meaning of what follows immediately visible to both groups: both recognize death before it is removed before them. The report thereby links their own knowledge of death with the subsequent proclamation of its final removal.

HAD-2997.text: Then it is commanded that death be slaughtered, and it is slaughtered between Paradise and Jahannam.
HAD-2997.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2997.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2997.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains the slaughter of the visible form as a sign that death itself will no longer occur thereafter. The scene makes the final duration of their state visible to the inhabitants of both abodes.

HAD-2998.text: O inhabitants of Paradise: eternity, and no death! O inhabitants of the Fire: eternity, and no death!
HAD-2998.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2998.speaker: Then it is called out:
HAD-2998.sharh: Al-Māzirī links the visible depiction and the slaughter of death with this proclamation: for both groups every expectation of a later death comes to an end. Paradise remains permanently Paradise, and the Fire remains permanently Fire for its abiding inhabitants.

HAD-2999.text: After death has been slaughtered and it has been called out that there is no longer any death, the joy of the inhabitants of Paradise continues to increase, and the grief of the inhabitants of the Fire continues to increase.
HAD-2999.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2999.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2999.sharh: The report itself explains the effect of the final proclamation: the certainty that death will no longer occur increases the joy of the inhabitants of Paradise and increases the grief of the inhabitants of the Fire. Thereby the irreversibility of both states is brought out.

HAD-3000.text: The molar or the canine tooth of the Kāfir will be in the Fire like the mountain Uḥud, and the thickness of his skin corresponds to a journey of three days.
HAD-3000.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3000.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3000.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats the immense body size of the inhabitants of the Fire as part of the otherworldly reality reported from the Prophet. The enlargement increases the reach of the punishment; the report is affirmed on the basis of the authentic transmission, without seeking to measure it by earthly body dimensions.

HAD-3001.text: The distance between the two shoulders of the Kāfir in the Fire corresponds, for a fast rider, to a journey of three days.
HAD-3001.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3001.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3001.sharh: Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Qurṭubī explains the enlargement of the body in the Fire by the fact that the punishment thereby becomes greater and the pain is intensified. He also points out that the Kuffār do not all have the same degree in the punishment.

HAD-3002.text: Shall I inform you about the inhabitants of Paradise? Every weak person whom the people regard as weak.
HAD-3002.narrator: Ḥāriṯah ibn Wahb رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3002.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3002.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the description as praise of humility, unobtrusiveness, and the lowering of one’s own self before Allah. Meant especially are people who are little esteemed in the world, while arrogance and violence form the opposite pole.

HAD-3003.text: If he were to swear an oath before Allah, Allah would have it fulfilled.
HAD-3003.narrator: Ḥāriṯah ibn Wahb رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3003.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said about this person:
HAD-3003.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains this statement by the special standing of such a sincere servant with Allah: his supplication is answered, or Allah preserves him from his hope placed in Allah and his oath being disappointed.

HAD-3004.text: Shall I inform you about the inhabitants of the Fire? Every coarse, greedy, and arrogant person.
HAD-3004.narrator: Ḥāriṯah ibn Wahb رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3004.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3004.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ sets these qualities over against the praise of the humble: coarseness, self-exaltation, and domineering harshness are among the marks by which the report describes the people of the Fire.

HAD-3005.text: Many a one is disheveled and is turned away at the doors.
HAD-3005.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3005.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3005.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains “disheveled” as unkempt, dusty hair, and “turned away at the doors” as someone who has so little standing among people that he is not let in and is turned back.

HAD-3046.text: Seek refuge with Allah from the punishment of the Fire.
HAD-3046.narrator: Zayd ibn Ṯābit رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3046.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3046.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ presents this call as a practical consequence of the otherworldly dangers described before: the believer is to ask Allah explicitly for protection from the punishment of the Fire.

HAD-3047.text: Seek refuge with Allah from the punishment of the grave.
HAD-3047.narrator: Zayd ibn Ṯābit رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3047.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3047.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ connects the call to seek refuge with the real trial and punishment in the Barzaḫ. The Ḥadīṯ does not make this mere information, but a regular plea to Allah for protection.

HAD-3048.text: Seek refuge with Allah from the temptations – the visible ones and the hidden ones.
HAD-3048.narrator: Zayd ibn Ṯābit رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3048.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3048.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ classifies the wording as a comprehensive plea for protection: it covers trials that are openly recognizable as well as those whose danger is hidden, inward, or at first not recognizable.

HAD-3049.text: Seek refuge with Allah from the temptation of the Daǧǧāl.
HAD-3049.narrator: Zayd ibn Ṯābit رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3049.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3049.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ cites the Fitnah of the Daǧǧāl separately, although refuge had already been sought in general from visible and hidden temptations. The special mention underlines the extraordinary gravity of this Fitnah.

HAD-3050.text: When the servant is laid in his grave and his companions depart, he hears the sound of their footsteps.
HAD-3050.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3050.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3050.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats the hearing of the departing footsteps in direct connection with the questioning in the grave that follows. The record therefore stays with this expressly transmitted situation and does not generalize it beyond the text.

HAD-3051.text: Allah’s statement about establishing the believers with the firm word was revealed in connection with the trial and the punishment in the grave.
HAD-3051.narrator: al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3051.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3051.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ cites this report in the chapter on the grave. The establishing of the believer is Allah’s help in the trial of the grave, and the record stays with this expressly transmitted connection.

HAD-3052.text: The believer is asked in the grave: “Who is your Lord?” He answers: “My Lord is Allah, and my Prophet is Muḥammad ﷺ.”
HAD-3052.narrator: al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3052.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3052.sharh: The answer to the question of the grave is explained in the Ḥadīṯ itself as the effect of the establishing granted by Allah. Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats it in the immediate context of the trial of the grave, and nothing further is added.

HAD-3053.text: When the soul of the believer leaves the body, two angels receive it and carry it upward; its pleasant scent is described as musk.
HAD-3053.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3053.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3053.sharh: The report describes the honoring reception of the believing soul after death. The Šarḥ is limited to the expressly named signs of good and honor, and is not extended into speculative statements about the nature of the soul.

HAD-3054.text: The inhabitants of heaven welcome the good soul and invoke ṣalāh upon it and upon the body it inhabited.
HAD-3054.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3054.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3054.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats the report as part of the otherworldly honoring of the believer. What is decisive is the contrast between the good reception of the believing soul and the rejection of the bad soul.

HAD-3055.text: When the soul of the disbeliever leaves the body, its foul smell and the curse are mentioned.
HAD-3055.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3055.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3055.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ sets the honoring reception of the believer over against the humiliating reception of the disbelieving soul. The record keeps to this transmitted contrast, without claiming further details about the unseen.

HAD-3056.text: About the soul of the disbeliever the inhabitants of heaven say that a foul soul has come from the earth; afterwards it is brought to its appointed end.
HAD-3056.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3056.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3056.sharh: The rejection is presented in the wording of the Ḥadīṯ as a counter-image to the good soul. Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ’s treatment stays within this text and its statement about honor or humiliation after death.

HAD-3057.text: At those killed at Badr, the Prophet ﷺ explained that the living did not hear his words more clearly than those; the slain, however, could not answer him.
HAD-3057.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3057.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3057.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats this passage as a particular event reported by the Prophet ﷺ at Badr and as a sign of his truthfulness. It is not generalized into the claim that the dead hear everything at every time.

HAD-3058.text: Whoever is subjected on the Day of Resurrection to a thorough and gapless reckoning will be punished, or will perish.
HAD-3058.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3058.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the thorough reckoning as a complete examination. He names as the meaning that already the holding forth and exposing of the sins is painful, or that the exact reckoning leads to punishment if Allah does not forgive.

HAD-3059.text: The easy reckoning named in the Qurʾān is the mere presentation of the deeds; it is not the thorough examination of every single point.
HAD-3059.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3059.sharh: The Prophet ﷺ expressly distinguishes between al-ʿarḍ, the presentation of the deeds, and munāqašat al-ḥisāb, the detailed examination. Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains precisely this distinction.

HAD-3060.text: None of you should die except while he thinks well of Allah.
HAD-3060.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3060.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3060.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains this as a warning against ruinous despair and as a call, especially at the end of life, to let hope in Allah’s mercy prevail. Fear and hope remain foundations of worship.

HAD-3061.text: When Allah decrees punishment for a people, the punishment strikes those who are among them.
HAD-3061.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3061.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3061.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ shows that a general worldly affliction can strike people in the same place together. The final otherworldly judgment is not equated with that, for the report afterwards separates expressly according to deeds.

HAD-3062.text: After a shared worldly affliction, the people are raised according to their own deeds.
HAD-3062.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3062.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3062.sharh: The second half of the Ḥadīṯ prevents equating the shared worldly destruction with an identical otherworldly judgment. What remains decisive are one’s own deeds and the state of the individual before Allah.

HAD-3063.text: The Prophet ﷺ warned: Woe threatens the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near.
HAD-3063.narrator: Zaynab bint Ǧaḥš رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-3063.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3063.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats the statement as a warning of approaching Fitan and of great signs of the end of time. The wording is a grave warning, not a dating of the coming of the Hour.

HAD-3064.text: The Prophet ﷺ reported that an opening had arisen from the wall of Yaʾǧūǧ and Maʾǧūǧ, and he made its size clear with his fingers.
HAD-3064.narrator: Zaynab bint Ǧaḥš رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-3064.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3064.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats the movement of the hand as an illustration of a small opening and the report as a sign of the approach of great Fitan. The different transmission forms of the indication by the fingers are not multiplied into several cards.

HAD-3065.text: To the question whether people can perish even though righteous ones are among them, the Prophet ﷺ answered: “Yes, when the bad gains the upper hand.”
HAD-3065.narrator: Zaynab bint Ǧaḥš رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-3065.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3065.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains al-ḫabaṯ as sin and corruption and also mentions the explanation by Zinā. The core is: when corruption becomes massive, a general worldly affliction can also seize the righteous.

HAD-2786.text: Whoever cheats is not of me.
HAD-2786.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2786.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2786.sharh: Ġišš means concealing a relevant defect and thereby deceiving the other person. The Prophet ﷺ required that the wet part be made visible. «Not of me» intensifies the prohibition and does not mean, in a blanket sense, that every cheater leaves Islam.

HAD-2787.text: A hidden defect in goods should be made visible, so that people can see it.
HAD-2787.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2787.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2787.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ establishes transparency in trade: a defect relevant to the buyer must not be concealed in such a way that a false impression of the goods arises. Visible disclosure removes the fraudulent character.

HAD-2788.text: Not of us is one who, out of grief, strikes his cheeks, tears the garments, or calls with the calls of the Ǧāhiliyyah.
HAD-2788.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2788.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2788.sharh: Forbidden are forms of mourning of the Ǧāhiliyyah that appear in self-harm, tearing of garments, and corresponding cries of lament. The formula of disavowal shows the gravity of the act; it does not automatically mean Kufr akbar of the individual doer.

HAD-2789.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ disavowed the woman who wails loudly at a misfortune, shaves off her hair, or tears her garments.
HAD-2789.narrator: Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2789.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2789.sharh: What is meant are ritualized mourning acts of the Ǧāhiliyyah: loud wailing, shaving off the hair, and tearing garments out of despair. The prophetic disavowal shows the gravity of the prohibition, without automatically deriving Kufr akbar from the act alone.

HAD-2790.text: A Nammām — someone who carries words for the purpose of causing corruption among people — does not enter Paradise simply.
HAD-2790.narrator: Ḥuḏayfah ibn al-Yamān رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2790.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2790.sharh: Namīmah is the harmful carrying on of statements among people. The denial of entry into Paradise is a severe threat against this major sin; for a Muwaḥḥid it does not automatically mean eternal exclusion from Paradise, but stands under the known texts of Waʿīd and Allah’s will.

HAD-2791.text: Three people Allah will not address on the Day of Resurrection, will not look upon with the glance of mercy, and will not purify; for them is a painful punishment.
HAD-2791.narrator: Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2791.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2791.sharh: The threefold negation is an especially severe threat and shows that the following acts belong to the major sins. It is not understood, without further evidence, as automatic Kufr akbar of the doer.

HAD-2792.text: Among them is the one who lets his garment hang down.
HAD-2792.narrator: Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2792.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2792.sharh: Isbāl is joined in the Ḥadīṯ to an exceptionally severe threat. The text serves to deter from this forbidden act; details of motive and of further reports are to be brought together separately and are not to be read into the wording.

HAD-2793.text: Among them is the one who, after a gift, holds his favor over the recipient.
HAD-2793.narrator: Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2793.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2793.sharh: What is meant is later holding a gift already given over the recipient and thereby hurting him, or playing one’s own favor against him. The act damages the character of the gift and is therefore met with a severe Waʿīd.

HAD-2794.text: Among them is the seller who sells off his goods by a false oath.
HAD-2794.narrator: Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2794.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2794.sharh: The seller here joins two offenses: lying, or a false oath, and deception in trade, in order to make the goods appear more salable. Precisely this combination explains the exceptionally severe threat.

HAD-2795.text: Three people are met by a severe threat on the Day of Resurrection: an old man who commits Zinā, a lying ruler, and a needy arrogant man.
HAD-2795.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2795.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2795.sharh: The particular gravity lies in this: with these three persons the respective occasion for the sin ought to be weaker. Advanced age ordinarily lessens desire, authority makes lying less necessary, and neediness offers no worldly reason for arrogance. Thereby the corruptness of the trait stands out especially.

HAD-2796.text: Among the people under a severe threat on the Day of Resurrection is a man who sells his goods after ʿAṣr by a false oath and claims that he paid a higher price for them.
HAD-2796.narrator: Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2796.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2796.sharh: The merchant deceives the buyer by a false oath about the value, or the purchase price, of the goods. The Ḥadīṯ joins to this an especially severe threat and underscores the inviolability of truth and trust in trade.

HAD-2797.text: Among them is a man who denies a traveler surplus water, although he himself does not need it.
HAD-2797.narrator: Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2797.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2797.sharh: The threat concerns refusing surplus water to someone in need on a journey, although the owner himself does not need that water. The text stresses the gravity of withholding help necessary for life without a justified reason.

HAD-2798.text: Among them is a man who gives Bayʿah to an Imām only for worldly gain: if he receives some of it, he keeps it; if he receives nothing, he does not keep it.
HAD-2798.narrator: Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2798.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2798.sharh: What is blamed is treating the Bayʿah not on account of its religious obligation, but solely as a means of personal worldly gain. Loyalty is then made dependent on one’s own advantage rather than on the bond that is owed.

HAD-2799.text: Whoever kills himself will be recompensed in the Hereafter with the means corresponding to his deed.
HAD-2799.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2799.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2799.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ belongs to the sharpest texts of threat against killing oneself and makes its severe prohibition clear. Such Waʿīd texts are understood together with the other texts about Tawḥīd and Allah’s will, and are not extended on one’s own authority into a blanket judgment on an individual case.

HAD-2800.text: Whoever knowingly and falsely swears by a religion other than Islam, upon him lies a severe threat corresponding to what he has uttered.
HAD-2800.narrator: Ṯābit ibn aḍ-Ḍaḥḥāk رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2800.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2800.sharh: The report is an extremely sharp warning against knowingly and falsely adopting another religion as an oath formula. The concrete legal assessment depends on the wording intended, on knowledge, on intent, and on the known rules concerning such statements; the threat text must not be turned mechanically into Takfīr of a specific person.

HAD-2801.text: Whoever kills himself will be recompensed on the Day of Resurrection with the means corresponding to his deed.
HAD-2801.narrator: Ṯābit ibn aḍ-Ḍaḥḥāk رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2801.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2801.sharh: The various wordings of Muslim 110 confirm the same severe Waʿīd against killing oneself. The text describes a threat in the Hereafter; it is not an instruction, and it is not extended into a blanket judgment of Kufr upon every person concerned.

HAD-2802.text: A person is not obligated to a Naḏr concerning something that he does not own.
HAD-2802.narrator: Ṯābit ibn aḍ-Ḍaḥḥāk رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2802.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2802.sharh: A Naḏr requires that its object stand at all within the person’s legal disposal. The Ḥadīṯ denies an obligation concerning something that does not belong to him.

HAD-2803.text: Cursing a believer is compared, in its gravity, with killing him.
HAD-2803.narrator: Ṯābit ibn aḍ-Ḍaḥḥāk رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2803.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2803.sharh: The comparison serves as a massive deterrent against the unjustified Laʿn of a believer. It does not mean equality of all legal consequences between a verbal curse and actual killing.

HAD-2804.text: Whoever sets up a false claim in order thereby to increase his property or his rank, Allah thereby increases for him only the deficiency.
HAD-2804.narrator: Ṯābit ibn aḍ-Ḍaḥḥāk رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2804.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2804.sharh: What is blamed is deliberate false self-presentation for the purpose of worldly increase. In the threat text the expected gain becomes precisely the opposite of its aim.

HAD-2805.text: Only a Muslim soul enters Paradise.
HAD-2805.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2805.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2805.sharh: The sentence attaches the final promise of Paradise to Islam. In context it follows the account of a man whose outwardly impressive fighting alone was no proof of a good end.

HAD-2766.text: Allah is beautiful and loves beauty.
HAD-2766.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2766.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2766.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains that the sentence affirms Allah's perfection and the love of lawful beauty. Beautiful clothing in itself is not Kibr.

HAD-2767.text: Kibr is to reject the truth and to belittle people.
HAD-2767.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2767.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2767.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains baṭar al-ḥaqq as rejection of the truth and ġamṭ an-nās as belittling people. Thus Kibr is defined morally, not through outward beauty.

HAD-2768.text: Whoever carries in the heart Īmān the weight of a mustard seed will not remain in the Fire forever.
HAD-2768.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2768.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2768.sharh: The statement denies eternal remaining in the Fire for the one who possesses the essential core of Īmān; other sins can nevertheless entail punishment.

HAD-2769.text: Whoever carries in the heart Kibr the weight of a mustard seed does not enter Paradise simply.
HAD-2769.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2769.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2769.sharh: The threat shows the gravity of Kibr. For a Muslim who has Īmān it does not automatically mean eternal exclusion from Paradise.

HAD-2770.text: Whoever dies while associating something with Allah enters the Fire.
HAD-2770.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2770.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2770.sharh: Whoever dies upon Širk falls under the threat of the Fire; whoever dies upon Īmān and without Širk stands under the promise of Paradise. Decisive is the state upon which the person dies.

HAD-2771.text: Whoever dies without associating anything with Allah enters Paradise.
HAD-2771.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2771.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2771.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ names Tawḥīd as the basis of the final promise of Paradise. This does not mean that every sinful Muwaḥḥid must enter without prior reckoning or punishment; whoever dies without Širk remains under Allah's will, and his final end is Paradise.

HAD-2772.text: Whoever dies while associating something with Allah enters the Fire.
HAD-2772.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2772.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2772.sharh: Decisive is the state at death: whoever dies upon Širk falls under the threat of the Fire. The direct contrast in the same Ḥadīṯ separates this case from the sinful Muwaḥḥid who dies without Širk.

HAD-2773.text: Whoever meets Allah without associating anything with Him enters Paradise; whoever meets Him with Širk enters the Fire.
HAD-2773.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2773.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2773.sharh: Meeting Allah upon Tawḥīd is the basis of final salvation; meeting Him upon Širk leads to the threat of the Fire. The wording concerns the state of faith upon which the person meets Allah.

HAD-2774.text: Ǧibrīl عليه السلام brought me the glad tidings: Whoever of your Ummah dies without associating anything with Allah enters Paradise.
HAD-2774.narrator: Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2774.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2774.sharh: The glad tidings apply to the one who dies upon Tawḥīd. The following addition concerning grave sins shows that major sins alone do not automatically remove a Muwaḥḥid from Islam; they nevertheless remain sins and can entail punishment.

HAD-2775.text: Even if he has committed Zinā and stolen, the final promise of Paradise remains for the one who dies upon Tawḥīd.
HAD-2775.narrator: Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2775.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2775.sharh: The addition refutes equating every major sin with Kufr akbar. A Muwaḥḥid can fall under punishment because of grave sins, yet if he dies without Širk his final end remains Paradise. The text does not make Zinā and theft lawful or slight.

HAD-2776.text: Whoever says «Lā ilāha illā Allah» and dies upon it enters Paradise, even if he has committed Zinā and stolen.
HAD-2776.narrator: Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2776.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2776.sharh: What is meant is the one who dies upon Tawḥīd. Grave sins do not automatically cancel Tawḥīd; their doer nevertheless remains under Allah's will and can be punished. The promise concerns his final entry into Paradise, not necessarily an entry without prior punishment.

HAD-2777.text: If a combatant declares Islam, he may not be killed after that.
HAD-2777.narrator: al-Miqdād ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2777.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2777.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the spoken sign of Islam grants the person concerned outward protection. Earlier combat actions do not permit ignoring this new, outwardly established protected status out of personal retaliation.

HAD-2778.text: If you kill him after his spoken Islam, he possesses the protection that you previously possessed; and with regard to the outward combat status you are where he was before his profession.
HAD-2778.narrator: al-Miqdād ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2778.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
