HAD-2778.sharh: The statement does not mean that al-Miqdād would automatically become a Kāfir through such a killing. Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ relates the comparison to the outward status regarding protection and the inviolability of blood: the spoken profession of Islam makes the killing forbidden.

HAD-2779.text: Did you kill him after he had said «Lā ilāha illā Allah»?
HAD-2779.narrator: Usāmah ibn Zayd رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2779.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2779.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ grounds the judgment on the outwardly recognizable Islam. Usāmah's assumption that the man had uttered the Tahlīl only out of fear did not remove his outward protected status.

HAD-2780.text: Did you cut open his heart in order to know whether he said it sincerely or not?
HAD-2780.narrator: Usāmah ibn Zayd رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2780.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2780.sharh: People judge what is outwardly recognizable; the hidden intention is known to Allah. Therefore the mere assumption that the Tahlīl had been spoken only out of fear was not permitted to lead to killing.

HAD-2781.text: What will you do with «Lā ilāha illā Allah» when it steps before you on the Day of Resurrection?
HAD-2781.narrator: Ǧundab ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2781.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2781.sharh: The repetition strengthens the inviolability that arises through the outwardly spoken sign of Islam. A mere assumption about the inward does not justify removing this protected status.

HAD-2782.text: Whoever raises a weapon against us is not of us.
HAD-2782.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2782.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2782.sharh: The wording is a grave warning against unlawful armed action against Muslims. «Not of us» here does not mean in a blanket way that every perpetrator leaves Islam; it denies his conformity with the obligatory prophetic way and intensifies the prohibition.

HAD-2783.text: Whoever draws the sword against us is not of us.
HAD-2783.narrator: Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2783.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2783.sharh: Drawing the sword against Muslims is forbidden by a sharp formula of disavowal. The wording serves to deter from this major sin; it is not to be read, without further preconditions, as Takfīr of every single perpetrator.

HAD-2784.text: Whoever raises a weapon against us is not of us.
HAD-2784.narrator: Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2784.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2784.sharh: The repetition through a further Ṣaḥābī underscores the gravity of the prohibition. The formula of disavowal is a threat against the deed and must not, without the known preconditions, be turned into a blanket Takfīr of the individual case.

HAD-2785.text: Whoever raises a weapon against us is not of us; and whoever deceives us is not of us.
HAD-2785.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2785.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2785.sharh: The Prophet ﷺ joins two grave violations of the rights of Muslims: armed aggression and fraudulent deception. «Not of us» here is an especially strong rebuke and a disavowal of the obligatory prophetic conduct, not a blanket judgment of Kufr akbar upon every perpetrator.

HAD-2826.text: You have accepted Islam together with the good that you did before.
HAD-2826.narrator: Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2826.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2826.sharh: Ḥakīm’s earlier good deeds, such as Ṣadaqah, manumission and maintaining kinship, were not dismissed as meaningless in the prophetic reply. The variants 123a–d carry the same core.

HAD-2827.text: Among the good deeds about which Ḥakīm asked were Ṣadaqah, manumission and the maintenance of kinship.
HAD-2827.narrator: Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2827.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2827.sharh: The report names concrete forms of earlier good. Decisive is the prophetic reply that Ḥakīm accepted Islam upon the good he had previously accomplished.

HAD-2828.text: The “Ẓulm” that mixes the Īmān in this verse is here Širk.
HAD-2828.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2828.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2828.sharh: The Ṣaḥābah first understood the verse generally as every wrong against oneself. The Prophet ﷺ explained it through Luqmān’s statement: Širk is a mighty Ẓulm. Thus the concrete Qurʾān term in this context is determined prophetically.

HAD-2829.text: The Ṣaḥābah were very worried because of the verse about Īmān and Ẓulm, until the Prophet ﷺ explained to them that Širk is meant here.
HAD-2829.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2829.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2829.sharh: The reaction of the Ṣaḥābah shows their fear of texts of threat. The prophetic explanation at the same time prevents arbitrarily generalizing a Qurʾān term without its concrete context.

HAD-2830.text: When the Ṣaḥābah were distressed because of the reckoning over what is hidden in the heart, the Prophet ﷺ commanded them: Say: We hear and we obey.
HAD-2830.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2830.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2830.sharh: The Ṣaḥābah found the revelation about inner processes hard. Their stance was not to be contradiction, but submission and obedience; thereupon followed the easing revelation.

HAD-2831.text: The Prophet ﷺ taught, at the hard question about inner thoughts: We hear, we obey and we submit.
HAD-2831.narrator: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2831.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2831.sharh: Muslim 126 confirms the same context of revelation through Ibn ʿAbbās. The reply to the initial burden was Taslīm and obedience, whereupon Allah revealed relief.

HAD-2832.text: Allah does not burden any soul beyond its capacity.
HAD-2832.narrator: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2832.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2832.sharh: The report links the submission of the believers with the revelation that Allah imposes on no one what he cannot bear. This forms the basis of the chapter in Muslim.

HAD-2833.text: Allah has pardoned this Ummah the inner whisperings so long as they are not spoken or put into deed.
HAD-2833.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2833.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2833.sharh: Involuntary inner thoughts are not treated like spoken or carried-out acts. 127b repeats the same wording, 127c only the same report through further chains.

HAD-2834.text: A mere Waswasah that is neither spoken nor carried out is not reckoned to the person as a deed.
HAD-2834.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2834.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2834.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ distinguishes between thoughts that occur and the willful passage to word or deed. Precisely this boundary prevents treating mere unwanted notions as a completed sin.

HAD-2835.text: Some Ṣaḥābah found in themselves thoughts that seemed to them so grave that they did not want to utter them. The Prophet ﷺ said: “That is clear Īmān.”
HAD-2835.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2835.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2835.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains that it is not the Waswasah itself that is praised. The clear sign of Īmān lies in the heart loathing these whisperings, feeling them as grave and shrinking from uttering them.

HAD-2836.text: The Šayṭān comes to one of you and asks: “Who created this? Who created that?”, until he asks: “Who created your Lord?”
HAD-2836.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2836.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2836.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains the stepwise Waswasah as the Šayṭān’s attempt to lead the person from questions about created causes to an inadmissible question about the Creator Himself. The error lies in transferring the rules of the created onto Allah.

HAD-2837.text: When this Waswasah reaches the point: “Who created your Lord?”, he should seek refuge with Allah and stop with that.
HAD-2837.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2837.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2837.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains two means of protection: istiʿāḏah with Allah and the conscious breaking off of the chain of thought. The servant should not expand the satanic whispering further, but turn away from it.

HAD-2838.text: Whoever seizes the right of a Muslim by a false oath, for him Allah has made the Fire a severe threat and has denied him Paradise.
HAD-2838.narrator: Abū Umāmah Iyās ibn Thaʿlabah al-Ḥāriṯī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2838.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2838.sharh: Al-Māzirī treats the Ḥadīṯ as an extremely severe warning against the joining of a false oath and the unlawful appropriation of others’ rights. The wording is a Waʿīd text about a major sin; it is not understood as a blanket statement that every sinful Muwaḥḥid necessarily remains excluded from Paradise forever.

HAD-2839.text: When it was asked whether this severe warning also applies to something slight, the Prophet ﷺ said: “Even for a twig from the Arāk tree.”
HAD-2839.narrator: Abū Umāmah Iyās ibn Thaʿlabah al-Ḥāriṯī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2839.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2839.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains the mention of the small Arāk twig as excluding the notion that slight material values may be taken by lying or a false oath. The inviolability of another’s right does not depend on whether the value appears great.

HAD-2840.text: Whoever swears an oath in order to appropriate wealth thereby, while he lies sinfully in doing so, will meet Allah while He is angry with him.
HAD-2840.narrator: al-Ašʿaṯ ibn Qays رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2840.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2840.sharh: Al-Māzirī treats the statement as a severe warning against the deliberate false swearing by which another’s wealth is obtained. The anger of Allah is here especially emphasized because of the joining of lie, oath and wrong.

HAD-2841.text: When a man asked what he should do if someone wanted to take his wealth, the Prophet ﷺ said: “Do not give him your wealth.”
HAD-2841.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2841.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2841.sharh: Al-Māzirī understands the statement within the defense against a present unlawful attack on protected wealth. It establishes no right to later retaliation or private penal power, but concerns the defensive repelling of the attacker within the legal limits.

HAD-2842.text: When the man asked: “And if he fights against me?”, the Prophet ﷺ said: “Then defend yourself against him.”
HAD-2842.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2842.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2842.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains this as the defensive repelling of an actual attacker. The statement does not concern vigilante justice or later retaliation; the defense remains bound to necessity and the lawful limits of the concrete danger.

HAD-2843.text: When the man asked: “And if he kills me?”, the Prophet ﷺ said: “Then you are a Šahīd.”
HAD-2843.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2843.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2843.sharh: Al-Māzirī assigns the promise to the one who is killed in a lawful defense against an unlawful attacker. The rank of Šahīd is here tied to the defensive situation, not to seeking combat.

HAD-2844.text: When the man asked: “And if I kill him?”, the Prophet ﷺ said about the unlawful attacker: “Then he is in the Fire.”
HAD-2844.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2844.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2844.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains the threat in the context of the one who attacks knowingly and unlawfully and is killed in the continuing attack. The text concerns this concrete situation of aggression and is no general permission to punish people privately or to judge their final individual outcome without the known conditions.

HAD-2845.text: There is no servant to whom Allah entrusts responsibility for people and who dies deceitful and faithless toward them, except that Allah denies him Paradise.
HAD-2845.narrator: Maʿqil ibn Yasār رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2845.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2845.sharh: Al-Māzirī treats the Ḥadīṯ as a severe warning to everyone to whom people are entrusted: responsibility demands sincere care and Naṣīḥah instead of deception. The wording is a Waʿīd text about a major sin and is not understood as proof of a blanket eternal exclusion of every sinful Muwaḥḥid from Paradise.

HAD-2866.text: His veil is light; were He to remove it, the radiance of His Face would encompass everything of His creation as far as His gaze reaches.
HAD-2866.narrator: Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2866.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2866.sharh: The narration affirms the Ḥiǧāb of light and mentions the radiance of His Face. The attributes are affirmed according to the text, without Takyīf or equating with the creation.

HAD-2867.narrator: Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2867.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2867.sharh: The closing of the Ḥadīṯ describes the comprehensive divine perception. It stands in connection with Allah’s perfection, His watchfulness, and His sovereignty.

HAD-2868.text: Allah rejoices over the Tawbah of His servant more strongly than someone who, after complete hopelessness, finds his lost mount again.
HAD-2868.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2868.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2868.sharh: The comparison serves to make the greatness of Allah’s joy over the Tawbah understandable. The divine attribute is affirmed without equating it with created joy.

HAD-2869.text: Allah rejoices over the Tawbah of His servant when he returns to Him.
HAD-2869.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2869.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2869.sharh: The report emphasizes Allah’s great grace toward the repentant servant. Tawbah is not merely permitted, but loved by Allah.

HAD-2870.text: Out of overwhelming joy a person can misspeak; in the Ḥadīṯ the man accidentally said the opposite of what he wanted to say.
HAD-2870.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2870.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2870.sharh: The slip of the tongue arose expressly from extreme joy and not from an intended statement of belief. The report is therefore an important evidence that wording, intention, and state are not to be separated from one another.

HAD-2871.text: Allah stretches out His Hand in the night so that the one who sinned by day may repent, and by day so that the one who sinned in the night may repent.
HAD-2871.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2871.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2871.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ shows the continually open door of Tawbah. The transmitted attribute is affirmed without defining its manner or equating it with the attributes of creation.

HAD-2872.text: The door of Tawbah remains open until the sun rises from its west.
HAD-2872.narrator: Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2872.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2872.sharh: The report links the general acceptance of Tawbah with an eschatological limit. Until this great sign, the way of turning back remains open in principle.

HAD-2873.text: Whoever repents before the sun rises from its west, Allah accepts his Tawbah.
HAD-2873.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2873.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2873.sharh: The narration names the same eschatological limit in a direct form. It is a call not to postpone Tawbah.

HAD-2874.text: A man who had killed a hundred people asked about Tawbah; a knowledgeable man told him that nothing stood between him and Tawbah.
HAD-2874.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2874.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2874.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ shows the breadth of Allah’s forgiveness even after enormous sins, when the Tawbah is sincere. It does not relativize the sin, but opens the way to genuine turning back.

HAD-2875.text: The repentant one was commanded to leave the place of evil and to go to people who serve Allah.
HAD-2875.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2875.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2875.sharh: Tawbah here included a concrete change of surroundings: removal from the place that favored the sin, and turning toward righteous company. This underscores that Tawbah requires a real turning back.

HAD-2876.text: The man who had killed a hundred people sincerely set out on the way to Tawbah and to a righteous place.
HAD-2876.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2876.speaker: It was transmitted:
HAD-2876.sharh: The sincerity of his turning back showed itself not only in the wish, but in the actual departure away from the bad surroundings toward people of obedience.

HAD-2877.text: When the repentant man died on the way, the angels of mercy and the angels of punishment disputed over him.
HAD-2877.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2877.speaker: It was transmitted:
HAD-2877.sharh: The report shows the significance of his actual state at death: as a repentant one he had turned his heart to Allah and had practically begun the turning back.

HAD-2878.text: The repentant man was found nearer to the land of the righteous and thereby belonged to them.
HAD-2878.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2878.speaker: It was transmitted:
HAD-2878.sharh: The narration closes with Allah’s mercy toward the one who turns back sincerely. It is no license for killing, but an evidence against despair of Tawbah.

HAD-2879.text: On the Day of Resurrection, Muslim people with enormous sins receive Allah’s forgiveness.
HAD-2879.narrator: Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2879.speaker: It was transmitted:
HAD-2879.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ emphasizes the breadth of Allah’s forgiveness. It lifts neither responsibility nor the prohibition of grave sins, but describes divine forgiveness in the hereafter.

HAD-2880.text: The Prophet ﷺ described for the Muslim a deliverance from the Fire on the Day of Resurrection.
HAD-2880.narrator: Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2880.speaker: It was transmitted:
HAD-2880.sharh: The various versions of Muslim 2767 are understood within the frame of Allah’s forgiveness and His final salvation of the believers; they do not establish a human transfer of personal guilt onto the uninvolved.

HAD-2881.text: The believer is brought near to his Lord on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah has him acknowledge his sins.
HAD-2881.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2881.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2881.sharh: The report describes a special, private reckoning of the believer. Allah confronts him with his sins without exposing him before the whole of creation.

HAD-2882.text: Allah says to the believer about his sins: I concealed them for you in the Dunyā, and today I forgive them for you.
HAD-2882.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2882.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2882.sharh: Satr and Maġfirah are joined in the Ḥadīṯ: Allah covered the believer’s sins in this world and forgives them for him on the Day of Resurrection.

HAD-2883.text: The forgiven believer is given the book of his good deeds on the Day of Resurrection.
HAD-2883.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2883.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2883.sharh: After the private acknowledgment and forgiveness of his sins, the believer receives his writ of good deeds. The report joins reckoning with divine mercy.

HAD-2884.text: It is proclaimed about the Kuffār and the Munāfiqūn before the creation that they have lied about Allah.
HAD-2884.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2884.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2884.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ contrasts the private covering of the believing sinner with the public exposure of those who denied Allah or hypocritically lied about Him. It is no basis for an unsubstantiated Takfīr of particular persons.

HAD-2885.text: Kaʿb remained behind from the campaign to Tabūk without a valid excuse, although at that time he had sufficient strength and means.
HAD-2885.narrator: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2885.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-2885.sharh: Kaʿb رضي الله عنه did not gloss over his failure. Precisely his open acknowledgment of his own guilt forms the starting point of his later accepted Tawbah.

HAD-2906.text: Umm Misṭaḥ informed ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها about the Ifk talk; thereby her illness became even more severe.
HAD-2906.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2906.sharh: Knowledge of the slander weighed heavily on ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها. The report shows the real harm that an unproven violation of honor can cause to the person affected.

HAD-2907.text: When ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها learned of the slander, she asked the Prophet ﷺ for permission to go to her parents and examine the facts.
HAD-2907.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2907.sharh: She sought clarification from her family instead of herself passing rumors on. The report documents her effort to obtain certainty about what had occurred.

HAD-2908.text: Usāmah ibn Zayd رضي الله عنه said about the family of the Prophet ﷺ that he knew of them only good.
HAD-2908.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2908.sharh: Usāmah spoke on the basis of what he actually knew. This is a counter-image to suspicions without proof.

HAD-2909.text: Barīrah رضي الله عنها was asked about ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها and said that she had seen nothing that would give cause for such a suspicion.
HAD-2909.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2909.sharh: Direct questioning of a person with actual closeness yielded no incriminating circumstance. The report underlines the difference between verifiable knowledge and a circulating claim.

HAD-2910.text: The Prophet ﷺ declared publicly that he knew only good about his wife and about Ṣafwān رضي الله عنه.
HAD-2910.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2910.sharh: The Prophet ﷺ expressly recorded what was known to him about their actual uprightness. The slander did not become proof by mere repetition.

HAD-2911.text: When a dispute arose between al-Aws and al-Ḫazraǧ because of the Ifk matter, the Prophet ﷺ calmed both sides until they fell silent.
HAD-2911.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2911.sharh: The report shows that tribal loyalty can let a factual matter escalate. The Prophet ﷺ worked against the escalation and brought the groups to calm.

HAD-2912.text: The Prophet ﷺ said to ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها: If you are innocent, Allah will make your innocence manifest; if someone has sinned, he should ask Allah for forgiveness and repent.
HAD-2912.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2912.sharh: Before the revelation arrived, no final decision was made from mere supposition. At the same time the general way of Tawbah in the case of an actual sin was explained.

HAD-2913.text: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها held fast to her innocence and sought help from Allah in her distress.
HAD-2913.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2913.sharh: Her reaction joins the certainty of her own innocence with Ṣabr and the request for Allah’s help against false descriptions.

HAD-2914.text: The revelation concerning the matter of ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها came even before the Prophet ﷺ left the room.
HAD-2914.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2914.sharh: The final clarification of her innocence took place through Waḥy. Thereby the matter was not decided on the basis of the social mood, but through revelation.

HAD-2915.text: The Prophet ﷺ announced to ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها the glad tiding: Allah has declared your innocence.
HAD-2915.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2915.sharh: The Baraʾah of ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها is in the report expressly confirmed as divine and thereby does not belong to the realm of mere historical difference of opinion.

HAD-2916.text: Allah revealed, concerning the Ifk slander, verses from Sūrat an-Nūr, through which ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها was acquitted of the accusation.
HAD-2916.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2916.sharh: The Qurʾān verses are the authoritative revelatory basis of her Baraʾah. The Ḥadīṯ expressly reports that these verses were revealed because of the Ifk matter.

HAD-2917.text: Abū Bakr رضي الله عنه first swore no longer to support Misṭaḥ financially after his participation in the slander.
HAD-2917.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2917.sharh: The report shows Abū Bakr’s understandable personal reaction to the grave violation of his daughter’s honor. The subsequent revelation, however, corrected the lasting cessation of his charity.

HAD-2918.text: After the revelation «Do you not want Allah to forgive you?» Abū Bakr رضي الله عنه said: Yes, by Allah, I love that Allah forgives me.
HAD-2918.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2918.sharh: Abū Bakr placed the hope of Allah’s own forgiveness above his personal hurt. The Qurʾān appeal led directly to a change in his action.

HAD-2919.text: Abū Bakr رضي الله عنه resumed the financial support for Misṭaḥ and declared that he would no longer withdraw it from him.
HAD-2919.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2919.sharh: Forgiveness did not remain with Abū Bakr a mere statement. He put the revelation into practice and restored the support previously granted.

HAD-2920.text: Zaynab bint Ǧaḥš رضي الله عنها said about ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها: By Allah, I know only good about her.
HAD-2920.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2920.sharh: Although there was rivalry among the wives, Zaynab رضي الله عنها guarded her tongue from an unproven accusation and testified only to the good that she actually knew.

HAD-2921.text: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها said that Allah had preserved Zaynab bint Ǧaḥš رضي الله عنها, through her fear of Allah, from participation in the slander.
HAD-2921.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2921.sharh: The report links the guarding of the tongue with Waraʿ. Personal rivalry did not justify for Zaynab a statement without knowledge.

HAD-2922.text: Ḥamnah bint Ǧaḥš, by contrast, took part in the Ifk talk and thereby belonged to those who fell in it.
HAD-2922.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2922.sharh: The report sets two different reactions within the same family side by side: Waraʿ protects, while participation in unproven slander harms the person himself.

HAD-2923.text: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها did not want Ḥassān ibn Ṯābit رضي الله عنه to be insulted in her presence.
HAD-2923.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2923.sharh: Despite his participation in the Ifk matter, ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها preserved the later recognition of his service to the Prophet ﷺ. The report warns against undifferentiated lasting disparagement.

HAD-2924.text: The revelation of the innocence of ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها came after a long time of severe trial and public slander.
HAD-2924.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2924.sharh: The delay of the revelation did not mean a confirmation of the rumor. The report shows that the lack of immediate clarification must never serve as proof of an accusation.

HAD-2925.text: The Ḥadīṯ al-Ifk shows that the honor of a Muslim is not annulled by rumors, group pressure, or repeated claims.
HAD-2925.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2925.sharh: The entire report sets verifiable knowledge, testimony, and finally revelation against mere rumors. The central lesson is summarized from the individual events of the authentic report, without inventing a new legal ruling beyond the wording.

HAD-3066.text: People will seek refuge at the Kaʿbah, although they possess neither a protecting power nor a great number nor equipment.
HAD-3066.narrator: One of the mothers of the believers رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-3066.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3066.sharh: The report describes a future group that seeks refuge at the House of Allah and is outwardly weak. The record limits itself to this prophecy and derives from it no identification of present-day groups.

HAD-3067.text: An army will attack the House; when it reaches a desert plain, it will be swallowed by the earth.
HAD-3067.narrator: Ḥafṣah Umm al-Muʾminīn رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-3067.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3067.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats the ḫasf as an event still to occur and truly announced. The various Isnād variants and wording variants are brought together into one core of the statement.

HAD-3068.text: Among the people on the way with the army are those who take part knowingly, those who are compelled, and travelers; they perish in one common worldly destruction.
HAD-3068.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3068.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains al-mustabṣir as the one who recognizes the matter and intends it knowingly, and al-maǧbūr as the one who is compelled. The common outward destruction therefore does not mean the same otherworldly judgment for all.

HAD-3069.text: Although they perish together, they will be raised before Allah according to their intentions.
HAD-3069.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3069.sharh: The report expressly separates the common worldly event from the otherworldly outcome. Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ's explanation of the different groups of persons makes clear that the intention remains decisive for the final judgment.

HAD-3070.text: The Prophet ﷺ saw the places of coming Fitan among the houses of Madīnah as numerous as places upon which rain falls.
HAD-3070.narrator: Usāmah ibn Zayd رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3070.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3070.sharh: The simile of the places of rain denotes the great number and wide spread of the Fitan. The report is a prophetic warning against their occurrence and not a call to turn toward them.

HAD-3071.text: In coming Fitan the one sitting is better than the one standing, the one standing better than the one walking, and the one walking better than the one hurrying.
HAD-3071.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3071.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3071.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the gradation as a sign of the greatness of the danger: the more someone enters into the Fitnah, the greater is his share of its danger. The Ḥadīṯ calls for distance from such unclear Fitan.

HAD-3072.text: Whoever exposes himself to a Fitnah and looks out for it will be seized by it; whoever finds a place of refuge should seek protection there.
HAD-3072.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3072.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3072.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that exposing oneself to the Fitnah increases its power over the person. The instruction is therefore to keep distance and to use a permitted way of protection, instead of seeking the Fitnah.

HAD-3073.text: When a Fitnah occurs, the owner of camels should withdraw to his camels, the owner of sheep to his sheep, and the owner of land to his land.
HAD-3073.narrator: Abū Bakrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3073.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3073.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ places this instruction within the principle of keeping away from the described Fitnah and not being drawn into it. The forms of possession mentioned are concrete possibilities of withdrawal in the wording of the Ḥadīṯ.

HAD-3074.text: Whoever has neither animals nor land should make the edge of his sword unusable with a stone and escape the Fitnah if he can.
HAD-3074.narrator: Abū Bakrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3074.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3074.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ mentions, for the instruction about the sword's edge, both the literal meaning and the explanation as an image for refraining from fighting. In the context of the Ḥadīṯ the flight from the described Fitnah stands in the foreground.

HAD-3075.text: When two Muslims confront each other with their swords and both want to kill the other, the killer and the killed are in the Fire; the reason for the killed one is that he too wanted to kill his companion.
HAD-3075.narrator: Abū Bakrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3075.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3075.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ links the warning to an actual intention to kill on both sides. It must not be applied blanket-wise to every armed conflict or to someone who does not take part with this intention.

HAD-3076.text: Allah let the Prophet ﷺ see the eastern and western ends of the earth.
HAD-3076.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3076.sharh: The report is a prophetic communication about the extent shown by Allah. Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats this in connection with the later-mentioned expansions of the Ummah; the statement is not interpreted geographically beyond the wording.

HAD-3077.text: The Prophet ﷺ announced that the dominion of his Ummah would reach those eastern and western regions that were shown to him.
HAD-3077.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3077.sharh: The statement is formulated as a prophecy about the expansion of Muslim dominion. It is not a guarantee for every age or every single state, but concerns the announced reaching of these spaces.

HAD-3078.text: The red treasure and the white treasure were given to the Prophet ﷺ.
HAD-3078.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3078.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ places the two treasures in the context of the great realms and their wealth. The record stays with the transmitted wording and avoids speculative additional interpretations.

HAD-3079.text: Allah granted the Prophet ﷺ for his Ummah that it will not be completely destroyed by a general famine.
HAD-3079.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3079.sharh: The granted request concerns the complete annihilation of the Ummah by a general famine. It does not mean that individual lands or generations never experience hunger or severe crises of supply.

HAD-3080.text: Allah granted that an external enemy will not completely destroy the Ummah and wipe out its whole, even if many opponents gather against it.
HAD-3080.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3080.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ understands the assurance as protection from the complete destruction of the entire Ummah by an external opponent. It does not exclude local defeats, losses, or temporary foreign rule.

HAD-3081.text: The Prophet ﷺ warned that people from the Ummah itself will kill one another and take one another captive.
HAD-3081.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3081.sharh: The close of the Ḥadīṯ shifts the central danger from a complete external destruction to internal conflicts. The text is a warning against Fitnah and mutual bloodshed, not a justification of them.

HAD-3082.text: The Prophet ﷺ mentioned three immense Fitan that would leave nothing untouched.
HAD-3082.narrator: Ḥuḏayfah ibn al-Yamān رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3082.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3082.sharh: Ḥuḏayfah's report stresses the extraordinary reach of certain future Fitan. The transmission here gives a warning of their severity, without the record making unsubstantiated historical identifications.

HAD-3083.text: Among the announced Fitan there would also be such as pass over the people like the violent winds of a hot summer.
HAD-3083.narrator: Ḥuḏayfah ibn al-Yamān رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3083.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3083.sharh: The simile describes the force and rapid spread of the Fitan. Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats such images as a warning against comprehensive trials, not as an instruction to equate concrete events with them without evidence.

HAD-3084.text: The Prophet ﷺ reported to his Companions in a gathering about things that would happen until the coming of the Hour; some preserved them in memory and others forgot them.
HAD-3084.narrator: Ḥuḏayfah ibn al-Yamān رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3084.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3084.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ establishes the extensive prophetic instruction about future events and, at the same time, the differing ability of the listeners to remember. Not every later claim about the future is thereby automatically confirmed as prophetic.

HAD-3085.text: The Prophet ﷺ spoke repeatedly to the Companions from after Fajr until sunset and reported about what has passed and what is coming; the most knowledgeable about it was the one who had preserved it best.
HAD-3085.narrator: Abū Zayd ʿAmr ibn Aḫṭab رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3085.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3085.sharh: The report stresses the scope and seriousness of the prophetic teaching. The Companions differed according to how much of it they could preserve; the transmission itself remains the measure for what is securely attributed.

HAD-3026.text: All wealth that I have given to a servant is lawful for him.
HAD-3026.narrator: ʿIyāḍ ibn Ḥimār al-Muǧāšiʿī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3026.speaker: Allah says in the Ḥadīṯ qudsī:
HAD-3026.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats the statement in connection with the prohibitions that people later invented. The principle of the Ḥadīṯ is that Allah’s original grant may not be declared forbidden on one’s own authority through human or satanic innovations.

HAD-3027.text: I created all My servants as ḥunafāʾ.
HAD-3027.narrator: ʿIyāḍ ibn Ḥimār al-Muǧāšiʿī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3027.speaker: Allah says in the Ḥadīṯ qudsī:
HAD-3027.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ assigns ḥunafāʾ to the original straight orientation toward Allah. The following sentence of the Ḥadīṯ itself explains that it is the intervention of the devils that leads people away from this original orientation.

HAD-3028.text: Then the devils came to them and led them away from their religion.
HAD-3028.narrator: ʿIyāḍ ibn Ḥimār al-Muǧāšiʿī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3028.speaker: Allah says in the Ḥadīṯ qudsī:
HAD-3028.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the phrase «fa-ǧtālat-hum» as diverting and leading away. The sentence describes the devils as the cause of people being turned aside from the original straight religious orientation.

HAD-3029.text: The devils forbade them what I had made lawful for them.
HAD-3029.narrator: ʿIyāḍ ibn Ḥimār al-Muǧāšiʿī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3029.speaker: Allah says in the Ḥadīṯ qudsī:
HAD-3029.sharh: The clause shows a form of misguidance: what is lawful is declared forbidden without a proof from revelation. Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats this, together with the following Širk passage, as part of the satanic leading away from Allah’s religion.

HAD-3030.text: The devils commanded them to associate with Me something for which I had not sent down any proof at all.
HAD-3030.narrator: ʿIyāḍ ibn Ḥimār al-Muǧāšiʿī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3030.speaker: Allah says in the Ḥadīṯ qudsī:
HAD-3030.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ cites the wording as the climax of the satanic deviation: besides invented Ḥarām, the misguidance reaches Širk. The Ḥadīṯ expressly indicates for this the absence of every proof-permission sent down by Allah.

HAD-3031.text: Allah looked upon the inhabitants of the earth and detested their condition — Arabs and non-Arabs alike — except some remaining people of the Scripture.
HAD-3031.narrator: ʿIyāḍ ibn Ḥimār al-Muǧāšiʿī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3031.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported from his Lord:
HAD-3031.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ places the statement as a description of the widespread religious corruption before the sending of the Prophet ﷺ. The expressly mentioned «remnants of the People of the Book» form the exception within that situation of that time.

HAD-3032.text: I have sent you in order to test you and to test others through you.
HAD-3032.narrator: ʿIyāḍ ibn Ḥimār al-Muǧāšiʿī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3032.speaker: Allah says to the Prophet ﷺ:
HAD-3032.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ understands the sending of the Prophet ﷺ here at once as a test of his steadfastness in the commission and as a test of the people through their response to his message.

HAD-3033.text: I sent down to you a Book that water does not blot out; you recite it awake and in sleep.
HAD-3033.narrator: ʿIyāḍ ibn Ḥimār al-Muǧāšiʿī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3033.speaker: Allah says to the Prophet ﷺ:
HAD-3033.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats the wording as an indication of the special preservation of the Qurʾān: its transmission and recitation do not depend on a single writable writing-support that water could blot out.

HAD-3034.text: Spend, then I will spend for you.
HAD-3034.narrator: ʿIyāḍ ibn Ḥimār al-Muǧāšiʿī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3034.speaker: Allah says to the Prophet ﷺ:
HAD-3034.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ cites the statement in connection with Allah’s support of the Prophet ﷺ. It links spending in obedience to Allah with the promise of divine provision and support.

HAD-3035.text: Among the inhabitants of Paradise is a ruler who acts justly, gives, and is enabled toward the good.
HAD-3035.narrator: ʿIyāḍ ibn Ḥimār al-Muǧāšiʿī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3035.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3035.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ connects in this first category power with justice and beneficence. What is praised is not mere authority, but a rule marked by balance, giving, and divine support toward what is right.

HAD-3036.text: Among the inhabitants of Paradise is a merciful man with a soft heart toward every relative and every Muslim.
HAD-3036.narrator: ʿIyāḍ ibn Ḥimār al-Muǧāšiʿī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3036.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3036.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains this category through Raḥmah and softness of the heart. The Ḥadīṯ links kindness to close kin with a mercy that goes beyond that toward Muslims in general.

HAD-3037.text: Among the inhabitants of Paradise is an abstinent person who, despite having his own family, holds himself back from what is forbidden.
HAD-3037.narrator: ʿIyāḍ ibn Ḥimār al-Muǧāšiʿī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3037.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3037.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ understands the wording as praise of ʿiffah: despite need and family responsibility, the person maintains self-restraint and keeps away from unlawful gain and unworthy desire.

HAD-3038.text: Among the inhabitants of the Fire is the weak one without firm resolve, who merely follows others and strives neither for family nor for wealth.
HAD-3038.narrator: ʿIyāḍ ibn Ḥimār al-Muǧāšiʿī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3038.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3038.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains this first group as people without sustaining resolve and without an independent moral orientation, who attach themselves to others and show neither responsible attachment nor ordered striving.

HAD-3039.text: Among the inhabitants of the Fire is the traitor from whom no desire, however slight, remains hidden without his committing betrayal on account of it.
HAD-3039.narrator: ʿIyāḍ ibn Ḥimār al-Muǧāšiʿī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3039.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3039.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ highlights the connection between hidden greed and ḫiyānah: even a small material advantage can be, for this person, an occasion to betray entrusted rights or relationships.

HAD-3040.text: Among the inhabitants of the Fire is a man who, morning and evening, is intent on deceiving you with regard to your family and your wealth.
HAD-3040.narrator: ʿIyāḍ ibn Ḥimār al-Muǧāšiʿī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3040.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3040.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats here a disposition to fraud that has become lasting: what is described is not a single lapse, but the recurring deception concerning the most important worldly spheres of protection — family and wealth.

HAD-3041.text: He also mentioned, among the traits of the inhabitants of the Fire, stinginess or lying.
HAD-3041.narrator: ʿIyāḍ ibn Ḥimār al-Muǧāšiʿī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3041.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3041.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ leaves the transmitted variant situation as it stands. What is decisive is that the report names a further blameworthy character trait; the app therefore expressly preserves the «or» of the transmission.

HAD-3042.text: Among the inhabitants of the Fire is the coarse person who speaks obscenely.
HAD-3042.narrator: ʿIyāḍ ibn Ḥimār al-Muǧāšiʿī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3042.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3042.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ assigns the wording to a coarse, wounding, and shameless manner of speech. The report thereby places a bad tongue and vile conduct among the grave character traits against which warning is given.

HAD-3043.text: Allah revealed to me that you should be humble, so that none exalts himself over another and none treats another unjustly.
HAD-3043.narrator: ʿIyāḍ ibn Ḥimār al-Muǧāšiʿī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3043.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3043.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats this additional wording as a clear link between Tawāḍuʿ and the prohibition of two consequences of arrogance: boastful self-exaltation over others and unjust transgression of their rights.

HAD-3044.text: When one of you dies, his place is shown to him morning and evening: a place in Paradise if he belongs to its inhabitants, or a place in the Fire if he belongs to its inhabitants. It is said to him: This is your place, until Allah raises you to it on the Day of Resurrection.
HAD-3044.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3044.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3044.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ cites the Ḥadīṯ as evidence for the state in the Barzaḫ: the deceased is repeatedly shown his future abode. The text distinguishes this vision before the Resurrection from the final entry after the Resurrection.

HAD-3045.text: This Ummah will be tested in its graves.
HAD-3045.narrator: Zayd ibn Ṯābit رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3045.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3045.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ expressly places the report among the evidences for the trial in the grave. The statement confirms that after death a real trial takes place in the Barzaḫ, without details being invented beyond what is transmitted in the text.

HAD-3086.text: The Hour will not come until the Euphrates uncovers a mountain of gold.
HAD-3086.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3086.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3086.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ announces a specific future event at the Euphrates. Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats it as a sign and a Fitnah; the record does not of its own accord identify present-day finds or projects with this report.

HAD-3087.text: When the Euphrates uncovers the mountain of gold, people will fight over it, and ninety-nine out of a hundred will be killed.
HAD-3087.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3087.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3087.sharh: The high number of the dead shows the extreme Fitnah that arises from greed for this treasure. The Ḥadīṯ thereby warns against taking part in this fighting and against the delusion of hoping to be oneself the one survivor.

HAD-3088.text: Whoever is present at the uncovered gold of the Euphrates should take nothing of it.
HAD-3088.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3088.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3088.sharh: The explicit instruction protects against the Fitnah connected with this treasure. It is bound to the event described in the Ḥadīṯ and is not transferred to arbitrary finds at the Euphrates.

HAD-3089.text: The Prophet ﷺ announced that Iraq would withhold its dirhams and its Qafīz, aš-Šām its Mudd and Dīnār, and Egypt its Irdabb and Dīnār.
HAD-3089.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3089.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3089.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats the statement as a prophetic report about later changes in levies and supply. The various measures and coins are understood as the respective regional names of the levies; the record does not set a modern dating of its own accord.

HAD-3090.text: The Hour will not come until the Romans land at al-Aʿmāq or Dābiq.
HAD-3090.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3090.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3090.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ names concrete places in connection with a future great confrontation. The record keeps to the transmitted prophecy and does not identify present-day conflicts with it without a clear proof.

HAD-3091.text: From Madīnah an army will march out against them, consisting of the best people of the earth of that time.
HAD-3091.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3091.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3091.sharh: The report describes the special standing of this future army in precisely this announced event. No general claim of rank about later armed groups is derived from it.

HAD-3092.text: In that battle one third will flee, one third will fall as especially distinguished martyrs, and one third will be victorious and conquer Constantinople.
HAD-3092.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3092.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3092.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ divides the army into three clearly different groups. Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats this as part of the end-time prophecy; the statements about flight, martyrdom and victory remain bound to this concrete event.

HAD-3093.text: After the conquest of Constantinople a false call will sound, that the Dajjāl has appeared among their families; only later, when they reach aš-Šām, does he actually come forth.
HAD-3093.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3093.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3093.sharh: The report expressly distinguishes between the initially false report and the later actual appearance of the Dajjāl. This urges that, even in great events, not every alarming message be accepted without examination.

HAD-3094.text: When ʿĪsā ibn Maryam عليه السلام descends and the Dajjāl sees him, the latter will perish; Allah will kill the Dajjāl by means of ʿĪsā عليه السلام.
HAD-3094.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3094.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3094.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ confirms the descent of ʿĪsā عليه السلام and the end of the Dajjāl as real end-time events. The presentation is left as it has been authentically transmitted, without speculative reinterpretation.

HAD-3095.text: The Prophet ﷺ said that, at the entry of the Hour, the Romans will be very numerous among the people.
HAD-3095.narrator: al-Mustawrid al-Qurašī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3095.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3095.sharh: The statement is a prophetic report about a condition near the Hour. The subsequent comment of ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ is a separate statement of a Ṣaḥābī and is not mixed here with the prophetic word.

HAD-3096.text: The Prophet ﷺ announced: You will fight the Arabian Peninsula, and Allah will give you the victory; then Persia, and Allah will give you the victory.
HAD-3096.narrator: Nāfiʿ ibn ʿUtbah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3096.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3096.sharh: The four-part prophecy names a sequence of conquests. This record brings the first two limbs together, without transferring them to present-day political projects.

HAD-3097.text: The Prophet ﷺ thereafter announced the confrontation with the Romans and said that Allah would give the victory.
HAD-3097.narrator: Nāfiʿ ibn ʿUtbah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3097.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3097.sharh: The statement is the third limb of the transmitted sequence. It remains as a prophecy in the context of the text and is not used as a general call to present violence.

HAD-3098.text: The Prophet ﷺ finally announced the confrontation with the Dajjāl and said that Allah would give the victory.
HAD-3098.narrator: Nāfiʿ ibn ʿUtbah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3098.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3098.sharh: This is the fourth limb of the prophecy. Nāfiʿ understood from it that the appearance of the Dajjāl would lie after the events named before; the record keeps the prophetic wording and this placement apart.

HAD-3099.text: The Hour will not come until ten great signs appear: smoke, the Dajjāl, the animal, sunrise in the west, the descent of ʿĪsā عليه السلام, Yaʾǧūǧ and Maʾǧūǧ, three great subsidences of the earth, and a fire that drives the people to the place of their gathering.
HAD-3099.narrator: Ḥuḏayfah ibn Usayd al-Ġifārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3099.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3099.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats this transmission as a compilation of great signs immediately before the Hour. Variants of the tenth naming are brought together in the source citation, without producing additional cards from them.

HAD-3100.text: The Hour will not come until a fire comes forth from the land of the Ḥiǧāz, whose light illuminates the necks of the camels in Buṣrā.
HAD-3100.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3100.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3100.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ announces a clear event from the Ḥiǧāz. The record limits itself to the transmitted statement and does not of its own accord declare a particular historical or modern fire to be the final fulfillment.

HAD-3101.text: The Hour will not come until the dwelling areas of Madīnah have extended to Īhāb or Yahāb.
HAD-3101.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3101.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3101.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ names the spatial extension of Madīnah as a future sign. The precise historical identification is not claimed beyond the transmitted place name.

HAD-3102.text: Severe drought does not mean only the failure of rain: it can rain abundantly, while the earth nevertheless brings forth nothing.
HAD-3102.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3102.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3102.sharh: The Prophet ﷺ describes a form of severe hardship in which the visible occasion of the rain is present, but the expected benefit fails to come. The core of the statement concerns scarcity of provision despite precipitation.

HAD-3103.text: The Prophet ﷺ pointed toward the east and said that Fitnah would come forth from there, where the horns of Satan rise.
HAD-3103.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3103.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3103.sharh: The various versions repeat the same prophetic core. Therefore only one card is made from them; the statement about direction and Fitnah is not multiplied by variants of the chains of transmission.

HAD-3104.text: The Hour will not come until the women of Daws move again around Ḏū al-Ḫalaṣah; it was an idol sanctuary that Daws venerated in the Ǧāhiliyyah.
HAD-3104.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3104.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3104.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ announces the return of a concrete pre-Islamic idol worship. It describes a future event and legitimizes neither idolatry nor unproven equations with arbitrary places.

HAD-3105.text: Night and day will not end until al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā are worshipped again.
HAD-3105.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3105.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ shows that open idolatry will occur again before the Hour. The statement stands in connection with the later taking away of the believers.

HAD-2886.text: Kaʿb رضي الله عنه kept postponing the preparation until the Prophet ﷺ set out with the army and he remained behind.
HAD-2886.narrator: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2886.speaker: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2886.sharh: The report shows the danger of repeated postponement despite the ability being present. The omission did not arise from inability, but from continued hesitation.

HAD-2887.text: When the Prophet ﷺ returned from Tabūk, those who had stayed behind came with excuses; Kaʿb رضي الله عنه, by contrast, chose the truth.
HAD-2887.narrator: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2887.speaker: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2887.sharh: Kaʿb’s Tawbah began with Ṣidq. He recognized that an invented excuse might bring short-term approval, but would not avert Allah’s displeasure.

HAD-2888.text: Kaʿb رضي الله عنه told the Prophet ﷺ openly that he had no excuse and that he had never been stronger or wealthier than at that time.
HAD-2888.narrator: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2888.speaker: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2888.sharh: The complete acknowledgment of one’s own responsibility is a core of the report. Kaʿb shifted the blame neither onto circumstances nor onto other people.

HAD-2889.text: The Prophet ﷺ said about Kaʿb رضي الله عنه: This one has spoken the truth.
HAD-2889.narrator: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2889.speaker: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2889.sharh: The prophetic confirmation highlights Kaʿb’s truthfulness in contrast to the excuses that were put forward. The immediate consequence was nevertheless not an instant lifting of all consequences.

HAD-2890.text: Concerning Kaʿb ibn Mālik, Murārah ibn ar-Rabīʿ and Hilāl ibn Umayyah رضي الله عنهم, the decision was at first deferred.
HAD-2890.narrator: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2890.speaker: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2890.sharh: The three were distinguished from those whose outward excuses were accepted at first. Their case remained suspended until Allah decided about their Tawbah.

HAD-2891.text: The Muslims were commanded not to speak with Kaʿb and his two companions رضي الله عنهم.
HAD-2891.narrator: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2891.speaker: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2891.sharh: The temporary social avoidance was ordered in this concrete prophetic case. It is not transferred as a general private authority to isolate any persons without a corresponding basis.

HAD-2892.text: Kaʿb رضي الله عنه felt the earth, despite its vastness, to be narrow after the people had ceased to associate with him.
HAD-2892.narrator: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2892.speaker: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2892.sharh: The report describes the inner weight of the trial and the effect of the ordered distancing upon the one who repents sincerely.

HAD-2893.text: Kaʿb رضي الله عنه sought from his beloved relative Abū Qatādah رضي الله عنه the confirmation that he loved Allah and His Messenger.
HAD-2893.narrator: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2893.speaker: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2893.sharh: Despite his fault, Kaʿb held fast to his love for Allah and His Messenger ﷺ. The report separates the sin committed from a hasty claim that his entire Īmān was thereby annulled.

HAD-2894.text: A messenger of the king of Ġassān offered Kaʿb رضي الله عنه refuge; Kaʿb recognized in it a further trial and burned the letter.
HAD-2894.narrator: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2894.speaker: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2894.sharh: Kaʿb did not take the political invitation during his distress as a way out. His reaction shows steadfastness and the refusal to evade the trial by turning away from the Muslim community.

HAD-2895.text: After forty days Kaʿb رضي الله عنه was commanded to keep away from his wife as well, without a divorce being meant by that.
HAD-2895.narrator: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2895.speaker: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2895.sharh: The report expressly distinguishes between a temporary separation and Ṭalāq. The measure belonged to this particular, revealed case of trial.

HAD-2896.text: On the fiftieth morning the acceptance of Kaʿb’s رضي الله عنه Tawbah was announced to him.
HAD-2896.narrator: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2896.speaker: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2896.sharh: The long trial ended with an express divine acceptance of the Tawbah. The report joins patience, truthfulness and hope in Allah’s relief.

HAD-2897.text: When Kaʿb رضي الله عنه heard the glad tidings, he fell into Suǧūd out of gratitude.
HAD-2897.narrator: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2897.speaker: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2897.sharh: His first reaction to the news of the accepted Tawbah was thanks toward Allah. This shows to whom Kaʿb ascribed the deliverance from his distress.

HAD-2898.text: The Prophet ﷺ said to Kaʿb رضي الله عنه that this was the best day for him since the day his mother had given birth to him.
HAD-2898.narrator: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2898.speaker: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2898.sharh: The acceptance of the Tawbah is set forth as an extraordinary grace. The worth of the day lay in Allah’s forgiveness and renewed acceptance.

HAD-2899.text: Kaʿb رضي الله عنه recognized that Allah had saved him because of his truthfulness.
HAD-2899.narrator: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2899.speaker: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2899.sharh: Ṣidq appears at the end of the report as the central means of his deliverance. The truth was at first bound up with a severe trial, but it finally led to the revealed acceptance of his Tawbah.

HAD-2900.text: Kaʿb رضي الله عنه bound himself, as part of his Tawbah, to speak only the truth for the rest of his life.
HAD-2900.narrator: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2900.speaker: Kaʿb ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2900.sharh: The accepted Tawbah led to a lasting ethical obligation. Kaʿb did not understand the deliverance through Ṣidq as a one-time event, but as a ground for lasting truthfulness.

HAD-2901.text: The Prophet ﷺ drew lots among his wives when he went on a journey; on this campaign the lot fell to ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها.
HAD-2901.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2901.sharh: The report shows the practical upholding of justice among the wives by drawing lots for a journey.

HAD-2902.text: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها lost her necklace on the way back and remained behind while searching, while the caravan moved on.
HAD-2902.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2902.sharh: The beginning of the event is described as an actual circumstance of the journey. The later slander did not arise from suspicious conduct that she herself had set.

HAD-2903.text: Ṣafwān ibn al-Muʿaṭṭal رضي الله عنه found ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها left behind; he spoke no word to her except the Istirǧāʿ and led her mount to the army.
HAD-2903.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2903.sharh: The report stresses the restraint of Ṣafwān رضي الله عنه and preserves the actual circumstances against the later slander.

HAD-2904.text: ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl took the greatest share in the Ifk slander.
HAD-2904.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2904.sharh: The narration names the main bearer of the slander. The finding rests here on the authentic report and must not be used as a pattern for unfounded accusations of others.

HAD-2905.text: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها was ill for a month and at first knew nothing of the rumor that the people were spreading.
HAD-2905.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2905.sharh: The report shows how a harm to reputation can circulate while the innocent person concerned herself knows nothing of it.

HAD-2926.text: The Šayṭān has given up hope that those who pray on the Arabian Peninsula worship him.
HAD-2926.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2926.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2926.sharh: Al-Māzirī treats the report in the context of the temptations of the Šayṭān. The statement describes his despair regarding a general return of those who pray on the Arabian Peninsula to his direct worship; it does not mean that no individual deviation or sin can occur there anymore.

HAD-2927.text: The Šayṭān, however, hopes to sow discord and incitement among them.
HAD-2927.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2927.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2927.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains the remaining strategy of the Šayṭān through Taḥrīš: enmity, dispute, and mutual incitement. The Ḥadīṯ thereby warns against breaking up the religious community through personal and social conflicts.

HAD-2928.text: Iblīs sets his throne upon the water.
HAD-2928.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2928.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2928.sharh: Al-Māzirī treats this depiction as part of the prophetic report about the organization of temptation by Iblīs. The text is left as it was authentically transmitted, without adding speculative details beyond the reported wording.

HAD-2929.text: Then Iblīs sends out his troops so that they lead the people into temptation.
HAD-2929.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2929.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2929.sharh: Al-Māzirī places this passage within the warning against the many paths of Fitnah. The report shows that temptation is described not only as a single impulse, but as a continued effort to lead people into sin and dispute.

HAD-2930.text: Those of his helpers who cause the greatest Fitnah stand nearest to Iblīs.
HAD-2930.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2930.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2930.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains the ranking in the report according to the extent of the Fitnah caused. The more strongly people are led away by a temptation from obedience, cohesion, and right, the greater this success appears from the perspective of Iblīs.

HAD-2931.text: One comes to Iblīs and reports what he has done; Iblīs says to him: You have done nothing significant.
HAD-2931.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2931.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2931.sharh: Al-Māzirī, through the gradation in the report, brings out that Iblīs values certain sins as especially effective means of destruction. Not every temptation stirred by his helpers has the same weight for him.

HAD-2932.text: Another reports that he did not leave a man until he had separated him from his wife.
HAD-2932.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2932.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2932.sharh: Al-Māzirī treats separation between spouses as an especially grave form of Fitnah, because it destroys an existing family bond and often brings further harm to the family and those around them.

HAD-2933.text: Iblīs draws near to himself the one who has separated the spouses, and praises him for it.
HAD-2933.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2933.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2933.sharh: Al-Māzirī understands the special nearness and recognition from Iblīs as a strengthening of the warning: the destruction of a marriage belongs to the aims that this report presents as especially grave satanic Fitnah.

HAD-2934.text: To each of you a companion from the Ǧinn is assigned.
HAD-2934.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2934.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2934.sharh: Al-Māzirī treats the Qarin as part of the human being's trial. The statement explains the continuing nearness of satanic whispering, without thereby removing the person's own responsibility for his decisions.

HAD-2935.text: They asked: Also to you, O Messenger of Allah? He answered: Also to me.
HAD-2935.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2935.speaker: The Ṣaḥābah asked the Prophet ﷺ:
HAD-2935.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains that the Prophet ﷺ also mentions the Qarin, yet immediately describes the special divine help by which he was protected from its harmful influence. The text shows both the generality of the trial and the special protection of the Prophet ﷺ.

HAD-2936.text: Allah helped me against my Qarin; therefore my Qarin commands me only good.
HAD-2936.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2936.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2936.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains Allah's special help for the Prophet ﷺ as protection from the harmful influence of the Qarin. The report affirms the prophetic preservation, without denying the general existence of the trial for other people.

HAD-2937.text: To every human being a companion from the Ǧinn and a companion from the angels are assigned.
HAD-2937.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2937.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2937.sharh: Al-Māzirī places the transmission variant in the overall context of whispering, trial, and divine support. Despite the companions, the human being remains responsible and is obliged to accept the good and ward off the evil.

HAD-2938.text: When the Prophet ﷺ went out one night, ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها felt Ġayrah.
HAD-2938.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-2938.sharh: Al-Māzirī treats the Ġayrah in the report as a real human stirring which the Prophet ﷺ perceived and addressed. The text also shows that such stirrings must not be left to themselves when the Šayṭān seeks to raise them to false suspicion or conduct.

HAD-2939.text: The Prophet ﷺ asked ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها: Has your Šayṭān come to you? He confirmed that she too has a Qarin.
HAD-2939.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2939.sharh: Al-Māzirī links the question of the Prophet ﷺ with the general principle of the Qarin. The report makes clear that emotional stirrings can be a point of entry for whispering and should therefore be placed under knowledge and self-control.

HAD-2940.text: None of you is saved by his deeds alone.
HAD-2940.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2940.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2940.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains that deeds are not understood as an independent price that creates a claim to salvation against Allah. Obedience is a cause and a sign, while entry into Paradise and final salvation come through Allah's Raḥmah and Faḍl.

HAD-2941.text: The Prophet ﷺ too is not saved by his deeds alone, but by Allah encompassing him with Raḥmah and favor.
HAD-2941.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2941.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2941.sharh: Al-Māzirī stresses with this answer the complete dependence of all creatures on Allah's favor. Even the highest deeds of the Prophet ﷺ establish no independent claim; his salvation and elevation are from Allah's Raḥmah and Faḍl.

HAD-2942.text: Strive to act correctly and uprightly.
HAD-2942.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2942.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2942.sharh: Al-Māzirī understands Saddidū as orientation toward what is right and as hitting the prescribed path as completely as possible. The servant should act correctly in earnest, without relying on his deed itself.

HAD-2943.text: If you do not attain perfection, draw as near to it as possible.
HAD-2943.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2943.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2943.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains Qāribū as drawing near to what is right when complete perfection is not possible. The Sunnah requires earnest steadfastness within human ability and protects against despair because of unavoidable imperfection.

HAD-2944.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2944.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2944.sharh: Al-Māzirī links the glad tidings with the balanced path between earnest action and hope in Allah's Raḥmah. The servant should neither trust proudly in his deeds nor despair because of his own imperfection.

HAD-2945.text: The Prophet ﷺ stood in prayer so long that his feet swelled.
HAD-2945.narrator: al-Muġīrah ibn Šuʿbah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2945.speaker: al-Muġīrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2945.sharh: Al-Māzirī treats the long standing of the Prophet ﷺ as an expression of intense ʿIbādah and gratitude. The report shows that forgiveness already granted did not lead to negligence, but further increased his gratitude.

HAD-2946.text: Should I not then be a grateful servant?
HAD-2946.narrator: al-Muġīrah ibn Šuʿbah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2946.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2946.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains the reply of the Prophet ﷺ as an expression of Šukr. The forgiveness already granted did not lead to less ʿIbādah, but to still greater gratitude toward Allah.

HAD-2947.text: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reminded and instructed his listeners on certain days instead of every day.
HAD-2947.narrator: Šaqīq رحمه الله reported about ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-2947.speaker: Šaqīq رحمه الله reported:
HAD-2947.sharh: Al-Māzirī understands the measured timing of the Mawʿiẓah as a pedagogical Sunnah. Knowledge should be conveyed regularly, yet so that attention, capacity to receive, and appreciation remain.

HAD-2948.text: We love your instruction and would wish that you teach us every day.
HAD-2948.narrator: Šaqīq رحمه الله reported about ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-2948.speaker: The listeners said to Ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-2948.sharh: Al-Māzirī shows by this request that the benefit and popularity of an instruction do not automatically mean repeating it without measure. Good teaching also takes into account the endurance and attention of the learners.

HAD-2949.text: Only the concern of boring you holds me back.
HAD-2949.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-2949.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-2949.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains the concern about boredom as a legitimate reason to limit the frequency of admonitions. The aim is not as much speech as possible, but lasting benefit without weariness.

HAD-2950.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ chose certain days for the admonition, because he feared that we might otherwise feel weariness.
HAD-2950.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2950.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه said about the Prophet ﷺ:
HAD-2950.sharh: Al-Māzirī explains this as a model for teachers and preachers: admonition is planned so that hearts remain receptive. Excessive repetition can weaken the effect even when the content is good.

HAD-2951.text: Allah has prepared for His righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has imagined.
HAD-2951.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2951.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported from his Lord عز وجل:
HAD-2951.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the text as an indication that the reality of the gifts of Paradise prepared for the righteous surpasses human experience and imagination. What was described through revelation is only a part of what Allah keeps hidden in readiness.

HAD-2952.text: In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider would travel for a hundred years without traversing it completely.
HAD-2952.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2952.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2952.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the journey of a hundred years as an expression of the immense extent of this tree and its shade. The additional description of the swift, trained mount reinforces that the size here goes far beyond earthly measures.

HAD-2953.text: Allah calls out to the inhabitants of Paradise: O inhabitants of Paradise!
HAD-2953.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2953.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2953.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats this address as part of the final honoring of the inhabitants of Paradise. After entry into the lasting grace there follows a direct address from their Lord, which prepares for the greatest additional gift.

HAD-2954.text: At Your service, our Lord, and all good lies in Your hand.
HAD-2954.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2954.speaker: The inhabitants of Paradise reply:
HAD-2954.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ places the reply within the complete acknowledgment of Allah’s favor. The inhabitants reply with readiness, praise, and the confession that all good comes from Allah.

HAD-2955.text: Are you pleased? They say: How should we not be pleased, when You have given us what You have given to none of Your creatures?
HAD-2955.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2955.speaker: Allah asks the inhabitants of Paradise:
HAD-2955.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the reply as an expression of complete satisfaction with the gift of Paradise already received. Precisely after they confess their complete satisfaction, a gift that stands still higher is announced to them.

HAD-2956.text: Shall I not give you something that is still better than that?
HAD-2956.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2956.speaker: Allah says:
HAD-2956.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ emphasizes that the gift which follows goes beyond the already immeasurable bodily and visible gifts of Paradise. The dialogue prepares for Allah’s lasting good pleasure.

HAD-2957.text: I let My good pleasure rest upon you, and thereafter I shall never again be angry with you.
HAD-2957.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2957.speaker: Allah says to the inhabitants of Paradise:
HAD-2957.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ highlights this promise as one of the highest gifts of Paradise: lasting Riḍwān without later wrath. Thereby the security of the inhabitants becomes complete, and every fear of loss or change is ended.

HAD-2958.text: The inhabitants of Paradise will see the people in the high chambers above them as you see a bright star in the sky.
HAD-2958.narrator: Sahl ibn Saʿd and Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2958.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2958.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the comparison with the shining stars as an image of the great height and clear visibility of the higher ranks of Paradise. The Ḥadīṯ confirms differing ranks among the inhabitants of Paradise.

HAD-2959.text: These high ranks are not reserved for the prophets alone; people who believe in Allah and confirm the messengers will reach them.
HAD-2959.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2959.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2959.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the high chambers do represent extraordinary ranks, yet they are not reserved exclusively for the prophets. True Īmān and confirmation of the messengers are among the causes by which other believers can reach such high degrees.

HAD-2960.text: Among the people of my Ummah who love me especially strongly there will be people after me, one of whom would wish to see me even if it cost him his family and his wealth.
HAD-2960.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2960.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2960.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ understands the statement as an extraordinary love of later believers for the Prophet ﷺ despite the absence of a personal meeting. The readiness to give up great worldly goods for a single glance at him makes clear the strength of this love.

HAD-2961.text: In Paradise there is a market which its inhabitants visit every Friday.
HAD-2961.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2961.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2961.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the “market” as a gathering place of the inhabitants of Paradise, not as a place of earthly trade out of need. The designation describes their regular gathering and the additional joy received there.

HAD-2962.text: There a wind blows that touches their faces and garments, and thereby they increase in beauty and grace.
HAD-2962.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2962.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2962.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that the wind mentioned brings the inhabitants additional beauty and a paradisiacal fragrance. He links the naming of the wind with the wind known among the Arabs, which brings clouds and desired rain.

HAD-2963.text: When they return from the market to their families, both sides have increased in beauty and grace.
HAD-2963.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2963.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2963.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the mutual recognition of the increased beauty as part of the renewing enjoyment of Paradise. The inhabitants experience no decrease, but a continued increase of joy, beauty, and well-being.

HAD-2964.text: The first group that enters Paradise will shine like the full moon on a night of the full moon; those who follow them will be like the brightest stars in the sky.
HAD-2964.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2964.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
