HAD-2964.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ brings together the wordings of this report in which the first group is compared with the full moon and the following groups with especially bright stars. The comparison describes the extraordinary brightness and beauty of their appearance at their entry into Paradise.

HAD-2965.text: The inhabitants of these groups neither relieve themselves in Paradise nor do they urinate; they do not blow their noses and they do not spit.
HAD-2965.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2965.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2965.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the wordings about blowing the nose and spitting linguistically and thereby confirms the literal statement of the report: the bodily states of the inhabitants of Paradise are free of the excretions of earthly life that are felt to be impure or bothersome.

HAD-2966.text: Their combs are of gold, their sweat is fragrant with musk, and aloeswood is used for their censers.
HAD-2966.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2966.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2966.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that by «Rašaḥ» their sweat is meant and that «al-Alūwah» denotes the Indian aloeswood used as incense. With this the Ḥadīṯ describes fragrance and purity instead of the earthly concomitants of the body.

HAD-2967.text: Their disposition is like that of a single man; their stature corresponds to that of their father Ādam: sixty cubits.
HAD-2967.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2967.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2967.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ points to the two transmitted readings: one refers to the shared disposition and concord, the other to the same form. The following statement of sixty cubits joins the bodily description to the form of their father Ādam.

HAD-2968.text: The inhabitants of Paradise eat and drink. Their food does not lead to earthly excretions, but to belching and to sweat whose fragrance is like musk.
HAD-2968.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2968.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2968.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ cites this report as evidence that the joys of Paradise are real and sensory and remain lasting. Eating and drinking there are true enjoyment, yet without the impure and burdensome consequences of the earthly body.

HAD-2969.text: Tasbīḥ and Taḥmīd are instilled in the inhabitants of Paradise as easily as breathing is instilled in them.
HAD-2969.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2969.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2969.sharh: Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Qurṭubī explains that this Tasbīḥ does not arise from obligation, for Paradise is not a place of Taklīf. The comparison with breathing means that the remembrance of Allah is instilled in the inhabitants easily and without effort, as breathing is natural for a person.

HAD-2970.text: Whoever enters Paradise will live in enjoyment and experience no hardship; his clothing does not wear out and his youth does not pass away.
HAD-2970.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2970.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2970.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats this statement in the chapter on the permanence of the enjoyment of Paradise: there is no passage from prosperity to hardship, no wearing out of clothing, and no aging. The state of the inhabitants remains without the transience of this world.

HAD-2971.text: A caller proclaims to the inhabitants of Paradise: You remain healthy and will never fall ill; you live and never die; you remain young and never grow old; you enjoy and never experience hardship.
HAD-2971.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī and Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-2971.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2971.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains «you remain young and do not grow old» as the lasting continuance of youth. «You experience no hardship» means that neither distress nor a worsening of their state reaches the inhabitants of Paradise.

HAD-2972.text: For the believer there is in Paradise a tent of a single hollowed pearl, whose extent is sixty miles.
HAD-2972.narrator: Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2972.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2972.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains «hollowed» as opened within and made empty. He further explains the tent as a round house and expressly treats the extraordinary size as part of the description of this tent of Paradise.

HAD-2973.text: In the various areas of this tent of Paradise are relatives of the believer; because of its immense expanse some do not see the others, while the believer visits them.
HAD-2973.narrator: Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2973.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2973.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the «corners» as various sides or areas. That the inhabitants do not see one another he traces to the enormous expanse and the great distances within this tent.

HAD-2974.text: Sayḥān, Ǧayḥān, the Euphrates and the Nile are among the rivers of Paradise.
HAD-2974.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2974.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2974.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ names two possible interpretations: either the statement is connected with the spread of Īmān over the lands of these rivers and their inhabitants, or it is left in its outward sense, according to which these rivers have a supply from Paradise. He refers in this to the reports about the Nile and the Euphrates at the Isrāʾ.

HAD-2975.text: People will enter Paradise whose hearts are like the hearts of birds.
HAD-2975.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2975.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2975.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ names as a possible meaning the tenderness and weakness of their hearts; the comparison may also denote their strong fear and awe, since birds are especially easily startled and cautious. He connects this with people whose hearts are deeply moved by admonition and godly fear.

HAD-2976.text: Allah created Ādam in his form; his length was sixty cubits.
HAD-2976.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2976.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2976.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ understands the immediately following statement «sixty cubits» as a clarification of the wording and explains that the pronoun in this report refers back to Ādam: he was created from the beginning in the form that he had, without passing through the developmental stages of his descendants.

HAD-2977.text: Go to that group of seated angels, greet them, and hear how they return your greeting; for this will be your greeting and the greeting of your offspring.
HAD-2977.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2977.speaker: Allah said to Ādam عليه السلام:
HAD-2977.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ cites the greeting scene as part of the same report. The text makes the Salām that Ādam learned from the angels expressly the greeting form of his offspring.

HAD-2978.text: Everyone who enters Paradise will enter in the form of Ādam and with a length of sixty cubits; thereafter the body size of people continued to decrease until today.
HAD-2978.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2978.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2978.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ connects the Paradise form of people with the form of Ādam named in the report and explains that Ādam did not attain this form only through phases of growth. The concluding formulation then expressly reports the later decrease of human body size.

HAD-2979.text: On the Day of Resurrection Jahannam will be brought forth; it has seventy thousand reins, and at each rein seventy thousand angels pull.
HAD-2979.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2979.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2979.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ also transmits, regarding this report, the early isnād-critical discussion of the marfūʿ wording. For the app, therefore, the wording transmitted by Muslim is reproduced exactly as the Ṣaḥīḥ-Muslim text, without additional speculation about the nature of the reins or the how of this event.

HAD-2980.text: The fire that the children of Ādam kindle is only one part of seventy parts of the heat of Jahannam.
HAD-2980.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2980.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2980.sharh: The direct classical commentary places the statement within the description of the extraordinary heat of Jahannam. The comparison takes the familiar earthly fire as the measure and makes clear that the heat of the fire of the Hereafter far exceeds this measure.

HAD-2981.text: Jahannam was intensified beyond the earthly fire by sixty-nine further parts; each of these parts has the same heat as the earthly fire.
HAD-2981.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2981.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2981.sharh: The second numerical statement completes the comparison of the Ḥadīṯ: to the one known heat of the earthly fire, sixty-nine parts of the same kind are added. The report thus serves to make clear the extraordinary severity of the heat of Jahannam.

HAD-2982.text: A stone was thrown into Jahannam seventy years ago and fell downward the whole time.
HAD-2982.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2982.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2982.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the «Waǧbah» heard in the report as the sound of a violent fall or impact. The long fall of the stone is part of the prophetic description of the immense depth of Jahannam.

HAD-2983.text: The stone has now reached the bottom of Jahannam; the sound that was heard was its impact.
HAD-2983.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2983.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2983.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ points to the two transmitted formulations: the stone «reached» the bottom or «fell» there. Both versions explain the sound heard before as the conclusion of its long fall.

HAD-2984.text: Among the inhabitants of the Fire there are people whom the fire reaches up to the ankles.
HAD-2984.narrator: Samurah ibn Ǧundub رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2984.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2984.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats the various heights to which the fire reaches as a graded description of the measure of punishment. The report thus shows that the intensity of the punishment is not the same for all those affected.

HAD-2985.text: Among them there are people whom the fire reaches up to the knees.
HAD-2985.narrator: Samurah ibn Ǧundub رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-2985.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-2985.sharh: The second Muslim wording expressly adds the level up to the knees. Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ places it, together with the other levels, as an indication of differing degrees of punishment.

HAD-3006.text: If he were to swear an oath by Allah, Allah would have his oath fulfilled.
HAD-3006.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3006.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said about this little-regarded servant:
HAD-3006.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that a person's low standing among people does not contradict his high standing with Allah. The fulfillment of his oath, or of his insistent Duʿāʾ, points to Allah's special honoring of this servant.

HAD-3007.text: Why does one of you strike his wife like a slave, and then perhaps still seek her closeness at the end of the same day?
HAD-3007.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Zamʿah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3007.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3007.sharh: Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Qurṭubī explains the statement as a sharp disapproval of harsh treatment of the wife. Whoever humiliates her with hard blows destroys closeness, affection, and mutual familiarity, even though a short time later he again expects marital closeness from her.

HAD-3008.text: Why does one of you laugh at something that he himself does?
HAD-3008.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Zamʿah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3008.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3008.sharh: An-Nawawī derives from this the prohibition of laughing at another person's unintentional passing of wind. The proper Adab is to pass over it, to continue the conversation, and not to expose the person concerned any further.

HAD-3009.text: I saw ʿAmr ibn Luḥayy in the Fire, dragging his intestines behind him.
HAD-3009.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3009.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3009.sharh: Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Qurṭubī treats the report about ʿAmr ibn Luḥayy in connection with his alteration of the religion of Ibrāhīm and the pre-Islamic animal customs that he introduced. «Quṣbahu» means his intestines.

HAD-3010.text: He was the first who released the animals as a Sāʾibah for the idols.
HAD-3010.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3010.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said about ʿAmr ibn Luḥayy:
HAD-3010.sharh: Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Qurṭubī connects the report with the pre-Islamic practices of releasing animals for false deities and thereby arbitrarily forbidding their permitted use. The Ḥadīṯ names ʿAmr ibn Luḥayy as one origin of this religious innovation.

HAD-3011.text: If you live long enough, you will see people carrying whips like cattle tails in their hands.
HAD-3011.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3011.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3011.sharh: Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Qurṭubī explains «you will soon see» as the announcement of a state soon to come. The description of the whips marks people who mistreat others with such striking instruments.

HAD-3012.text: They go out in the morning under Allah's wrath and return in the evening under His wrath, or His curse.
HAD-3012.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3012.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said about these people:
HAD-3012.sharh: Al-Qurṭubī treats these wordings as a severe threat against those who unjustly torment people. The two versions in Muslim mention wrath, displeasure, and curse, and thereby intensify the gravity of their deed.

HAD-3013.text: The people will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised.
HAD-3013.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3013.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains «ġurlan» as uncircumcised. The meaning is that at the Ḥašr people are restored as they were originally created, without worldly possessions or adornment.

HAD-3014.text: The matter will be too tremendous for men and women to look at one another there.
HAD-3014.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ answered:
HAD-3014.sharh: The commentary places this reply among the terrors of the Ḥašr: people are so occupied with the tremendous situation and with what awaits them that ordinary attention to one another recedes.

HAD-3015.text: You will meet Allah: on foot, barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised.
HAD-3015.narrator: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3015.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3015.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ connects this wording with the general description of the Ḥašr: people will be gathered before Allah without the usual worldly provisions and brought back to their original bodily state.

HAD-3016.text: The first human being to be clothed on the Day of Resurrection is Ibrāhīm عليه السلام.
HAD-3016.narrator: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3016.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3016.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats this special distinction of Ibrāhīm عليه السلام within the description of the Ḥašr. The statement confirms a specific honoring of Ibrāhīm on the Day of Resurrection, without a general order of all the other honors being derived from it.

HAD-3017.text: Men from my Ummah will be brought and taken to the left side.
HAD-3017.narrator: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3017.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3017.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that this passage must not be applied wholesale to all the Ṣaḥābah. The subsequent words of the report limit those concerned to people who deviated after the Prophet ﷺ or who accepted newly introduced things.

HAD-3018.narrator: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3018.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ then says:
HAD-3018.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ reads the address together with the reply that the Prophet ﷺ did not know what these people changed after him. The expression alone is therefore not a statement that the known whole of his faithful Ṣaḥābah is meant.

HAD-3019.text: You do not know what they newly introduced, or changed, after you.
HAD-3019.narrator: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3019.speaker: Thereupon it is said to the Prophet ﷺ:
HAD-3019.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ uses this additional wording to explain that the warning refers to people who deviated from his path after the death of the Prophet ﷺ. The statement also shows that not every later action of his Ummah is known to him from his own knowledge.

HAD-3020.text: Since your separation from them, they did not cease turning back on their heels.
HAD-3020.narrator: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3020.speaker: It is further said:
HAD-3020.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that this wording supports the interpretation as referring to people who actually fell back and deviated from the path of the Prophet ﷺ. Thereby the preceding address «my companions» is made precise by the further wording of the Ḥadīṯ.

HAD-3021.text: The people will be gathered in three ways: hoping and fearing; two on one camel, three on one camel, four on one camel, and ten on one camel.
HAD-3021.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3021.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3021.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that this Ḥašr described in the Ḥadīṯ still takes place in this world, shortly before the Hour. The mention of mounts, of riding together, and of movement distinguishes it from the later Ḥašr after the Resurrection.

HAD-3022.text: The remaining people will be driven together by a fire; it stays with them where they spend the night, rest, spend the morning, and reach the evening.
HAD-3022.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3022.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3022.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains this fire as the fire that drives people at the end of the world to their place of gathering. That it spends the night with them and rests with them confirms, for him, that this event still takes place before the final end of this world.

HAD-3023.text: When the people stand before the Lord of the worlds, one of them will stand in his sweat up to the middle of his ears.
HAD-3023.narrator: Ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3023.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3023.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that on the Day of Resurrection people may be affected by sweat to different degrees according to their deeds. The description belongs to the terrors of standing before Allah.

HAD-3024.text: On the Day of Resurrection the sweat will go seventy fathoms deep into the earth and reach the mouths or the ears of the people.
HAD-3024.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3024.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3024.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ mentions as a possibility that each person is affected by his own sweat according to fear, situation, and deeds; likewise the sweat of the people may gather, while the burden is distributed differently according to their deeds.

HAD-3025.text: On the Day of Resurrection the sun will be brought near to the people to the distance of one mile; they will then stand in the sweat at different depths according to their deeds, some up to the ankles, some up to the knees, some up to the hips, and some such that the sweat reaches their mouth.
HAD-3025.narrator: al-Miqdād ibn al-Aswad رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3025.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3025.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the different heights of the sweat as a graded burden according to the deeds of the people. The report therefore names several degrees, up to a sweat that reaches the mouth like a bridle; the differences belong to the individual reckoning and the severity of that Day.

HAD-3106.text: Allah will send a good, pleasant wind by which everyone dies in whose heart there is even only the weight of a mustard seed of Īmān.
HAD-3106.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3106.sharh: In the report the good wind is an end-time mercy for the believers. The statement is not transferred to ordinary deaths or natural events.

HAD-3107.text: After the people with Īmān have been taken away, those without good remain and return to the religion of their forefathers.
HAD-3107.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3107.sharh: The report links the revival of idolatry to a time in which the believers have already been taken away. This prevents an isolated reading of individual parts of the sentences.

HAD-3108.text: A time will come in which the killer does not know why he killed, and the one killed does not know why he was killed.
HAD-3108.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3108.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3108.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ describes extreme confusion and senseless bloodshed. The nearly identical second version is not counted as a separate record.

HAD-3109.text: The Prophet ﷺ called this state Harǧ — general killing and bloodshed — and, in the case described, warned of the Fire for the perpetrator and the one killed.
HAD-3109.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3109.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3109.sharh: The warning belongs to the specifically described Harǧ, in which people kill one another without a lawful cause. It is not applied wholesale to every person killed, regardless of intention and situation.

HAD-3110.text: A man from Abyssinia, described as Ḏū as-Suwayqatayn, will destroy the Kaʿbah.
HAD-3110.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3110.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3110.sharh: Muslim transmits the same core in several versions. They are brought together; the statement remains an end-time prophecy and is not anticipated as history.

HAD-3111.text: The Hour will not come until a man from Qaḥṭān appears and directs the people with his staff.
HAD-3111.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3111.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3111.sharh: The expression of the staff describes rule and leadership. The record names no historical candidate without a clear proof.

HAD-3112.text: Days and nights will not pass until a man named al-Ǧahǧāh rules.
HAD-3112.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3112.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3112.sharh: The report names the name and the rule as a future event. Further biographical speculation is avoided.

HAD-3113.text: Before the Hour the Muslims will fight people whose faces are described like hammered shields and who wear shoes of hair.
HAD-3113.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3113.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3113.sharh: The physical features repeated several times are treated as one shared core of the statement. Variants of the same image are not multiplied as separate cards.

HAD-3114.text: Among the people who will be fought before the Hour will be those with small eyes, broad flat noses and reddish faces; in further versions, clothing and shoes of hair are mentioned.
HAD-3114.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3114.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3114.sharh: The versions complete one shared descriptive image. They are gathered on one card, instead of counting every small wording variant separately.

HAD-3115.text: At the end of time a caliph will distribute wealth generously without counting it.
HAD-3115.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī and Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3115.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3115.sharh: Several paths of transmission give the same core: a great abundance of wealth and a generous distribution by a later caliph. The versions are therefore brought together.

HAD-3116.text: The Prophet ﷺ announced to ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir رضي الله عنه that a rebellious group would kill him.
HAD-3116.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī and Umm Salamah رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3116.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3116.sharh: The numerous paths confirm the same prophetic core of the statement. The record calls the group named in the wording bāġiyah and avoids further political generalizations.

HAD-3117.text: The Prophet ﷺ warned that a certain group from Qurayš would cause severe destruction among people of his Ummah.
HAD-3117.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3117.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3117.sharh: The warning refers to the group meant in the Ḥadīṯ and must not be transferred wholesale to Qurayš as a whole.

HAD-3118.text: When asked what one should do toward this dangerous group, the Prophet ﷺ directed that one keep away from them.
HAD-3118.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3118.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3118.sharh: The instruction for action stands directly in the same report as the warning about this group. It is an independent core of the statement and is therefore recorded separately.

HAD-3119.text: The Prophet ﷺ announced that after the end of Kisrā no Kisrā would remain after him.
HAD-3119.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3119.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3119.sharh: The various versions repeat the same prophetic core about the end of this ruling line. They are not counted more than once.

HAD-3120.text: The Prophet ﷺ announced that after the end of Qayṣar no Qayṣar would remain after him.
HAD-3120.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3120.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3120.sharh: This part belongs to the same report as the statement about Kisrā, yet it is its own prophetic core about the second great power.

HAD-3121.text: The Prophet ﷺ swore that the treasures of Kisrā and Qayṣar would be spent or distributed in the path of Allah.
HAD-3121.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3121.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3121.sharh: The statement links the announced political upheavals with the later disposal of their treasures. It is not understood as a general statement about any state wealth.

HAD-3122.text: A group of the Muslims or of the believers will obtain the treasure of the family of Kisrā in the White Palace.
HAD-3122.narrator: Ǧābir ibn Samurah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3122.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3122.sharh: Muslim transmits this statement expressly as a prophetic announcement. The parallel version is not counted in addition.

HAD-3123.text: Before the Hour, seventy thousand from Banū Isḥāq will go to a city one side of which lies on land and the other at the sea.
HAD-3123.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3123.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3123.sharh: The report describes a concrete future city and a specific number. The record refrains from further geographical identifications that go beyond the wording.

HAD-3124.text: At this city they will not fight with weapons and will not shoot arrows; rather they say Lā ilāha illā Allah and Allahu akbar, whereupon the way in opens to them.
HAD-3124.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3124.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3124.sharh: This unusual course is part of the same end-time prophecy. It must not be read as a general military procedure outside this announced event.

HAD-3125.text: While they are distributing the booty after entering the city, the news reaches them that the Dajjāl has come forth; thereupon they leave everything behind and turn back.
HAD-3125.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3125.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3125.sharh: The end of the report links the conquest with a report about the Dajjāl that follows immediately. The card keeps to this sequence and adds no dating of its own.

HAD-3226.text: The angels were created from light.
HAD-3226.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3226.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ names the origin of the angels explicitly and is left without a speculative description of their constitution.

HAD-3227.text: The Ǧinn were created from a flame-like essence of fire.
HAD-3227.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3227.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ clearly distinguishes the origin of the Ǧinn from that of the angels and of the human being.

HAD-3228.text: Ādam عليه السلام was created from that which was described to you.
HAD-3228.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3228.sharh: The Prophet ﷺ refers to the already revealed description of the human creation and adds no speculative details.

HAD-3229.text: Of a community from Banū Isrāʾīl it was not known what had become of it; the Prophet ﷺ mentioned in this connection the mouse as a possible transformation.
HAD-3229.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3229.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3229.sharh: The report is rendered as a prophetic communication about an earlier community; later animal species are not assessed religiously in a blanket manner on that basis.

HAD-3230.text: As an indication the Prophet ﷺ mentioned that a mouse does not drink camel milk, while it drinks sheep milk.
HAD-3230.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3230.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3230.sharh: The observation belongs to the same report and is not generalized beyond its concrete context.

HAD-3231.text: Excessive praise can ruin a person; the Prophet ﷺ said to someone who was praising, in substance: You have broken the neck of your companion.
HAD-3231.narrator: Abū Bakrah and Abū Mūsā رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3231.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3231.sharh: The various wordings carry the same core of warning: praise can harm the one praised when it produces exaggeration and Fitnah.

HAD-3232.text: If someone must praise another, he should only say: I consider him to be such and such; Allah is his reckoner, and I declare no one pure before Allah.
HAD-3232.narrator: Abū Bakrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3232.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3232.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ permits restrained praise when needed, but binds it to uncertainty about the unseen and to Allah’s final judgment.

HAD-3233.text: When you see those who constantly shower people with excessive praise, then throw dust in their faces.
HAD-3233.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3233.sharh: The report is directed against harmful, exaggerated flattery; the several paths in Muslim are carried as one core.

HAD-3234.text: The Prophet ﷺ saw in a dream two men contending over a Miswāk. When he first gave it to the younger one, he was told to give precedence to the older one; thereupon he gave it to the older one.
HAD-3234.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3234.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3234.sharh: The report establishes the Adab of giving precedence to the older person in such a situation of handing over.

HAD-3235.text: Do not write down anything from me together with the Qurʾān; whoever had written down from me something other than the Qurʾān was to erase it in that context of that time.
HAD-3235.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3235.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3235.sharh: The early wording is rendered in the historical context of protecting the Qurʾān; later permissions to record Ḥadīṯ are not thereby annulled.

HAD-3236.text: Transmit from me; there is no objection to that.
HAD-3236.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3236.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3236.sharh: The Prophet ﷺ permits the reliable oral transmission of his statements; this stands alongside the duty not to attribute anything false.

HAD-3237.text: A king from an earlier community had a sorcerer. When this one grew old, he asked that a boy be sent to him so that he might teach him sorcery.
HAD-3237.narrator: Ṣuhayb ar-Rūmī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3237.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-3237.sharh: This opens the long authentic report and describes the starting point of the later trial of faith.

HAD-3238.text: On the way to the sorcerer the boy met a monk, heard his words and took a liking to them; from then on he sat with him regularly.
HAD-3238.narrator: Ṣuhayb ar-Rūmī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3238.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-3238.sharh: The report shows the beginning of the boy’s turning toward the truth within the story.

HAD-3239.text: When a large beast blocked the people’s path, the boy asked Allah to show, by its death, whether the monk’s cause was more beloved to Him than that of the sorcerer. He threw a stone, the beast died and the path became free.
HAD-3239.narrator: Ṣuhayb ar-Rūmī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3239.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-3239.sharh: The report shows how the boy sought to clarify his uncertainty through Duʿāʾ to Allah and was thereby strengthened in his turning.

HAD-3240.text: The monk said to the boy: Today you are further than I. You will be tested; when you are tested, do not betray me.
HAD-3240.narrator: Ṣuhayb ar-Rūmī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3240.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-3240.sharh: The monk recognizes the coming Fitnah and admonishes the boy to steadfastness and to the protection of others.

HAD-3241.text: The boy treated the blind, the lepers and other sick people, but said explicitly: I heal no one; Allah alone heals.
HAD-3241.narrator: Ṣuhayb ar-Rūmī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3241.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-3241.sharh: The core separates the permitted cause and the actual healing: the boy does not attribute the healing to himself, but to Allah.

HAD-3242.text: A blinded confidant of the king believed in Allah after the boy had explained to him that Allah alone heals; thereupon Allah restored his sight to him.
HAD-3242.narrator: Ṣuhayb ar-Rūmī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3242.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-3242.sharh: In the report the healing follows upon the Īmān and the boy’s petition, and is explicitly attributed to Allah.

HAD-3243.text: When the king asked who had given the man his sight back, he answered: My Lord. To the question whether he had another lord, he said: My Lord and your Lord is Allah.
HAD-3243.narrator: Ṣuhayb ar-Rūmī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3243.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-3243.sharh: The report shows an open confession of Tawḥīd before a ruler who raised a false claim for himself.

HAD-3244.text: The king tortured his confidant until he pointed to the boy; thereafter he also tortured the boy until he pointed to the monk.
HAD-3244.narrator: Ṣuhayb ar-Rūmī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3244.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-3244.sharh: The narration describes the escalating persecution and at the same time records how the chain of those involved was disclosed under compulsion.

HAD-3245.text: The monk was called upon to abandon his religion. He refused and was killed because of his steadfastness.
HAD-3245.narrator: Ṣuhayb ar-Rūmī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3245.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-3245.sharh: The report highlights the refusal to give up the faith under threat of death.

HAD-3126.text: The Prophet ﷺ announced, concerning a future end-time confrontation, that Muslims will fight against Jews and that even a stone will point out someone hidden behind it.
HAD-3126.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3126.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3126.sharh: The statement describes a specific future end-time event. It is not a general command against Jews outside this context announced by the Prophet.

HAD-3127.text: Before the onset of the Hour, many liars will appear.
HAD-3127.narrator: Ǧābir ibn Samurah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3127.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3127.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ warns against an accumulation of deceivers before the Hour. The parallel version adds no new prophetic core of the statement and is not counted separately.

HAD-3128.text: The Prophet ﷺ called upon Ibn Ṣayyād to testify that he was the Messenger of Allah; Ibn Ṣayyād rejected this and himself laid claim to messengership.
HAD-3128.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3128.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ spoke to Ibn Ṣayyād:
HAD-3128.sharh: The report documents the testing of Ibn Ṣayyād and his presumptuous reply. It is not used as proof that Ibn Ṣayyād was unequivocally the great Dajjāl.

HAD-3129.text: When the Prophet ﷺ had concealed something from Ibn Ṣayyād and the latter answered only with „duḫḫ“, he ﷺ said to him that he would not go beyond the rank set for him.
HAD-3129.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3129.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said to Ibn Ṣayyād:
HAD-3129.sharh: Ibn Ṣayyād’s incomplete answer shows, in the report, a limited and confused perception. The Prophet ﷺ rejected him and set a limit to his claim.

HAD-3130.text: When ʿUmar رضي الله عنه asked that Ibn Ṣayyād be killed, the Prophet ﷺ said: If he is the feared Dajjāl, you will not be able to kill him.
HAD-3130.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3130.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said to ʿUmar رضي الله عنه:
HAD-3130.sharh: The Prophet ﷺ did not permit ʿUmar رضي الله عنه, in this report, to kill on his own out of mere suspicion. Precisely the uncertainty about Ibn Ṣayyād is thereby made plain.

HAD-3131.text: When Ibn Ṣayyād said that he saw a throne over the water, the Prophet ﷺ said to him: You see the throne of Iblīs over the sea.
HAD-3131.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3131.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said to Ibn Ṣayyād:
HAD-3131.sharh: The Prophet ﷺ interpreted Ibn Ṣayyād’s perception expressly in this sense. Other confused statements of Ibn Ṣayyād were not treated, in the same report, as reliable revelation.

HAD-3132.text: It is transmitted about the Dajjāl that he will have no children and will enter neither Makkah nor Madīnah.
HAD-3132.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3132.speaker: Abū Saʿīd رضي الله عنه confirmed from the statement of the Prophet ﷺ:
HAD-3132.sharh: These features are cited in the report by Ibn Ṣayyād himself and are confirmed by Abū Saʿīd رضي الله عنه as prophetic statements he had heard. They serve there precisely the discussion of Ibn Ṣayyād’s identity.

HAD-3133.text: The ground of Paradise is like fine, white, pure musk.
HAD-3133.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3133.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3133.sharh: The two versions give the same core of the statement about the nature of the ground of Paradise. They are brought together into one card.

HAD-3134.text: No prophet remained without warning his people of the Dajjāl; Nūḥ عليه السلام also warned his people of him.
HAD-3134.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3134.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3134.sharh: The warning against the Dajjāl is described as a continuous prophetic warning. Paths of repetition of the same statement are not counted as new cards.

HAD-3135.text: The Dajjāl is one-eyed; Allah is not one-eyed.
HAD-3135.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3135.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3135.sharh: The Prophet ﷺ names a bodily feature of the Dajjāl and expressly sets Allah apart from it. The statement is retained without figurative reinterpretation.

HAD-3136.text: Between the eyes of the Dajjāl is written „kāfir“; every Muslim will be able to read it.
HAD-3136.narrator: Some Companions of the Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-3136.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3136.sharh: The marking of the Dajjāl belongs to the expressly transmitted signs of recognition. The various wording variants are not artificially multiplied.

HAD-3137.text: None of you will see Allah before he dies.
HAD-3137.narrator: Some Companions of the Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-3137.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3137.sharh: The statement stands in the context of the warning against the Dajjāl and guards against his claim to deceive. It distinguishes this-worldly life from the otherworldly Ruʾyah.

HAD-3138.text: The Dajjāl will emerge through an anger that enrages him.
HAD-3138.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3138.sharh: The statement is cited in both versions as the ground for particular caution toward a provocation of Ibn Ṣayyād. The parallel version is not counted twice.

HAD-3139.text: With the Dajjāl there will be something that people see as water and fire; what appears like fire is cold, good water, and what appears like water is fire.
HAD-3139.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3139.sharh: The several versions describe the same deception. The instruction of the Prophet ﷺ is that one should not let oneself be deceived by the outward appearance; therefore the core is recorded only once.

HAD-3140.text: The Dajjāl will come with an image of Paradise and of the Fire; what he calls Paradise is in truth the Fire.
HAD-3140.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3140.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3140.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ describes the deception of the Dajjāl by means of reversed outward impressions. It supplements the water-and-fire report with the expressly mentioned Paradise-and-Fire deception.

HAD-3141.text: Whoever encounters the Dajjāl should recite over him the opening verses of Sūrah al-Kahf.
HAD-3141.narrator: an-Nawwās ibn Samʿān رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3141.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3141.sharh: The Prophet ﷺ here names a concrete protective instruction for the one who encounters the Dajjāl. The card is limited to this expressly transmitted wording.

HAD-3142.text: The Dajjāl will appear on the road between aš-Šām and Iraq and will spread his Fitnah to the right and to the left.
HAD-3142.narrator: an-Nawwās ibn Samʿān رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3142.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3142.sharh: The place indication and the wide spread of the Fitnah belong to the long authentic report. The record does not of its own accord identify any present-day event with it.

HAD-3143.text: The Dajjāl will remain on the earth for forty days: one day like a year, one day like a month, one day like a week, and the remaining days like ordinary days.
HAD-3143.narrator: an-Nawwās ibn Samʿān رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3143.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3143.sharh: The report expressly distinguishes between three extraordinarily long days and the remaining ordinary days. The number forty is not reinterpreted beyond the wording.

HAD-3144.text: For the day that will be like a year, it does not suffice to limit oneself to the prayer of a single day; the prayer times must be estimated.
HAD-3144.narrator: an-Nawwās ibn Samʿān رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3144.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3144.sharh: This prophetic instruction shows that the obligatory prayers are performed according to estimated periods of time, despite the extraordinary length of the day.

HAD-3145.text: The Dajjāl will move swiftly like a cloud driven by the wind; people who follow him will experience rain and a visible abundance of livestock and produce.
HAD-3145.narrator: an-Nawwās ibn Samʿān رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3145.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3145.sharh: The report describes material enticements as part of his Fitnah. Outward prosperity is thereby precisely not presented as proof of truth.

HAD-3246.text: The former confidant of the king was also called upon to leave his religion. He refused and was killed.
HAD-3246.narrator: Ṣuhayb ar-Rūmī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3246.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-3246.sharh: The second killing confirms the same framework of trial, but in an independent person of the story.

HAD-3247.text: The king had the boy brought onto a mountain, so that he would be thrown down if he refused apostasy. The boy asked Allah to save him; the mountain quaked, his guards fell, and he returned to the king.
HAD-3247.narrator: Ṣuhayb ar-Rūmī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3247.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-3247.sharh: The boy seeks his rescue directly from Allah; the report then describes an extraordinary preservation.

HAD-3248.text: After that the boy was to be drowned in the sea. He again asked Allah to save him from them; the boat capsized, his guards drowned, and he returned once more to the king.
HAD-3248.narrator: Ṣuhayb ar-Rūmī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3248.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-3248.sharh: The second rescue does not merely repeat the event, but shows the renewed steadfastness and that Allah preserved him from the planned death.

HAD-3249.text: The boy told the king that he could kill him only if he gathered the people, took an arrow and said publicly: In the name of Allah, the Lord of the boy. When the king did this, the boy died and the people cried out: We believe in the Lord of the boy.
HAD-3249.narrator: Ṣuhayb ar-Rūmī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3249.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-3249.sharh: The boy made his own killing the occasion to make the truth of Tawḥīd publicly visible; the immediate outcome was the Īmān of the people.

HAD-3250.text: When the people believed in the Lord of the boy, the king had trenches with fire dug and compelled them to apostasy. A woman with her child hesitated; the child said to her: Mother, be steadfast, for you are upon the truth.
HAD-3250.narrator: Ṣuhayb ar-Rūmī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3250.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-3250.sharh: The end of the report shows the final trial of the believers: they were to choose between faith and fire. The child’s encouragement affirms their steadfastness upon the truth.

HAD-3251.text: A debtor of Abū al-Yasar رضي الله عنه hid from him, because he was insolvent and feared promising him something and then being unable to fulfill it.
HAD-3251.narrator: ʿUbādah ibn al-Walīd رحمه الله reported about Abū al-Yasar رضي الله عنه:
HAD-3251.speaker: Abū al-Yasar رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3251.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats the account of Abū al-Yasar in connection with dealing with a debtor who is actually without means, and with the virtue of making things easy.

HAD-3252.text: After the debtor had affirmed his insolvency, Abū al-Yasar رضي الله عنه had the debt document brought, erased it and said: If you can pay, then pay; otherwise you are released from it.
HAD-3252.narrator: ʿUbādah ibn al-Walīd رحمه الله reported about Abū al-Yasar رضي الله عنه:
HAD-3252.speaker: Abū al-Yasar رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-3252.sharh: The report shows the practical application of forbearance toward the one without means: Abū al-Yasar joined the possibility of later payment with an explicit release in the case of continued inability.

HAD-3253.text: Whoever grants a respite to an insolvent person, or remits for him a part or, respectively, the debt, Allah will shade him in His shade.
HAD-3253.narrator: Abū al-Yasar رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3253.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3253.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ cites this prophetic statement as the basis for the great virtue of respite and remission toward the debtor without means.

HAD-3254.text: Abū al-Yasar رضي الله عنه and his servant each wore garments of the same kind, so that the servant was not set apart by inferior clothing.
HAD-3254.narrator: ʿUbādah ibn al-Walīd رحمه الله reported about Abū al-Yasar رضي الله عنه:
HAD-3254.speaker: Abū al-Yasar رضي الله عنه acted thus:
HAD-3254.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats the report as a practical implementation of good treatment of servants and of sharing in food and clothing.

HAD-3255.text: Give your servants to eat of that which you yourselves eat.
HAD-3255.narrator: Abū al-Yasar رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3255.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3255.sharh: The Šarḥ assigns the statement to good treatment and to the servant’s sharing in the food of his master.

HAD-3256.text: Clothe your servants with that with which you clothe yourselves.
HAD-3256.narrator: Abū al-Yasar رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3256.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3256.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the report within the framework of Iḥsān toward servants and of avoiding degrading unequal treatment.

HAD-3257.text: It was preferable to him to give his servant something of the goods of this world rather than that the servant take from his good deeds on the Day of Resurrection.
HAD-3257.narrator: ʿUbādah ibn al-Walīd رحمه الله reported about Abū al-Yasar رضي الله عنه:
HAD-3257.speaker: Abū al-Yasar رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-3257.sharh: The statement shows Abū al-Yasar’s fear of the reckoning in the hereafter for a wrong toward a servant, and explains his generous practical attitude.

HAD-3258.text: Ǧābir رضي الله عنه deliberately prayed in a single garment, although his upper garment lay beside him, so that an ignorant person would see his action and learn from it.
HAD-3258.narrator: ʿUbādah ibn al-Walīd رحمه الله reported about Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-3258.speaker: Ǧābir رضي الله عنه explained:
HAD-3258.sharh: The report shows that a scholar can visibly practice a permitted action in order to remove a false impression about its permissibility.

HAD-3259.text: The Prophet ﷺ saw spittle on the Qiblah side of the mosque and removed it with a twig.
HAD-3259.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3259.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ did:
HAD-3259.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats the removal of the impurity as an expression of honoring and caring for the mosque.

HAD-3260.text: After he had removed the trace, the Prophet ﷺ repeatedly asked his Companions: Who among you would like Allah to turn away from him?
HAD-3260.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3260.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3260.sharh: The insistent question makes clear the gravity of heedless conduct toward the direction of prayer and within the Ṣalāh.

HAD-3261.text: When one of you stands for the prayer, Allah تبارك وتعالى is before his face.
HAD-3261.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3261.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3261.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ cites this wording in connection with reverence, orientation, and the prohibition of spitting toward the direction of prayer.

HAD-3262.text: The one praying should not spit in front of himself toward the Qiblah.
HAD-3262.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3262.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3262.sharh: The prohibition stands directly in the context of reverence before Allah and of safeguarding the direction of prayer.

HAD-3263.text: The one praying should not spit to his right side.
HAD-3263.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3263.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3263.sharh: The report expressly distinguishes between the forbidden front side and right side and the permitted direction of avoidance to the left.

HAD-3264.text: If the one praying must spit something out, he should do it to his left side under his left foot.
HAD-3264.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3264.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3264.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ cites the left side as the direction of avoidance named in the report, after the front side and the right side have been excluded.

HAD-3265.text: If something suddenly presses the one praying to spit, he can use his garment and afterwards fold together or, respectively, cover the affected part.
HAD-3265.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3265.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ showed:
HAD-3265.sharh: The report names a practical solution for the case that the intended direction of avoidance is not immediately possible.

HAD-3346.text: ʿUmar رضي الله عنه furthermore wished for a concluding prophetic instruction concerning certain doors of Ribā.
HAD-3346.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3346.speaker: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-3346.sharh: The wording expressly names “doors from the doors of Ribā”; the record does not extend this beyond ʿUmar’s formulation.

HAD-3347.text: Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه swore that Qurʾān 22:19 was revealed concerning the men who stepped forward for single combat on the day of Badr.
HAD-3347.narrator: Qays ibn ʿUbād رحمه الله reported:
HAD-3347.speaker: Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه swore:
HAD-3347.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ cites the statement of Abū Ḏarr on p. 594; the attribution to the single combat of Badr is adopted unchanged.

HAD-3348.text: The two opposing parties described in the verse Qurʾān 22:19 were, in this report, related to the men who faced one another in single combat at Badr.
HAD-3348.narrator: Qays ibn ʿUbād رحمه الله reported:
HAD-3348.speaker: Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه explained:
HAD-3348.sharh: The independent core of the Tafsīr is the identification of the two contending parties with the specific duelists of Badr.

HAD-3349.text: On the side of the believers, Ḥamzah, ʿAlī and ʿUbaydah ibn al-Ḥāriṯ رضي الله عنهم stepped forward.
HAD-3349.narrator: Qays ibn ʿUbād رحمه الله reported:
HAD-3349.speaker: Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه named:
HAD-3349.sharh: The three names of the believing side are expressly enumerated in the Muslim report.

HAD-3350.text: Facing them at Badr stood ʿUtbah and Šaybah, the two sons of Rabīʿah, and al-Walīd ibn ʿUtbah.
HAD-3350.narrator: Qays ibn ʿUbād رحمه الله reported:
HAD-3350.speaker: Abū Ḏarr رضي الله عنه named:
HAD-3350.sharh: The Muslim report expressly names these three men as the opposing side of the single combat.

HAD-3351.text:
Taqwā toward Allah does not consist in fasting by day and praying by night while committing offenses in between.

Rather, Taqwā consists in refraining from what Allah has forbidden and in fulfilling what Allah has made obligatory.

Whoever is granted further good beyond that, for him it is good added to further good.
HAD-3351.narrator: It is transmitted concerning ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz رحمه الله:
HAD-3351.speaker: It is attributed to him:

HAD-3352.text:
A man has acquired 30,000 dirhams unlawfully and says: I will utter Tasbīḥ, Taḥmīd and Takbīr until I have gathered just as many good deeds. What do you say about that?

He should first return the money. For his Ḏikr will not be accepted until he has returned it.
HAD-3352.narrator: It is reported from Sufyān aṯ-Ṯawrī رحمه الله:
HAD-3352.speaker: He answered a question:

HAD-3353.text: They call upon Him with Tawḥīd and sincerity toward Him, and they serve Him.
HAD-3353.narrator: Imām Abū Isḥāq az-Zaǧǧāǧ (d. 311 A.H.) explained regarding al-Kahf (18:28):
HAD-3353.speaker: Tafsīr of “They call upon their Lord morning and evening”:

HAD-3354.text: One protects one’s family by calling them to obedience toward Allah, restraining them from disobedience, and helping them thereby to fulfill Allah’s commands.
HAD-3354.narrator: It is transmitted concerning Qatādah ibn Diʿāmah (Tābiʿī):
HAD-3354.speaker: Transmitted saying:

HAD-3355.text: Adorn knowledge through yourselves – and do not adorn yourselves with knowledge.
HAD-3355.narrator: It is transmitted concerning Sufyān aṯ-Ṯawrī رحمه الله:
HAD-3355.speaker: Transmitted saying:

HAD-3356.text: The proceeds from the sale of a dog, the payment for fornication, and the fee of a soothsayer.
HAD-3356.narrator: Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3356.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade:
HAD-3356.sharh: An-Nawawī explains the terms of the Ḥadīṯ directly: by “mahr al-baġī” is meant the payment for fornication; this income is forbidden. “Ḥulwān al-kāhin” denotes the fee that someone receives for soothsaying. He also treats the forbidden money from the sale of a dog separately in this chapter and discusses the legal views transmitted concerning it. This is thus a warning against certain unlawful sources of acquisition; the wording is not a blanket condemnation of lawful work.

HAD-3357.text: If you transmit to people something that their intellect cannot grasp, this will be a Fitnah for some of them.
HAD-3357.narrator: It is transmitted from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-3357.speaker: The following saying is attributed to him:

HAD-3358.text: They learned the exemplary conduct of life just as they learned knowledge.
HAD-3358.narrator: It is transmitted concerning Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn:
HAD-3358.speaker: Transmitted saying:

HAD-3359.text:
The believer watches over himself and calls himself to account for the sake of Allah.

The reckoning on the Day of Resurrection will be easier for those who have already called themselves to account in this world.

The reckoning will be heavy, however, for those who have conducted their affairs without accountability.
HAD-3359.narrator: It is transmitted concerning al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī:
HAD-3359.speaker: Transmitted saying:

HAD-3266.text: After the trace on the Qiblah side had been removed, the Prophet ﷺ had scent brought and applied it at the place.
HAD-3266.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3266.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ did:
HAD-3266.sharh: The action supplements the mere removal with purification and a pleasant scent and shows the special care of the mosque.

HAD-3267.text: Ǧābir رضي الله عنه traced the custom of using scent in the mosques back to this action of the Prophet ﷺ.
HAD-3267.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما said:
HAD-3267.speaker: Ǧābir رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-3267.sharh: Ǧābir draws from the concrete prophetic action a practical explanation for the later use of scent in mosques.

HAD-3268.text: On the journey with the Prophet ﷺ, five, six, or seven men at a time shared one pack camel and took turns riding.
HAD-3268.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3268.speaker: Ǧābir رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3268.sharh: The report documents the scant means of travel and the orderly taking of turns by the Companions on the same riding opportunity.

HAD-3269.text: When the camel of a man from the Anṣār hesitated at being driven on, the man cursed his own animal.
HAD-3269.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3269.speaker: Ǧābir رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3269.sharh: The narration forms the concrete occasion for the immediately following prophetic correction of cursing.

HAD-3270.text: The Prophet ﷺ immediately asked who had cursed his camel and had the one responsible acknowledge it.
HAD-3270.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3270.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ asked:
HAD-3270.sharh: The inquiry makes clear that uttered imprecations were not treated as words without consequence.

HAD-3271.text: The man should dismount from the cursed camel; a cursed animal should not accompany the travel company.
HAD-3271.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3271.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3271.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats the prophetic reaction as emphatic education against careless cursing.

HAD-3272.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3272.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3272.sharh: The Prophet ﷺ forbade negative Duʿāʾ against one’s own person, because Duʿāʾ must be taken seriously.

HAD-3273.text: Do not call against your children.
HAD-3273.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3273.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3273.sharh: The prohibition protects against uttering in anger words against one’s own children whose being answered one would in fact not wish.

HAD-3274.text: Do not call against your wealth.
HAD-3274.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3274.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3274.sharh: Possession and livelihood, too, should not be burdened in anger with an imprecation.

HAD-3275.text: The reason for these prohibitions is that such a call could meet an hour in which Allah is asked for a gift and the request is answered.
HAD-3275.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3275.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3275.sharh: The close of the report explains the danger: An unconsidered negative Duʿāʾ can coincide with a time of acceptance.

HAD-3276.text: When the travel group drew near a watering place, the Prophet ﷺ asked who could go ahead, seal the trough with clay, draw water into it, and supply the group.
HAD-3276.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3276.speaker: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3276.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the stage of the journey as an orderly preparation of the watering place and as a practical supply of the group.

HAD-3277.text: After Ǧābir and Ǧabbār رضي الله عنهم had prepared and filled the trough, the Prophet ﷺ asked them for permission before he let his she-camel drink from it.
HAD-3277.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3277.speaker: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3277.sharh: The Šarḥ highlights the fine Adab: Although the watering place had been prepared for the travel group, the Prophet ﷺ took account of the work of the two and asked them.

HAD-3278.text: The Prophet ﷺ performed Wuḍūʾ from the prepared trough; afterwards Ǧābir رضي الله عنه also performed Wuḍūʾ there.
HAD-3278.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3278.speaker: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3278.sharh: The scene joins travel supply and ritual purification; the report expressly names the successive Wuḍūʾ action.

HAD-3279.text: When Ǧābir رضي الله عنه stood at prayer to the left of the Prophet ﷺ, the Prophet ﷺ took him by the hand and placed him on his right side.
HAD-3279.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3279.speaker: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3279.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats from this the position of a single fellow worshipper to the right of the Imam.

HAD-3280.text: When Ǧabbār ibn Ṣaḫr رضي الله عنه arrived, the Prophet ﷺ placed the two men together behind him.
HAD-3280.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3280.speaker: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3280.sharh: The report shows the differing position: a single fellow worshipper to the right of the Imam, two fellow worshippers behind the Imam.

HAD-3281.text: During the prayer the Prophet ﷺ noticed that Ǧābir رضي الله عنه was holding his only garment unsuitably, and signaled to him with his hand to tie it fast at the hip.
HAD-3281.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3281.speaker: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3281.sharh: The Šarḥ classifies the gesture as a practical correction of the clothing in prayer.

HAD-3282.text: The Prophet ﷺ explained to Ǧābir رضي الله عنه: If the garment is wide, one lays its two ends crosswise; if it is narrow, one ties it around the hip.
HAD-3282.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3282.speaker: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3282.sharh: The concluding instruction expressly distinguishes between a wide and a narrow garment and describes the fitting form of covering in each case.

HAD-3283.text: On a journey with the Prophet ﷺ the daily ration of each man consisted at times of only one date.
HAD-3283.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3283.speaker: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3283.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ cites this report as clear evidence of the great deprivation and patience of the Companions on journeys.

HAD-3284.text: The Companions sucked their single date and afterwards kept it in their garment, in order to subsist on it as long as possible.
HAD-3284.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3284.speaker: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3284.sharh: The report makes the extreme measure of scarcity concrete: a single date was used over the course of the day.

HAD-3285.text: Out of hunger the Companions struck leaves from the trees with their bows and ate them, until the corners of their mouths became sore.
HAD-3285.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3285.speaker: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3285.sharh: The Šarḥ understands this as a description of actual hardship and not as an idealized form of livelihood.

HAD-3146.text: He will leave the people who reject the Dajjāl; afterwards they will be affected by drought and loss of property.
HAD-3146.narrator: an-Nawwās ibn Samʿān رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3146.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3146.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ shows that steadfastness toward the Fitnah can be connected with worldly trial. Material scarcity does not thereby become a sign of religious falsehood.

HAD-3147.text: The Dajjāl will pass through uninhabited land and command it to bring forth its treasures; these will gather with him.
HAD-3147.narrator: an-Nawwās ibn Samʿān رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3147.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3147.sharh: This extraordinary appearance also belongs to the described Fitnah. It is reported as a trial of deception and is not understood as divine confirmation of his claim.

HAD-3148.text: The Dajjāl is barred from entering the approaches of Madīnah; he will settle outside on a barren tract.
HAD-3148.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3148.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3148.sharh: The protection of Madīnah from his entry is expressly named in the report. The parallel version 2938b contains no new independent core statement.

HAD-3149.text: A particularly righteous man will confront the Dajjāl. The Dajjāl will kill him and bring him back to life; thereby the man's certainty about the Dajjāl will only grow stronger, and a second time the Dajjāl will not be able to kill him.
HAD-3149.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3149.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3149.sharh: The report highlights the steadfastness of this believer. His being brought back to life by the Dajjāl is a special Fitnah, and what it heightens is not the latter's truth but the believer's certainty of his falsehood.

HAD-3150.text: Despite what is ascribed to the Dajjāl of food, water, and outward power, he is too insignificant before Allah for this to change his falsehood.
HAD-3150.narrator: al-Muġīrah ibn Šuʿbah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3150.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3150.sharh: The Prophet ﷺ took from al-Muġīra the excessive worry by emphasizing the complete insignificance of the Dajjāl before Allah. The multiple versions are brought together into one core statement.

HAD-3151.text: After the destruction of the Dajjāl, people will live seven years without there being enmity between any two people.
HAD-3151.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3151.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3151.sharh: The seven years are expressly named in the authentic report after the end of the Dajjāl. The record does not make of this a general chronological calculation about end-time events that go beyond that.

HAD-3152.text: After the believers have been taken away, the worst people remain: they know no good and reject no evil.
HAD-3152.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3152.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3152.sharh: The report describes a late end-time condition after the taking away of the people with Īmān. It is not transferred to ordinary generations or individual societies without a clear proof.

HAD-3153.text: At the first sounding of the horn, a man who is just then preparing the trough of his camels is struck by it first; afterwards the people collapse.
HAD-3153.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3153.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3153.sharh: The concrete everyday scene emphasizes the sudden force of the event. The record connects it exclusively with the Nafḫ aṣ-Ṣūr described in the Ḥadīṯ.

HAD-3154.text: Thereafter Allah will send water from heaven, whereby the bodies of the people will come forth and grow.
HAD-3154.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3154.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3154.sharh: The report describes the bodily reawakening with a water sent by Allah. The image of growing is named in the Ḥadīṯ itself as an actual process of the raising.

HAD-3155.text: At the next blowing into the horn, the people will stand up and look.
HAD-3155.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3155.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3155.sharh: This sentence marks in the report the transition from the first shock to the actual resurrection. It is carried as its own core statement.

HAD-3156.text: After the resurrection the people will be called to come to their Lord; at the same time it will be commanded to hold them, for they will be questioned.
HAD-3156.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3156.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3156.sharh: The statement connects resurrection with accountability. It underscores that standing before Allah is connected with questioning and responsibility.

HAD-3157.text: Out of every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine are set apart for the fire; this is that tremendous day on which even children turn gray.
HAD-3157.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3157.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3157.sharh: The report depicts the magnitude of the terror on the Day of Resurrection. The number and the description are rendered as a prophetic communication, without additional calculations being made.

HAD-3158.text: Among the great signs that follow immediately upon one another are the rising of the sun in the west and the emergence of the beast; whichever of the two occurs first, the other follows it soon.
HAD-3158.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3158.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3158.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ emphasizes the temporal nearness of these two extraordinary signs. Other great signs are not thereby forced, without further proofs, into a complete sequence.

HAD-3159.text: Tamīm and his companions were, on a sea voyage, driven about by the waves for about a month, until they landed on an island.
HAD-3159.narrator: Fāṭimah bint Qays رضي الله عنها reported the report of Tamīm ad-Dārī رضي الله عنه:
HAD-3159.speaker: Tamīm ad-Dārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3159.sharh: This is the entry into the authentic Ǧassāsah report. The long sea voyage and the island form the concrete frame of the later meeting.

HAD-3160.text: On the island they met a heavily haired being whose front and back were hardly to be distinguished; it called itself al-Ǧassāsah and directed them to a man in a building.
HAD-3160.narrator: Fāṭimah bint Qays رضي الله عنها reported the report of Tamīm ad-Dārī رضي الله عنه:
HAD-3160.speaker: Tamīm ad-Dārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3160.sharh: The record keeps to the unusual description of the authentic report and adds no speculative zoological or symbolic identification.

HAD-3161.text: The bound man asked about the date palms of Baysān and whether they still bore fruit; afterwards he announced that they would soon bear fruit no longer.
HAD-3161.narrator: Fāṭimah bint Qays رضي الله عنها reported the report of Tamīm ad-Dārī رضي الله عنه:
HAD-3161.speaker: Tamīm ad-Dārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3161.sharh: The question about Baysān belongs to the signs asked about by the bound man. The record renders only the statement named in the report and does not itself date its fulfillment.

HAD-3162.text: The bound man asked about the lake of Ṭabariyyah; when its great quantity of water was described to him, he said that its water would soon disappear.
HAD-3162.narrator: Fāṭimah bint Qays رضي الله عنها reported the report of Tamīm ad-Dārī رضي الله عنه:
HAD-3162.speaker: Tamīm ad-Dārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3162.sharh: This statement too appears in the report as one of the signs asked about. Present water levels are not, on one's own authority, designated as the final fulfillment.

HAD-3163.text: The bound man asked about the spring of Zuġar; he was told that it carries abundant water and that the people irrigate their fields with it.
HAD-3163.narrator: Fāṭimah bint Qays رضي الله عنها reported the report of Tamīm ad-Dārī رضي الله عنه:
HAD-3163.speaker: Tamīm ad-Dārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3163.sharh: The spring Zuġar is expressly named in the authentic report as part of the local conditions asked about. The record adds no prediction concerning this spring that is not transmitted.

HAD-3164.text: The bound man asked whether the Prophet of the unlettered community had already come forth and whether the Arabs had obeyed him; when this was affirmed, he said that obedience toward him was better for them.
HAD-3164.narrator: Fāṭimah bint Qays رضي الله عنها reported the report of Tamīm ad-Dārī رضي الله عنه:
HAD-3164.speaker: Tamīm ad-Dārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3164.sharh: The report confirms from the mouth of the bound man himself the sending of the Prophet ﷺ that had already taken place, and that obedience toward him is good. This is not understood as recognition of any claim of the Dajjāl.

HAD-3165.text: The bound man declared that he was the Dajjāl, and said that it would almost be permitted to him to come forth.
HAD-3165.narrator: Fāṭimah bint Qays رضي الله عنها reported the report of Tamīm ad-Dārī رضي الله عنه:
HAD-3165.speaker: Tamīm ad-Dārī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3165.sharh: The report expressly identifies the bound man as the Dajjāl and describes his condition before the later emergence. Additional determinations of place or time are not added.

HAD-3166.text: When the Dajjāl camps before Madīnah, the city will quake three times; thereupon Allah will let every Kāfir and Munāfiq go out from it to him.
HAD-3166.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3166.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3166.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ links the protection of Madīnah from the Dajjāl’s entry with a threefold shaking, through which the hidden hypocrites and disbelievers are driven out.

HAD-3167.text: Seventy thousand Jews from Aṣbahān, who wear ṭayālisah, will follow the Dajjāl.
HAD-3167.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3167.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3167.sharh: The statement is a concrete end-time prophecy about a particular following. It is not transferred wholesale to Jews in general or to present-day population groups.

HAD-3168.text: The people will flee from the Dajjāl into the mountains.
HAD-3168.narrator: Umm Šarīk رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-3168.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3168.sharh: The statement describes the intensity of the Fitnah and the flight of the people in that time. It is not a general order of withdrawal outside this context.

HAD-3169.text: When Umm Šarīk رضي الله عنها asked where the Arabs would then be, the Prophet ﷺ answered that at that time they would be only few.
HAD-3169.narrator: Umm Šarīk رضي الله عنها asked:
HAD-3169.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3169.sharh: The small number of the Arabs is named as a condition at the time of the great Dajjāl-Fitnah. The record does not equate this with a present-day demographic condition.

HAD-3170.text: Between the creation of Ādam عليه السلام and the coming of the Hour there is no greater creation, or respectively no greater Fitnah, than the Dajjāl.
HAD-3170.narrator: Hišām ibn ʿĀmir رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3170.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3170.sharh: The wording underscores the extraordinary magnitude of the trial through the Dajjāl. The formulation is understood in the sense of the transmitted immense Fitnah, not as a divine exaltation of his person.

HAD-3171.text: Precede six things with good deeds: the sunrise in the west, the smoke, the Dajjāl, the animal, the personal end of each one of you, and the general event.
HAD-3171.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3171.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3171.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ calls for not waiting with righteous deeds until decisive personal or end-time limits occur. The six points are summarized as a framework of warning.

HAD-3172.text: My sending and the Hour stand to each other like these two fingers; in this the index finger and the middle finger were shown side by side.
HAD-3172.narrator: Sahl ibn Saʿd and Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنهم reported:
HAD-3172.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3172.sharh: The parable emphasizes the nearness of the Hour in relation to the world-time that has passed, without fixing a calendar date.

HAD-3173.text: The Hour will strike people completely suddenly: while milking, in the middle of a transaction, and while someone is just preparing his water basin.
HAD-3173.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3173.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3173.sharh: The three everyday scenes form a shared core of the statement: the final event interrupts ordinary activities without prior warning.

HAD-3174.text: Between the two blasts into the horn there are forty; Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه did not fix whether days, months, or years are meant by that.
HAD-3174.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3174.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3174.sharh: The transmission preserves the number forty, but leaves the unit expressly open. The record follows this restraint and adds no unattested specification.

HAD-3175.text: Of the human being everything perishes in the ground except one bone, the ʿaǧb aḏ-ḏanab; from it the creation is put together again on the Day of Resurrection.
HAD-3175.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3175.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3175.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ names the ʿaǧb aḏ-ḏanab as the remaining starting point of the bodily recomposition. The record leaves this otherworldly statement in its transmitted sense.

HAD-3176.text: Allah’s Messenger ﷺ showed his Companions a dead, defective kid and explained that the Dunyā is even less with Allah than this animal in their eyes.
HAD-3176.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3176.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3176.sharh: The comparison is meant to loosen the hearts from excessive attachment to the passing world. The statement does not deny permitted use of the Dunyā; it ranks its value in relation to the Hereafter.

HAD-3177.text: The son of Ādam says: «My wealth!» In fact, of it only what he has eaten, what he has worn and worn out, or what he has sent ahead as Ṣadaqah belongs to him.
HAD-3177.narrator: Muṭarrif رحمه الله reported from his father:
HAD-3177.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3177.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ distinguishes between temporary possession and the share actually used or sent ahead for the Hereafter. Possession alone is not a lasting gain.

HAD-3178.text: Three things follow the deceased: his family, his wealth, and his deeds. Family and wealth return; his deeds remain with him.
HAD-3178.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3178.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3178.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ orders the priorities of the human being: social closeness and possession end at the grave, while his own deeds accompany the person into the next world.

HAD-3179.text: The Prophet ﷺ said to the Anṣār that he did not fear poverty for them.
HAD-3179.narrator: ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3179.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3179.sharh: The statement does not mean that poverty is not a trial. In the concrete prophetic comparison, the greater concern is directed to the later abundance and its temptations.

HAD-3180.text: The Prophet ﷺ feared that the Dunyā would be opened wide to them, that they would compete with one another over it, and that they would perish by it as earlier communities did.
HAD-3180.narrator: ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3180.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3180.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ does not warn against permitted possession as such, but against competition, distraction, and destructive attachment to worldly abundance.

HAD-3181.text: After the opening of Persia and Rome, the Prophet ﷺ warned that people would compete over the Dunyā, envy one another, turn away from one another, and hate one another.
HAD-3181.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3181.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3181.sharh: The prophecy links outward prosperity with inward dangers. Conquest and possession guarantee no spiritual improvement; they can trigger competition and enmity.

HAD-3182.text: Allah tested three men from Banū Isrāʾīl — a leper, a bald man, and a blind man — by means of an angel.
HAD-3182.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3182.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3182.sharh: The report presents healing and wealth expressly as a test. What is decisive is not the possession itself, but gratitude and truthfulness after the favor received.

HAD-3183.text: The leper was healed, received beautiful skin, and was given a pregnant she-camel, for which blessing was asked for him.
