HAD-3183.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3183.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3183.sharh: The healing and the wealth are, in the report, gifts of Allah and at the same time part of the test. The later dealing with them shows whether the recipient acknowledges the original hardship.

HAD-3184.text: The bald man was healed, received beautiful hair, and was given a pregnant cow, for which blessing was asked for him.
HAD-3184.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3184.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3184.sharh: Here too the report links bodily healing with growing possession. The favor is not presented as a self-earned merit.

HAD-3185.text: Allah restored the blind man’s eyesight; in addition he received a sheep, from which great possession arose.
HAD-3185.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3185.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3185.sharh: The later success of this man is traced back to the sight restored by Allah and the blessed possession. His test thereafter consists in gratitude and generosity.

HAD-3286.text: When a man had accidentally not received his daily date and had to be supported because of weakness, his Companions testified to this until his date was handed over to him.
HAD-3286.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3286.speaker: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3286.sharh: The report shows both the severity of the shortage and the mutual care and testimony of the Companions.

HAD-3287.text: When the Prophet ﷺ wanted to relieve himself in a wide valley and found no cover, he looked for something that could screen him.
HAD-3287.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3287.speaker: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3287.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats the passage in connection with the special value of covering and of preserving privacy when relieving oneself.

HAD-3288.text: Two trees obeyed the Prophet ﷺ with Allah's permission, moved toward him and joined together, so that they screened him.
HAD-3288.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3288.speaker: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3288.sharh: The Šarḥ cites the movement of the trees as an extraordinary sign of prophethood and as help granted by Allah.

HAD-3289.text: After the Prophet ﷺ had finished relieving himself, the two trees again stood separately in their original places.
HAD-3289.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3289.speaker: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3289.sharh: The Šarḥ also treats the trees' returning of their own accord as part of the extraordinary prophetic sign.

HAD-3290.text: The Prophet ﷺ passed by two graves and reported that their occupants were punished.
HAD-3290.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3290.speaker: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3290.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ cites this passage in connection with the Prophet's ﷺ knowledge of the specific punishment of these two grave occupants.

HAD-3291.text: The Prophet ﷺ had fresh branches laid at the two graves and explained that he hoped, through his intercession, that their punishment would be lightened as long as the branches remained fresh.
HAD-3291.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3291.speaker: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3291.sharh: The wording expressly binds the lightening to the intercession of the Prophet ﷺ and to this specific situation; no general grave practice is constructed from it.

HAD-3292.text: When the travel group reached its camp, the Prophet ﷺ had water called for, yet at first no water was found in the entire caravan.
HAD-3292.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3292.speaker: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3292.sharh: The Šarḥ opens the water passage with the complete lack of available water in the camp.

HAD-3293.text: In an old water skin of a man from the Anṣār, Ǧābir رضي الله عنه found only a tiny amount of water that would hardly have sufficed for a single sip.
HAD-3293.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3293.speaker: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3293.sharh: The small initial supply is expressly emphasized in the report and forms the contrast to the following extraordinary event.

HAD-3294.text: The Prophet ﷺ took the small amount of water into his hand, spoke words whose content Ǧābir رضي الله عنه did not know, and pressed or moved the water skin with his hand.
HAD-3294.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3294.speaker: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3294.sharh: The report expressly preserves that Ǧābir did not know the spoken wording; therefore no Duʿāʾ text is added or invented.

HAD-3295.text: The Prophet ﷺ commanded Ǧābir رضي الله عنه to call for the large bowl or the trough of the travel group.
HAD-3295.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3295.speaker: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3295.sharh: The large bowl is used in the report as the vessel for the subsequent supplying of the entire group.

HAD-3296.text: The Prophet ﷺ instructed Ǧābir رضي الله عنه to pour water over his hand and, while doing so, to say "Bismillah".
HAD-3296.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3296.speaker: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3296.sharh: The Šarḥ cites the expressly mentioned Basmalah as part of this specific action.

HAD-3297.text: Ǧābir رضي الله عنه saw water streaming forth from between the fingers of the Prophet ﷺ.
HAD-3297.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3297.speaker: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3297.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats the streaming forth of the water as a manifest sign of prophethood.

HAD-3298.text: The water continued to flow until the large bowl was completely filled.
HAD-3298.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3298.speaker: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3298.sharh: The filling of the vessel from the previously extremely small amount of water belongs to the same miracle, yet it is a distinct visible core of the event.

HAD-3299.text: The people came to the water and supplied themselves from it until they had met their need and quenched their thirst.
HAD-3299.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3299.speaker: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3299.sharh: The report makes clear that the extraordinary increase was not only observed, but was practically used to supply the travel group.

HAD-3300.text: When no one needed water any longer, the Prophet ﷺ lifted his hand out of the bowl; the bowl was still full.
HAD-3300.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3300.speaker: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3300.sharh: The conclusion of the report emphasizes that after the people had been fully supplied, water was still present in the vessel.

HAD-3301.text: When the people complained of their hunger to the Prophet ﷺ, he said: "Perhaps Allah will give you something to eat."
HAD-3301.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3301.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3301.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ cites the sentence as an introduction to the extraordinary supplying of the travel group and as an expression of trust in Allah's provision.

HAD-3302.text: At the seashore the sea cast up an enormous sea creature, by which the hungry travel group was supplied.
HAD-3302.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3302.speaker: Ǧābir رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3302.sharh: The Šarḥ treats the cast-up creature as a concrete supplying of the group after their complaint of hunger.

HAD-3303.text: The Companions cooked and roasted from the sea creature and ate of it until they were full.
HAD-3303.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3303.speaker: Ǧābir رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3303.sharh: The report makes clear that the creature was actually used as food and fully satisfied the hungry group.

HAD-3304.text: Ǧābir رضي الله عنه and four other men were able to step into the eye socket of this sea creature without being seen from outside.
HAD-3304.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3304.speaker: Ǧābir رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3304.sharh: The unusual indication of size is transmitted as part of the Companions' concrete observation and is not reinterpreted symbolically.

HAD-3305.text: A rib of the sea creature was so large that the tallest man of the travel group could pass underneath it on the largest camel with his load, without lowering his head.
HAD-3305.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3305.speaker: Ǧābir رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3305.sharh: This measurement too serves in the report to describe concretely the extraordinary size of the creature.

HAD-3306.text: Qurʾān 4:3 concerns, according to her explanation, among other things the orphan girl under the guardianship of a man whose property she shares with him, and whom he wishes to marry because of her property and her beauty, without giving her an appropriate bridal gift.
HAD-3306.narrator: ʿUrwah ibn az-Zubayr رحمه الله reported from ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها:
HAD-3306.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها explained:
HAD-3306.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats the report as an explanation of the prohibition of exploiting the dependence of an orphan woman; what is decisive is just treatment and an appropriate bridal gift.

HAD-3307.text: After the people later asked the Prophet ﷺ once again about the orphan women, Qurʾān 4:127 was revealed.
HAD-3307.narrator: ʿUrwah ibn az-Zubayr رحمه الله reported from ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها:
HAD-3307.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها explained:
HAD-3307.sharh: The report links the people’s later inquiry with the revelation of the further clarification in Sūrat an-Nisāʾ.

HAD-3308.text: The words in Qurʾān 4:127 about “what is recited to you in the Book concerning them” refer, according to her explanation, to the earlier statement in Qurʾān 4:3.
HAD-3308.narrator: ʿUrwah ibn az-Zubayr رحمه الله reported from ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها:
HAD-3308.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها explained:
HAD-3308.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ reproduces the connection of the two verses within the framework of the transmitted explanation of ʿĀʾišah.

HAD-3309.text: Qurʾān 4:127 also covers the case that a guardian keeps his distance from an orphan woman because of lesser property or lesser beauty, while he wishes to claim for himself a wealthy or beautiful orphan; what remains decisive is justice.
HAD-3309.narrator: ʿUrwah ibn az-Zubayr رحمه الله reported from ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها:
HAD-3309.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها explained:
HAD-3309.sharh: The Šarḥ preserves the standard of equality in the report: personal attractiveness or property must not lead to treating the rights of the dependent orphan woman differently.

HAD-3310.text: Qurʾān 4:6 allows the needy guardian of an orphan child to take from the child’s property in an appropriate measure.
HAD-3310.narrator: ʿUrwah ibn az-Zubayr رحمه الله reported from ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها:
HAD-3310.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها explained:
HAD-3310.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the report within the framework of the difference between the wealthy guardian, who abstains, and the needy guardian, who takes only in an appropriate measure.

HAD-3311.text: The words in Qurʾān 33:11, that the believers were tested there and violently shaken, refer to the day of the trench (al-Ḫandaq).
HAD-3311.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn az-Zubayr رحمه الله reported from ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها:
HAD-3311.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها explained:
HAD-3311.sharh: The report determines the historical reference of the āyah to the severe trial of the believers during the battle of the trench.

HAD-3312.text: Qurʾān 4:128 concerns, according to her explanation, among other things a woman whose long marital companionship the husband wishes to end; she can offer him to remain with him and voluntarily to forgo certain marital claims.
HAD-3312.narrator: ʿUrwah ibn az-Zubayr رحمه الله reported from ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها:
HAD-3312.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها explained:
HAD-3312.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats this as a voluntary marital settlement by which a woman can choose the continuance of the marriage, provided the agreement takes place by mutual consent.

HAD-3313.text: The revelation of Qurʾān 4:128 stands in connection with such a mutually agreed reconciliation between spouses; the verse explains that an agreement is better.
HAD-3313.narrator: ʿUrwah ibn az-Zubayr رحمه الله reported from ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها:
HAD-3313.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها explained:
HAD-3313.sharh: The Šarḥ classifies the report as evidence that a voluntary and permissible understanding between spouses can be preferable to a forced conflict.

HAD-3314.text: The people were commanded to ask forgiveness for the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ; instead, some of them reviled the Companions.
HAD-3314.narrator: ʿUrwah ibn az-Zubayr رحمه الله reported:
HAD-3314.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها said to him:
HAD-3314.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ classifies the statement as a rebuke of reviling the Ṣaḥābah and links it with the qurʾānic praise of those who ask forgiveness for the earlier believers.

HAD-3315.text: The āyah about the one who kills a believer intentionally (Qurʾān 4:93) belonged, according to his statement, to the āyāt revealed last; nothing had abrogated it.
HAD-3315.narrator: Saʿīd ibn Ǧubayr رحمه الله reported from Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-3315.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما said:
HAD-3315.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains the statement as an emphasis on the exceptional gravity of intentional killing. At the same time he makes clear that Ahl as-Sunnah affirm the fundamental acceptance of sincere Tawbah even in the case of major sins.

HAD-3316.text: The verses in Sūrat al-Furqān about Širk, unlawful killing and Zināʾ referred, in this revelation context, to people from the ranks of the Mušrikūn.
HAD-3316.narrator: Saʿīd ibn Ǧubayr رحمه الله reported from Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-3316.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما explained:
HAD-3316.sharh: The Šarḥ distinguishes the Meccan revelation context of the Furqān verses from the later severe threat in Q 4:93, without closing the general door of sincere Tawbah.

HAD-3317.text: Mušrikūn from Makkah asked what benefit Islam could bring them after they had committed Širk, unlawful killing and grave sexual immorality; thereupon the exception was revealed for the one who repents, believes and acts righteously.
HAD-3317.narrator: Saʿīd ibn Ǧubayr رحمه الله reported from Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-3317.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3317.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ cites this part as clear evidence for the breadth of Tawbah for those who had committed grave sins before Islam.

HAD-3318.text: To the question about the Tawbah of a Muslim who intentionally kills a believer, Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما answered in this report with a particularly strict denial.
HAD-3318.narrator: Saʿīd ibn Ǧubayr رحمه الله reported from Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-3318.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما said in the transmitted strict view:
HAD-3318.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ does not isolate this strict statement as a general Sunni dogma: he names as the view of Ahl as-Sunnah that sincere Tawbah can in principle be accepted, and he understands contrary reports of the Salaf within the framework of the massive deterrence from intentional killing.

HAD-3319.text: The threat in Qurʾān 4:93 was related by him to the one who knows Islam and its rulings and thereafter intentionally kills a believer.
HAD-3319.narrator: Saʿīd ibn Ǧubayr رحمه الله reported from Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-3319.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما explained:
HAD-3319.sharh: The Šarḥ treats this as the utmost threat against intentional killing. The wording is not used as a Takfīr of the perpetrator or as a setting aside of the general Sunni teaching of the possible Tawbah.

HAD-3320.text: As the last sūrah that was revealed completely as a whole sūrah, Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما named Sūrat an-Naṣr: “When Allah’s help and the victory come.”
HAD-3320.narrator: ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbdillāh ibn ʿUtbah رحمه الله reported:
HAD-3320.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما said:
HAD-3320.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats the wording as a statement about the last sūrah revealed in full; it is not to be equated with every statement about the chronologically last single āyah.

HAD-3321.text: A man with his herd met Muslims and greeted them with Salām. They killed him nonetheless and took his herd; thereupon Qurʾān 4:94 was revealed as a rebuke of this conduct.
HAD-3321.narrator: ʿAṭāʾ رحمه الله reported from Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-3321.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3321.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ emphasizes the protection of the one who shows a recognizable sign of Islām, and the severe rebuke of hasty judgments out of worldly interest.

HAD-3322.text: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما read in this connection the relevant passage of Qurʾān 4:94 with “as-salām” and linked it with the spoken greeting of peace of the killed man.
HAD-3322.narrator: ʿAṭāʾ رحمه الله reported from Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-3322.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما read:
HAD-3322.sharh: The Šarḥ treats the transmitted reading in the immediate context of the spoken Salām; from this follows the duty of restraint toward a recognizable sign of Islām.

HAD-3323.text: The Anṣār used, after the Ḥaǧǧ, not to enter their houses through the doors, but from behind. When a man entered through his door, Qurʾān 2:189 was revealed: Righteousness does not consist in entering houses from behind.
HAD-3323.narrator: Abū Isḥāq رحمه الله reported from al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib رضي الله عنه:
HAD-3323.speaker: al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-3323.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ classifies the report as the abolition of a pre-Islamic or customary practice and binds righteousness to Taqwā rather than to such self-imposed forms.

HAD-3324.text: Between their entry into Islam and Allah’s admonition through Qurʾān 57:16 – that the hearts of the believers should humble themselves before Allah’s remembrance – there lay, according to his statement, only four years.
HAD-3324.narrator: ʿAwn ibn ʿAbdillāh رحمه الله reported from Ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه:
HAD-3324.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-3324.sharh: The report shows how early the believers were admonished to inner humility and to protection against the hardening of hearts.

HAD-3325.text: A woman performed, in pre-Islamic practice, the Ṭawāf unclothed and sought only a cloth to cover her private parts; thereupon Qurʾān 7:31 was revealed: “Take your adornment/clothing at every place of prayer.”
HAD-3325.narrator: Saʿīd ibn Ǧubayr رحمه الله reported from Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-3325.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3325.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ links the āyah with the removal of the naked Ṭawāf from the Ǧāhiliyyah and with the command of appropriate covering.

HAD-3326.text: The «gain of the life of this world» mentioned in Qurʾān 4:94 referred, in this occasion of revelation, to the herd of the man that was taken after he was killed.
HAD-3326.narrator: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3326.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما explained:
HAD-3326.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ cites the report at this place in the Tafsīr context; the worldly gain is related to the captured livestock of the one who was killed.

HAD-3327.text: ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl said to one of his slave women that she should go out and earn something for him through fornication.
HAD-3327.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3327.speaker: Ǧābir رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3327.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ cites the occasion of revelation on p. 590; the card is limited to the concrete compulsion to prostitution in the report.

HAD-3328.text: Two women under the disposal of ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy, Musaykah and Umaymah, were compelled by him to fornication.
HAD-3328.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3328.speaker: Ǧābir رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3328.sharh: The second wording in Muslim names the two women concerned and makes the compulsion explicit.

HAD-3329.text: Musaykah and Umaymah complained to the Prophet ﷺ that they had been compelled to fornication.
HAD-3329.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3329.speaker: Ǧābir رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3329.sharh: The complaint of the two women is the immediate narrative step before the revelation mentioned in the report.

HAD-3330.text: In connection with this compulsion, Qurʾān 24:33 was revealed: slave women may not be compelled to prostitution if they desire chastity.
HAD-3330.narrator: Ǧābir ibn ʿAbdillāh رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3330.speaker: Ǧābir رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3330.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ cites the report as the occasion of revelation; the card reproduces only the connection to the verse transmitted by the Ṣaḥābī.

HAD-3331.text: Some people among the Arabs worshipped a group of Ǧinn.
HAD-3331.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3331.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه explained:
HAD-3331.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ cites this Tafsīr report on p. 591 without an additional detailed commentary; the card stays with the transmitted core.

HAD-3332.text: The Ǧinn worshipped by these people later accepted Islam.
HAD-3332.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3332.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه explained:
HAD-3332.sharh: The report expressly states that the worshipped Ǧinn themselves became Muslims.

HAD-3333.text: The people who worshipped these Ǧinn did not notice their Islam and at first held fast to their worship.
HAD-3333.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3333.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه explained:
HAD-3333.sharh: The distinct point of the report is the ignorance of the human worshippers about the Ǧinn’s change of faith.

HAD-3334.text: In this connection Qurʾān 17:57 was revealed: precisely those who are called upon themselves seek nearness to their Lord.
HAD-3334.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3334.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه explained:
HAD-3334.sharh: The Ṣaḥābī connects the described state of the Ǧinn directly with the revelation of Qurʾān 17:57.

HAD-3335.text: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما designated Sūrat at-Tawbah as «al-Fāḍiḥah» – the exposing Sūrah.
HAD-3335.narrator: Saʿīd ibn Ǧubayr رحمه الله reported from Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-3335.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما said:
HAD-3335.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ cites the Tafsīr report on p. 592; the byname is taken directly from the statement of Ibn ʿAbbās.

HAD-3336.text: About Sūrat at-Tawbah, Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما said that statements such as «and among them …» were revealed in succession, and thereby ever further conditions were laid open.
HAD-3336.narrator: Saʿīd ibn Ǧubayr رحمه الله reported from Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-3336.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما said:
HAD-3336.sharh: The report explains the byname al-Fāḍiḥah through the repeated laying open of various groups and qualities.

HAD-3337.text: The successive disclosures in Sūrat at-Tawbah went so far that they feared that no one among them would remain unmentioned.
HAD-3337.narrator: Saʿīd ibn Ǧubayr رحمه الله reported from Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-3337.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما said:
HAD-3337.sharh: This sentence describes the effect of the repeated revelations and is kept apart from the mere byname of the Sūrah.

HAD-3338.text: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما designated Sūrat al-Anfāl as the Sūrah of Badr.
HAD-3338.narrator: Saʿīd ibn Ǧubayr رحمه الله reported from Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-3338.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما said:
HAD-3338.sharh: The assignment of Sūrat al-Anfāl to Badr stands expressly in the authentic Tafsīr report.

HAD-3339.text: Sūrat al-Ḥašr was, according to the explanation of Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما, revealed concerning Banū an-Naḍīr.
HAD-3339.narrator: Saʿīd ibn Ǧubayr رحمه الله reported from Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما:
HAD-3339.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما said:
HAD-3339.sharh: The assignment of Sūrat al-Ḥašr to Banū an-Naḍīr stands expressly in the authentic Tafsīr report.

HAD-3340.text: ʿUmar رضي الله عنه delivered this address on the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
HAD-3340.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3340.speaker: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-3340.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ cites the report on p. 593; the place of the address is expressly named in the Isnād text as the pulpit of the Prophet ﷺ.

HAD-3341.text: ʿUmar رضي الله عنه recalled that the prohibition of Khamr had been revealed.
HAD-3341.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3341.speaker: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-3341.sharh: The report begins with the reminder of the revelation of the prohibition of alcohol; Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ refers thereby to the Khamr topic already treated earlier.

HAD-3342.text: In this report Khamr was named from five source substances: wheat, barley, dates, raisins or grapes, and honey.
HAD-3342.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3342.speaker: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-3342.sharh: The five named source substances serve in the report to not limit the category to a single drink or a single material.

HAD-3343.text: Khamr is that which covers the intellect.
HAD-3343.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3343.speaker: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-3343.sharh: ʿUmar رضي الله عنه formulates here the decisive standard of meaning: what is decisive is the covering or the impairing of the intellect.

HAD-3344.text: ʿUmar رضي الله عنه wished that the Prophet ﷺ had left them a conclusive, unambiguous instruction regarding the inheritance question of the grandfather.
HAD-3344.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3344.speaker: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-3344.sharh: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ refers to the questions of inheritance law already treated elsewhere; here only ʿUmar’s expressly stated wish is recorded.

HAD-3345.text: ʿUmar رضي الله عنه likewise wished for a conclusive prophetic instruction concerning the Kalālah.
HAD-3345.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3345.speaker: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-3345.sharh: The Kalālah is named by ʿUmar as an independent legal question alongside the grandfather’s inheritance and the questions of Ribā.

HAD-3206.text: When ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها finally measured the remaining barley, it came to an end.
HAD-3206.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-3206.sharh: The report is rendered as a concrete observation, without a general rule about measuring being derived from it.

HAD-3207.text: The Prophet ﷺ died without having been satiated twice on a single day from bread and oil.
HAD-3207.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-3207.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ emphasizes the simple way of life of the Prophet ﷺ.

HAD-3208.text: The Prophet ﷺ died at a time when the people were already able to be satiated with dates and water.
HAD-3208.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-3208.sharh: The report contrasts generally available food with his personal simple way of life.

HAD-3209.text: The Prophet ﷺ and his family were never, until his death, satiated for three consecutive days with wheat bread.
HAD-3209.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3209.speaker: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3209.sharh: This temporal core is kept separate from similar two-day and month reports.

HAD-3210.text: He reminded his listeners that the Prophet ﷺ at times did not even find enough inferior dates to fill his belly.
HAD-3210.narrator: an-Nuʿmān ibn Bašīr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3210.speaker: an-Nuʿmān ibn Bašīr رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3210.sharh: The report contrasts later abundance with earlier deprivation.

HAD-3211.text: The poor Muhāǧirūn will precede the rich by forty years in entering Paradise on the Day of Resurrection.
HAD-3211.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3211.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3211.sharh: The precedence is connected in the report with the reckoning over possessions; it is not a blanket rule of rank concerning every poor person and every rich person.

HAD-3212.text: Do not enter the dwellings of those who wronged themselves except in a state of weeping and of fear that the like may befall you.
HAD-3212.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3212.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3212.sharh: The Prophet ﷺ classifies such places as an admonition, not as an ordinary sight.

HAD-3213.text: The Prophet ﷺ hastened his way until he had left the region of al-Ḥiǧr behind him.
HAD-3213.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3213.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3213.sharh: The prophetic action supplements the verbal warning of the same report.

HAD-3214.text: When the people in the region of Ṯamūd took water from its wells and prepared dough with it, the Prophet ﷺ commanded that the water be poured away, that the dough be given to the camels, and that water be drawn only from the well that the she-camel had sought out.
HAD-3214.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3214.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-3214.sharh: The instruction shows practical distancing from the water places especially connected with the punishment.

HAD-3215.text: Whoever exerts himself for a widow and a needy person is like someone who exerts himself on Allah’s path; in the transmission he is also compared with one who prays and fasts continually.
HAD-3215.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3215.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3215.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ highlights continuous care as a great ʿIbādah.

HAD-3216.text: The one who cares for an orphan — whether a relative of his own or a stranger — will be with the Prophet ﷺ in Paradise as close as the index finger and the middle finger.
HAD-3216.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3216.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3216.sharh: The comparison of the fingers describes a special closeness in Paradise and emphasizes the high standing of reliable care for orphans.

HAD-3217.text: A man heard in a cloud a voice that commanded: Water the garden of so-and-so; the cloud discharged its water precisely in the direction of that garden.
HAD-3217.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3217.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ reported:
HAD-3217.sharh: The beginning of the report shows a special provision for a man on account of his responsible use of the yield.

HAD-3218.text: He divided the yield of his garden into three parts: one he gave as Ṣadaqah, one he used for himself and his family, and one he returned to the garden.
HAD-3218.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3218.speaker: The garden owner explained:
HAD-3218.sharh: The report joins charity, provision for the family, and sustainable cultivation; precisely this balanced use explains the special blessing in the context.

HAD-3219.text: I am the One least in need of an associate. Whoever performs a deed and associates someone else with Me in it, I leave him with his associate.
HAD-3219.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3219.speaker: Allah تبارك وتعالى said:
HAD-3219.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ qudsī warns against performing acts of worship for Allah and at the same time for the recognition of others.

HAD-3220.text: Whoever causes his deeds to be heard, Allah will cause his reality to be heard; and whoever shows off, Allah will expose his reality.
HAD-3220.narrator: Ibn ʿAbbās and Ǧundub رضي الله عنهم reported:
HAD-3220.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3220.sharh: The two versions in Muslim carry the same core and are therefore brought together into one card: public self-display turns back against the doer.

HAD-3221.text: A servant can speak a word without heeding its import, and thereby fall deeper into the fire than the distance between East and West.
HAD-3221.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3221.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3221.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ makes the tongue an object of serious responsibility and warns against careless speech.

HAD-3222.text: Forgiveness can be granted to all of my Ummah except those who make their sins public; this includes that Allah covers a sin and the person himself discloses it in the morning.
HAD-3222.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3222.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3222.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ is directed against a proud or careless disclosure of one’s own sins after divine covering.

HAD-3223.text: When one of you sneezes and praises Allah, then wish him mercy; if he does not praise Allah, then do not do it.
HAD-3223.narrator: Abū Mūsā al-Ašʿarī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3223.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3223.sharh: The Tašmīt is in the Ḥadīṯ expressly tied to the Ḥamd of the one who sneezes.

HAD-3224.text: When a man sneezed again in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, he said about him: The man has a cold.
HAD-3224.narrator: Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3224.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3224.sharh: The report distinguishes ordinary sneezing from repeated sneezing on account of a cold and prevents a mechanical, unlimited repetition of the same response.

HAD-3225.text: When one of you yawns, he should place his hand over his mouth, for the Satan enters.
HAD-3225.narrator: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3225.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3225.sharh: This core is independent with respect to the already present general instruction to suppress yawning.

HAD-3186.text: When the angel later, in the earlier form of the leper, asked for help, this one denied his earlier poverty and claimed to have inherited the property from his ancestors.
HAD-3186.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3186.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3186.sharh: The report connects the refusal of help with the denial of one's own past. Precisely this untruthfulness makes the ingratitude especially clear.

HAD-3187.text: The formerly bald man also refused the help and answered like the leper.
HAD-3187.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3187.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3187.sharh: The second person falls into the same test: a favor received is not acknowledged, and the need of others is not answered with gratitude.

HAD-3188.text: The formerly blind man confessed: I was blind and Allah gave me my eyesight back. Take from my property whatever you wish; I will not withhold from you anything that you take for the sake of Allah.
HAD-3188.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3188.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3188.sharh: His answer combines remembrance of his own need, acknowledgment of Allah's favor, and practical generosity. Thereby he passes the test.

HAD-3189.text: At the end of the test of the three men, the angel explained to the grateful formerly blind man that Allah was pleased with him and was angry with his two companions.
HAD-3189.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3189.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3189.sharh: The outcome makes the standard clear: acknowledgment of Allah's favor, truthfulness, and readiness to give lead to passing the test; denial and stinginess lead to the opposite.

HAD-3190.text: Allah loves the God-fearing, content, and hidden servant.
HAD-3190.narrator: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3190.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3190.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ praises Taqwā, inner contentment, and the avoidance of unnecessary self-display. Hiddenness here does not mean the neglect of obligatory responsibility.

HAD-3191.text: By Allah, I was the first man among the Arabs who shot an arrow on the path of Allah.
HAD-3191.narrator: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-3191.speaker: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-3191.sharh: Saʿd recalls his early participation and his long earlier life in Islam. The statement is mawqūf upon him and is therefore carried as an Āṯar.

HAD-3192.text: We set out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and at times had nothing to eat except the leaves of wild trees, until the hardship became clearly visible on their bodies.
HAD-3192.narrator: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-3192.speaker: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-3192.sharh: The report documents the actual deprivation of the early companions and places later prosperity in a historical contrast. As a Ṣaḥābī report it is mawqūf.

HAD-3193.text: The Dunyā has announced its end and is departing swiftly; you will pass from it into an abode that knows no end.
HAD-3193.narrator: ʿUtbah ibn Ġazwān رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-3193.speaker: ʿUtbah ibn Ġazwān رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-3193.sharh: ʿUtbah calls in his sermon for the transience of the Dunyā to be measured against the lasting Hereafter and for good deeds to be sent ahead for this transition.

HAD-3194.text: It was reported to us that a stone is thrown down from the edge of Hell and falls for seventy years without reaching its bottom.
HAD-3194.narrator: ʿUtbah ibn Ġazwān رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-3194.speaker: ʿUtbah ibn Ġazwān رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-3194.sharh: The statement appears within the authentically transmitted sermon of ʿUtbah with the wording that this had been reported to them. It is therefore conservatively carried as a mawqūf Āṯar in the context of Muslim.

HAD-3195.text: It was reported to us that between the two leaves of a gate of Paradise there lies a journey of forty years, and yet a day will come when it is densely filled with people.
HAD-3195.narrator: ʿUtbah ibn Ġazwān رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-3195.speaker: ʿUtbah ibn Ġazwān رضي الله عنه said:
HAD-3195.sharh: This sentence too stands within the sermon of ʿUtbah and is reproduced without an additional marfūʿ attribution. It combines enormous breadth with the great number of those who enter.

HAD-3196.text: The believers will see their Lord on the Day of Resurrection, with no greater difficulty than in clearly seeing the sun or the full moon.
HAD-3196.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3196.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3196.sharh: The Ḥadīṯ confirms the Ruʾyah in the Hereafter and compares the clarity of seeing, not Allah with the sun or the moon. The statement is affirmed in accordance with the transmitted wording.

HAD-3197.text: A servant is reminded of Allah's gifts and asked whether he had reckoned with meeting Allah. If he denies this, he is recompensed according to his own disregard.
HAD-3197.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3197.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3197.sharh: The wording of 'forgetting' stands here in the context of punishment and recompense and means abandonment or disregard, not a deficiency in Allah's knowledge.

HAD-3198.text: A hypocrite will argue on the Day of Judgment with the faith-services and worship-services he claimed; then his mouth will be sealed and his body will bear witness concerning his actual deeds.
HAD-3198.narrator: Abū Hurayrah رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3198.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3198.sharh: Outward claims do not suffice before Allah. The report shows that the human being is deprived of the possibility of false self-presentation and that his own limbs become witnesses.

HAD-3199.text: A servant will demand that only a witness from himself against himself be accepted. Thereupon his mouth will be sealed and his hands and feet will speak about his deeds.
HAD-3199.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3199.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-3199.sharh: The report emphasizes complete justice: the human being receives precisely the kind of testimony that he demands, yet his own limbs refute his excuses.

HAD-3200.text: The family of Muḥammad ﷺ never ate wheat bread to satiety for three consecutive nights from their arrival in Madīnah until the death of the Prophet ﷺ; barley bread also was not permanently available in abundance.
HAD-3200.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-3200.sharh: The parallel versions describe the same core: despite his station, the Prophet ﷺ did not live with his family in lasting abundance of food. The variants are therefore not artificially multiplied.

HAD-3201.text: The family of Muḥammad ﷺ was not sated with wheat bread on two consecutive days without dates being present on one of the two days.
HAD-3201.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-3201.sharh: The statement specifies the simplicity of the household provision in the house of the Prophet ﷺ and places the value of worldly abundance in relation to the Hereafter.

HAD-3202.text: Over the course of two months the family of the Prophet ﷺ saw three new moons without a fire for cooking being lit in his houses.
HAD-3202.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-3202.sharh: The report shows the long duration of simple provision without cooked meals and serves to place the Dunyā.

HAD-3203.text: In this time their basic food consisted of dates and water.
HAD-3203.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-3203.sharh: The record separates the actual core of the provision from the time indication of the same report.

HAD-3204.text: Neighbors of the Prophet ﷺ from the Anṣār sent him milk from their animals, and he gave his family to drink of it.
HAD-3204.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-3204.sharh: The report shows concrete neighborly help in the simple situation of provision.

HAD-3205.text: When the Prophet ﷺ died, there remained with ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها only half a measure of barley; she ate of it for a long time.
HAD-3205.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها reported:
HAD-3205.sharh: The report connects small stores with an unusually long benefit.

HAD-3360.text: Abū Qilābah said: Recording [knowledge] in writing is dearer to me than forgetting it.
HAD-3360.narrator: It is reported concerning Abū Qilābah:
HAD-3360.speaker: Early āṯar:

HAD-3361.text: Ibrāhīm an-Naḫaʿī considered it unobjectionable to record in writing short beginnings of transmissions, or excerpts from them.
HAD-3361.narrator: It is reported concerning Ibrāhīm an-Naḫaʿī:
HAD-3361.speaker: Early āṯar:

HAD-3362.text: It is reported of Saʿīd ibn Ǧubayr that, while traveling, he recorded on a part of his riding saddle the reports he had heard with Ibn ʿAbbās, and after dismounting he copied them out neatly.
HAD-3362.narrator: It is reported concerning Saʿīd ibn Ǧubayr:
HAD-3362.speaker: Early āṯar:

HAD-3363.text: A woman disputed with her husband over a gift she had previously given him. When the man cited Qurʾān 4:4 as his basis, Šurayḥ replied: If she had truly been content with the gift, the two of you would not be disputing over it.
HAD-3363.narrator: Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn reported about the judge Šurayḥ:
HAD-3363.speaker: Šurayḥ’s reply in a dispute:

HAD-3364.text: Ibrāhīm an-Naḫaʿī said, in substance: If a woman gives her husband something voluntarily and of her own decision, this gift is valid.
HAD-3364.narrator: It is transmitted from Ibrāhīm an-Naḫaʿī:
HAD-3364.speaker: His statement relating to fiqh:

HAD-3365.text: ar-Rabīʿ ibn Saʿd reported that he had seen Ǧābir writing on tablets in the presence of Ibn Sābiṭ. The report describes an early form of recording knowledge in writing.
HAD-3365.narrator: It is reported concerning ar-Rabīʿ ibn Saʿd, who reported about Ǧābir:
HAD-3365.speaker: Transmitted report:

HAD-3366.text: ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Ḥarmalah said that he had had a weak memory. For that reason Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib permitted him to write down knowledge.
HAD-3366.narrator: It is reported concerning ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Ḥarmalah:
HAD-3366.speaker: Transmitted report:

HAD-3367.text: From ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb the counsel is transmitted: “Hold knowledge fast by written records.” The authenticity of precisely this path of transmission remains to be examined.
HAD-3367.narrator: It is reported concerning ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb:
HAD-3367.speaker: Transmitted report:

HAD-3368.text: Maʿn reported: ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbdillāh showed him a written document and swore that his father had written it with his own hand. The report concerns the preservation of an old written record.
HAD-3368.narrator: It is reported concerning Maʿn, who reported about ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbdillāh:
HAD-3368.speaker: Transmitted report:

HAD-3369.text: Ḥusayn ibn ʿAqīl said: “aḍ-Ḍaḥḥāk dictated to me the rites of the Ḥaǧǧ.” With that, the passing on of knowledge by dictation is described.
HAD-3369.narrator: It is reported concerning Ḥusayn ibn ʿAqīl, from aḍ-Ḍaḥḥāk:
HAD-3369.speaker: Transmitted report:

HAD-3370.text: Bašīr ibn Nuhayk reported: He wrote down what he heard from Abū Hurayrah. Before they parted, he showed Abū Hurayrah his writing and asked whether he had heard that from him. Abū Hurayrah confirmed it.
HAD-3370.narrator: It is reported concerning Bašīr ibn Nuhayk:
HAD-3370.speaker: Transmitted report:

HAD-3371.text: Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn reported that he used to come to ʿUbaydah with beginnings of transmissions, or with excerpts from them, in order to ask him about them. The report does not expressly say whether these excerpts were in writing.
HAD-3371.narrator: It is reported concerning Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn:
HAD-3371.speaker: Transmitted report:

HAD-3372.text: Abū l-Malīḥ replied to those who criticized them because of written records: “They reproach us for writing, yet Allah said: ‘The knowledge of that is with my Lord in a Book.’” In doing so he referred to Qurʾān 20:52.
HAD-3372.narrator: It is reported concerning Abū l-Malīḥ:
HAD-3372.speaker: Transmitted report:

HAD-3373.text: ʿAbdullāh ibn Ḥanaš reported that he had seen people with al-Barāʾ writing with reed pens on the palms of their hands. This is an observation of early written notes, not a transmitted formula of command.
HAD-3373.narrator: It is reported concerning ʿAbdullāh ibn Ḥanaš (the reading of the name has not been collated independently):
HAD-3373.speaker: Transmitted report:

HAD-3374.text: Ibn ʿAwn reported that Ibn Sīrīn, al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad and Raǧāʾ ibn Ḥaywah were especially careful to pass on Ḥadīṯe as they had heard them. When another procedure was mentioned, Ibn Sīrīn replied that the more precise rendering would be better.
HAD-3374.narrator: It is reported concerning Ibn ʿAwn, together with a reply of Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn:
HAD-3374.speaker: Transmitted report:

HAD-3375.text: Aš-Šaʿbī transmitted that ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbdillāh used to record in writing what he heard. This report describes his personal practice in learning.
HAD-3375.narrator: It is reported concerning ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbdillāh:
HAD-3375.speaker: Early āṯar:

HAD-3376.text: When learners asked Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī to record his Ḥadīṯe for them in writing, he refused this in the conversation that is described and called on them to take the knowledge from him in the manner in which he had taken it from the Prophet ﷺ.
HAD-3376.narrator: It is reported concerning Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī:
HAD-3376.speaker: Early āṯar:

HAD-3377.text: Sulaymān ibn al-Aswad reported that Ibn Masʿūd did not prefer the recording of knowledge in writing. Since the report names no concrete occasion, no uniform stance of all the Ṣaḥābah may be derived from it.
HAD-3377.narrator: It is reported concerning ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd:
HAD-3377.speaker: Early āṯar:

HAD-3378.text: Ibrāhīm an-Naḫaʿī reported that ʿUbaydah called on him not to bind a book of his statements. The transmitted sentence is short and itself contains no further reason.
HAD-3378.narrator: It is reported concerning ʿUbaydah as-Salmānī:
HAD-3378.speaker: Early āṯar:

HAD-3379.text: Abū Burdah reported that he had compiled from his father’s knowledge an extensive book. When he brought it at his father’s request, his father washed out the records. The report transmits no additional sentence of justification.
HAD-3379.narrator: It is reported concerning Abū Burdah:
HAD-3379.speaker: Early āṯar:

HAD-3380.text: Aš-Šaʿbī transmitted an incident in which those present wrote down the statements of Zayd ibn Ṯābit without his knowledge. When he learned of it, he expressed the concern that not all the wordings might have been rendered exactly as he had said them.
HAD-3380.narrator: It is reported concerning Zayd ibn Ṯābit:
HAD-3380.speaker: Early āṯar:

HAD-3381.text: Ibn ʿAwn reported that al-Qāsim did not prefer the writing down of Ḥadīṯe. The report names no detailed reason and does not establish a general agreement of the early scholars.
HAD-3381.speaker: Early āṯar:

HAD-3382.text: Saʿīd ibn Ǧubayr reported that he used to record disputed questions in a book and then go with it to Ibn ʿUmar in order to ask him about them in person. The learning practice is here described by himself.
HAD-3382.narrator: It is reported concerning Saʿīd ibn Ǧubayr:
HAD-3382.speaker: Early āṯar:

HAD-3383.text: It is reported of Abū Maʿmar that he would pass on a Ḥadīṯ, even in a linguistically faulty form, as far as possible just as he had heard it. This describes his personal care in transmission, not a binding rule of grammar.
HAD-3383.narrator: It is reported concerning Abū Maʿmar:
HAD-3383.speaker: Early āṯar:

HAD-3384.text: Ismāʿīl ibn Umayyah related that they wanted to move Nāfiʿ to a linguistic correction in the transmission. He refused the desired change and held to the form he had heard.
HAD-3384.speaker: Early āṯar:

HAD-3385.text: Abū Saʿīd encouraged people to speak with one another about Ḥadīṯe, because discussing a transmission brings other transmissions to mind.
HAD-3385.narrator: Abū Naḍrah reported from Abū Saʿīd al-Ḫudrī:
HAD-3385.speaker: Transmitted statement:

HAD-3386.text: To ʿAlī is attributed the counsel that people visit one another and repeat the Ḥadīṯe together, since otherwise they fall into oblivion with time.
HAD-3386.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn Buraydah transmitted from ʿAlī:
HAD-3386.speaker: Transmitted statement:

HAD-3387.text: According to this report, Ismāʿīl ibn Raǧāʾ used to go to the children in their writing lessons and recite his Ḥadīṯe to them so that he would not forget them.
HAD-3387.narrator: Al-Aʿmaš transmitted about Ismāʿīl ibn Raǧāʾ:
HAD-3387.speaker: Transmitted statement:

HAD-3388.text: Ibrāhīm an-Naḫaʿī recommended that a newly heard transmission be passed on as soon as possible, because what was heard can thereby become anchored in the memory like a written document.
HAD-3388.narrator: ʿĪsā ibn al-Musayyib reported that he heard Ibrāhīm:
HAD-3388.speaker: Transmitted statement:

HAD-3389.text: ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā presented repeating together as a preservation of the Ḥadīṯe. ʿAbdullāh ibn Šaddād replied to that with how many transmissions he had revived in his memory in this way.
HAD-3389.narrator: Yazīd reported from a conversation about repeating transmissions:
HAD-3389.speaker: Transmitted statement:

HAD-3390.text: To ʿAbdullāh is attributed the saying that forgetting is one of the dangers to preserved knowledge.
HAD-3390.speaker: Early transmitted statement:

HAD-3391.text: It is transmitted from ʿUmar that he instructed his governors in writing not to gather his communications into a bound book. This report concerns the administrative context that is named.
HAD-3391.narrator: Al-Muġīrah reported from an instruction of ʿUmar:
HAD-3391.speaker: Early transmitted statement:

HAD-3392.text: In a transmitted saying, Ibn Sīrīn traced the going astray of the Children of Israel to writings they had received from their forebears. The report is to be treated as an admonition attributed to him, and not as a verse of the Qurʾān or a word of the Prophet.
HAD-3392.narrator: This historical warning is attributed to Ibn Sīrīn:
HAD-3392.speaker: Early transmitted statement:

HAD-3393.text: In a report, Ibn ʿAbbās permitted a learner to write down knowledge, yet according to the wording he did so only hesitantly. This concrete learning incident is not extended into a general prohibition or a general command.
HAD-3393.narrator: A decision about writing down was transmitted concerning Ibn ʿAbbās:
HAD-3393.speaker: Early transmitted statement:

HAD-3394.text: Al-Aʿmaš asked Abū aḍ-Ḍuḥā about the grammatical form of an Arabic word in a transmission. His answer was al-muṣawwirīn instead of the form presented, al-muṣawwirūn. It is a concrete correction of wording.
HAD-3394.narrator: Al-Aʿmaš related a linguistic question put to Abū aḍ-Ḍuḥā:
HAD-3394.speaker: Early transmitted statement:

HAD-3395.text: Aš-Šaʿbī said, in substance: He knew no one, across the different regions, who had sought knowledge more eagerly than Masrūq.
HAD-3395.speaker: Transmitted report:

HAD-3396.text: After aš-Šaʿbī had passed on a Ḥadīṯ, he explained to his student that such a transmission had become available to him without a journey, although formerly people had traveled to Medina even for less than that.
HAD-3396.narrator: A transmitter reported about a lesson with aš-Šaʿbī:
HAD-3396.speaker: Transmitted report:

HAD-3397.text: Qays ibn ʿAbbād said that he had set out for Medina in order to seek knowledge and honor, that is, standing. The statement documents his personal motive for the journey.
HAD-3397.narrator: Qays ibn ʿAbbād reported from his own life:
HAD-3397.speaker: Transmitted report:

HAD-3398.text: Ibn Sīrīn asked ʿUbaydah whether he might read a book he had found. ʿUbaydah answered: “No.” The report names no further circumstances about the origin or the content of this book.
HAD-3398.narrator: Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn reported a question put to ʿUbaydah:
HAD-3398.speaker: Transmitted report:

HAD-3399.text: Aḍ-Ḍaḥḥāk warned against making quires for Ḥadīṯe in the manner in which quires are made for the Muṣḥaf. The report concerns the outward form of written collections; this short wording does not name a further reason.
HAD-3399.narrator: ʿAbdullāh, the muʾaḏḏin of aḍ-Ḍaḥḥāk, transmitted his words:
HAD-3399.speaker: Transmitted report:

HAD-3400.text: It is reported of Muǧāhid that he did not prefer the making of Ḥadīṯ quires (karārīs). This transmission does not name a closer reason.
HAD-3400.speaker: Transmitted report:

HAD-3401.text: It is reported of Ibrāhīm an-Naḫaʿī that he disliked the use of such quires for collecting transmissions. The sentence describes the stance attributed to him, not a prophetic command.
HAD-3401.narrator: It is reported concerning Ibrāhīm an-Naḫaʿī:
HAD-3401.speaker: Transmitted report:

HAD-3402.text: Ibrāhīm an-Naḫaʿī reported that it was disapproved when someone, in a gathering, brought out precisely his best transmission. The short report does not explain more closely to which persons this judgment referred.
HAD-3402.narrator: Ibrāhīm an-Naḫaʿī reported about an earlier manner of conduct:
HAD-3402.speaker: Transmitted statement:

HAD-3403.text: A questioner wanted to know how he should deal with a linguistic error in a Ḥadīṯ he had heard. Aš-Šaʿbī answered: “Correct it.” This single answer stands alongside reports about other transmitters who deliberately held to the linguistic form they had heard.
HAD-3403.narrator: It is reported concerning a conversation with aš-Šaʿbī (ʿĀmir):
HAD-3403.speaker: Transmitted report:

HAD-3404.text: Al-Aswad ibn Hilāl described how a sheet containing transmissions was presented to ʿAbdullāh, which he had wiped out and then burned. In the same account he warned against putting transmitted writings in the place of Allāh’s Book. The concrete act is not presented as a general rule.
HAD-3404.narrator: Al-Aswad ibn Hilāl reported an incident with ʿAbdullāh:
HAD-3404.speaker: Transmitted report:

HAD-3405.text: When Zirr ibn Ḥubayš explained that he had come seeking knowledge, Ṣafwān ibn ʿAssāl reminded him that the angels lower their wings for the seeker of knowledge.
HAD-3405.narrator: Zirr ibn Ḥubayš reported an encounter with Ṣafwān ibn ʿAssāl:
HAD-3405.speaker: Ṣafwān ibn ʿAssāl al-Murādī said, in substance:

HAD-3406.text: Ibn ʿAbbās said about someone who teaches good that all things ask forgiveness for him, even the fish in the sea.
HAD-3406.narrator: Saʿīd ibn Ǧubayr transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās:
HAD-3406.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās said, in substance:

HAD-3407.text: Ibn ʿAbbās described two people whose striving is not satisfied: the seeker of knowledge and the seeker of worldly goods.
HAD-3407.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās said, in substance:

HAD-3408.text: ʿAbdullāh admonished to acquire knowledge, since a person does not know when others will depend on his knowledge and ask him about it.
HAD-3408.narrator: An admonition is transmitted from ʿAbdullāh:
HAD-3408.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd said, in substance:

HAD-3409.text: Abū ad-Dardāʾ called people to learn before knowledge is lost, and said that the teacher and the learner are equal in reward.
HAD-3409.narrator: Sālim ibn Abī l-Ǧaʿd transmitted an admonition of Abū ad-Dardāʾ:
HAD-3409.speaker: Abū ad-Dardāʾ said, in substance:

HAD-3410.text: No one is born a scholar; knowledge is acquired through learning.
HAD-3410.narrator: Abū l-Aḥwaṣ transmitted from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd:
HAD-3410.speaker: ʿAbdullāh said, in substance:

HAD-3411.text: Whoever learns Ḥadīṯe only in order to dispute with the ignorant by means of them, to boast of them before scholars, or to draw the attention of other people to himself, the Fire threatens him according to Makḥūl’s sharp admonition.
HAD-3411.speaker: Makḥūl warned, in substance:

HAD-3412.text: When Ibn ʿAbbās conveyed a Ḥadīṯ to him, Saʿīd ibn Ǧubayr felt such reverence that he would have liked to stand up and kiss Ibn ʿAbbās’s head, if he had permitted it.
HAD-3412.narrator: ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Ǧazarī reported that he heard Saʿīd ibn Ǧubayr:
HAD-3412.speaker: Saʿīd reported:

HAD-3413.text: ʿAbdullāh ibn Idrīs reported that he had been angered with al-Aʿmaš over a matter and for that reason did not visit him for a whole year. The report describes a personal incident among scholars.
HAD-3413.narrator: Ḥafṣ ibn Ġiyāṯ transmitted that he heard ʿAbdullāh ibn Idrīs:
HAD-3413.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn Idrīs reported:

HAD-3414.text: When her visitors asked whether the shared conversation wearied her, Umm ad-Dardāʾ denied it. She explained that she had sought worship in many things, yet had found nothing more beneficial for herself than discussing knowledge together; according to another wording: discussing fiqh.
HAD-3414.narrator: ʿAwn ibn ʿAbdillāh ibn ʿUtbah transmitted from a conversation with Umm ad-Dardāʾ:
HAD-3414.speaker: Umm ad-Dardāʾ said, in substance:

HAD-3415.text: To Ibn ʿAbbās is attributed the view that answering a writing one has received is a right, similar to returning the greeting. It is his transmitted assessment, and not a statement of the Prophet.
HAD-3415.narrator: Aš-Šaʿbī transmitted a saying of Ibn ʿAbbās:
HAD-3415.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās

HAD-3416.text: Mudrik ibn ʿAwf met Bilāl sitting in the early morning and asked why he still remained. Bilāl answered that he was waiting for the sunrise. The report describes a concrete habit without a general command for all Muslims.
HAD-3416.narrator: Mudrik ibn ʿAwf reported an encounter with Bilāl in aš-Šām:
HAD-3416.speaker: Bilāl ibn Rabāḥ

HAD-3417.text: When gazelles appeared before Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ and turned back, a man advised him likewise to turn back. Saʿd asked him by what he recognized the unfavorable sign: by the horns when they came, or by the tails when they fled? He then warned against making superstition out of such signs.
HAD-3417.narrator: Ziyād ibn Abī Maryam reported about a journey of Saʿd:
HAD-3417.speaker: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ

HAD-3418.text: ʿAbdullāh said that hearts have times of readiness to receive and times of withdrawal. One should convey something to people as long as they are turned toward it with interest, instead of continuing to address them without regard for their condition.
HAD-3418.narrator: An instruction for passing on knowledge is reported concerning ʿAbdullāh:
HAD-3418.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd

HAD-3419.text: ʿAṭāʾ advised, when there are two conflicting possibilities, to lead people to the easier of the two. The short statement describes his transmitted way of dealing with facilitations; it does not establish an unlimited choice according to personal convenience.
HAD-3419.narrator: This reply is transmitted from ʿAṭāʾ:
HAD-3419.speaker: ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ

HAD-3420.text: Simāk al-Ḥanafī said that he had heard Ibn ʿAbbās disapprove of a person describing himself with the words “I am lazy.” The brief note names no detailed reason and must not be presented as an independent statement of the Prophet.
HAD-3420.narrator: Simāk al-Ḥanafī reported about a choice of wording by Ibn ʿAbbās:
HAD-3420.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās

HAD-3421.text: To ʿUmar is attributed the counsel to say often to one’s brother “Ǧazāka Allāhu ḫayran.” He explained that if people knew the reward of these words, they would thank one another with them more often.
HAD-3421.narrator: Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbaydillāh ibn Karīz transmitted this saying from ʿUmar:
HAD-3421.speaker: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb

HAD-3422.text: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz preferred, for a supplication, “O Allāh, grant me Your favor” rather than the wording “O Allāh, give me a charitable gift.” This fine choice of words is reported as his personal transmitted stance.
HAD-3422.narrator: Muḫtār reported that he heard ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz himself:
HAD-3422.speaker: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz

HAD-3423.text: In a conversation about Ibrāhīm at-Taymī, Iyās ibn Muʿāwiyah said that it was precisely his high esteem for him that kept him from praising him at length. When asked, he referred to the saying current at that time, that praise was regarded as a form of repayment or return.
HAD-3423.narrator: Al-ʿAwwām ibn Ḥawšab described a conversation with Iyās ibn Muʿāwiyah:
HAD-3423.speaker: Iyās ibn Muʿāwiyah

HAD-3424.text: ʿUmar warned those who lead the people in the communal prayer or admonish them publicly against overburdening them by excessive length. They should not convey the religion in a manner that produces aversion in the listeners.
HAD-3424.narrator: ʿUbaydillāh ibn ʿAdī ibn al-Ḫiyār transmitted an admonition of ʿUmar:
HAD-3424.speaker: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb

HAD-3425.text: ʿUmar first addressed his visitor as “my nephew.” When he asked about his lineage and learned that his father had not lived to see Islam, he called him “my son.” The report describes the change in his form of address in this concrete encounter.
HAD-3425.narrator: The grandson of aṣ-Ṣaʿb ibn Ḥakīm reported his encounter with ʿUmar:
HAD-3425.speaker: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb

HAD-3426.text: When al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUbaydillāh called the son of an acquaintance “my son,” Ibrāhīm disapproved of this form of address. It is a reported personal linguistic stance, not a general religious prohibition.
HAD-3426.speaker: Ibrāhīm (in the report without an added name)

HAD-3427.text: When a woman called Ibn Sīrīn “my son,” he asked her whether she had given birth to him or nursed him. After she denied both, he objected to the form of address that did not correspond to the facts. This single encounter is not extended into a general legal ruling.
HAD-3427.narrator: Muḥārib reported about the form of address used toward Ibn Sīrīn:
HAD-3427.speaker: Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn

HAD-3428.text: When Uways al-Qaranī spoke to them, his words left a particular impression in their hearts, such as the speech of others, in Usayr’s perception, did not produce. This is the observation of a listener, and not a verbatim quotation from Uways.
HAD-3428.narrator: Usayr ibn Ǧābir described the effect of the words of Uways:
HAD-3428.speaker: Usayr ibn Ǧābir about Uways al-Qaranī

HAD-3429.text: When someone speaks to people, his speech enters their hearts according to the place it has in his own heart. The report describes the effect of the inner stance of a speaker; an individual examination of the isnād is still pending.
HAD-3429.narrator: It is transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās:
HAD-3429.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās

HAD-3430.text: ʿUmar warned against the person who exalts himself and exceeds his measure: despite his high opinion of himself, he becomes of little worth in the eyes of people. The drastic comparison belongs to the transmitted admonition and is not permission to treat others with contempt.
HAD-3430.narrator: ʿUbaydillāh ibn ʿAdī ibn al-Ḫiyār reported an admonition of ʿUmar:
HAD-3430.speaker: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb

HAD-3431.text: He warned: “No arrogant person enters Ḥaẓīrat al-Quds.” The expression is deliberately left here in its original designation; the statement is attributed to him and is not presented as a prophetic Ḥadīṯ.
HAD-3431.narrator: It is reported from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr:
HAD-3431.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr

HAD-3432.text: To Abū Idrīs is attributed the statement that Allāh does not lift the covering of a servant so long as there is in his heart even a tiny measure of good. According to the source, this statement is from Abū Idrīs, not from the Prophet ﷺ; its transmission and its theological classification have not yet been finally examined.
HAD-3432.narrator: Abū Qilābah transmitted a statement of Abū Idrīs:
HAD-3432.speaker: Abū Idrīs

HAD-3433.text: When Ibn ʿAwn wanted to excuse himself for a matter that had been spread about him, Ibrāhīm replied: “Do not excuse yourself; we have already excused you before you excused yourself.” The more precise identification of Ibrāhīm’s name and the assessment of the individual isnād remain open.
HAD-3433.narrator: Ibn ʿAwn reported that he excused himself before Ibrāhīm:
HAD-3433.speaker: Ibrāhīm (reported by Ibn ʿAwn)

HAD-3434.text: When the strap of his sandal tore, ʿAbdullāh pronounced the Istirǧāʿ. When he was asked in surprise about this small occasion, he explained that the size of the strap was not what decided the matter: this loss, too, was a mishap. The isnād transmitted here between ʿAwn and Ibn Masʿūd is broken; the attribution is not established by this path.
HAD-3434.narrator: ʿAwn ibn ʿAbdillāh reported about ʿAbdullāh:
HAD-3434.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd

HAD-3435.text: He used to say: Only the one who has resolved upon the fast before dawn is fasting.
HAD-3435.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما

HAD-3436.text: Ibn ʿUmar used not to fast when traveling.
HAD-3436.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما

HAD-3437.text: He traveled in Ramaḍān, and we traveled with him. ʿUrwah fasted, while we did not fast, and he did not call on us to fast.
HAD-3437.speaker: ʿUrwah ibn az-Zubayr رحمه الله

HAD-3438.text: Whoever has days of Ramaḍān to make up and does not make them up, despite being able, until the next Ramaḍān, should, according to his view, feed a needy person a mudd of wheat for each day and also make up the days.
HAD-3438.speaker: al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad رحمه الله

HAD-3439.text: When ʿĀʾišah was in iʿtikāf, she inquired about a sick person only in passing, without stopping.
HAD-3439.speaker: ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها

HAD-3440.text: Ibn ʿUmar wore garments dyed with red earth or with saffron.
HAD-3440.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما

HAD-3441.text: A man from Yemen greeted Ibn ʿAbbās with as-Salāmu ʿalaykum wa-raḥmatullāhi wa-barakātuh and added something. Ibn ʿAbbās said: The salām ends with the blessing (al-barakah).
HAD-3441.narrator: Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAṭāʾ reported:
HAD-3441.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما

HAD-3442.text: A man greeted ʿUmar, and he returned the greeting. ʿUmar asked: How are you? The man answered: I praise Allah before you. ʿUmar said: That is precisely what I wanted from you.
HAD-3442.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-3442.speaker: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه

HAD-3443.text: Ibn ʿUmar used to go to the market and greet everyone he met, merchants and the needy alike. When he was asked the reason, he said: We go out in the morning only for the sake of the salām, in order to greet.
HAD-3443.narrator: aṭ-Ṭufayl ibn Ubayy ibn Kaʿb reported:
HAD-3443.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما

HAD-3444.text: When Ibn ʿUmar sneezed and it was said to him, “May Allah have mercy on you,” he answered: “May Allah have mercy on us and on you, and forgive us and you.”
HAD-3444.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما

HAD-3445.text: When the commanders combined the Maġrib and ʿIšāʾ prayers in the rain, Ibn ʿUmar prayed together with them.
HAD-3445.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما

HAD-3446.text: He was asked whether one may combine Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr when traveling. He answered: Yes, there is nothing wrong with that. Have you not seen how the people pray at ʿArafah?
HAD-3446.speaker: Sālim ibn ʿAbdillāh رحمه الله

HAD-3447.text: He was asked how long his father Ibn ʿUmar had delayed the Maġrib prayer when traveling. He said: The sun set while we were at Ḏāt al-Ǧayš, and he prayed Maġrib at al-ʿAqīq.
HAD-3447.speaker: Sālim ibn ʿAbdillāh رحمه الله

HAD-3448.text: When Ibn ʿUmar set out for the Ḥaǧǧ or the ʿUmrah, he shortened the prayer at Ḏū l-Ḥulayfah.
HAD-3448.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما

HAD-3449.text: Nāfiʿ traveled with Ibn ʿUmar a distance of one barīd (a historical stretch of road), and Ibn ʿUmar did not shorten the prayer.
HAD-3449.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما

HAD-3450.text: I pray the prayer of a traveler so long as I have not resolved to stay, even if this keeps me twelve nights.
HAD-3450.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما

HAD-3451.text: When ʿUmar came to Makkah, he led the people in two rakʿāt and then said: O people of Makkah, complete your prayer, for we are travelers.
HAD-3451.speaker: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḫaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه

HAD-3452.text: When traveling, Ibn ʿUmar prayed nothing additional before or after the obligatory prayer, except in the middle of the night. Then he prayed on the ground or on his mount, whichever way it turned.
HAD-3452.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما

HAD-3453.text: On the festival of breaking the fast, Ibn ʿUmar performed the washing of the whole body before going in the morning to the prayer place.
HAD-3453.speaker: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما

HAD-3454.text: When he was ill, Abū Ṭalḥah had a bedding with images removed from under him. Sahl ibn Ḥunayf reminded him of the transmitted exception for patterns on cloth. Abū Ṭalḥah confirmed this and said: But this way is more pleasing to me.
HAD-3454.narrator: ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbdillāh ibn ʿUtbah reported:
HAD-3454.speaker: Abū Ṭalḥah al-Anṣārī رضي الله عنه

HAD-0520.text: The Most Merciful has mercy on those who are merciful. Be merciful to those on the earth, then the One who is in heaven will have mercy on you.
HAD-0520.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-0520.speaker: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
HAD-0520.sharh: The commentator explains “The Most Merciful has mercy on those who are merciful” as kindness and compassion toward created beings, especially people and animals, who are met with gentleness and beneficence. The mercy of Allah promised from this includes His favor and His kind dealing with them. Regarding the call to be merciful toward those on the earth, he explains the difference from the shorter version in Abū Dāwūd and points out that at-Tirmiḏī transmits a more extensive report that contains a statement about kinship ties. He also discusses the known transmission tradition of the “first Ḥadīṯ heard”: its special characteristic of chain can be weaker than the original Ḥadīṯ. The original German dataset wrongly named Abū Hurayrah; the authentic principal transmitter is ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr, through Abū Qābūs and ʿAmr ibn Dīnār.

HAD-0524.text: The Most Merciful has mercy on those who are merciful.
HAD-0524.narrator: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr رضي الله عنهما reported:
HAD-0524.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0524.sharh: The sentence “The Most Merciful has mercy on those who are merciful” is the same beginning of the report through ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr, which is given more fully in HAD-0520. The commentary on Abū Dāwūd 4941 explains the reciprocal connection between mercy toward created beings and the mercy of Allah that is hoped for. It discusses that at-Tirmiḏī transmits a longer version in which the maintaining of kinship ties also occurs. An additional independent saying with another chain is not claimed together with this shortened dataset; the isnāds of the versions must be determined one by one.

HAD-0526.text: Protect yourselves from the Fire, even with half a date. Whoever finds nothing, then with a good word.
HAD-0526.narrator: ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim رضي الله عنه reported:
HAD-0526.speaker: The Prophet ﷺ said:
HAD-0526.sharh: Ibn al-Mulaqqin comments on the report of ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim about protection from the Fire even by means of half a date. The Prophet ﷺ turned his face away repeatedly, as if he saw the Fire before him, and urged precaution through charity. Ibn al-Mulaqqin explains the good word as an important act of beneficence: just as a material gift can gladden the needy person, a kind word can improve the inner state of the other. It can remove hatred and enmity. The Ḥadīṯ expressly names the good word as a possibility for the one who cannot give even a small material gift.
